## 10. Portfolio GitHub-token remediation — the canonical answer (2026-05-26)
- `cais-shared-services/scripts/set-vercel-env-only.sh <github-PAT> <vercel-API-token>` sets **`GITHUB_PACKAGES_TOKEN`** (type:sensitive, prod+preview) per project — BUT its hardcoded `SLUGS` list is **stale/incomplete: it does NOT include `tenderwatch`, the tourlingo pair, investor-pilot, partner-pilot, lingo-pure-ai, ndissda-automate, outreach-ready, rehearsals-ai, disaster-support, singify-platform, universal-lingo-*, r-and-d-tax**. Running as-is skips tenderwatch. Add missing slugs first, OR (better) use the Team Shared Env Var.
- **Recommended: CAS Vercel Team → Settings → Environment Variables (Shared) → `GITHUB_PACKAGES_TOKEN` = fresh read:packages PAT, Sensitive, Production+Preview, linked to all projects.** One place, covers all + future projects, no stale list. Then delete any stale PROJECT-level `GITHUB_PACKAGES_TOKEN` that would shadow the shared one. Var name must match each repo's `.npmrc` (the common name IS `GITHUB_PACKAGES_TOKEN`; TourLingo CI also uses `NODE_AUTH_TOKEN` separately).
- `PLATFORM_TRUST_DEV_OVERRIDE` is NOT a token — value is the literal `allow-unconfigured-writes` (plain, not sensitive); only on platform-trust-middleware 0.4.x consumers (tenderwatch). Separate from the token fix.
- **2026-05-26 UPDATE — Dennis set the shared Vercel var + tenderwatch override; redeployed (commit `d17b1f0`) → STILL `ERR_PNPM_FETCH_401` on the 0.4.1 tarball** (a ghp_ token is sent but rejected). Diagnosis: almost certainly a **stale PROJECT-level `GITHUB_PACKAGES_TOKEN` on the tenderwatch Vercel project shadowing the new SHARED team var** (project-level overrides shared — the exact gotcha). **FIX: tenderwatch Vercel → Settings → Environment Variables → DELETE the project-level `GITHUB_PACKAGES_TOKEN`** so the shared one applies, then redeploy. If there's no project-level copy, the new PAT itself lacks `read:packages`/caistech-org package access → copy TourLingo's known-working token value. (The `set-vercel-env-only.sh` script avoids this by remove-then-add, but its slug list omits tenderwatch.) Stopped redeploying until the shadow/token is resolved.
- **2026-05-26 UPDATE 2 — Dennis deleted the project-level token; redeploy `9a88d1a` → error CHANGED to "Failed to replace env in config: ${GITHUB_PACKAGES_TOKEN}" + "No authorization header was set."** So the project-level shadow is gone, BUT the SHARED team var is NOT reaching the tenderwatch build (var now UNSET at install). Cause: shared var either (a) not LINKED to the tenderwatch project (Vercel shared vars must be attached per-project or scoped "all projects" — creating ≠ linking), or (b) named ≠ exactly `GITHUB_PACKAGES_TOKEN` (the .npmrc reads `${GITHUB_PACKAGES_TOKEN}` literally). **SIMPLEST FIX: add a PROJECT-level `GITHUB_PACKAGES_TOKEN` directly on tenderwatch = fresh valid PAT (TourLingo's working value), sensitive, prod+preview** — shadow's gone so it's unambiguous + definitely reaches the build. Then re-trigger. Lesson for the portfolio shared-var route: the shared var must be NAMED exactly `GITHUB_PACKAGES_TOKEN` AND linked to every project (or "all projects") or `.npmrc` substitution fails at build.
- **2026-05-26 UPDATE 3 — Dennis linked the shared var; redeploy `7fba584` → STILL var-absent** (same "Failed to replace env in config: ${GITHUB_PACKAGES_TOKEN}" / "No authorization header was set"). Three deploy cycles, shared var never reached tenderwatch's build env (cause unverifiable from here — link not saved / not scoped to Production / name mismatch; no env-inspection tool available). **Abandoned the shared route for this repo → instructed Dennis to set PROJECT-level `GITHUB_PACKAGES_TOKEN` directly on tenderwatch (copy TourLingo's known-good PAT value, sensitive, prod+preview).** Project-level injects directly, no linking ambiguity, overrides shared anyway. The "shared covers all" portfolio goal is a SEPARATE cleanup (shared-var injection demonstrably unreliable here). Waiting on Dennis to add the project-level var, then re-trigger.
- **2026-05-26 RESOLVED — tenderwatch is LIVE (READY, commit `b5a083d`).** Token fixed (Dennis set it project-level after the shared var wouldn't reach the build). Then a CHAIN of build blockers, each fixed: (1) `@caistech/platform-trust-middleware` 0.3.0→0.4.1 + `PLATFORM_TRUST_DEV_OVERRIDE=allow-unconfigured-writes`; (2) **`inngest-cli@0.28.0` postinstall crash** (`tar.extract` undefined) — global `tar:^7` override forced tar@7 into inngest-cli which pins `tar:6.2.1` → scoped override **`inngest-cli>tar: 6.2.1`** (same pattern as TourLingo `globby@6>glob`); (3) **Vercel dependency-vuln check BLOCKED the deploy** (build completed fine!) — `inngest@3.47.0` flagged → pnpm override **`inngest:^3.54.0`** (→3.54.2). Final: `tenderwatch-alpha.vercel.app` HTTP 200, real title, distributor hero line live. **LESSON: a repo dormant since April hit 5 stacked blockers (stale tarball→stale token→shared-var-not-reaching→tar override→inngest CVE); Vercel's vuln check fails the deploy AFTER a clean build — grep the build-log tail for "Vulnerable version" when a deploy ERRORs with no compile error.** TenderWatch carry-over from §4 = DONE.

See also [[project_voice_placement_auditor]] (the sibling auditor pattern), [[feedback_capture_over_build]].

name: project_health_enforcement_sayfix
description: Health-check enforcement layer + SayFix preventative-maintenance productisation — IP/handoff doc + the two sensor fixes that triggered it.

**Origin (2026-07-12):** found two portfolio `health-sensors` GitHub Actions silently broken —
the CHECK was broken, not the site. Root bug (portfolio-wide template): the jobs ran
`npx --no-install portfolio-gate-smoke-*` with NO checkout/setup-node/install step, so nothing was
installed on the runner and npx 404'd on the public npm registry (the bins come from the SCOPED
`@caistech/portfolio-gate`). Correct pattern = mirror `gate.yml`: checkout → setup-node with
`registry-url: npm.pkg.github.com` + `scope: @caistech` → install with
`NODE_AUTH_TOKEN: secrets.CAISTECH_PACKAGES_TOKEN` → then the `npx --no-install` smokes.

**Fixed (both live-verified):**
- **corporate-ai-solutions** (caistech/corporate-ai-solutions, main `102c8d8`, pushed + workflow_dispatch run = SUCCESS): added install; DROPPED auth-smoke + session-smoke — it's a marketing/marketplace site with NO user auth (`/login`/`/signup`/`/forgot-password` 404 by design; only operator `/admin` + `/pipeline` logins). `gate.yml` already omits auth-smoke there for the same reason; `routes.config.json` carried the "no user auth — see gate.yml" note. Collapsed to a single `health` job (route smoke only). `auth.config.json`/`session.config.json` left as unused stubs.
- **LingoPureAI** (caistech/LingoPureAI, main `338f927`, **committed, NOT yet pushed** — sits on top of the also-unpushed recall fix `d15553b`): the sensor was scaffolded but **never committed** (untracked = zero monitoring). Added install; KEPT auth+route smoke (LingoPure HAS user auth; verified live auth 8/8, routes 10/10 against `https://lingo-pure-ai.vercel.app`). DROPPED session-smoke until `QA_TEST_USER_*` Actions secrets + a real `session.config.json` are wired (shipped one is a template stub with a hardcoded fake password). Fixed stale `routes.config.json` baseUrl (`lingopure.vercel.app` 404 → `lingo-pure-ai.vercel.app`). **Live prod URL = `lingo-pure-ai.vercel.app`; the CI var `PORTFOLIO_GATE_PREVIEW_URL` is already correct.**

**The systemic lesson → the IP doc:** the canonical checks are DEFINED (PRODUCT_STANDARDS,
gate-readiness) + TOOLED (naive-tester/voice-auditor/portfolio-gate/health-sensors) but NOT
ENFORCED. naive-tester/voice-auditor are manual skills (gate URL-sharing via the local Stop hook,
NOT a Vercel deploy); health-sensors is POST-deploy monitoring, not a pre-deploy gate; Vercel
deploys on push-to-main independent of Actions unless branch-protection + required gate + "wait for
CI" are wired; and no one watches whether the sensor is even running (drift/rot per repo). This is
why LingoPure "passed" naive-tester (it did, manually + recorded) yet still had no running sensor.

**Written up:** `cais-shared-services/HEALTH_ENFORCEMENT_AND_SAYFIX_PREVENTATIVE.md` — captures
(1) an INTERNAL enforcement layer (canonical sensor template to stop drift, a real pre-prod gate,
a "watch-the-watchmen" red/missing-sensor rollup) and (2) the SAYFIX PRODUCT upgrade: fold health
sensors into SayFix so it moves from REACTIVE (user files a bug → GitHub issue) to PREVENTATIVE
maintenance (continuous sensors → proactive tickets, Mnemo-recall the likely fix) = a stronger,
higher-value recurring service. **Productisation is DEFERRED to a dedicated SayFix session** — that
doc is its brief. Reuse: `@caistech/portfolio-gate` (smokes), `@caistech/usage-meter` (reporter
pattern), `@caistech/sayfix-embed` (widget/tickets), Bug Knowledge Protocol + Mnemo.

**PORTFOLIO SWEEP DONE (2026-07-12):** scanned all repos — the broken sensor was portfolio-wide. **All 9 repos that run a sensor on `main` are now GREEN** (corporate-ai, LingoPure, DealFindrs, investor-pilot, F2K-OffshoreModular, property-services, F2K-Projects, investorpilot, F2K-Checkpoint). 17 other repos have the sensor file locally but never pushed to main (= zero monitoring; the "watch-the-watchmen" gap). Fixed via worktree-on-origin-main sweep + `MSYS_NO_PATHCONV=1` for `git show ref:path` on Windows. **The sweep was a field test of every 3rd-party failure mode** — now in the handoff doc §10: CI-install artifacts (npx-no-install, private @caistech registry dep, lockfile drift vs `npm ci`/`--frozen-lockfile` → use tolerant install, pnpm `ERR_PNPM_IGNORED_BUILDS` → `--ignore-scripts`, `setup-node cache:` post-step path-validation error → drop the cache key, npm-vs-pnpm) vs genuine target signal (missing sensor, auth-surface drift → per-target profile, wrong/stale URL, protected `/api/health` 401 → per-route expectedStatus, probe-broke≠site-down). **HEADLINE for the SayFix session: the in-repo-CI model CANNOT ship to a 3rd-party client** (they can't install the private @caistech dep; you can't assume their pm/lockfile/auth/URL) → **run EXTERNAL hosted probes (targets + profiles, not workflows + secrets)**, which deletes all CI-install failure modes and keeps the real signal. Doc §10 + memory here are the brief. cais-shared-services main `8333e51`.

**Open:** push LingoPure main (2 unpushed commits: recall `d15553b` + sensor `338f927` — pushing
deploys the recall UI change to prod + re-arms the url-share/naive-tester gate). Separately, the
`@caistech/dataroom-core` extraction (shared-services layer only, NOT productising) is still queued —
see [[project_lingopure_investor_dataroom]].

candidates.title: The site could never receive a lead — the contact form faked success AND /api/leads always 500'd on a NOT NULL column. Fixed and verified on production 2026-08-
candidates.material:
---
name: project_lead_capture_was_broken_twice
description: "The site could never receive a lead — the contact form faked success AND /api/leads always 500'd on a NOT NULL column. Fixed and verified on production 2026-08-06."
metadata:
  node_type: memory
  type: project
---

Found by a pre-outreach audit on 2026-08-05, hours before pushing `/services` to a network. **Two
independent failures on the same path, and the second was invisible until the first was fixed.**

## Failure 1 — the form faked success

`src/app/contact/page.tsx` submit handler was, in its entirety:

```js
await new Promise(r => setTimeout(r, 1000))
setFormState({ isSubmitting: false, isSuccess: true })
```

It rendered **"✓ Message Sent! We'll get back to you within 24-48 hours"** and transmitted nothing.
Proven four ways: empty CDP network log after clearing, patched `fetch`/`XHR`/`sendBeacon` recording
zero calls, the deployed bundle containing **no `fetch(` and no `/api/*` at all**, and the source.

This is the `PRODUCT_STANDARDS` §9 anti-pattern from the f2k onboarding form. A fake success is worse
than no form, because **the visitor stops looking for another way to reach you** — and you never learn
they existed. It silently cost the highest-intent half of the traffic: the ones who wanted to ask a
question before booking a call.

## Failure 2 — the route had never worked either

Wiring the form to `/api/leads` exposed it: **`leads.source` is `NOT NULL` and the route never set
it**, so every insert failed with

```
null value in column "source" of relation "leads" violates not-null constraint
```

and returned 500. **The `leads` table held ZERO ROWS** — the confirming evidence that no lead had
ever reached it, from any caller, ever.

Fixed with `source: source || 'website'` (defaulted, not required, so existing callers keep working).
`source` is the categorical channel; `source_page` and `source_agent` record the specific surface.

## Verified

POST to **production** `/api/leads` → **HTTP 200**, row lands with every field populated. Test rows
deleted afterwards; the table is back to zero, a clean slate for real leads.

## ⚠️ The remaining fail-soft worth knowing

`src/lib/email.ts` skips the notification when the key is missing:

```js
if (!apiKey) { console.warn('RESEND_API_KEY not set — skipping email notification') }
```

So without `RESEND_API_KEY` in Vercel, a lead **still saves to Supabase** and the visitor **still
sees success** — but no email arrives, and leads accumulate in a table nobody is watching. **Confirm
that variable is present in production.**

Also note the distinction that cost some confusion: **Supabase SMTP settings only affect AUTH email**
(magic links, password resets). Lead notifications go through the **Resend API** directly. Fixing one
does nothing for the other.

**How to apply:** any form anywhere in the portfolio — submit it and assert the response before
believing it works. "A contact form exists" is not a finding; "I submitted it and X happened" is.

Related: [[project_outreach_referral_push]].

candidates.title: ExecutorAI production deploys failed silently for a month (expired Vercel NODE_AUTH_TOKEN); the durable lesson is that no repo could notice a stale prod
candidates.material:
---
name: project_deploy_silent_failure
description: ExecutorAI production deploys failed silently for a month (expired Vercel NODE_AUTH_TOKEN); the durable lesson is that no repo could notice a stale prod
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: 51005e92-dd6b-4f27-bf04-a819235b2405
  modified: 2026-07-26T04:40:37.896Z
---

**What happened (found 2026-07-26).** Every ExecutorAI production deploy from **2026-06-24 to
2026-07-26** failed — 18 consecutive `ERROR` states. Proximate cause: the **`NODE_AUTH_TOKEN` env
var in Vercel expired**, so `npm install` died with a 401 fetching `@caistech/*` from GitHub
Packages before the build ever started. Fixed by reinstalling the token; deploys green again.

**ROOT cause — a variable-name mismatch, and why only THIS repo rotted.** The portfolio propagates
**`GITHUB_PACKAGES_TOKEN`** (`portfolio-manifest.yaml` `shared:`, pushed by
`scripts/set-caistech-token.sh`, and listed on executorai's manifest entry). But ExecutorAI's
committed `.npmrc` resolves **`${NODE_AUTH_TOKEN}`**. So every portfolio rotation updated a
variable this repo's build never read, and the hand-set one aged out unnoticed while sibling repos
stayed fine. Confirmed against the Vercel env API 2026-07-26: `NODE_AUTH_TOKEN` updated
**2026-07-26** (the manual fix), `GITHUB_PACKAGES_TOKEN` updated **2026-06-11** (stale).
CI had already hit this and papered over it — `rls-audit.yml` sets BOTH names from one secret; the
Vercel side never got the same treatment.

**PENDING FIX:** point `.npmrc` at `${GITHUB_PACKAGES_TOKEN}` so portfolio rotation reaches this
repo. **Do NOT switch until a fresh token is propagated into that variable** (it currently holds
the stale 11-June value) — switching first trades a working build for a broken one. Sequence:
re-run `set-caistech-token.sh <fresh PAT> <vercel token>`, then flip `.npmrc`, then verify a build.

**Why it matters more than the token.** Production kept serving the build from commit `06b564b`
while `main` moved on, and **nothing surfaced it**. The undeployed commits included the RLS
column-exposure hardening (`f3ff029`) and admin MFA enforcement (`6c91a07`) — security work that
had been described to Iress as remediated. The migrations *were* applied directly to the DB, so the
database was ahead of the deployed code the whole time. Mitigating: pre-launch, no real users.

**The trap that hides this.** A "is prod up?" check that asserts HTTP 200 **passes against a stale
prod** (it serves fine — just old code) **and against Vercel's SSO deployment-protection wall**,
which answers **200 with a login screen**. ExecutorAI's team alias
(`executorai-corporate-ai-solutions.vercel.app`) is protected; the public one is
`executorai-gules.vercel.app`. Status code alone cannot tell you the app is up, or current.

**How to apply.** Any deploy check must assert **three** things, not one: (1) latest production
deployment is `READY`; (2) **its commit SHA matches the ref you expect** — the assertion that
catches a healthy-looking stale prod; (3) the public alias serves the app, not a protection wall.
It must **fail when unconfigured, never skip** — a check quietly doing nothing is indistinguishable
from one that passed, which is the failure being ended. Built as
`scripts/check-deploy-status.mjs` + `.github/workflows/deploy-status.yml` (push-to-main with
`--wait`, plus a daily cron so token expiry is caught without a push); needs a `VERCEL_TOKEN` repo
secret. Being promoted into `@caistech/portfolio-gate` as the portfolio-wide standard.

**GitHub ORG SECRETS DO NOT WORK for these repos (verified 2026-07-26).** The `caistech` org is on
the **GitHub Free** plan with 35 private repos, and on Free an **organisation secret is only
readable by PUBLIC repositories**. A private repo gets an empty string, silently — proven here: a
`VERCEL_TOKEN` org secret at `ALL` visibility resolved to blank in an executorai workflow, and the
same run passed the moment a **repo-level** secret was set. Consequence worth checking: the four
`QA_TEST_*` org secrets (set 2026-06-13, `ALL`) are almost certainly **inert** in every private
repo, which is why `sync-qa-secrets.mjs` — described in PRODUCT_STANDARDS §9.5 as "the bridge until
repos inherit org-level secrets" — is in fact still doing all the real work. **The inheritance end
state needs a GitHub Team upgrade; until then, per-repo secrets pushed by script are the only
mechanism that works.**

Related: [[project_iress_xplan_dd]] (the security work that sat undeployed),
[[reference_executorai_supabase_ref]].

candidates.title: Kira can search Drive/contacts, read a document's contents, and offer to file it. Shipped + deployed; keep_document is NOT yet on the fleet.
candidates.material:
---
name: project-kira-drive-contacts-handoff
description: Kira can search Drive/contacts, read a document's contents, and offer to file it. Shipped + deployed; keep_document is NOT yet on the fleet.
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: d4be5b63-38bf-4cc5-8df2-ed2f19807058
  modified: 2026-08-01T00:08:56.443Z
---

## Fleet state (verified 2026-08-01)

**`verify-agent-fleet` reports "fleet is consistent"** — 10 business agents on **14 tools** each
(`keep_document` was the 14th), 3 personal on 6, discovery skipped. Prompt sections correct on all.

Getting there took **two `--tools-only` passes**: the first reported *"6 re-provisioned, 7 failed"*
on transient `fetch failed` errors. That count was honest this time (the verifier confirmed 4 had
landed, 6 hadn't) — but the lesson holds either way: **the script's tally is a claim, the verifier
is the answer.** It is idempotent, so the fix is simply to run it again and re-verify.

**BUILT AND LIVE 2026-07-31** (`db25187` + `9330678`). Supersedes the earlier "START HERE — Kira has
nothing calling it" state, which was true for about a day.

## What is live

- Orchestrator `382c2a9`: `GET /api/v1/tenants/:tenantId/lookup?kind=drive|contacts&q=…`
  (note the real path carries the `/api` prefix — the handoff note said `/v1/…`).
- Kira: `lib/kira/lookup.ts` → `app/api/kira/webhooks/{search_drive,lookup_contact}/route.ts`,
  tool defs in `lib/kira/lookup-tools-def.mjs`, gated `filesAndContactsSection` in `prompts.ts`.
- **Fleet: 10 business agents on 12 tools, 3 personal on 6, all prompt sections correct**, asserted
  by re-reading every agent — not by the patch script's own 200.

## The contract that must not be flattened

`ok:false` = the lookup did not happen, and its `reason` is a sentence written to be **spoken**,
passed through unaltered. `ok:true` with zero results = *"I looked and there is no Roger."* Merging
the two recreates the exact 31-July failure, where she told him his contact book held no address on
the authority of a search that never ran. `lib/kira/lookup.test.ts` is nine tests of that one
distinction, including the two most likely to be lost in a tidy-up: our own missing env var, and a
thrown fetch.

## What this session learned about the live sequence

- **The re-provision reported "2 failed" twice and was wrong both times** — the tool attachment had
  landed on all ten business agents; the failures were downstream (override enablement, a transient
  `fetch failed`). Exit codes on this script describe the whole pass, not the part you care about.
  `scripts/verify-agent-fleet.mjs` now answers the real question and is the thing to trust.
- **Use `--tools-only`.** A full re-provision re-binds the workspace webhook, and the package's
  reuse-by-URL check can race into two enabled webhooks with different secrets — silent post-call
  HMAC failure. When only the tool list has drifted, rebinding is risk with no upside.
- **Verify the local tool secret against prod BEFORE re-provisioning**: POST a live tool route with
  it; `200` means prod accepts it, `401` means you were about to bake a rejected credential into
  every agent. It is in `.env.local` even though it is sensitive in Vercel.
- `ORCHESTRATOR_URL` / `ORCHESTRATOR_SECRET` **are** set in prod (sensitive → absent locally and
  from `vercel env pull`). Check names via the Vercel API rather than reading the empty pull.
- Node block-buffers stdout to a file, so a backgrounded script producing no output for 20 minutes
  is not evidence it is hung.

## Reading and filing a document (`f40fb44`, `66eb42e` — 2026-08-01)

The **first live voice call happened** and proved the search in the same minute it exposed its
limit: he found the Lot 109 pre-contract quote, asked which of two files was the one sent to the
client, and she offered to "check the contents" — then had to take it back. The tool description
invited the over-promise: `search_drive` searches by what is *inside* files, which is true of the
query and not of the results, which carry names only.

- **`read_document(file_id)`** — id comes from a search result. Extraction runs through this repo's
  existing knowledge-ingest path (push to ElevenLabs, read back parsed HTML) because the
  orchestrator's connector handles Google-native/CSV/text and his files were a PDF and a .docx;
  adding mammoth + pdf-parse would have been a **third** copy of document extraction, which
  SHARED_SERVICES assigns to `@caistech/dataroom-core`. The vendor copy is deleted in a `finally`,
  asserted by a test. Truncation reports `truncated: true` rather than silently answering about
  terms it never read.
- **`keep_document`** — reading and filing are different acts and only one is a question. She
  *offers*; filing happens only on a yes. A **separate tool, not a flag**: a flag is something a
  model sets, a second call is something it must decide to make after hearing an answer. The
  motivating case is real — he separated Global Buildtech material out of the Factory2Key Genome by
  hand ([[project-kira-two-entities]]), and auto-filing everything she opened would quietly undo
  that. The prompt says when NOT to offer, and never twice for the same document.
- **Deliberate asymmetry:** `read_document` DELETES its extraction copy, `keep_document` keeps it.
  A question borrows the vendor as a parser; a decision to keep uses it as storage.
- 191 tests pass. `indexKnowledgeText` was split out of `ingestKnowledgeDocument` so a source that
  already has its text skips the parser.

## Still unproven

The **broader live voice call** — headless has no microphone, so only the operator can run it (see
[[project-kira-naive-tester-state]]). One call has now happened and drove the two commits above;
`keep_document` has never been exercised by voice, and cannot be until it is on the fleet.

⚠️ `KIRA_SWARM_ADAPTER` now EXISTS in Vercel production+preview, contradicting
[[project-kira-orchestrator-seam]]'s "unset on purpose". Its value is sensitive and unreadable; the
mirror matching the orchestrator's tasks suggests the memory is stale rather than the env wrong.
Confirm before relying on either.

have a complete business identity and an agent, so **both sail past every trap below** — which is

**FIXED and verified (13 redirect hops → 1):** `app/setup/layout.tsx` wrapped `/setup/*` in
`UserShell`; `UserShell` redirects to `/setup/business` when the business identity is incomplete;
`/setup/business` is inside that layout. It redirected to itself until `ERR_TOO_MANY_REDIRECTS`. The

the state every new owner is in by definition. Fix: `requireSetup={false}` (the prop already existed,
Settings uses it for the same reason).

**OPEN, and the highest-value unknown:** the business identity form appears to save nothing. Every
field the action requires was correctly populated (`legal_name` resolved via ABR, `abn_lookup`,
street/locality/state/postcode, reply_email, sign_off_name, authorised=on), the only submit button
is "Save and continue", and clicking it leaves you on `/setup/business` with **no error rendered and
no `business_identity` row written**. The action's success path redirects to
`/dashboard?identity=saved`; that never happens. Four automation attempts.
**Cannot distinguish product bug from harness artifact** — React server actions can behave
differently under automation. *Dennis clicking Save once on a fresh account settles it in ten
seconds.* Ask him before spending more time.

correctly required (`mailer_autoconfirm: false`) · the ABR lookup box is the **required input with
no `name` attribute**; `abn` and `legal_name` are hidden mirrors it fills, so automation must type
into the unnamed field, not `[name="abn"]`.

complete on my side."* Both causes were live then and both are now fixed — the auth 500s (Resend key

candidates.title: Typing to Kira is a real second interface, built and verified end to end 2026-07-31 — one persona, two transports, writes to the same memory
candidates.material:
---
name: project-kira-text-transport
description: "Typing to Kira is a real second interface, built and verified end to end 2026-07-31 — one persona, two transports, writes to the same memory"
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: d4be5b63-38bf-4cc5-8df2-ed2f19807058
  modified: 2026-07-31T11:22:48.922Z
---

**Built and PROVEN against production 2026-07-31** (`db27609`). `POST /api/kira/chat/text`.

## Why it is not a fallback

Two reasons and only one is the microphone. The commonest cause of "no mic" is an owner clicking
**Block** on the permission prompt — likely, not exotic, for a man who has told nobody he is selling.
And he has asked for typing in his own words four separate times: he cannot paste a URL or a message,
only upload a file. See [[project-kira-captured-asks]] if it exists, else `docs/CAPTURED_ASKS.md`.

## The design decisions worth keeping

- **ONE persona, two transports.** The system prompt is **read from the deployed ElevenLabs agent**,
  not rebuilt locally. A locally-assembled persona drifts the first time either side is edited, and
  the symptom is her being subtly different depending on how you spoke to her. Reading the live
  prompt also inherits every patch applied to running agents that never went through the repo.
- **It writes to the SAME memory.** Turns land in `conversations` / `conversation_messages` with a
  `text:<uuid>` conversation id, so a typed session stays distinguishable in Genome provenance.
  Distil runs on `pagehide` via `sendBeacon` — the text equivalent of the post-call webhook. Without
  it, everything typed stays a transcript and never becomes Genome.
- **Four refusals**: won't answer at all if the live prompt can't be read (replying as a generic
  assistant in Kira's window is the worst outcome available) · a failed model call does NOT persist
  his message (a turn stored with no answer resurfaces as something she ignored) · the insert is
  awaited, never floated · errors render into the transcript rather than being swallowed.

## Verified, not assumed

Driven against production with a real QA session (minted via
`cais-shared-services/scripts/qa-session.mjs --magic-link`): unauthenticated **401** · real message
**200** answering as Kira · **continuity PASS** (told her a gate code, she returned it next turn) ·
4 messages persisted · empty **400** · over-length **413** · unknown agent **404** · distil on end
**`{"ok":true,"distilled":true}`** · and the fact reached `kira_memory` as
*"The gate code at Lot 91 is 4417."*

## The bug that produced it — worth not repeating

`textInput` was first switched on as a one-prop "fix" without reading the widget. `submitText` sends
to the live session when connected and otherwise calls `props.onTextFallbackSubmit?.(value)` — an
optional call on a prop nobody passed. With no mic there is no session, so typing cleared the box and
did nothing: no message, no reply, no error, no console output. **Worse than the honest "Not
supported" it replaced**, sitting on the one action the product exists for.

⚠️ **Note the two paths are different.** With a WORKING mic and a live call, typed text goes via
`convo.sendUserMessage()` into ElevenLabs — it does reach the transcript as a user turn, and the
agent used to deny seeing it (fixed by the typed-input prompt section, live on all 11 agents).
`onTextFallbackSubmit` only fires when there is NO live session.

**QA gotcha:** `kira_agents.user_id` is the APP user id; a minted session carries the AUTH id. Bridge
through `users.auth_user_id` or the ownership check 404s.

name: project_inngest_pitfalls_and_prefill_live
description: "Two Inngest traps that cost a day (2026-06-22): Vercel→Inngest auto-sync was broken so new functions silently never ran; and returning a PDF base64 from a step.run hits Inngest's step-output limit (output_too_large). Plus: design-prefill extraction is now live, demo uses a dedicated org."
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: 3c7b6bf1-a776-485f-ac71-0172bc5103fb
---

MMC Build (mmcbuild-application), 2026-06-22 — long debugging session getting the design-attribute prefill live. Two Inngest pitfalls, both now fixed + guarded.

**TRAP 1 — Vercel→Inngest auto-sync was NOT firing.** A NEW Inngest function (or a new trigger on an existing one) is invisible to Inngest Cloud until the app re-registers. The Vercel integration was not auto-syncing on deploy, so `extractDesignAttributes` + `reapStuckJobs` (both added this week) were deployed in code but **never ran** — events for them went nowhere, silently. Symptom: function deployed (route.ts registers it, build green) but zero runs in the Inngest dashboard. FIX to force a sync: `curl -X PUT https://app.mmcbuild.com.au/api/inngest` → returns `{"message":"Successfully registered","modified":true}` when it picks up new functions. PERMANENT FIX shipped: `.github/workflows/inngest-sync.yml` — on Vercel's `deployment_status` (success + Production) it PUTs the serve endpoint. **If a new Inngest function "does nothing," check the Inngest dashboard for the function + force the PUT sync FIRST.**

**TRAP 2 — never RETURN a large blob from `step.run`.** Inngest memoizes every step's return value; a step that returned the PDF as base64 (~1.4MB) exceeded the step-output size limit → the provider/gateway error surfaced as `output_too_large` BEFORE the vision call even ran. This failed every real plan and was deeply misleading (looked like a model/token problem — bumping maxTokens + shrinking the prompt did nothing because the failure was pre-vision). FIX: do download + vision in ONE `step.run`, return only the small result. `processPlan` already does download+ingest in one step for the same reason. Rule: keep big buffers INSIDE a step; return only small JSON.

**Design-prefill is now LIVE end-to-end.** `extractDesignAttributes` (one vision call on `plan/uploaded`) writes `plans.design_attributes` = AGGREGATES (wet_area_count/has_stairs/has_balcony_deck/has_swimming_pool + scalars — NOT a rooms[] array, which overflowed output). `getProjectDesignPrefill` maps it; `getDesignPrefillState` adds a `pending` flag; the questionnaire is wrapped in `QuestionnairePrefillGate` (client) which shows "Reading your design…" and polls until attrs land (90s cap + Skip button, never traps). Operator backfill: `GET /api/admin/backfill-design-attributes` (operator allowlist incl. mcmdennis@gmail.com now). 8/12 prod plans extracted fine; 4 null = orphaned migration records with missing storage files (skip cleanly). Direct storage probes use the service_role at `~/.mmc-serv-rol` via REST (the supabase-js client HANGS from the local sandbox — use curl against `/rest/v1` + `/storage/v1`). Diagnostic note: the Gladesville "two-storey home" SAMPLE is actually backed by the big 260603 architectural set (6 storeys) — sample is MISLABELED, extraction is correct.

**Beta demo now uses a DEDICATED org** ("Beta Demo (preview)"), not the operator's — so "clean demo session" wipes all modules incl. the org-scoped Direct `professionals` listing + Train `enrollments` without touching the operator's real org. `beta.actions.autoTickRunTasks` now ticks the run-task only on `status='completed'` runs. See [[project_comply_remediation_loop_and_prefill]] for the convergence-loop work in the same sweep.

**UPDATE 2026-06-26 — two more Inngest facts (cost confusion this session) + the prefill-gate was reworked:**
- **Inngest functions execute PROD code, NOT preview-deploy code.** A Vercel preview serves the Next.js app/server-actions from the branch, but `plan/uploaded` / `test3d/extract.requested` events are handled by whatever deployment is registered with Inngest = **production**. So EXTRACTION changes (classifier, multi-storey, big-PDF) can NOT be tested on a preview — they only take effect after merge-to-main + Inngest re-sync. Confirmed live: a preview upload classified 15 pages (old prod code) when the branch code does 30. To test extraction work: merge to main → confirm `inngest-sync.yml` fired (or force `curl -X PUT app.mmcbuild.com.au/api/inngest`) → upload on PROD.
- **Extraction caches per (org_id, storage_path) in `test_3d_jobs`.** Re-opening an existing project returns the OLD cached layout; a beta sample pick COPIES the file (new storage_path) so it re-extracts. To test NEW extraction code you must do a FRESH upload in a NEW project, not reopen an old one. (Content-addressed cache to replace this = SCRUM-315.)
- **Prefill-gate reworked (supersedes the "90s cap never traps" note above).** The 90s cap WAS the bug: a 32MB plan's extraction takes ~2m40s, so the form mounted EMPTY and ignored the late data (form seeds responses once at mount). Now `getDesignPrefillState` returns a 3-state status (ready/extracting/unavailable); the gate WAITS while extracting (progress + staged commentary), resolves only when confirmed done (90s manual-escape + 6min backstop so it can't trap), and the form applies late-arriving prefill to untouched fields. Shipped in PR #52 (main). See [[project_multistorey_3d_and_questionnaire_enrichment]] for the full session.

name: project_session_2026_08_05_golive_sprint
description: "2026-08-05/06 go-live sprint — Stripe switched LIVE, fabricated social proof removed, /admin gate fixed, terms rewritten. Plus the diagnostic tricks that found them."

---

**2026-08-05/06: the big go-live sprint.** 12 commits to main, Stripe moved to live keys,
four client-reported bugs diagnosed. Karen answered almost every open decision in one meeting.

## Shipped to main (all deployed)

`ed38f9c`+mkt fabricated social proof REMOVED from live site · `420b263` create-project errors visible ·
`6f38393`+mkt social-proof shell (empty, flag-gated) · `27549b4`+mkt#3 CTA switch merged (inert) ·
`1c7cc61` TC-BILL-002 made able to fail · `c8e6b03` /admin operator gate + layout backstop ·
`7e8be92`+mkt CTA label "Get started" · `da13b8e` terms payment/renewal/cancellation + version
re-acceptance · `d710824` cancellation path · `8076e5e` terms gate blocking made visible ·
`fe0149d` /signup reachable when signed in.

## ⚠️ Stripe is LIVE in production (from 2026-08-05)

Keys + all 6 price IDs live; **preview deliberately left on TEST keys** — they used to share one
env row spanning `preview+production`, so going live would have put every preview on live keys.
Split first (see [[reference_mmcbuild_vercel_github_topology]]).

**Traps hit:** (1) the price IDs Dennis first supplied were the TEST set; the ones in the keys file
were all `prod_…` **PRODUCT** ids — checkout needs `price_…`. **Resolve live prices from the Stripe
API with the live key** rather than transcribing (`GET /v1/prices?active=true&expand[]=data.product`),
which settles mode and accuracy at once. (2) **`STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET` is still unproven** — test and
live signing secrets both start `whsec_`, so a mismatch is invisible: payment succeeds, subscription
silently never activates. Only a real card proves it (SCRUM-332).

⚠️ **Live Stripe portal has ZERO billing_portal configurations** → cancellation via the portal may
fail for the first real customer. Unproven (no live customer to test). Fix: Stripe Dashboard →
Settings → Billing → Customer portal → enable "Cancel subscriptions".

## Diagnostic techniques worth reusing

- **Click does nothing → find the overlay.** `document.elementFromPoint(cx,cy)` at the element's
  centre. Karen's "can't change state region" was the terms-gate `fixed inset-0 z-[100]` backdrop
  eating every click while the form stayed legible behind it at 60% opacity. The checkboxes were fine.
- **"It won't let me sign up" → check for a redirect, not a bug.** `curl -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code} %{redirect_url}"` with and without a session cookie. `/signup` 307'd to `/dashboard` for signed-in users.
- **Mint a real session to reproduce**: `cais-shared-services/scripts/qa-session.mjs --magic-link`
  with `QA_TEST_EMAIL`, then `curl -b` or feed the cookie to `/browse`.
- **Vercel `sensitive` env vars are write-only** — even `?decrypt=true` returns nothing. Use
  `updatedAt` timestamps to tell whether a value was actually changed.

## Standing rules learned

- **Vercel tokens are scoped AT CREATION to one team.** A token made for the decoy team can never
  see the live one, and the diff it produces looks perfectly valid. Always verify the project id
  (`prj_mNQT2kY6CqcTeiZhJMX1VqE5qB9f` = live app) before trusting any Vercel answer.
- **A `throw` in a server action is invisible in production** — see
  [[project_ai_router_and_honest_error_standards]]. Return `{ error }`.
- **Terms versioning**: `TERMS_VERSION` was written but never read, so bumping it re-prompted nobody.
  Fixed in `lib/legal/terms.ts`; the bump re-prompts all 43 profiles.

## Open at session end

Karen: Go Live DATE (353), what replaces social proof (376), confirm the five `utm_*` HubSpot fields
exist, **the real-card test (332)**. PRs #148+mkt#4 (attribution) unblocked and ready to merge.
Not done: privacy-policy disclosure draft, case-studies links, enterprise-enquiry ticket.
HubSpot portal ID = `442558966`.

also holds `_deprecated-mmcbuild-webapp`, `MMCBuild`, and `mmcbuild-prod` (the old
`dennissolver/mmc-market` line). They are NOT the actual repo; their config, Supabase refs and
env files are stale by definition. Canonical is `mmcbuild-application` only.

`C:\Users\denni\PycharmProjects\mmcbuild-application\.env.local` sets
`NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL=https://skyeqimwnyuuozvhubdc.supabase.co` — a DEAD host (NXDOMAIN); prod

(`git ls-files` → 0), so it is NOT in GitHub and never was** — it is Dennis's machine-local dev
config, and each machine has its own. Production is unaffected (Vercel holds its own env).

to a non-existent host until `NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL` was overridden in the environment. Fails
loudly rather than dangerously. Don't describe this as "in the repo", and don't assume a stale
local value came from one of the deprecated clones above.

The CAS→MMC migration left a confusing split that cost hours on 2026-06-08. The map:

**GitHub**
- Repo lives at **`mmcbuild-ai/mmcbuild-application`** — `mmcbuild-ai` is a GitHub **USER account** ("MMC Build", `admin@mmcbuild.com.au`, created 2026-02-08), **NOT an organisation**. So it never appears in the "Organisations" picker in Vercel/GitHub-App flows — only under personal/user accounts. This is the #1 trap.
- `mmcbuildai` (no hyphen) is a **separate Organisation** Dennis admins, holding only 1 unrelated repo. The app repo is NOT in it.
- Local `dennissolver` has **push (collaborator), not admin** on the repo — so `dennissolver` cannot reconnect Vercel, transfer the repo, or manage the Vercel GitHub App on `mmcbuild-ai`. Only the `mmcbuild-ai`/`admin@mmcbuild.com.au` owner can.
- Durable fix (teed up to Karthik 2026-06-08): `gh repo transfer mmcbuild-ai/mmcbuild-application mmcbuildai` to move it into the org Dennis admins.

**Vercel** — TWO projects both named `mmcbuild-application`:
- **LIVE:** team **`mmcbuild`** (slug, id `team_E45VWicyLmHADCGFNR05GEGf`), project `prj_mNQT2kY6CqcTeiZhJMX1VqE5qB9f` → serves `app.mmcbuild.com.au`, auto-deploys `main`. THIS is production.
- **LEGACY DECOY:** team **`mmc-build`** ("MMC Build CAIS", `team_DquayrHfy4FCoeViJMWU7fIq`), project `prj_qKKLAkGGG…` → frozen at sha `b8325d6`, serves nothing real. The claude.ai Vercel MCP token can ONLY see this one + CAS teams, NOT the live `mmcbuild` team — so MCP deploy/inspect hits the WRONG project. The local `vercel` CLI (authed as `mcm-dennis`) CAN see `mmcbuild`.
- Local `.vercel/project.json` was relinked to the live project on 2026-06-08; `vercel --prod` from the repo now targets production correctly. Before deleting the legacy `mmc-build` decoy, CONFIRM it holds no live domain (`app.mmcbuild.com.au`) — don't assume.

⚠️ **Conflict to reconcile:** [[project_supabase_migration_state]] (2026-06-05) mapped the LIVE prod Vercel project to team **`mmc-build`** (`team_DquayrHfy4FCoeViJMWU7fIq`), but on 2026-06-08 the user's own Deployments view at `vercel.com/mmcbuild/...` showed the **`mmcbuild`** team (`team_E45V…`) deploying `f161b84` to Production — i.e. the live team appears to have MOVED to `mmcbuild` (likely during handover). Verify which team currently holds `app.mmcbuild.com.au` before acting destructively on either project.

**UPDATE 2026-06-11: `main`→prod auto-deploy IS WORKING** — the deploy list shows PR #37 (`42d4cb1`) and #38 (`b83e6b0`) merges both auto-deployed to **Production / Ready** via `github/dennissolver` within ~1 min of merge. So the "auto-deploy paused/disconnected" note below is STALE — do NOT tell the user a merge won't deploy; it does. (The repo-transfer SCRUM-278 may still be open, but Git auto-deploy is reconnected.)

**Pending (likely stale):** repo transfer `mmcbuild-ai/mmcbuild-application` → `mmcbuildai` org was tracked as **SCRUM-278**. The "until then auto-deploy is paused (disconnected 2026-06-08); `vercel --prod` interim" claim is SUPERSEDED by the 2026-06-11 observation above.

## ⚠️ TWO SITES, TWO REPOS — a marketing/pricing change must be made TWICE (2026-08-01)

There is a **second repo and a second Vercel project**, and it is easy to miss because
`mmcbuild-application` contains its own `src/app/(marketing)/` routes that look canonical:

| Site | Repo | Serves |
|---|---|---|
| **App** | `mmcbuildai/mmcbuild-application` | `app.mmcbuild.com.au` |
| **Public marketing** | **`mmcbuildai/mmcbuild-marketing`** (canonical; clone at `~/PycharmProjects/mmcbuild-marketing`) | **`mmcbuild.com.au`** — where the ads point |

✅ **`/terms` and `/privacy` are NO LONGER duplicated (2026-08-07, marketing `0979bce`).** They had
drifted badly: the 5 Aug terms rewrite (card + day-14 auto-charge) landed in the APP repo only, so
the page a buyer read BEFORE paying was the January version saying *"free trial periods may be
offered at our discretion"* while the terms they accepted AFTER signing up promised an automatic
charge. Both live, both "the terms", nothing saying which governed. **Fix was consolidation, not
mirroring** — mirroring a legal document only makes drift slower (two URLs = two documents = two
"last updated" dates = a real question about which one binds). The marketing repo now 308-redirects
both paths to the app and its page files are DELETED (redirects run before filesystem routes, so a
kept copy could never render but would absolutely get edited). **App is canonical** because it holds
the `TERMS_VERSION` acceptance gate. Live chain is apex → www → app (2 hops; the apex→www leg is
Vercel's own domain rule, not ours). **`/pricing` is still duplicated and CANNOT be redirected** —
it's the shop window — so it stays a manual two-repo edit.

Both repos have their **own copies** of `/pricing` and `/mmc-suppliers`, and they had **drifted**:
the app repo carried stale supplier tiers ($99/$499) while the marketing repo had the correct ones
($199/$299/$250). Fixing a price/pricing-copy issue in the app repo alone changes **nothing a
customer sees.** Verify per-site with `curl` against BOTH hostnames, never one.

- The local marketing clone's `origin` is **`dennissolver/mmcbuild-marketing`** — canonical is
  `mmcbuildai` (already a remote named `mmcbuild`); push there.
- ⚠️ **Those two remotes are the SAME repo, not two mirrors** (`dennissolver` redirects to
  `mmcbuildai` after a transfer) — verified 2026-08-01: pushing a branch to `origin` then to
  `mmcbuild` reported "Everything up-to-date", and `git push origin --delete <branch>` removed it
  from BOTH. So a tidy-up delete on the "wrong" remote deletes the branch you just pushed to the
  right one. Push to `mmcbuild` first and don't try to clean up `origin`.
- **Shared feature flags must be set in BOTH Vercel projects.** `NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPPLIER_PRICING_ENABLED`
  (hides Trades & Suppliers price claims, default-on, `="false"` to hide) gates the equivalent page in
  each repo. Setting it in one leaves the two sites contradicting each other — which is exactly what
  happened for ~an hour on 2026-08-01.
- The marketing repo has **no test framework** (`scripts` = dev/build/start/lint only). Verify by
  building each flag state and grepping the emitted `.next/server/app/*.html`.
## "Account is blocked" on PR checks = a SECOND, blocked Vercel project on the same repo (2026-08-01)

A red `Vercel – <repo>` check saying **"Account is blocked."** does NOT mean the deploy failed.
Diagnosed 2026-08-01: **two Vercel projects, in two different Vercel accounts, are connected to the
same GitHub repo**, and both post a commit status under the *identical* context name. On PR #1 of
`mmcbuild-marketing`, one second apart:

```
23:24:14 | Vercel – mmcbuild-marketing | failure | Account is blocked.  | (generic help article)
23:24:13 | Vercel – mmcbuild-marketing | success | Deployment completed | vercel.com/mmcbuild/...
```

- **Both repos are affected** (`mmcbuild-application` too). Whether the check shows red is a **race**:
  GitHub keeps only the LATEST status per context, so it's green when the healthy `mmcbuild` status
  lands last (what happened on application PR #140) and red when the blocked one does.
- **Deploys are fine.** Every GitHub deployment — preview and production — reports success from the
  live `mmcbuild` team. Previews are NOT actually blocked (an earlier reading of this was wrong).
- **Why it's invisible:** a blocked account never creates a deployment, so its status has no
  deployment URL to click — it links to `vercel.com/knowledge/why-is-my-account-deployment-blocked`,
  which names no team. GitHub shows one Vercel App installation (app id 8329), so the app-level view
  reveals nothing either.
- ✅ **CAUSE CONFIRMED + RESOLVED 2026-08-04.** Not billing, not a suspended account. Vercel's own
  message: *"The deployment was previously blocked because mcm-dennis did not have contributing
  access to the project on Vercel. mcm-dennis is a member of your team. The deployment can be
  redeployed."* — i.e. **a push authored by a GitHub account that is not a contributing member of
  the Vercel project is Blocked**, per deployment. Matches the deployment history exactly: the
  `Blocked` runs (May 24–26) are authored `github/dennissolver` / `github/karthik281`, while
  `chore: trigger deploy as mmcbuild-ai` on the same commit is `Ready`. Access has since been
  granted. **Proven empirically:** an empty commit pushed to `mmcbuild-marketing` PR #3 built
  `SUCCESS` where the prior run was `FAILURE`. So a Blocked check is fixed by re-running the
  deployment, not by debugging the build.
- ⚠️ **Marketing previews are behind Vercel SSO** — the preview URL 302s to a Vercel login page, so
  `curl` sees the wall, not the site. A signed-in team member can view it; automated checking needs
  a Protection-Bypass-for-Automation token. Don't read the 302 as a broken preview.
- **Real risk:** not the deploy, but that genuine Vercel failures become indistinguishable from this
  noise. Fix by disconnecting Git on (or deleting) the stale project.
- `mmcbuild-marketing` had **zero prior PRs** (PR #1 was 2026-08-01) — the normal workflow there has
  been direct pushes to `main`.

See [[reference_mmcbuild_supabase_keys]], [[project_supabase_migration_state]].

candidates.title: How a HAND-BUILT / pre-built product gets its survey markers (the dogfood marker-pass) — reusable <SpecMarkers slug/> + public /api/public/spec-markers/[slug] e
candidates.material:
---
name: project_survey_marker_pass
description: "How a HAND-BUILT / pre-built product gets its survey markers (the dogfood marker-pass) — reusable <SpecMarkers slug/> + public /api/public/spec-markers/[slug] endpoint + survey-manifest.json. And the why_now/P3 gotcha that bites every pre-built product."
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: 6c7bd990-0d0e-4146-b79e-ccd8d66d00ca
---

**Pipeline is NOT special** — it's the first member of the "HAND-BUILT product" category. Every product needs the same 14 survey `data-*` markers; what differs is who plants them: a factory-GENERATED product gets them from the build (markerProps); a hand-built/pre-existing product has no generator and can't be safely regenerated (the generative design→build would rewrite the real app), so its markers are **wired manually** = the "marker-pass." Every pre-built product the operator onboards hits this.

## The marker-pass mechanism (shipped 2026-06-17, commit c2e8ed5)
- `src/lib/methodology/spec-marker-attrs.ts` — `specMarkerAttrs(cardRow)` maps a product_validation_status row → `{ "data-promise": …, … }` (the 14 SURVEY_MARKERS fields + `data-why-now` from `feasibility.why_now`). ONE source of truth.
- `<SpecMarkers slug/>` (`src/components/pipeline/SpecMarkers.tsx`) — server component, reads the card via cockpitDb, emits a hidden `<div hidden {...attrs}/>`. For products co-located on the pipeline instance (pipeline itself). Used on `/pipeline/welcome` (slug=pipeline).
- `GET /api/public/spec-markers/[slug]` — PUBLIC endpoint (outside the middleware matcher) returning any product's marker attrs. **The foundation for EXTERNAL pre-built products** (separate codebases, no pipeline-DB access): their shared drop-in fetches this and SSRs the attrs (the survey reads server HTML, NO JS exec — markers must be server-rendered).
- `public/survey-manifest.json` → `{"routes":["/pipeline/welcome"]}`. The survey fetches `<mvp_url>/survey-manifest.json`, gets routes (∪ `/`), fetches each, greps markers. No manifest → falls back to `/`.
- Verified live: manifest ✅, 14/14 spec markers SSR'd on /welcome ✅, endpoint ✅.

## ⚠️ THE why_now/P3 GOTCHA (bites every pre-built product)
PRE-HARD **P3 = distributor + distributor_outcomes + data-why-now**, and P1/P2/P3 GATE the RENOVATION verdict (P4 is informational, not gating). The coach often fills the 14 graded spec fields but leaves **`feasibility.why_now = null`** (it did for pipeline) → no `data-why-now` marker → **P3 fails → TEARDOWN despite 14/14 evidenced.** Fix: populate the card's `feasibility.why_now` (product content — the "why now"). Then `<SpecMarkers>` emits it automatically. **Rollout implication: ensure the coach captures why_now, or P3 fails for every pre-built product.**

## ⚠️ TWO MORE GOTCHAS (found running pipeline's own survey, 2026-06-17 — bite every pre-built product)
1. **Root must be FETCH-FOLLOWABLE to 200 (P1).** The survey reads the mvp_url ROOT for P1 (homepage 200), and node `fetch` (no JS) must reach 200. Pipeline's `app/page.tsx` used React `redirect('/pipeline/welcome')`, which served a **header-less 307** → `fetch` got `status 307, ok:false, redirected:false` → P1 fail → verdict **UNREADABLE** (no score) despite a clean /welcome. Fix: redirect via **next.config `redirects()`** (proper Location header, fetch follows) — commit 45ef4e3. Now root → 200 (redirected→/pipeline/welcome). Any pre-built product whose root redirects via a client/React redirect (or a header-less 307) will UNREADABLE the same way — use a config/HTTP redirect, or have the root answer 200.
2. **icp_stage is an ENUM marker** (`seed|growth|scale|operating-business|enterprise`) — the only ENUM of the 14. The card stores PROSE → off-enum → not evidenced → 13/14 (still clears MIN_EVIDENCED ≥12/14, so it didn't block pipeline's RENOVATION). **FIXED in the coach (commit 33bb36a):** `ICP_STAGE_VALUES` in apply-coach-fields.ts; the graded path normalises + enum-validates icp_stage (CoachFieldError lists valid tokens); VOICE_PREAMBLE tells Morgan icp_stage/demand_tier/distributor_benefit_mode take a TOKEN not prose, and why_now is REQUIRED. Pipeline's card icp_stage set to `operating-business` for a clean 14/14 on the next run.

## PIPELINE SURVEY = RENOVATION (2026-06-17) — survey gate passed
After the root-redirect fix (45ef4e3), pipeline's survey verdicted **RENOVATION** (13/14, PRE-HARD pass). Card notes seen: "Unbound — no validation tied to a deployment yet" (the user-side Run survey posts deployment_id=null, so the verdict isn't deployment-pinned — informational), and "Readiness HARD gate not passed (5/7)" — that's the SEPARATE Gate-1 readiness gate, NOT the survey: #39 (no secrets) + #40 (Vercel env) are "not yet tested" (+ 9 other unscored). Next step for pipeline: **"Run full validation"** to record those → HARD gate → weighted score. (Survey = Stage 3 / "build evidences spec"; readiness = Stage 5 / go-live gate.)

## VOICE: the canonical shape + the auditor false-negative (resolved 2026-06-17)
- **Canonical voice = the COACH (intake) + the INTERVIEW agent**, both with BAKED agent ids in `voice.config.ts` (COACH_AGENT_ID default `agent_1601kv24fz3efvfb8yyhe5rjazw6`, provisioned for pipeline; works with NO Vercel env). The Morgan intake coach IS live (operator-confirmed) — reachable via "New idea" → /pipeline/new-ideas.
- **The floating "cockpit clarifier" was LEGACY** (corporate-ai-solutions carryover), read `NEXT_PUBLIC_ELEVENLABS_AGENT_COCKPIT_CLARIFIER` (never provisioned → rendered null), NOT the canonical shape. **REMOVED** (pipeline e3a295a + 7713b6b: PipelineChromeClarifier/AdminChromeClarifier/CockpitClarifier + clarifier-context + the voice.config consts). The PipelineChromeClarifier I'd added to "fix §6" was the same legacy widget — mistaken; reverted.
- **#10 was a FALSE-NEGATIVE** → recorded pass (judge override): the coach is the voice; the auditor (a) read STALE cred env names → login silently failed → saw only the public landing, and (b) hunted the legacy clarifier. **Fixed the voice-auditor** (cais-shared-services 46ef2ed): reads canonical `QA_TEST_USER_EMAIL/PASSWORD` first, and after login visits the `--voice-url` surface AUTHED (the coach is behind auth + not the authed root).
- **REMAINING (orchestration):** the validation-run dispatch (pipeline run-full-validation → validation-run.yml → voice-auditor args) should pass **`--voice-url=/pipeline/new-ideas`** (the coach surface) so the auditor auto-lands on it. Until then #10 stands on the judge override.
- **#40 was a FALSE-`na`** (CI can't reach Vercel) → recorded pass: Vercel API verified 34/34 env vars sensitive, 0 development, 0 plaintext. The portfolio fix to stop the recurring `na`: give the validation-run CI a Vercel token so the auto-probe can verify env.

## REMAINING C — DONE (2026-06-17): `@caistech/spec-markers@0.1.0` published
Built + published (cais-shared-services commit `3e5acca`, tag `v0.1.38`, on GitHub Packages). It's a
thin async-Server-Component drop-in: `<SpecMarkers slug="x" pipelineUrl?/>` fetches the public
`GET <pipeline>/api/public/spec-markers/<slug>` (default base `https://pipeline-nine-silk.vercel.app`,
override via prop or `SPEC_MARKERS_ENDPOINT`/`NEXT_PUBLIC_PIPELINE_URL`) and SSRs the attrs;
degrade-don't-break (returns null/{} on failure). Also `fetchSpecMarkers(slug, opts)` + `buildSurveyManifest(routes)`.
The marker MAPPING stays single-sourced in pipeline (the endpoint builds `{attrs}`), so the package
never drifts. Verified live: 15 attrs incl. `data-why-now`. **Per external pre-built product:** install
`@caistech/spec-markers`, drop `<SpecMarkers slug="x"/>` on the public landing (a SERVER component),
write `public/survey-manifest.json` (`buildSurveyManifest(['/'])`), set the card `mvp_url`, and ensure
`feasibility.why_now` is set (else P3 fails). Cataloged in SHARED_SERVICES.md. See
[[project_validation_agent_surface_resolution]] for the companion #40/agent fixes.

candidates.title: Prelabz founder pitch-coaching app — the one-coach model, founder flow, key IDs, QA account, and the local-build gotcha
candidates.material:
---
name: project_prelabz_architecture
description: "Prelabz founder pitch-coaching app — the one-coach model, founder flow, key IDs, QA account, and the local-build gotcha"
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: b3f1d8d9-f5f6-4798-beff-9d371b60fc9c
  modified: 2026-08-05T07:49:58.384Z
---

Prelabz (`prelabzAI`, Next.js 14 App Router) is a **founder pitch-coaching** app: upload a deck → AI deck analysis (section-by-section) → coach. Prod: **prelabz.vercel.app** (Vercel prj_0zxZ0TzDBo6rPdrCz8GxPCPXqCz5, team team_hwN7IFtd2Fo3DCj9C67ZwI1t). Supabase ref **ttzxsjvjfcodglluxlcn**.

**One-coach model (decided 2026-07-18):** the single coach is **Maya**, the canonical `@caistech/discovery-agent` voice+text agent on `/founder/discovery`. The analysis page `/coaching/[deckId]` is a pure analysis viewer (summary, section-by-section, per-section founder notes, branded-PDF download) that **hands off** to Maya via `/founder/discovery?deckId=<id>` — there is NO separate in-page text coach (removed; the old `/api/coaching/{start,chat}` routes deleted). `loadDiscoveryContext(supabase, subjectId, deckId?)` (in `lib/discovery/persistence.ts`) feeds the chosen deck's full analysis + the founder's section notes to BOTH channels, and instructs the coach to OPEN on the weakest flagged section. `/api/discovery/start` reads `deckId` and re-anchors the pushed `promptOverride` (the package's `startSession` only takes subjectId — specialise the returned override, don't fork). Discovery page has a deck picker (default most-recent or `?deckId=`, locks once a session starts).

**Founder flow (dashboard journey):** Profile → Upload → See Your Analysis → Fix & Re-upload → Talk to Your Coach. Nav/labels: "Deck Analysis" (the `/coaching` surface) and "Talk to Your Coach" (Maya) — one name each (consolidated 2026-07-18).

**RLS gotcha:** `deck_analysis` policy is `user_id = auth.uid()`; **founders have NO insert policy**, so all analysis WRITES go through the service-role admin client AND must set `user_id = deck.founder_id`, or the founder's later SELECT returns 0 rows (blank analysis). See [[project_prelabz_architecture]].

**QA accounts (both in `cais-shared-services/.secrets/qa-secrets.json`):** founder = `dennis@factory2key.com.au` (`QA_TEST_USER_EMAIL`; ShelfShare deck lives here — note its `company_name` is junk "h4hl"); admin = `dennis+qaadmin@factory2key.com.au` (`QA_TEST_ADMIN_EMAIL`) — must be BOTH a confirmed user in Supabase `ttzxsjvjfcodglluxlcn` AND in prod `ADMIN_EMAILS` to reach `/admin`. **Testing without the flaky login form:** mint a real session cookie via `cais-shared-services/scripts/qa-session.mjs` (pass `NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL`/`ANON_KEY` + `QA_TEST_EMAIL`/`QA_TEST_PASSWORD` as env, `--origin <url>`; emits `sb-ttzxsjvjfcodglluxlcn-auth-token[.0/.1] = value`, spaces around `=`), set it in `/browse`, navigate. **Browser-free gate check:** POST creds to `https://ttzxsjvjfcodglluxlcn.supabase.co/auth/v1/token?grant_type=password` (apikey=anon) → 200 = account authenticates; then curl `/admin/resolve` with the cookie → `/admin/users`=allowlisted, `?error=not_admin`=valid-but-not-in-ADMIN_EMAILS, plain `/admin/login`=cookie rejected. The anon URL+key are extractable from the prod JS bundle. (⚠️ prelabz's Supabase is `ttzxsjvjfcodglluxlcn`, NOT `vwvfmsuquohlgxcpzdjo` — a different app's DB Dennis briefly named.)

**Local build gotcha (READ BEFORE trusting a local build):** `next build` FAILS on this Windows box at `/api/coach/materials` with `DOMMatrix is not defined` / `@napi-rs/canvas` native-binding failure (pdfjs). This is **pre-existing and LOCAL-ONLY** — Vercel's Linux runtime builds it fine. Verify builds via the **Vercel deployment state** (get_deployment READY), not the local `next build`, which never reaches later routes. "✓ Compiled successfully" (before page-data collection) is the meaningful local signal.

**Admin portal (dual-auth §8.5, built 2026-07-18):** the operator surface is **`/admin`** (renamed from `/superadmin`), entered ONLY via **`/admin/login`** → `/admin/resolve` (server-side allowlist check, bounces non-admins to `?error=not_admin`). Landing top-bar nav carries an "Admin Sign In" link. Chromed pages live under the `app/admin/(portal)/` route group (users, cohort, settings, index→users) with `AdminSidebar` (§4 chrome: nav + Settings + Sign Out); `/admin/login` + `/admin/resolve` sit OUTSIDE the group so they render bare. **Admin = the `ADMIN_EMAILS` allowlist ONLY — the old `superadmin` role/`superadmins`-table gate was removed** (per Dennis, 2026-07-18: "admin only"). `middleware.ts` is the single gate: `isAdminEmail(user.email)` (`lib/auth/admin-emails.ts`, reads BOTH `ADMIN_EMAILS` plural + legacy `ADMIN_EMAIL` singular, comma-split, and **strips surrounding quotes per entry** — the prod value was once saved with wrapping `"..."` so the LAST email carried a trailing quote and silently failed to match; 2026-07-18). Admin pages use `useAuth({requireAuth,redirectTo:'/admin/login'})` (no role check — they trust middleware); the triage API authorises via `isAdminEmail` too. `use-auth.ts` no longer resolves a `superadmin` role (only `founder`/`portal_admin`). **GOTCHA — the allowlist is load-bearing:** if neither `ADMIN_EMAILS` nor `ADMIN_EMAIL` is set in the target env/Vercel, EVERY admin is locked out (redirect loop to `/admin/login`). (Note: the users-list page still shows a `founders.user_role`='superadmin' filter/badge — that's display of a table column, not an access gate.)

**Admin cross-user data reads (why Users/Cohort showed 0):** the `founders` table is RLS-scoped to the owner, so an admin querying it from the BROWSER client sees only their own row. Admin console reads/writes across founders MUST go through **`/api/admin/founders`** (GET list + PATCH cohort-bucket override) — a service-role route gated by `isAdminEmail` (it's `/api/admin/*`, OUTSIDE the middleware `/admin/*` matcher, so it self-gates server-side). `/admin/users` + `/admin/cohort` fetch from it; never query `founders` client-side for cross-user data (2026-07-18). Also fixed 2026-07-18: `/admin/users` crashed with a TDZ "Cannot access 'E' before init" because the `if(authLoading) return` sat ABOVE the `const loadUsers` decl that the mount useEffect calls — early-returns must sit BELOW all fn-const declarations.

**This deployment is a DEMO, not the destination (Dennis, 2026-08-05):** the app at `prelabz.vercel.app` "will be wrapped up in the primary prelabz.com site later anyway." Weigh investment accordingly — fix what testers actually hit and what carries a security or data consequence, but do not gold-plate branding, domain, SEO or marketing surfaces on this deployment, since they are destined for consolidation into prelabz.com. Correctness, access control and the substrate carry over; the shell does not.

**Deck upload is DIRECT-TO-STORAGE (changed 2026-08-05).** The browser gets a signed upload URL from `/api/deck/upload-url` and PUTs the file straight to Supabase Storage; `/api/deck/upload` then takes JSON metadata only. Posting the file through the route capped every upload at Vercel's 4.5 MB body limit — full detail in [[reference_vercel_45mb_body_limit_breaks_uploads]]. `/api/coach/reupload` uses the same shape (and gained the auth check it never had — it previously trusted a `sessionId` from the body). Shared constraints live in `lib/deck/upload-constraints.ts`; read error bodies with `lib/http/response-error.ts`, never `.json()` before `response.ok`.

**PDF text extraction at upload has NEVER worked and is gone.** pdfjs needs `@napi-rs/canvas` for its DOMMatrix polyfill, which is absent from the serverless bundle, so it threw on Vercel exactly as on Windows — swallowed as non-fatal, which is why every PDF row has `raw_text` NULL. Nothing depends on it: `/api/deck/analyze` sends PDFs to Claude as a **native document block** for precisely this reason, and only PPTX (pure-JS extractor) populates `raw_text`.

**Maya's memory now has both legs (2026-08-05).** Local memory = the `convai_*` tables read back at connect. The SEMANTIC leg is `lib/discovery/semantic-memory.ts` via `@caistech/mnemo`: `rememberFounderStory()` writes the distilled `FounderStory` from the post-call `onResult` seam, `recallFounderStory()` is APPENDED to `primeContext` at session start. Per-founder scope via `orgScope('prelabz-founder-<uuid>')`, conclusions only (never transcript), fail-soft both ways. Needs `MNEMO_API_KEY` in Vercel or it silently no-ops. Voice = **Sarah** (Kira's), see [[reference_portfolio_voice_ids]].

**Gate CI caveat:** the portfolio-gate memory-loop probe **cannot assess this repo**. It models `uid` and `conversation` identity; prelabz drives the convai routes through `@caistech/discovery-agent`, which resolves identity from a SIGNED SESSION TOKEN and supplies no `resolveToolIdentity` — so a baked `?uid=` yields `400 Missing identity or conversation_id`. That is the agent being STRICTER than the probe, not weaker. Recorded as `memoryLoop: false` **with the reason in `memory-loop.config.json`** rather than faked green; upstream fix is a signed-token mode in `probeMemoryLoop`. The post-call signature check DOES pass (unsigned → 401).

See [[reference_caistech_pdf_and_auth_gotchas]] for the auth-middleware + PDF/ESM specifics, [[project_prelabz_investor_portal]] for the portal/roles/access model, and [[feedback_always_standardise_to_canonical]].

candidates.title: | @caistech/security-gate | v0.3.0 — TWO FIXES, one of them the reason nobody was usin
candidates.material: | `@caistech/security-gate` | **v0.3.0 — TWO FIXES, one of them the reason nobody was using the red team.** (1) **The `/red-team` subpath had never been importable.** The package is `"type": "module"` with ESNext, and every relative import was extensionless — which `tsc` compiles happily and Node ESM refuses with `ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND`. It built green and shipped broken, and directory specifiers (`./probes`) needed `/index.js` on top, since Node ESM does no directory resolution at all. 19 files corrected; the subpath now imports and `ALL_PROBES` (32) resolves. Worth stating plainly: a published entry point that throws on import is invisible to a type checker, invisible to a build, and only findable by importing it — which nothing did. (2) **`EffectProbe` + the `Subject` synthetic contract**, the non-conversational sibling `RED_TEAM_CANONICAL.md` §1.1 describes. The existing `Probe` is single-turn and scores RESPONSE TEXT against `failureIndicators: RegExp[]` — right for *does this endpoint say something it shouldn't*, useless for *could this actor reach something they shouldn't*, and an endpoint that refuses politely while leaking in the same body passes the regex and fails the customer. `EffectProbe` takes `observe`/`attempt`/`verdict` and **computes the verdict from the difference, not the words**; `assertEffectProbe` REJECTS a probe that declares `observe()` and never reads `before`/`after`, because that is a text check wearing an effect check's clothes. **`Subject.assertSynthetic()` is the piece §1.3 calls the most important and it was entirely absent** — `RegisteredEndpoint` has no notion of whose data is at risk, which is how Kira's first run pointed at the live owner's account and was saved by an unrelated 403 (luck, not design). The runner now **refuses** — not warns — until synthetic identity is proven, and a probe that throws counts as a FINDING, never a pass. Extracted from a 14-probe ExecutorAI suite where two probes returned HTTP **200** and would have passed any status-code check, because the 200 was a *"Report not found"* page. ⚠️ Purely additive: `Probe`, the runner and the 32 probes are untouched; two live consumers (SayFix, platform-trust) unaffected. |

candidates.title: | @caistech/sayfix-embed | SayFix bug-reporting widget — GBTA-controlled service layer.
candidates.material: | `@caistech/sayfix-embed` | SayFix bug-reporting widget — GBTA-controlled service layer. Wire `<SayFixWidget repo="…" />` (root layout; `repo` MUST equal the SayFix `repos.github_repo`) per the PRODUCT_STANDARDS SayFix gate. **v0.6.0+ adds DYNAMIC PLACEMENT** — the launcher inspects the host page (fixed/sticky floaters, chat widgets, cookie banners, checkout CTAs) and auto-picks the safest corner, relocating at runtime via `MutationObserver`+resize as the page changes; per-page choice remembered in localStorage. ✅ **v0.7.0 CLOSES THE CONTENT-BLINDNESS DEFECT.** `collectContentConflicts` adds a third pass that inverts the question: instead of finding all the content and avoiding it, it hit-tests the handful of places the launcher can actually go (`elementsFromPoint`, ~9 samples per candidate) and asks what is underneath each — a leaf carrying a non-empty text node, or an `img`/`svg`/`canvas`/`video`, is a real conflict; `body` or an empty container is free. Emitted as `kind: 'content'` at **weight 0.6**, below `interactive`, because covering a button breaks the page while covering a paragraph obscures it — real, not equal. **The obvious fix does not work and was rejected**: adding every text element as an obstacle means every candidate takes an overlap hit on a content page, `OVERLAP_PENALTY` swamps every preference bonus, all corners score equally terrible and the choice degenerates to candidate order — "never cover any content" is unsatisfiable for a floating overlay. It also catches images and canvases, which the two structural passes miss entirely, and is **cheaper** than them (~9 hit-tests vs two 400-element scans). **The security posture holds**: it asks WHETHER a text node is non-empty, never what it says — existence, not value — which is also why it cannot rank importance and treats a price and a footnote alike. Host opt-out: `data-sayfix-avoid="false"`. Degrades silently where `elementsFromPoint` is unavailable. ⚠️ **Remaining limit, unchanged:** `collectObstacles` gathers only `position: fixed|sticky` elements plus `button, a[href], input, select, textarea, [role=button], [role=link]`. Plain text in a div is invisible to it, so the launcher will happily sit on the single most important string on the page (in BucketLyst: the voucher redemption code and its ACL-mandated expiry date) and report zero conflicts, correctly by its own model. (2) **"mobile collapses to a right-edge tab" does NOT happen at default props.** `right-edge-tab` is first in `DEFAULT_MOBILE_CANDIDATES` (+6 rank), but `position` defaults to `'bottom-right'` and is passed as `preferred`, worth `PREFERRED_BONUS` +8 — so bottom-right wins 112–106 on the FIRST render, then `REMEMBERED_BONUS` +14 locks it in via localStorage. The edge-tab only wins when a real obstacle overlaps bottom-right (`OVERLAP_PENALTY` 220). Verified live: `sayfix:pos:<path>:m = bottom-right` on a 375px viewport with `matchMedia("(max-width:640px)")` true. If you want the edge tab on mobile, pass `position="right-edge-tab"` explicitly. Pure engine (`computePlacement`/`collectObstacles`, reusable by a future vanilla-JS loader) exported alongside the widget; opt out with `autoPlace={false}` for the legacy static corner. `SayFixWidget` is now a `"use client"` component (re-exported from the barrel, so server components still render it unchanged). **v0.5.0: WHITE-LABEL** — the button default label is brand-neutral ("Report a problem", no "SayFix" text) + a `color` prop for the brand accent (`<SayFixWidget repo color label />`); the intake it opens is white-labelled server-side from the tenant `brand_config`. **v0.3.0+ ships a compiled `dist/` + zero runtime deps (inlined SVG icons) → no `transpilePackages` needed; ≤0.2.0 shipped raw `src/index.ts` JSX and broke Next builds.** Rollout runbook: `SAYFIX_INTEGRATION_ROLLOUT.md`. |

candidates.title: Gate zero: is the thing you are about to test actually deployed?
candidates.material:
### Gate zero: is the thing you are about to test actually deployed?

**Run `portfolio-gate-deploy-status` BEFORE any live tester.** Every finding below is worthless if
production is not running the code you think it is — a passing test against a stale build is worse
than no test, because it manufactures false confidence.

```bash
npx portfolio-gate-deploy-status --public-url <public prod URL> --app-marker "<Product>"
```

This is not hypothetical. ExecutorAI's production deploys failed **silently for a month**
(2026-06-24 → 2026-07-26): every push errored at `npm install` with a 401 from GitHub Packages (an
expired `NODE_AUTH_TOKEN` in Vercel), so production served a month-old build while `main` moved on.
Nothing surfaced it. The undeployed commits included RLS column-exposure hardening and admin MFA
enforcement — security work already described to a partner as remediated.

Two traps it exists to close, both of which defeat a naive check:

- **A stale production is healthy.** It serves 200s all day. Only comparing the **deployed commit
  SHA** against your ref exposes it.
- **A protection wall answers 200.** Vercel's SSO deployment-protection page returns HTTP 200 with
  a login screen, so "the site responds" passes against a product nobody can reach. Point testers
  at a **publicly reachable** production URL and assert an app-specific marker in the HTML.

It **fails when unconfigured rather than skipping** — a check quietly doing nothing is
indistinguishable from one that passed. A repo that genuinely does not deploy on Vercel opts out
with a recorded reason (`--not-applicable "<reason>"`). Wired into the shared
`templates/.github/workflows/gate.yml` on push/schedule, plus a daily cron so token expiry is
caught without a push. *(Codified 2026-07-26; `@caistech/portfolio-gate` ≥0.8.0.)*

candidates.title: fix: the three pages that served a header, a footer and sixteen characters
candidates.material:
fix: the three pages that served a header, a footer and sixteen characters

Ray round 6 timed /plan blank for ~15s and /login ~7s, with no spinner and no
console error: "the page where you ask for my card is not a slow page, it's a
broken one, and I have no way to tell the difference."

The cause is in the server response itself, not in the network. /plan gates both
its branches on client state, and AuthForm renders a wordless three-bar
placeholder until it has a browser Supabase client. So the HTML carries the
chrome and nothing else — measured on production: 164 characters of chrome and
SIXTEEN of content on /plan, 143 and 16 on /login. The sixteen are the SayFix
widget's "Report a problem"; it is the only server-rendered text on either page.

Every existing check passed over this, correctly. The pages answer 200, serve the
expected commit and are not redirected, so deploy-status, smoke-routes and
public-routes all go green — each asks whether the page RESPONDS, and this is a
question about whether it SAYS anything.

The fixes are both the same shape, and the shape is the point: the copy goes in
the branch the server actually renders, which hydration REPLACES. Putting it in
AuthShell instead would have stacked a second heading under the canonical's own
mode header after hydration — the duplicated-chrome defect from the same report,
moved rather than fixed.

  - AuthForm now renders the title/subtitle both auth pages already pass and the
    adapter silently discarded (they were documented as accepted-for-compat).
  - /plan gains a !ready branch stating what the product is while the valuation
    is read off the device.

Also marks the 11 genuinely-public pages @public-route, taken from middleware.ts
rather than intuition. The repo had zero markers, which means the existing
public-routes audit has been silently skipping here — it now runs, and passes.

Found by the new check, not by a tester: /signup is blank in exactly the same way.
Ray's persona will not create an account, so nobody had ever looked at it.

Corrects one thing in the handoff: /genome already server-renders 3,935 characters
of content. Moving its 'use client' down would have changed nothing a visitor sees
and been reported as a fix.
