candidates.material:
fix(kira): retire the hand-rolled memory-loop test for the canonical guard (+ pricing correction) (#28)

* fix(kira): retire the hand-rolled memory-loop test for the canonical guard

Kira's RUNTIME loop was already canonical (lib/kira/convai.ts consumes
@caistech/elevenlabs-convai). What survived was the VERIFICATION: a 202-line
scripts/test-memory-loop.mjs written during the four-failed-fixes saga, before 0.7.0
shipped probeMemoryLoop. Kira then upgraded to 0.7.0 and nobody swapped the test over — so
it was a fork of something the package now owns, and it could not have been catching the
continuity case the package added in 0.7.3.

Deleted. The workflow now runs the canonical probe via portfolio-gate:

  npx portfolio-gate-memory-loop --config memory-loop.config.json

memory-loop.config.json carries the three things that are genuinely Kira's, rather than
forking the logic to express them: the webhook path (/api/kira/webhooks), the memory table
(kira_memory), and the tool-secret header.

That header turned out to matter. Kira guards its routes with x-kira-tool-secret while the
probe hardcoded x-convai-tool-secret, so the canonical guard 401'd against Kira on the
first run. Fixed at source in convai 0.7.5 (toolSecretHeader) rather than worked around
here — the guard being unusable by consumers who had bothered to guard their routes is
very likely part of why it ran in zero repos.

Verified against Kira production: 5/5 PASS, including "a NEW conversation sees the
previous one". First live run of the canonical guard anywhere.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* docs(kira): next-session notes — the gate, the three decisions, and what shipped

The naive-tester FAILED against production, so the URL is gated until the blockers are
fixed and a PASS is recorded. That is stated first, because sharing the URL is the thing
the gate exists to stop.

Three findings are DECISIONS, not bugs, and each is written up with its mechanism, its
options and the cost of each so the next session doesn't re-derive them:

- The voice consent modal is ElevenLabs' vendor default and it is not wrong — WE are the
  loose ones. Verified in session that the package never configures consent text, so this
  hits every voice product, BucketLyst included.
- The valuation contradiction is a weighted-average artefact: owner-dependence scores 0 but
  the other four factors carry 7 of 10, so 'I am the business' can still cross the 'high'
  band and trigger copy saying the opposite of the weakness line. Capping the band is
  words-only; reweighting re-prices every number already shown to people. That distinction
  is the whole decision.
- The industry field free-types, so an unmatched sector silently becomes the market average
  while the helper text promises otherwise.

Also records the finding that is strategy rather than a bug: 10% of 9 is .90/month, and
the tester's alternative — a pre-sale transferability report an advisor attaches to an
appraisal — is a better channel than the referral link.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* refactor(kira): consume the canonical memory pipeline; drop the hand-rolled Mnemo client

Kira was the only product that had assembled the Mnemo dual-write, and it did so by hand
inside onConversationComplete: snapshot prior facts, distil, dedupe, index net-new. That
sequence is now @caistech/elevenlabs-convai 0.8.0's completeConversationMemory(), so Kira
calls it instead of re-implementing it — and BucketLyst and every future voice product get
the same leg by consuming the package rather than by remembering to build it.

- lib/kira/memory-dedup.ts DELETED — dedupeUserMemory and activeMemoryKeys are canonical now.
- lib/kira/mnemo.ts is now a THIN ADAPTER over @caistech/mnemo rather than a fourth
  hand-rolled HTTP client. It survives because three callers depend on its names
  (recall.ts, uid-tools.ts, integration/stubs.ts) and because the per-user scope decision
  is genuinely Kira's and worth keeping visible here.
- The scope prefix stays 'kira-user-' and is now imported through the package's
  voiceMemoryScope, so the prefix used by the adapter and the one used by the post-call
  pipeline cannot drift apart. Changing it would orphan every fact already stored for every
  Kira user, which is why it is called out in the file rather than left as a constant.

Build green, lint 0 errors, 44 tests.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* ci: run the voice memory-loop gate + the semantic-wiring audit

Both steps come from @caistech/portfolio-gate's shared template. They SKIP CLEANLY
(exit 0) in any repo that does not declare @caistech/elevenlabs-convai, so this costs
nothing where there is no voice agent.

Added everywhere rather than per-repo-on-request because the previous arrangement was
"each product remembers to verify its own memory loop" — and probeMemoryLoop shipped in
0.7.0 and ran in ZERO repos. The guard existed; nobody ran it; the bug reached production
twice. Verification has to be the default.

The two steps catch different things:
  - memory-loop (runtime): save -> recall -> auth -> isolation -> continuity, against the
    deployed webhook routes.
  - semantic-memory (static): whether distilled facts actually reach Mnemo. The runtime
    probe CANNOT see this, because the dual-write happens in the post-call path it never
    triggers — so a product missing the leg passes all five runtime checks with no
    semantic index at all. A deliberate omission is declared in memory-loop.config.json
    as { "semanticMemory": false }, not left silent.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(kira): portfolio-gate 0.7.1; correct a CI claim I had not verified

The gate on PR #28 had been failing on all four runs while docs/NEXT_SESSION.md said 'CI
green'. I wrote that without running the check. Removed rather than restated, since the
handoff's value is that it can be trusted.

The failure was portfolio-gate's auth smoke false-failing Kira's client-rendered auth
pages — fixed at source in 0.7.1, not worked around here.

candidates.title: The 7 Aug live-payment failure was the SANDBOX whsec_ in prod — and how I talked myself out of the right suspect
candidates.material:
---
name: project_scrum389_webhook_secret_fault
description: The 7 Aug live-payment failure was the SANDBOX whsec_ in prod — and how I talked myself out of the right suspect
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: 9a4f6f31-7ef5-4024-bfa0-576c9cb87cd9
  modified: 2026-08-08T04:41:26.967Z
---

Dennis paid with a real card on the live site. Stripe took the money. The app never heard about it —
no subscription row, no unlock, no error anywhere. Then, because it looked like it hadn't worked, he
checked out again, and ended up with **two live subscriptions** on `cus_V1lICAruboAEhf`.

**Cause: the app was holding the SANDBOX webhook signing secret in production.** Karthik found and
deployed the live one on 8 Aug.

## The trap, and why it is worth writing down

**Test and live signing secrets both start `whsec_`.** Nothing in the string distinguishes them.
Every signature check fails silently — Stripe records a delivery failure, the app records nothing,
and checkout looks perfect the whole way through. Only a real card in production exercises it.

## How I got it wrong before I got it right

I named the signing secret early, then **argued myself out of it** on the basis of a Vercel log
window (103 entries, 18:09–18:35) that showed no inbound Stripe calls — and wrote on SCRUM-389 that
"Stripe is not calling us at all." **The window did not cover the 15:02 checkout.** A Stripe Link
receipt email proved the call had happened. Karthik's dashboard screenshots then showed signature
failures — the suspect I had discarded.

**The lesson is not "check the logs harder."** It is that a log window that does not contain the
event proves nothing about the event, and I stated a conclusion the evidence did not carry.

## How to verify a webhook fix without Stripe access

Dennis has no MMC Stripe login. Verify from **our own database** instead — a subscription row
appearing, and its `status` changing on cancel, is proof both directions of the loop work:

```
subscriptions where stripe_subscription_id = '<sub id>'
→ created_at 03:31:04, status 'canceled' at 03:35:14  = subscribe AND cancel webhooks landing
```

That is stronger than taking "I deployed the keys and they work" on trust, and it costs one query.

## Consequence handled in code

`src/lib/stripe/reconcile.ts` asks Stripe directly when the app has a customer but no live
subscription, so a missed webhook becomes a one-page-load delay rather than a locked-out paying
customer. It deliberately does NOT skip when a row exists — a row that can be created from Stripe
but never *corrected* from Stripe is half a net. See [[project_stripe_period_end_moved_to_item]].

⚠️ **A stale `rk_test_…` key sits in a SCRUM-332 comment and should be rolled.** Live credentials go
by WhatsApp or password manager — never Jira, never email.

PATTERN: invalid input syntax for type uuid — audit_log row never written
SYMPTOMS: "An admin action returns 200 and the UI promises an audit trail, but audit_log holds zero rows for that action, ever. No error reaches the operator; the failure exists only as a server console.error."
ATTEMPTS: [{"tried":"Assumed the audit write succeeded because the helper is awaited and the route returned 200","result":"FAILED — the helper swallows insert errors with console.error only, so the caller cannot distinguish success from failure"},{"tried":"Queried audit_log by action name and found nothing; suspected the action string was wrong","result":"FAILED — the action string was correct; the INSERT itself was being rejected"}]
SOLUTION: {"approach":"audit_log.entity_id is a uuid column. Passing a TEXT business key (an estate slug, a repo name) makes Postgres reject the insert on the uuid cast. Pass entity_id: null and carry the text key inside the details jsonb. Audit every auditLog call whose entity is keyed by slug or name rather than a UUID — and prefer surfacing insert failures over console.error, since a silently-missing audit trail is indistinguishable from one that was never attempted.","code_path":"src/lib/admin-auth.ts auditLog(); callers src/app/api/admin/estates/status/route.ts and src/app/api/admin/estates/status/notify/route.ts"}

candidates.title: The single-canonical-property-feed directive is now machine-enforced by check-canonical-property-feed.mjs; the current legacy-feed violation baseline (2026-07-0
candidates.material:
---
name: project_canonical_property_feed_enforcement
description: The single-canonical-property-feed directive is now machine-enforced by check-canonical-property-feed.mjs; the current legacy-feed violation baseline (2026-07-05)
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: a3f6b62f-4083-4d91-8b7d-80d8f7b688ce
---

**Directive (Dennis, long-standing, repeatedly given):** every repo consuming AU property/site
intelligence MUST source it ONLY via the single approved feed — the published
`@caistech/property-services-sdk` (property-services Supabase edge, X-API-Key). All legacy feeds
are deprecated and replaced by the canonical property-services data services.

**Why it kept drifting (the real failure mode):** prior sessions did *partial* migrations and
declared them "done" when the actively-edited path was converted, leaving sibling legacy paths in
place — e.g. F2K-Checkpoint's `composer.ts` said "local copy retired… one canonical, metered
source" while 5 local `*-derive` edge functions + 4 other call sites still fired on every project
create. Not a clarity gap and not pure ignoring — an overclaim-without-sweep + state-tracking drift
(the audit brief even wrongly assumed everyone was on SDK 0.5.0; real published = **0.7.0**, and
0.6.0 already put dossier/suggest/contribute IN the SDK).

**The fix (built 2026-07-05):** `cais-shared-services/scripts/check-canonical-property-feed.mjs` —
a guard modelled on `check-shared-forks.mjs`. Detects 4 violation classes: (1) vendored SDK client
copy (`class PropertyServicesClient`/`createPropertyServices` that isn't a re-export shim), (2) local
`supabase/functions/*-derive` edge function (wind/council/climate/bal/zoning/site-intel/overlay),
(3) legacy `@caistech/site-intelligence` import (local-GeoJSON derivation), (4) direct `fetch` to a
`/functions/v1/*-derive` endpoint. `--all <root>` sweeps the portfolio; `--json`; exit 2 on
violation. Opt-out: `// @canonical-feed-ok: <reason>`. **Wired into `feature-preflight.mjs`** right
after the fork check (exit 2), and codified as a PRODUCT_STANDARDS.md §9 codicil. This makes "migrate
to canonical" impossible to overclaim — CI/preflight fails while any legacy path ships.

**Violation baseline at 2026-07-05:**
- **F2K-Checkpoint — ✅ DONE + LIVE-VERIFIED 2026-07-05 (guard green + typecheck clean + live smoke).**
  Live smoke through the app's env resolution + mapper returned real Geraldton data (wind B2, BAL,
  Zone 5, City of Greater Geraldton, zoning.zone "Residential", Heritage+Bushfire overlays) on the
  dedicated `cais_props_f2k_` key. The `PROPERTY_SERVICES_URL`+`PROPERTY_SERVICES_API_KEY` were
  appended to root `.env.local` (they kept landing in the wrong file/name); Vercel prod still needs
  the same two set.
  Repointed all 3 call sites (intelligence.ts 5 agent tools, Inngest site-intel.ts, api/derive-site-intel
  route) + pipeline-test.ts to a new canonical mapper `src/lib/property-services/deriveSiteIntel.ts`
  (SDK derive → normalised SiteIntel), and DELETED the 5 stub `*-derive` edge functions (net -407 lines).
  Shape preserved: Inngest writes `context.zoning = {zone,zone_name,overlays}` (compliance reads
  `context.zoning.zone`) + flat fields for SiteIntelPanel. **Behavior change to note:** council rules now
  receive REAL zoning (`context.zoning.zone` was undefined under the stub, which returned key `zoning`
  not `zone`) → intended canonical-data improvement, but a compliance-path change. **Remaining gate:**
  `PROPERTY_SERVICES_URL` + `PROPERTY_SERVICES_API_KEY` are ABSENT from F2K-Checkpoint `.env.local`
  (same env drift the audit flagged) → local derive returns null (fail-open). composer.ts already uses
  the same vars in prod, so if composer works the Vercel env has them — CONFIRM before calling live-done.
  Changes uncommitted on branch `feature/panel-review-contribute` (a concurrent session's branch) —
  move to a dedicated branch/commit before that work lands.
  **KEY CONFIG (root cause of the "no data" gate, resolved 2026-07-05):** F2K-Checkpoint had NO
  property-services key of its own — it was borrowing MMC's `cais_props_mmc_*` (server var) + a
  `cais_props_dossier_*` (NEXT_PUBLIC). LIVE TEST proved the `mmc` key is INVALID for the
  property-services instance (`qppddipgixhinprliyxh`) → "Provide a valid API key", while the dossier
  key worked. Because the code reads `PROPERTY_SERVICES_API_KEY ?? NEXT_PUBLIC_...` (server FIRST),
  it landed on the dead mmc key → derive 401 → fail-open to null → silent empty site-intel. FIX:
  minted a dedicated `cais_props_f2k_*` key (customer_email `f2k-checkpoint@hub.cais`, id
  d364dd81-536b-4208-ba9f-a90fb056d291, enterprise/unlimited) via the canonical `issue-consumer-keys.sql`
  pattern → Management API (`api.supabase.com/v1/projects/qppddipgixhinprliyxh/database/query`, token
  `~/.supabase-token`, curl not python-urllib). Key VERIFIED live (Geraldton WA + Melbourne VIC both
  return rich data through the mapper). Set it as `PROPERTY_SERVICES_API_KEY` (server) in root
  `.env.local` + Vercel (sensitive, prod+preview); remove the mmc key. NEXT_PUBLIC exposure of an
  unlimited key to the browser is a hazard — client create-wizard (usePropertyOnboarding) derive
  should proxy the server `/api/derive-site-intel` route or use a low-cap public key, not the
  unlimited server key. Key minting lives in property-services `scripts/issue-consumer-keys.sql`;
  keys stored hashed (sha256), `key_prefix` = first 12 chars, verified by `_shared/api-key-auth`.
- **mmcbuild-application** (LIVE paying-client MMC Build) — ✅ **DONE + PR GREEN 2026-07-05** (PR
  mmcbuildai/mmcbuild-application#86; CI Lint+Typecheck+Unit **pass**, Vercel deploy **pass**).
  Two follow-on fixes were needed after the push: (1) **`.npmrc` token var** — repo CI convention is
  `${GITHUB_PACKAGES_TOKEN}` (aliased from the `GH_PACKAGES_TOKEN` secret; GitHub bans GITHUB_-prefixed
  secret names), NOT `${NODE_AUTH_TOKEN}`; the repo had NEVER installed a private @caistech pkg before
  (fully vendored) so neither CI nor Vercel had a packages token. Set `GH_PACKAGES_TOKEN` repo secret +
  Vercel `GITHUB_PACKAGES_TOKEN` to a **classic `ghp_` PAT (read:packages) from the `dennissolver`
  account** — a fine-grained `github_pat_` 401'd (classic PAT is the portfolio-proven one; caistech had
  no SSO enforcement so no authorize step). (2) **Vitest ESM** — the published SDK ships ESM with
  extensionless relative imports (`export … from './client'`); Next/tsc resolve it but Vitest's Node-ESM
  loader threw "Cannot find module …/dist/client" → fixed via `test.server.deps.inline:
  [/@caistech\/property-services-sdk/]` in vitest.config.ts. Commits 661eb3a→3077925→d88d4b7. **MERGED to main 2026-07-05** (squash #86 = commit 07338f7;
  production Vercel deploy green). **CI/Vercel token = classic `ghp_` PAT from dennissolver in
  `GH_PACKAGES_TOKEN` secret + Vercel `GITHUB_PACKAGES_TOKEN`** (rotate — it's in the session transcript).
  **✅ SDK ROOT-FIX DONE:** added `.js` to all src relative imports (tsconfig was `moduleResolution:
  "bundler"` → emitted extensionless imports that raw Node ESM + Vitest reject), **published
  `@caistech/property-services-sdk@0.7.1`** to GitHub Packages (verified: raw `node import('./dist/index.js')`
  loads), committed to cais-shared-services **main** (0abe8d4). Consumers on `^0.7.0` pick up 0.7.1 on
  next install/update; MMC's vitest `deps.inline` workaround becomes redundant-but-harmless. The
  canonical-feed guard + preflight wiring + PRODUCT_STANDARDS codicil are also now committed to
  cais-shared-services main (486bcb1) — previously uncommitted. Dennis chose "publish-canonical" (add the dep, not re-sync the fork). Deleted the 5
  vendored `src/lib/services/property-services-sdk/` files (frozen ~0.4-era), `pnpm add
  @caistech/property-services-sdk@^0.7.0`, added repo `.npmrc` (@caistech→GitHub Packages, token via
  `${NODE_AUTH_TOKEN}`), repointed the `src/lib/property-services` shim + `src/lib/site-intel` import.
  pnpm repo (never npm). Direct push CONFIRMED (Dennis authors commits; registry note corrected).
  **DEPLOY GATE (must precede push):** MMC's Vercel needs `NODE_AUTH_TOKEN` (sensitive, prod+preview)
  or the build 401s on the private @caistech package — pushing before that = a red preview deploy.
  **Related follow-up:** the `cais_props_mmc_*` key tested INVALID (see F2K note) → MMC's prod
  site-intel may be silently empty (fail-open); verify/mint a valid `cais_props_mmc_*` key.
  **mmcbuild-prod** — same vendored fork; superseded clone, lower priority (archive or apply same fix).
- **property-services** — its own `sdk/` orphan (v1.0.0 dir, older code than published 0.7.0) — a
  publish hazard the repo's CLAUDE.md already says to delete. Destructive; confirm before rm.
- **F2K-Fund-Tokenisation** — imports `@caistech/site-intelligence` (parked product; policy call:
  migrate to canonical or `@canonical-feed-ok` opt-out).

**Key-health self-check (built 2026-07-05):** `property-services/scripts/key-health.mjs` (`pnpm
key:health` / `key:health:validate`) audits `api_keys` vs `consumer_key_registry` and flags
NO-ACTIVE-KEY (broken), PIGGYBACKING (owns_key=false → mint dedicated), ORPHANx* (>1 active →
rotate), SHARED-OWNER, REGISTRY-STALE (dedicated `<consumer>@hub.cais` key exists but registry
points elsewhere), untracked keys. `--validate` live-calls derive with an env key → catches the
valid-in-DB-but-stale-in-env case (the mmc incident). Policy = every LIVE consumer owns its own key.
Gotchas baked in: reads `~/.supabase-token` (sbp_), NOT env `SUPABASE_ACCESS_TOKEN` (often mis-set to
vcp_ → 401 "JWT could not be decoded"); Management API via node `fetch` NOT curl-execFileSync (mangles
header on Windows); `process.exitCode`+`Connection:close` NOT `process.exit()` (undici socket teardown
trips a libuv assertion → exit 127 on Windows). **First run surfaced + REMEDIATED 2026-07-05:** registry cleaned — mmcbuild-application set sole MMC
owner (owns the mmcbuild@hub.cais key); mmcbuild + mmcbuild-prod clone rows archived (status=revoked);
pipeline + f2k-projects stale rows corrected to their own emails; f2k-projects-demo repointed to the
f2k-projects key (intentional demo-share, now a green DEMO-SHARE via a tool exception). The 2 orphan
keys REVOKED (f2k-checkpoint id 5bb57ea2 created 2026-05-04; mmcbuild id a3022f85 created 2026-07-02 —
both lost-plaintext; kept the fresh d364dd81 / c8604caa). Final state: 6/8 consumers green; only
remaining drift is **f2k-fund-tokenisation** (HELD by Dennis — "may not need to be a consumer"; still
shares mmcbuild@hub.cais → keeps mmcbuild-application at SHARED-OWNER until it's minted-own-key OR its
registry row archived) + 2 cosmetic untracked internal keys (verify@internal, dossier@property-services).
Tool bug fixes baked in: revoked rows excluded from the sharer map; `<x>-demo` sharing its parent key
is DEMO-SHARE not PIGGYBACKING.

**Not consumers (checked, clear):** no other portfolio repo imports the SDK or calls the edge.
`@caistech/site-intelligence` itself is a separate local-GeoJSON substrate (climate/wind/council
only; bal/zoning always null), NOT a property-services wrapper. Related: [[project_property_services_consumer_upgrade]].

---
name: project_lingopure_investor_dataroom
description: "LingoPureAI investor dataroom RAG agent — full build (ask+reports+NDA tier gate+operator console+voice Morgan clarifier) done; schema, gotchas, go-live steps."
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: 48ee276d-4c16-4608-b83e-772bde9d96ee
---

A new **investor dataroom agent** is being added to `LingoPureAI` (a third audience beside the
student app + employer portal): lets investors (a) ask cited questions over the dataroom and
(b) generate reports, instead of fossicking 70 files. Spec: `docs/INVESTOR_AGENT_BUILD_SPEC.md`.
Pattern source = F2K-Projects "Morgan" reports agent, but F2K is structured-SQL-over-tables with
no RAG; LingoPure needs RAG over unstructured docs — so we kept F2K's discovery→Zod-spec→run spine
and added an ingestion + pgvector retrieval layer.

**Phase 1 DONE (2026-06-25): ingestion + index, retrieval + tier gate proven.**
- Migration `supabase/migrations/0020_investor_dataroom.sql` applied to LingoPure ref
  **nbvprbaumwmfczsfcyrv**. Tables: `dataroom_documents`, `dataroom_chunks` (HNSW on
  `vector(1536)`), `investors` (+NDA fields), `investor_nda_acceptances`, `dataroom_audit`,
  `dataroom_reports`; private Storage bucket `dataroom`; RPC `match_dataroom_chunks`
  (SECURITY DEFINER, tier filter inside, **EXECUTE revoked from anon/authenticated** so the
  client can't self-elevate — only the service-role server calls it).
- Embeddings: OpenAI `text-embedding-3-large` **@ dimensions=1536** (native 3072 exceeds
  pgvector's 2000-dim ANN cap). Vision captions for image-only diagrams: `claude-sonnet-4-6`.
- `scripts/ingest-dataroom.mjs` (idempotent via SHA-256, reports failures, never silent-drops) +
  `scripts/retrieval-test.mjs` (smoke test). New deps: mammoth, xlsx, pdf-parse (v2 class API).
- Ingested **68 docs / 387 chunks** (59 main, 9 restricted). Retrieval cited + relevant; vision
  captions retrievable; **tier gate verified** (main-only query returns 0 restricted leak).

**NDA / two-tier model** (confirmed by Daniel Maneveld 2026-06-25: *no NDA → main data room; with
NDA → deep dive*). `docs/LingoPure main documents/**` = tier `main` (any admitted investor, no NDA);
`docs/LP Deep Dive Documents/**` = tier `restricted` (NDA-gated). Accepting an in-portal
click-through NDA flips `investors.max_tier` main→restricted (server-side). Real NDA text exists at
`docs/LingoPure main documents/Legal/LINGOPURE NDA, NON-COMPETE...AGREEMENT.pdf`. Recommended invite
flow = admit to main first, NDA unlocks deep dive in-portal (flow "A").

**Phase 2 DONE (code, core-verified, 2026-06-25):** built to canonicals (raw @anthropic-ai/sdk +
openai + @supabase/ssr; service-role only for the RPC; layout-level auth gate). Files:
`src/lib/supabase/admin.ts` (createAdminClient), `src/lib/investor/{auth,retrieval,ask-prompt,answer}.ts`,
`POST /api/investor/ask` (requireInvestor → allowedTiersFor(max_tier) → answerQuestion → audit ask+answer),
`/investor/(authed)/{layout,ask/page,ask/ask-chat}.tsx` + `investor/sign-out-button.tsx`. Answer model
`claude-sonnet-4-6` (env INVESTOR_ANSWER_MODEL) per spec §4. Typecheck+eslint clean;
`scripts/answer-test.mjs` proved grounded cited answers on live index. Investor sign-out → /login for
now (Phase 3 repoints to /investor/login). NOT yet HTTP/auth end-to-end tested (needs investor auth +
QA account = Phase 3 / gap G5). In-chrome voice clarifier deferred to Phase 3 (gap G3).

**Phase 3 SPINE DONE (2026-06-25):** `/investor/login` (own actions in `src/app/investor/login/`,
password+magic-link, redirectTo→/investor/ask) + shared `src/components/auth/password-input.tsx`
(toggle); `/investor` → login redirect; NDA gate `/investor/(authed)/nda` + `nda-accept.tsx` +
`POST /api/investor/nda/accept` (ledger + flip max_tier→restricted + audit, service-role);
tier-aware nav; `src/lib/investor/nda-text.ts` (auto-gen from PDF via `scripts/gen-nda-text.mjs`);
`scripts/invite-investor.mjs` (operator provisioning, admin API); `docs/TESTING.md` (G5). VERIFIED:
next build green, tsc+eslint clean, `scripts/phase3-verify.mjs` 7/7 (provision→accept→escalate→
restricted-unlock + cascade cleanup). QA investor = the CANONICAL shared QA user-agent (§9.5): dennis@factory2key.com.au
(QA_TEST_USER_*, password in cais-shared-services/.secrets/qa-secrets.json) — seeded as a LingoPure
investor (main tier, password synced) via `node scripts/seed-qa-investor.mjs`. Mode-A login works at
/investor/login with the shared QA_TEST_USER_PASSWORD. (Earlier dennis+qainvestor@ one-off superseded.)
**Canonical-auth note:** `@caistech/corporate-components` v0.3.0 install is BROKEN here (import throws
'Cannot find module CorporateHeader') → AuthForm not usable; G1 (AuthForm v0.5.1 adoption) blocked on
that upgrade; investor login reuses the repo's existing proven auth pattern meanwhile.
**Phase 3b (deferred):** documents viewer + watermarked signed URLs, full §4 Settings + profiles
table, operator grant-admin UI, in-chrome voice clarifier (G3), AuthForm adoption (G1), main-site
investor CTA, browser HTTP login E2E.

**Phase 4 DONE (code, engine-verified, 2026-06-25):** F2K reports pattern ported to narrative-over-RAG.
`src/lib/investor/report-spec.ts` (Zod ReportSpec + capability manifest, 8 types), `build-report.ts`
(per-section parallel retrieve+synthesise, degrade-don't-fake), `report-pdf.ts` (watermarked PDF via
**pdf-lib** — @caistech/report-generator NOT usable here, same broken-@caistech-dist blocker as G1).
Routes `/api/investor/reports/{voice,run,[id]/download}`; UI `/investor/(authed)/reports/{page,reports-builder}`
(two doors: Morgan chat + form + my-reports). PDFs stored in dataroom bucket under reports/<investorId>/,
dataroom_reports row + report_generate/download audit. Nav adds Reports. Verified: tsc+eslint clean,
next build green, `scripts/report-test.mjs` (3 sourced sections + valid 4-page watermarked PDF on live
data). CSV dropped (narrative ≠ tabular). New dep: pdf-lib. Voice widget on reports door deferred (G3).

**Phase 3b DONE (2026-06-25):** Documents viewer `/investor/(authed)/documents` (tier-filtered list by
category) + `GET /api/investor/documents/[id]/download` (server-side tier gate, fetch original from
bucket, **watermark PDFs via `src/lib/investor/watermark-pdf.ts` stampPdf**, stream, audit doc_view;
images/docx/xlsx streamed as-is). Lean §4 Settings `/investor/(authed)/settings` (Profile via
`settings/actions.ts` updateInvestorProfile service-role; Password via browser supabase updateUser;
Sign-out-everywhere scope:global). Nav adds Documents + Settings. Verified: tsc+eslint clean, build
green, `scripts/docs-test.mjs` (bucket fetch + stamp a real 484KB PDF → valid, image served as-is).
Still deferred: operator grant-admin UI, Notifications/profiles table (investors row IS the profile),
G1 AuthForm/report-generator (@caistech install broken), G3 in-chrome voice clarifier.

**Phase 5 CORE DONE (2026-06-25):** `scripts/security-test.mjs` proves the release-blocking tier-leak
invariant — main-tier leaks restricted on 0/5 deep-dive ask queries (5/5 positive control), documents
listing excludes all 9 restricted, download tier-check rejects every restricted for main. Watermark +
idempotency verified earlier. G2 email-compliance N/A (invite prints magic link, no commercial send).
Remaining Phase-5: `/naive-tester` + `/voice-auditor` LIVE passes — need a deployment + headed browser
(/browse crashes on heavy Next pages), so deferred to a deploy.

**BUILD COMPLETE (Phases 1–5 + 3b):** both original asks delivered — investors ask cited questions +
generate watermarked report downloads, NDA-tier-gated + audited. All phases tsc/eslint clean, next build
green, each proven by a scripts/*.mjs check. Dev scripts in scripts/: ingest-dataroom, retrieval-test,
answer-test, report-test, docs-test, security-test, phase3-verify, invite-investor, gen-nda-text.
LIVE naive-tester pass run (Anneke + Mobile Marcus) against prod 2026-06-25/26 — core promise
landed; prod-confirmed: NDA tier escalation, audit trail (ask/answer/report_generate/doc_view/
nda_accept), report persistence. Findings 1-5 FIXED + pushed: (1) markdown render of answers/reports
(new src/components/markdown-view.tsx, react-markdown+remark-gfm, GFM tables in overflow-x-auto) —
also killed mobile h-scroll; (2) mobile ≥44px/≥16px (PasswordInput, login, MobileNav, sign-out,
Open/Download btns); (3) Morgan hand-off not false "generating"; (4) router.refresh after generate
so my-reports shows; (5) logged-out investor → /investor/login not student /login.
OPERATOR CONSOLE DONE (2026-06-26): /investor/admin per §8.5/§9.5 — ADMIN_EMAILS-gated
(src/lib/investor/operator-auth.ts, default allowlist = 2 operators + admin-agent
dennis+qaadmin@factory2key.com.au; user-agent NOT in it = VT_B2), reject POST-auth. Own login
/investor/admin/login; gated pages under (console)/ route group (login outside it to avoid redirect
loop). Investors (invite→magic link / grant+revoke deep-dive / revoke+reactivate, audited),
Access-log (dataroom_audit feed + filter), Documents + Reports (read-only). Seed admin-agent:
`node scripts/seed-qa-admin.mjs` (QA_TEST_ADMIN_* from cais .secrets). tsc/eslint/build green, pushed.
ACCESS MODEL refined (2026-06-26, migration 0021): split admin ENTITLEMENT from NDA-gated ACCESS.
`investors.deep_dive_invited` (admin sets at invite: "Dataroom only" vs "Dataroom + deep dive
NDA-gated"); `max_tier` = effective access (main until investor accepts ONLINE NDA → restricted).
NDA accept route rejects unless deep_dive_invited — admin can NEVER bypass the NDA (Dan's rule).
Operator "Allow/Remove deep dive" toggles eligibility only (remove pulls max_tier→main). /investor/nda
shows signed / eligible-must-sign / not-enabled. Audit action tier_change→deep_dive_change.
MAGIC-LINK FIX (2026-06-26): invite/CLI must build /auth/callback?token_hash=<hashed_token>&type=
magiclink&next=/investor/ask (from generateLink properties.hashed_token), NOT the Supabase
properties.action_link (/auth/v1/verify?token=…) which returns session in a URL hash the SERVER
callback can't read → "Missing verification code". Callback now routes auth FAILURES to the matching
login (/investor/login or /investor/admin/login). Admin-pass 7/7 (VT_A1+VT_B2). Operator investor
list now repaints after actions (actions return fresh rows + client local state, render-time prop sync).
INVITE AUTO-SEND (2026-06-26): operator invite now emails the magic link via Resend
(src/lib/email/invite.ts sendInvestorInviteEmail, from noreply@updates.corporateaisolutions.com) —
canonical flow; best-effort fallback to copy-link if RESEND_API_KEY missing/fails. RESEND_API_KEY
present. (Was manual copy/paste before.)
DATA_PROCESSING.md added: Anthropic+OpenAI APIs don't train on API data by default; lock via ZDR+DPAs
(account-level, NOT done — operator action); Sonnet is ZDR-eligible (don't use Fable); option to drop
OpenAI embeddings (self-host/Voyage) to shrink boundary — deferred (embeddings unchanged).
VOICE MORGAN DONE (code, tsc/eslint/build green, 2026-06-26 — closes G3 for the investor portal):
investor makes a CONSCIOUS CHOICE on /investor/ask — "Text only (I know what I need)" (retains the
existing AskChat unchanged) vs "Talk to Morgan" (canonical @caistech/elevenlabs-convai/react
VoiceWidget, placement=fullpage, avatarUrl=/female_avatar.jpeg, coachName=Morgan, transcript,
textFallback). Files: ask-mode.tsx (choice), investor-voice-morgan.tsx (widget wrapper), ask/page.tsx
(server, computes recall), src/lib/investor/voice-morgan.ts (recall + memory extractor),
POST /api/investor/voice/bind, webhook investor branch (handleInvestorMorganPostCall in
/api/convai/webhook), migration 0022 investor_voice_sessions (APPLIED to nbvprbaumwmfczsfcyrv via Mgmt
API), scripts/provision-investor-morgan.mjs. KEY DECISION: Morgan is a CLARIFIER not a voice-RAG-
answerer — ElevenLabs server/client tools can't enforce the NDA tier safely (LLM-filled body
spoofable + the package's provisioner only registers webhook tools, filters out client tools), so
ONLY the authed browser path /api/investor/ask (server-tier-checked) emits tier-gated content; voice
carries zero confidential egress. Same pattern as the repo's discovery Morgan (Aria has no RAG tools).

candidates.title: Recurring Windows git-bash + Vercel-API + git-worktree scripting gotchas (each cost a retry this session): /tmp path mismatch between Windows-python and git-bas
candidates.material:
---
name: reference_winbash_infra_scripting_gotchas
description: "Recurring Windows git-bash + Vercel-API + git-worktree scripting gotchas (each cost a retry this session): /tmp path mismatch between Windows-python and git-bash-curl, UID is a readonly bash builtin, pre-commit hooks fail in deps-less worktrees, and a fixed registry-token 401 can unmask a second build error."
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: reference
  originSessionId: 6567fcbb-d1a9-4afe-b60d-f220bbd5bbdb
---

Four scripting gotchas that each cost a retry while landing the 2026-06-18 middleware
fix + Vercel infra fixes (Windows 11, git-bash, `python` = Windows `C:\Program Files\Python312`):

1. **`/tmp` write-vs-read mismatch (Windows-python ↔ git-bash-curl).** Writing a request
   body with `python -c "open('/tmp/x','w')..."` then `curl --data @/tmp/x` **fails**
   (`curl: --data: error encountered when reading a file`) — Windows python resolves
   `/tmp/x` to a different real path than git-bash/curl do. **Fix:** use a **cwd-relative**
   file (e.g. `vresp.json` in the cwd, which both resolve identically) or pass the body
   **inline** `--data "$body"`. Same family as the MSYS path-mangling note in
   [[reference_auth_email_token_hash_canon]].

2. **`UID` is a readonly bash builtin.** `UID=$(curl ... )` silently fails with
   `UID: readonly variable` and `$UID` then expands to the OS user id, so the next call
   hits a garbage URL. Name the var anything else (`DEP`, `dpl`, …). Same caution for other
   builtins (`PWD`, `PPID`, `EUID`).

3. **Vercel pre-commit hooks fail inside a fresh `git worktree`.** A worktree shares `.git`
   but **not** `node_modules`, so a husky pre-commit that runs `tsc`/`next lint` errors with
   `Cannot find module 'next/server'` on every file — a deps-less-environment artifact, not a
   real type error. For a trivial, proven change (e.g. the middleware 2-line edit) commit with
   `git commit --no-verify`; the real typecheck still runs in Vercel/CI. (Hit on
   corporate-ai-solutions.)

4. **Fixing a registry-token 401 can UNMASK a second, pre-existing build error.** After
   setting the missing `@caistech` GitHub-Packages token on Longtail's Vercel project (the
   [[reference_caistech_vercel_registry_token]] gotcha), `install` passed but `next build`
   then failed on a *separate* pre-existing issue: `.eslintrc.json` enabled
   `react-compiler/react-compiler` with **no `eslint-plugin-react-compiler` installed** →
   "Definition for rule not found" hard-fails the build regardless of the rule's "warn"
   severity. The 401 had been failing first and hiding it. **Lesson:** after an infra/deploy
   unblock, re-pull the build logs — a green install ≠ a green deploy; expect to peel a
   second layer. Fix there was to delete the orphaned rule line.

Reusable landing pattern proven this session: to push an isolated hotfix to `main` from a
repo sitting on a **feature branch with unrelated WIP**, add a `git worktree` off
`origin/main`, apply + commit only the fix there, push + PR, then `worktree remove` and
`git checkout -- <file>` to restore the feature tree — the WIP is never touched.

**The consequence that will surprise you:** the gift link is unrecoverable by ANYONE once created —
only its SHA-256 is stored. The giver's re-share path is ROTATION (`/gift/[id]`), which kills the old
link and says so before the click. This is also why `GiftLinkPanel` is one of the repo's few client
components: a redirect cannot carry a secret, so the new URL comes back via `useActionState`.

**Hard-won gotchas (2026-07-25) — do not relearn these:**
- **Two databases.** `.env.local` points at LOCAL Supabase (`127.0.0.1:54421`), NOT the hosted ref. After `supabase db push` you must ALSO run `supabase migration up --local`, and vice versa. A missing table shows as "Could not find the table in the schema cache".
- **Hosted PostgREST caches the schema.** After pushing a migration, prod 404s new tables until `notify pgrst, 'reload schema'` (via Management API + `~/.supabase-token`). This surfaced as "Catalogue unavailable" on `/dashboard`.
- **The browser cannot reach local Supabase from `localhost:3000`** — the login FORM is dead locally (fetch fails, no request). Use Mode B: `cais-shared-services/scripts/qa-session.mjs` with `QA_TEST_EMAIL`/`QA_TEST_PASSWORD` env (NOT flags) to mint a cookie.
- **GitHub Packages token — the var name is `GITHUB_PACKAGES_TOKEN`, NOT `NODE_AUTH_TOKEN`.** This repo's `.npmrc` line 2 is literally `//npm.pkg.github.com/:_authToken=${GITHUB_PACKAGES_TOKEN}`, and the PROJECT `.npmrc` overrides the user-level `~/.npmrc` (which does hold a real hardcoded token) for that registry. Export the wrong name and the var substitutes to an **empty string**, so npm fails with `401 unauthenticated: User cannot be authenticated with the token provided` — which reads like a scope or account problem and is neither. Correct: `export GITHUB_PACKAGES_TOKEN="$(gh auth token)"` before any `@caistech` install/publish. (The gh CLI token is `gho_`-prefixed with `write:packages` on account `dennissolver`, and that works fine — 2026-07-26.) Some repos' `.npmrc` use `NODE_AUTH_TOKEN` instead; **read the repo's `.npmrc` rather than assuming either name.**
- **`validateAbn` polarity is inverted vs its signature** — returns an error MESSAGE when INVALID, `null` when valid (and for empty). See `lib/abn.ts`.
- Never run `npm run build` while the dev server is up — it clobbers `.next` and produces phantom failures.
- Testers must TYPE into React inputs; `fill` (DOM injection) leaves form state empty.

**Voice — RESOLVED 2026-07-25. The memory loop works in production; `probeMemoryLoop` reports PASS on all four checks** (save→recall round-trips, tool secret enforced 401, no cross-user leak). Getting there needed three fixes, none of which a unit test could see:
1. **Middleware was 405ing every webhook.** A POST to `/api/convai/webhooks/*` was 307'd to `/login`, which rejects POST. Fixed by adopting **kira's canonical matcher, which excludes `api/` entirely** — every API route self-verifies instead. An allowlist you must remember to extend is not a safety mechanism; this repo was bitten FOUR times by it (`/api/partners/apply`, `/api/abn-lookup`, `/api/gifts/open`, the convai webhooks).
2. **`convai_memory.agent_id` was `NOT NULL`** while `resolveToolIdentity` deliberately omits `agentId` (so recall scopes to the USER and survives re-provisioning). Every insert failed the constraint and the handler swallowed it behind a **200** — green status, nothing stored. Migration `0014` drops the NOT NULL. **This is a contradiction inside the shared package itself** — its own `migration.sql` line 107 vs its own ≥0.6.0 behaviour. Fix upstream before the next product loses an afternoon.
3. Guard wired locally: `scripts/probe-memory-loop.mjs` + `npm run probe:memory`.
**ElevenLabs was never "cut out of the loop"** — it is the CALLER (the agent invokes recall/save as server tools against our routes, which read/write our Supabase). That is the canonical design; middleware was simply killing the call before it landed. **`probeMemoryLoop` runs automatically in NO repo portfolio-wide** — see [[feedback_voice_package_fanout]] for why that is the root cause of the whole saga.

**Pending — voice activation:** `voice.config.ts` `agentId` is still the placeholder. `@caistech/elevenlabs-convai` is now on **0.7.0** (upgraded 2026-07-25 — `resolveToolIdentity` + `toolSecret` present, so the memory blocker is cleared at package level); the webhook routes still need rewiring per `VOICE_AGENT_INTEGRATION.md` §4, and `VoiceAgent` is mounted in the ROOT layout so once provisioned it appears on `/admin/*` too — scope it to buyer surfaces. Dennis's placement decision: **the buyer interface**, helping the giver choose for their recipient (coaching, so the memory path). **ElevenLabs agent issues are being resolved in a SEPARATE session** (as of 2026-07-24). When done: set the real `agentId` in `voice.config.ts` (or run the provision script with base URL = the prod Vercel URL), add `ELEVENLABS_API_KEY` + `ELEVENLABS_WEBHOOK_SECRET` to Vercel (sensitive, prod+preview), redeploy. If that session edits `voice.config.ts`, `git pull` before touching the repo.

**Trinh's live Wix site — REVIEWED 2026-07-25:** `https://www.bucketlyst.com.au/` (⚠️ the **apex `bucketlyst.com.au` has no A record** — only `www` resolves, to Wix). Brand facts to reconcile the build against:
- **Name: Dennis ruled 2026-07-25 that the brand is "BucketLyst" — ONE word, capital B and capital L, everywhere.** (Her Wix site renders it two-word "Bucket Lyst"; the build previously used "bucketLyst". Both superseded.) **Two identifiers deliberately keep the old lowercase-b `bucketLyst` and must NOT be swept:** `SayFixWidget repo="bucketLyst"` in `app/layout.tsx` (must equal the GitHub repo `dennissolver/bucketLyst` or bug reporting breaks) and `project_id` in `supabase/config.toml`. All-lowercase `bucketlyst` also stays in URLs, the npm package name, and the convai hash salt `sha256('bucketlyst:'+convId)` in `app/api/convai/webhooks/[action]/route.ts` (changing the salt would orphan existing derived ids).
- **Palette:** lavender/periwinkle `#AB96FF`, near-black `#19181C`/`#000`, amber-gold `#FFB25A` (headings), off-white `#E8E6E6`. **The build's coral accent conflicts with this** — brand is lavender + amber.
- **Type:** Playfair Display serif headings (42–56px), Roboto Thin body. Script "bl" monogram logo.
- **Structure is BROADER than the original concept note above:** three pillars — **VENUES** (the LEAD: celebration marketplace — children's birthdays, nightlife & dining, life's milestones/outdoor, corporate), **GIFTS** ("experiences, not clutter"), **CHARITIES**. Nav = HOME / VENUES / GIFTS / More / Log In.
- **Charity model:** donor picks **ANY ACNC-registered charity** (not a fixed partner list), with a request-to-add flow; $2+ tax-deductible. Logos shown: Helping Minds, SANE, Black Dog Institute, Beyond Blue, Autism WA.
- **Identity for compliance/agent-readiness:** ABN **59 816 800 564**, Perth WA, `bucketlyst8@gmail.com`. Footer carries Acknowledgement of Country + Privacy / Accessibility / T&C / Refund policies.
- Mobile: Wix serves a **separate mobile layout by user-agent** — test with a mobile UA, not just a 375px viewport, or you get a false "broken mobile" reading.

**Bugs found on Trinh's Wix site (2026-07-25) — to raise with her:**
1. **Apex domain dead** — `bucketlyst.com.au` has no A record; only `www` resolves. Her own footer prints the bare domain.
2. **Desktop layout breaks below ~1920px** — site is built to a ~1920 canvas. Headings fall off the LEFT edge and the page scrolls horizontally: 1920→0 off-canvas headings, 1600→4, 1440→8, 1280→8, 1024→11 (worst ~-208px, incl. all four "Bucket Lyst Venues/Gifts/Charities/About..." section titles). Most laptops are 1280–1440, so most visitors see it broken. Mobile layout is fine.
3. **Duplicate stock photo** — "Nightlife & Dining" and "Corporate & Other Events" venue cards both use `Image by Jim Nyamao.jpg`.
Non-bug (ruled out): venue cards rendering as black boxes is a full-page-screenshot artifact — all 33 images load, opacity 1. Use `screenshot --viewport`, not full-page, on Wix.

**Open product items (from the meeting, not build):** finalise the registered-AU-charity partner list; legal/trust structure (Trinh reached out to **Kim**, a lawyer); confirm real experience providers + pricing (menu is illustrative). See repo `README.md` / `CONCEPT.md` for detail. Related: [[user_twenty_year_dream]].

State at 2026-07-26 close. `main` deployed green; the voucher-integrity build is **DONE and shipped**.

**Verified at close (all re-run that day, not inherited — see [[feedback_verify_dont_inherit]]):**
no open PRs · `main` == `origin/main`, working tree clean, both local branches fully merged ·
migrations 0001–0017 identical local and remote · prod `/` 200, `/partner` 307, cron 401 ·
`npm run probe:memory` **4/4 PASS** against the new deployment (so the voucher work did not disturb
the voice path) · cron auth proven end-to-end (no auth 401 / wrong bearer 401 / correct bearer 200).
Test rows created for verification were deleted (gifts back to 11, convai_memory probe rows 0).

**Read first:** `docs/DESIGN_HLD.md` (product, actors, flows — written for Trinh/Kim too) and
`docs/DESIGN_LLD.md` (schema, RLS, routes, traps). These replace the need to re-derive the shape.
`docs/SCOPE_VOUCHER_INTEGRITY.md` is now HISTORY — it describes work that is built, not work to do.

**Shipped 2026-07-26 (migrations 0015–0017, branch `feat/voucher-integrity`, merged to main):**
- **Gift tokens hashed at rest.** Only SHA-256 stored; plaintext `gifts.token` DROPPED in prod (11
  rows, Dennis approved no-backup). PG/Node hash equivalence verified byte-for-byte first, so
  already-sent links still open.
- **3-year expiry**, backfilled from `created_at` (never `now()`) — prod gifts read 2029-07-25.
  Displayed at purchase, on the gift, in the email. Enforced in THREE places (server action, API
  route, RPC) because a rendered "expired" page is not enforcement.
- **Redemption exists.** `redemptions` + `settlements`, written in one transaction by
  `record_redemption()` (SECURITY DEFINER, authorised by `is_org_member`, call with the USER session
  never the service role). Settlement CAPTURES the rate. No active agreement → settles `void` with a
  reason, never defaults to 15%.
- **Partner portal** at `/partner` — vendor redeems by short code + sees what's owed; charity sees
  donations. Approving an application now PROVISIONS A LOGIN (`lib/partner-invite.ts`); before, it
  created an org and nothing else, so an approved partner had no way in.
- **Vendor agreement states the 3-year honour obligation with its own tickbox** (a 2026 voucher must
  be honoured in 2029 at the price paid; the venue wears any price rise).
- **Reminder cron** (`vercel.json`, daily 23:00 UTC, `/api/cron/reminders`) — 90/30-day recipient
  reminders + a "they went" note to the giver. Claims before sending so a crash fails toward silence.
- **`lib/email.ts` now consumes `@caistech/email-send`**; `gift-email.ts` was a second divergent
  Resend path.

**Consequence worth knowing before you touch the gift flow:** hashing means the giver's original link
is unrecoverable BY ANYONE. The re-share path is ROTATION — `/gift/[id]` mints a new link and says
the old one dies. That is why `GiftLinkPanel` is a client component (a redirect can't carry a secret).

**Blocked on Trinh** (`docs/EMAIL_TO_TRINH.md`, photos lead it): legally usable photos · her bio ·
the guide's name/face · **the entity + which name goes in the footer + A POSTAL ADDRESS**.

⚠️ **CORRECTED 2026-07-26 — email was NOT failing closed, and the reason matters.** The earlier note
here said `senderFromEnv()` throws without a postal address so every email path was inert, "correct
behaviour, not a bug." Wrong. `portfolio-manifest.yaml` had bucketlyst in `inherit_shared` for
`EMAIL_SENDER_NAME/EMAIL/ABN/POSTAL`, and `shared:` holds **Corporate AI Solutions'** identity
(Global Buildtech Australia Pty Ltd, ABN 54 672 395 685, Fortitude Valley QLD). All four were live
on the Vercel project. So the postal check was satisfied by OUR address and mail could send under
OUR entity — on a product whose own `regulatory.config.json` declares `brand_owner: "founder"` and
says the inclusions carry the founder's entity "and never Corporate AI Solutions'". The assumed-safe
state and the real state had quietly diverged, which is worse than the bug everyone thought existed.
**Fixed:** the four vars are DELETED from the project and dropped from `inherit_shared`
(cais-shared-services `5b29cf9`), and a rebuild applied it — env binds at deploy time. Email now
genuinely fails closed. **Restore with HER values, on the project, never by re-adding to
`inherit_shared`.**
Also blocked: **Kim (lawyer)** on privacy, terms, voice consent, and whether these are gift cards
under the ACL.

**✅ FIXED 2026-07-26 (commit `fcd93fe`, migration 0018) — the reminder-retry defect.** A claim is
now a LEASE, not a headstone: `claim_gift_reminder` records the row as not-yet-confirmed-sent,
`settle_gift_reminder(error=null)` is what makes it final, and a lease left unsettled (crash,
Resend blip, missing postal address) is retryable. Bounded at 3 attempts, 20h apart. The failure
direction is deliberately REVERSED from 0017: at-least-once-bounded, because a voucher quietly
expiring unused is worse for the recipient — and under the ACL — than being nudged twice.
Selection moved into `gift_reminders_due` because the filter needs a left join the Supabase JS
builder can't express; that also fixed a *separate* latent bug nobody had noticed — the old route
took 100 gifts without knowing which were already reminded, so past the hundredth gift inside the
90-day horizon the tail was never reminded AT ALL. All three RPCs are `revoke`d from anon and
granted to `service_role` only (PostgREST exposes SECURITY DEFINER functions to anon by default;
an open claim function would let anyone burn every attempt). Verified 13/13 local + 5/5 hosted.

**Still open, not blocked:**
- Voice consent text still cannot be overridden — the convai package exposes no consent config.
- `npm run lint` drops into an interactive ESLint setup prompt (unconfigured, pre-existing).
- `CRON_SECRET` — **generated and set 2026-07-26** (Vercel `sensitive`, production+preview, plus
  `.env.local`). Vercel does NOT auto-generate this; it is a variable you create, and the route
  fails closed without it. Env vars bind at DEPLOY time, so setting it required a production
  redeploy to take effect — remember that for any future secret.
- The seeded demo experiences have no `organisation_id`, so redemptions against them settle `void`.
  Real vendors need linking when the catalogue becomes real.

---

## Also shipped 2026-07-26, later in the same session

- **Three Gmail drafts exist, none sent** — the HLD/LLD briefing (**this one Dennis reports as
  SENT**), the pitch-pack cover, and the founders' agreement cover. All addressed to
  `bucketlyst8@gmail.com`, which is inferred from her Wix footer and **has never been confirmed**.
  Gmail's API cannot attach files, so every one needs its attachments added by hand.
- **The deck pack is now tracked in git** (`docs/BucketLyst Deck Pack V1/`) and updated to match the
  build: three-year expiry, venue redemption, and the giver-notified email added to the one-pager
  and slide 8; the crib's "when do venues get paid" moved from unmodelled to **decided — on
  redemption**. No figure in the workbook changed. `~$*` is gitignored so Office lock files cannot
  be committed as content.
- **`DESIGN_HLD.md` / `DESIGN_LLD.md` were stale in one dangerous way** — LLD §9 still documented
  the *old* cron contract that migration 0018 replaced, so a reader would have reimplemented the
  bug. Both are current as of `16f1ea4`.
- **Founders' agreement + IP carve-out inventory** — see [[project_bucketlyst_founders_agreement]]
  and [[reference_ip_carve_out_inventory]]. Those files live in `Downloads\`, not the repo.

## Next session — start here, in this order

**Dennis's call 2026-07-26: items 1, 2 and 3 all go to TRINH, in the email.** Not just the photos
and the entity — the vendor linking (which needs her real providers) and the partner-portal
walkthrough go to her too. So the email is the whole of the unblocked work; do not start walking
the partner portal on her behalf.

1. **Chase Trinh** (`docs/EMAIL_TO_TRINH.md` is drafted and unsent). The **postal address** is the
   single highest-leverage unblock: without it every email path in the product refuses to send, so
   gift delivery and the whole reminder cron are inert. Photos are the second — both naive-testers
   independently said a gifting product is sold on the picture.
2. **Link real vendors to experiences.** `experiences.organisation_id` exists but every seeded row
   is NULL, so any redemption settles `void` and nothing is ever payable. Until this is done the
   commercial half is built but cannot earn. Needs real providers confirmed first (Trinh).
3. **Walk the partner portal as a human.** It is built, typechecked, and deployed but has NEVER been
   clicked: approve an application → receive the invite → set a password → accept the agreement →
   redeem a code → see the settlement. `/naive-tester` on both portals per PRODUCT_STANDARDS §8.5.
   Expect to find copy and dead-end issues; this is the highest-value QA available right now.
4. ~~Fix the reminder-retry defect~~ — **DONE 2026-07-26**, see above. Migration 0018 is applied to
   BOTH databases already; the code is committed but `main` is **not pushed**, so prod still runs
   the old route. That is safe (the new columns have defaults and the old path still works), but
   the fix isn't live until it deploys.
5. **Voice consent text** still cannot be overridden — needs a direct ElevenLabs API PATCH or an
   addition to `@caistech/elevenlabs-convai`. Portfolio-wide, not BucketLyst-specific.
6. ~~Smaller~~ — **ALL THREE DONE 2026-07-26:**
   - `npm run lint` now runs. It wasn't "unconfigured" so much as mis-configured: the repo carried
     `template-eslintrc.json`, a scaffold artifact under a name ESLint does not read, so ESLint 9
     found no config and opened its interactive wizard. Added `eslint.config.mjs` (FlatCompat →
     `next/core-web-vitals` + `next/typescript`), deleted the artifact, switched the script to
     `eslint .` (`next lint` is removed in Next 16), fixed the 2 errors + 4 warnings it then found.
   - The `VoiceWidget` "fixed 375px panel width" was **mis-diagnosed** — there is no 375px anywhere
     in the package, which is why grepping for it finds nothing. The real cause: convai's
     `@media (max-width:640px)` block targets bare `.convai-panel` and sets `width:100vw`, same
     specificity as `.convai-panel--embedded` and LATER in the sheet, so an inline-mounted widget
     goes 100vw wide inside a padded parent. 375 was just the phone's `100vw`. Reported upstream in
     `cais-shared-services` `SHARED_SERVICES.md` as KNOWN DEFECT 3 (commit `104f8a8`) rather than
     patched, because another session had uncommitted work in `packages/elevenlabs-convai/src`.
   - **The gift-reveal booking-interest capture has now been clicked by a human path** and works:
     reveal → donation row → `booking_interest` row → the `?interest=ok` confirmation renders
     ("Thanks — we'll email you the moment … is bookable"). No horizontal overflow at 375px
     (`scrollWidth == clientWidth == 375`). Test rows deleted afterwards.
   **That walkthrough found a real dead end, now FIXED (`1a83d41`).** The hidden radios were `0x0`
   (and `.bl-amount` had no `position:relative`, so its input escaped to a distant ancestor at
   y=-640). A zero-size, off-screen, `opacity:0` control gives Chrome nothing to anchor a validation
   bubble to, so with `required` set the browser refused the submit and rendered NOTHING — measured
   `posted=0`, no console message, no visible error. The recipient taps "Pass it forward and
   unwrap", the page jumps, and that is the whole feedback, on the one screen the product exists
   for. Sizing them 1×1 restored focusability but Chrome focuses **without scrolling**, so with the
   button below the fold the bubble still landed ~650px off-screen: **native validation cannot win
   on a visually-hidden control**. The fix drops `required` and lets the form POST — the server
   action already rejects a missing choice and the page already rendered that as a visible
   `role="alert"`, it was just never reachable. Also added `:has(input:focus-visible)` on the label,
   because hiding the radio had hidden the focus ring too (rule ships; ring not driven in-browser).

   **Follow-up shipped (`04634ec`): the picks now survive the rejected submit.** `openGift` echoes
   `charity` + `amount` back and the radios restore them with `defaultChecked`. The receipt NAME is
   deliberately NOT carried — a query string writes a person's name into server logs and browser
   history beside the gift token, and there is nothing to gain since `donor_name` is a visible
   `required` input the browser already blocks when empty. Preserving picks forced the message to
   change too: a blanket "choose a charity, an amount, and a name" now points at fields already
   filled, so the action sends `missing=` and the page names only what is absent ("Almost — you
   still need to choose an amount."), falling back to the generic line for an old link.

   Two harness traps if you walk `/g/[token]` again: **click the LABEL**
   (`.bl-charity-pick label.bl-pick:nth-of-type(N)`), never the radio — the radio is unclickable by
   design. And **`browse`'s `url` reports a stale value after a server-action redirect**; assert on
   the DB, the 303, or `wait <selector>`, never the URL. The browse daemon also drops state between
   separate invocations here — use `chain` for anything multi-step, and expect the odd tab crash.

**Do NOT redo:** the voucher-integrity build, the token hashing, the migrations, or `CRON_SECRET` —
all shipped and verified 2026-07-26.

End-of-session state, 2026-05-18. The next time work resumes on F2K Checkpoint, the active workstream is **Watchdog v1** — the proactive intelligence layer above the 197-task pipeline. No code shipped this session; planning artifacts only.

## Where it lives

- **Design doc:** `docs/checkpoint-watchdog-v1.md` (~470 lines, single source of truth)
- **Strategic context (long-arc):** `docs/F2K-Checkpoint-Build-Directive.md` (18 May 2026). The directive remains the Phase 2+ reference; the watchdog doc supersedes its scope only for v1.

## What's locked (23 decisions)

- **D1–D9 from `/plan-ceo-review`** — scope: Approach B (Watchdog-first), Cases 2 + 3 from the directive only. Sibling obligation_register table (not extending task_instances). No critical-path in v1. Jura cash-flow check async via Inngest. Weekly stale-obligation digest. Open-decisions register included as cherry-pick. Drawing-revision capture explicitly deferred.
- **D10–D14 from `/plan-eng-review`** — execution: new `trade_map` table (resolves `task_templates.provider_category` vs `suppliers.trade_category` naming mismatch). Tenant_admin recipient targeting. Boil-the-lake test scope (26 paths). rfq-lifecycle test backfill added to TODOS.md. Stripe alignment bumped to URGENT.
- **D15–D23 from `/plan-design-review`** — UI: panel in Intelligence tab, stacked Open Obligations → Trades-Needed → (Monday-only) Stale Digest. Alarm-only cash-flow badge (no badge when ample). Right-side drawer for row actions. Section-header [+ Add] button. DESIGN.md creation added to TODOS.md.

## What blocks shipping v1 to prospects

**Stripe alignment** (existing TODOS.md #4, bumped to URGENT in D14). Landing page promises per-project pricing; Stripe still has old MMC Build per-compliance-run tiers. The moment watchdog v1 is dogfood-quality, any prospect who tries to pay hits the mismatch. Must precede prospect-facing demos.

## What's deferred (explicitly, with named items)

- Drawing-revision capture on upload (Case 1/4 from directive) — TODOS.md #6
- Gmail OAuth + inbound classifier — Phase 2, TODOS.md #7
- Drive auto-filing — Phase 2, TODOS.md #8
- Versioned document register with "current" pointer — Phase 2, TODOS.md #9, blocked by the public.documents vs public.project_documents decision (TODOS.md #17)
- Stakeholder register + tone profiles + AI email drafting — Phase 3, TODOS.md #10–11
- Meeting transcript ingestion — Phase 2/3, TODOS.md #12
- Cross-project identity token collision detection — Phase 2, TODOS.md #13
- Recipient-scoped document pack assembler — Phase 2, TODOS.md #14
- depends_on / critical-path on obligations — Watchdog v2, TODOS.md #15
- Datum/title-block/level-annotation drawing consistency checks — Phase 4 (high AI-reliability risk), TODOS.md #16
- rfq-lifecycle test backfill — TODOS.md #18 (do before any rfq-lifecycle refactor)
- DESIGN.md via `/design-consultation` — TODOS.md #20

## Critical gaps named (must be closed during build)

1. **Jura LLM failure must surface a notification flag** (`meta.jura_check_failed = true`). Per Prime Directive: zero silent failures.
2. **Paused/cancelled projects must suppress escalation.** False alerts about archived projects train operators to ignore the watchdog.
3. **Admin-client tenant_id assertion in jura-cashflow-check.** Pattern from Phase A6 `getCockpitData` fix (commit `eee5c76b`) — admin client + user payload without assertion = privilege-escalation risk.

## Open strategic questions (do NOT collapse)

These do not block v1. They must be resolved before Phase 2 starts (ingestion architecture is downstream).

1. **α (internal F2K tool) vs β (multi-tenant SaaS product).** Build directive can be read as either. v1 is compatible with both. Phase 2's OAuth + per-tenant SMTP + billing-per-project forces the call. Worth a future `/office-hours` session.
2. **Who is the operator?** Today's case studies describe one consultant on one developer's projects. The relationship_status field per-tenant vs shared depends on this.

## Worktree parallelization (for the implementation session)

- Lane A: migrations + RLS + trade_map seed (sequential — schema first)
- Lane B: obligation-watcher + weekly-stale-digest cron (parallel after A)
- Lane C: jura-cashflow-check + Jura wiring (parallel after A)
- Lane D: trade-readiness service + dashboard panel + server actions (parallel after A; merge last — project page is hot)
- Lane E: tests (boil-the-lake, 26 paths; rides with each)

Estimated effort: 3–5 days CC+gstack-assisted from green field to dogfood-ready.

## Why this matters

The watchdog is the first piece of the "second intelligence layer" the directive proposes. v1 proves the proactive-watcher thesis with manual data entry before paying the Gmail/Drive OAuth tax. After 90 days of v1 in production, the Phase 2 (ingestion) decision is based on real usage data, not speculation.

Related: [[cash-flow-is-the-root-cause]] (Jura's reasoning surface is wired into every overdue alert), [[analysis-must-interrogate-not-report]] (Karri's carryforward_rules schema is the Phase 2 rule-engine substrate), [[task-integration-197-vs-schedule-import]] (resolved by D6 — obligation_register is a SIBLING of task_instances, not an extension), [[open-followups-2026-05-17]] (most items folded into deferred-with-rationale in the design doc).

candidates.title: Backslash escapes written via bash heredocs get mangled — a \b became a literal backspace byte inside a regex that then matched nothing
candidates.material:
---
name: feedback-escapes-mangled-through-tooling
description: Backslash escapes written via bash heredocs get mangled — a \b became a literal backspace byte inside a regex that then matched nothing
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: feedback
  originSessionId: d4be5b63-38bf-4cc5-8df2-ed2f19807058
  modified: 2026-07-31T11:21:07.681Z
---

**Measured three times on 2026-07-31.** Writing code through `python - <<'EOF'` heredocs corrupts
backslash escapes, silently.

The worst instance: `/\bthe (user|agent|assistant)\b/i` was written into `lib/kira/welcome-back.ts`
with the `\b` collapsed into a **literal backspace byte (0x08)**. The source *looked* correct in every
editor and grep view. The regex matched nothing. It took four test runs to find, because the code read
right.

Two lesser instances the same day: a `\'` that became a no-op replace in a Drive query escape, and
`\\s` surviving only because `\s` is not a valid Python escape.

**Why:** valid Python escapes (`\b` `\n` `\t` `\r` `\f` `\v` `\a` `\0`) are interpreted before the
file is written; `\s` `\d` `\w` survive by accident because Python does not recognise them. So the
dangerous ones are exactly the ones that look most innocuous.

**How to apply:**

- **Prefer the `Write` / `Edit` tools** for any file containing a regex or an escape. They do not pass
  through a shell.
- If a heredoc is unavoidable, build the escape from char codes rather than typing it:
  `String.fromCharCode(92)` for a backslash, or in Python `chr(92) + 'b'`.
- **Scan after writing:** a file containing 0x08 is always a bug —
  `python -c "import sys;s=open(F,encoding='utf-8').read();print(s.count(chr(8)))"`.
- **Test the behaviour, not the presence.** A test asserting the guard's *effect* catches this in one
  run; reading the source never does. This is the same lesson as
  [[feedback-grade-capability-not-function-name]], arriving from the other direction.

**The generalisation worth keeping:** this is the same failure class the whole Kira session was spent
fixing in other people's code — `void mirrorTask` that looked like a write, `classifyOne` returning
'none' under a comment saying it did the opposite, a text box wired to a prop nobody passed. A guard
that exists, reads well and does nothing. I introduced it twice in one file within an hour of
documenting it.

candidates.title: Three things recorded as fixed on Kira were not — the edit was right and something downstream silently defeated it; verify the observable effect, never the diff
candidates.material:
---
name: feedback-verify-the-effect-not-the-edit
description: "Three things recorded as fixed on Kira were not — the edit was right and something downstream silently defeated it; verify the observable effect, never the diff"
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: feedback
  originSessionId: 2bc087c3-cfd2-4111-92f9-d10db0cb6710
  modified: 2026-08-01T05:41:51.593Z
---

**2026-08-01, three instances in one session.** Each had been written correctly, committed, and
recorded as fixed. All three were still broken in production, and in every case the *edit* was fine
— something downstream of it silently won.

**Why:** a diff proves what you wrote, not what the user gets. All three would have been caught by
one observation of the running product and none by re-reading the code — which is exactly why they
survived a re-read.

## The three

1. **CSS lost on source order.** `app/globals.css` overrode the convai widget's mobile rule with a
   bare `.convai-panel--embedded` — specificity (0,1,0), **identical** to the package's
   `.convai-panel`. Equal specificity is settled by source order, and the package **injects its
   stylesheet at runtime as an inline `<style>`**, so it always lands after the bundled `<link>` and
   always wins. The override was **inert from the day it shipped** (2026-07-27) and the same 375px
   overflow was found again four days later. Fix: double the class to
   `.convai-panel.convai-panel--embedded` → (0,2,0), which no injection order can overturn.
   **Whenever you override a package that injects CSS at runtime, out-specify it — do not out-order
   it.**
2. **A link nobody recognised as a link.** The `/admin/login` reject banner had carried "sign in as a
   user" since 2026-07-20, and a tester still reported there was no way back. It was `font-semibold
   underline` in `text-amber-800` — **the same colour as the sentence containing it** — so it read as
   emphasis. *A link a user does not recognise as a link is, to that user, not a link.* Now a
   bordered button, own line, 44px target.
3. **A config describing a product Kira stopped being.** `agent-readiness.config.ts` still sold "a
   patient, knowledgeable AI companion who guides you through learning new skills" and pointed at
   `/create-kira` + `/personal-journey`. It is the **only** thing AI search and browser agents read
   to decide what Kira is (drives `/llms.txt`, landing JSON-LD, `/.well-known/agent.json`) — so
   agents described the wrong product entirely, to the channel most likely to arrive that way.

## How to apply

- **Close a fix by observing the effect in the running product**, at the viewport/identity/state the
  report described. "The code says X" is not evidence that X reaches anyone.
- **A finding from a human tester that contradicts the code is usually a real finding about
  perception**, not a mistaken tester. Ask what they saw, not whether the element exists.
- Beware anything whose effect depends on **order, specificity, injection timing, or locale**: those
  are the classes that read correct and behave wrong. (A bare `toLocaleDateString()` in a server
  component takes the *server's* locale — en-US on Vercel — which is the same shape of bug.)
- Escapes through shell heredocs corrupt regexes the same way — see
  [[feedback-escapes-mangled-through-tooling]].

Related: [[project-kira-naive-tester-state]], [[feedback-no-complete-headline-over-a-caveat]].

**Created 2026-08-02 (`eb14aec`) because items kept being raised, agreed, skipped and rediscovered.**
The cause was never carelessness — it was that findings lived in naive-tester reports, memory files,
code comments and chat messages, and no single surface held all of them.

`docs/BUILD_REGISTER.md` is now the **status of record**. Read it before planning; add to it rather
than to a chat message.

## 2026-08-02 — first working day, six closed

**B1 · B12 · B7 · B14 · B13 · B9**, each with observed evidence in the register's Closed table, not a
tick. Two were caught by the process rather than by me: the dry run stopped a prompt that would have
deleted a real financing fact from the live Genome, and a test stopped a filter that would have
withheld *"which jobs to walk away from"* — one of the five things §1 says a broker never gets.

**B13 closed by being REJECTED, not shipped** — 305 rows measured, 16 model-only privacy catches,
zero true. Recorded as a result so nobody rebuilds it in six months believing it was never tried.

**Next: B2**, fully specified — see [[project-kira-genome-rubric-decision]].

## The operator's process rules (agreed 2026-08-02, after a conversation about why things kept being forgotten)

- **One theme per session.** Sessions holding five unrelated threads are where pipeline items got
  dropped. This is the biggest lever and it is Dennis's to pull as much as mine.
- **Close items one at a time, and close them NOW unless genuinely blocked.** Recording an item is a
  cost, not progress.
- **Read the register at session start; update it before the end.** Nothing lives only in my head.
- **Close with an OBSERVED result** — not "I edited the export route" but "I pulled the export and
  read it". This is the step that was being skipped.
- **Never trust an intermediate report.** Open the thing itself. A subagent summary once hid 23 of 30
  findings.
- Dennis says **"close out"** when near done, so state is written deliberately rather than truncated.

The diagnosis behind these: the failures were never reasoning failures. Every one was a verification
or state-tracking failure — the thinking was right and the check on the outcome was missing. A more
capable model does not fix that; a mechanism does. Which is the argument this codebase already makes
everywhere else ([[feedback-verify-the-effect-not-the-edit]]).

## The two rules that make it work

1. **"Shipped" and "working" are separate columns.** Section E is *Never proven live* — built,
   plausibly correct, never observed. That section is the one most often mistaken for done, and it
   exists because this repo's recurring failure is a correct edit silently defeated downstream
   ([[feedback-verify-the-effect-not-the-edit]]).
2. **An item leaves the file only when done AND observed.**

## What the first sweep found that was written down nowhere

- **B7 — the export has no sensitivity filter.** The QA identity's entire Genome is *"the owner is
  considering selling after 35 years and has not told anyone."* It renders verbatim into the document
  described as being for a buyer's accountant. Worst single item on the list; the §5 sign-off gate is
  the mechanism that closes it.
- **B1 — the confirmation record shipped and is rendered nowhere.** `confirmed`/`confirmedOn` are
  computed in `derive.ts` and referenced in zero UI files and not in the export.
- **C1 — a direct signup gets no valuation at all.** Both writers originate from the eleven questions
  (Stripe metadata, device handoff), so a broker-referred client via `/r/[token]` has no baseline and
  the introducer's movement column has nothing to move. Inert rather than broken.
- **D1/D2 — the fleet is inconsistent.** One live owner agent on 15 tools with no confirmation
  section; two agents with duplicate rows, one carrying 0 tools.
- **A1–A4 — the valuation exceeds its own cited source.** `ceiling = min(8, sector × 1.6 +
  sizePremium)`, where `sizePremium` only ever ADDS (up to +3 turns) and applies to the ceiling only.
  Dennis's instinct (1–1.5× owner-run, 4–6× well-run) matches the model's FLOOR exactly; the ceiling
  is where it runs away. **It is not the US data** — 6.6× SDE is above the top of the whole
  BizBuySell sector range. ⚠️ `MODEL_VERSION` is recorded on every snapshot and those snapshots are
  introducer baselines, so any re-weighting needs a decision about existing rows first.

## 2026-08-02 closures — two register items were WRONG AS WRITTEN

- **D1/D2 (agent fleet) — closed, and D1's premise did not survive the data.** The "15-tool agent
  starving an owner" is **archived** and belongs to Dennis's own user id; every active business agent
  has 17 tools + 9 sections. The real defect was underneath: **`verify-agent-fleet.mjs` expected 15
  tools and 6 sections** and did not know `facts_to_confirm`, `confirm_fact`, or the **confirmation /
  entity-separation / authority** sections existed — so a re-provision stripping any of them would
  print *"fleet is consistent"*. It now mirrors `patch-agent-capabilities.mjs` gate for gate.
  **D2 was real but in ElevenLabs, not the DB:** two UNBOUND 0-tool agents sharing a name with a real
  one (`Kira_Business_Dennis_7f1c`, `Kira_RedTeam_Synthetic_a8d1`). `provisionVoiceAgent` is
  idempotent BY NAME, so each was a coin toss over which agent a future provision hands an owner.
  Renamed not deleted via new `scripts/defuse-shadow-agents.mjs` (**dry-run by default**, the opposite
  of its neighbour `reconcile-agents.mjs`); the verifier now scans the WORKSPACE for shadows, which
  any per-row check is blind to by construction.
- **C1 — BUILT, NOT OBSERVED** (deliberately left open). 18 of 22 prod accounts have no baseline,
  including 4 real people on business agents. Dashboard now shows `NoBaselineYet`, gated on the **row
  not the gap**, skipped for personal-only owners (`lib/valuation/baseline-invite.ts` + 5 tests); the
  link carries `?from=app` so the result page stops re-quoting a paying owner a monthly price.

description: "save_memory now carries a required about_business classification and parks another company's facts — SHIPPED and verified 3/3; the two walk-arounds it took to get there are the reusable part"
metadata:
