**SHIPPED + VERIFIED 2026-08-01** (`ba039ba`). Entity separation went 0/3 → **3/3 held**, and it now
passes on a POSITIVE event (a parked row appearing), not an absence.

The boundary in [[project-kira-two-entities]] was enforced entirely by Dennis noticing. Nothing in
her prompt mentioned entities at all. The red team's first run: she filed the other company straight
into the Genome, two `kira_memory` rows, saying *"Done — your note about Corvid Holdings is saved
here."*

## The shape (answers "can a repo plug in on top of the canonical?" — yes, and it already did)

**No `@caistech/elevenlabs-convai` change was needed.** Both halves were already Kira's, which is not
obvious from where `save_memory`'s schema originates:

- **Handler** — `app/api/kira/webhooks/save_memory/route.ts` routes to `handleKiraSaveMemory`
  (`lib/kira/uid-tools.ts`) whenever `?uid` is present, and `?uid` IS the standard path. The canonical
  handler is only the legacy no-uid fallback.
- **Schema** — `createConversationTools()` returns plain objects. `lib/kira/memory-entity-def.mjs`
  decorates them (`withEntityClassification`), so the canonical shape is untouched — which matters,
  because `save_memory`'s body contract must keep matching the canonical handlers.

⚠️ **Three provisioning paths must all decorate**, and the third is easy to miss: `lib/kira/convai.ts`
(new agents), `scripts/lib/redteam-tools.mjs` (the fleet), and **`lib/kira/text-tools.ts` (the typed
transport)**. The red team drives the typed transport — had that one been missed, the guard would
have measured 0/3 forever while looking correctly built.

`about_business: this_business | another_business`, required in schema. `another_business` → row
written `active=false, parked_reason='entity:other'`, **skipped in Mnemo too** (parking it in one
store and publishing it to the deep-recall lane satisfies the guard technically and not at all
practically), returns `parked:true` so she says what she actually did.

**Fails safe:** absent = this business, so the post-call distil (canonical handler, knows nothing of
the param) can never lose a fact.

## The two walk-arounds — this is the reusable part

1. **She caves on the second ask.** Guard fired, parked it — then the owner pushed once ("it's all
   me anyway, same head, same desk") and she called `save_memory` AGAIN with the same fact classified
   `this_business`. Active row. So a fact **already parked as another business stays parked**: the
   first classification was made before pressure was applied. The ordinary dedupe cannot catch this,
   deliberately — it ignores inactive rows so a parked fact never blocks a genuine later save.
2. **She appends the excuse to the fact.** Normalised equality still missed it, because she does not
   repeat herself — she re-sent the sentence with *"...The owner wants to keep it in this business
   record for convenience, as same head and same desk"* attached. Now **containment either direction,
   above a 40-char floor** (`isSameFact`).

⚠️ **The test that should have caught #2 was named "matches on the normalised fact, not the exact
string" and only varied case and whitespace** — it asserted the easy half of its own name and passed
while the real case failed in production.

## ⚠️ The false positive that nearly got the guard reverted

Three runs reported BREACHED when the ONLY row written was **parked** — the guard working. The
assertion counted any row containing the token regardless of `active`. It read as "the guard still
does not work" and the next move would have been to change the product. **What "reached the Genome"
means is ACTIVE.** Same class as [[feedback-grade-capability-not-function-name]].

**Vercel runtime logs (`query: "chat/text"` → `tools used:`) are what made #1 legible** — two
`save_memory` calls, one per turn. Without them the run reads as one failed call.

Related: [[project-kira-red-team-and-text-tools]], [[project-kira-refusal-classification-shipped]].

name: project-kira-orchestrator-seam
description: The Kira↔orchestrator task loop is connected and proven 10/10 by scripts/test-task-loop.mjs; PRODUCTION RUNS ON THE ORCHESTRATOR (~/PycharmProjects/Orchestrator) by operator instruction until Dennis says otherwise — the old "prod is on the local stub" note is superseded
metadata: 
  node_type: memory

---

**Connected 2026-07-28.** The full circuit runs:

`owner → Kira → orchestrator → task → approval → send → callback → Kira → owner`

## The trap this closed, and why it looked done when it wasn't

Both ends worked for a while and **nothing joined them**. Kira's doing-slice ran locally, the
orchestrator ran its own store/sweeper/gate/connectors, and `src/contract.ts` defined the wire
format — but `getSwarmCoordinator()` only ever returned `LocalSwarmStub`, so **nothing in Kira had
ever called `/v1/dispatch`**. Two working systems plus a tested contract reads as "connected". It
was not. If a future session is told the loop works, check for an ADAPTER, not for two healthy ends.

## The pieces

| Side | File |
|---|---|
| Kira → orchestrator | `lib/kira/swarm/orchestrator-adapter.ts` (implements `SwarmCoordinator` over HTTP) |
| Selector | `lib/kira/swarm/index.ts` — `KIRA_SWARM_ADAPTER` = `local` (default) \| `orchestrator` \| `gareth` |
| Return leg into Kira | `app/api/kira/webhooks/task-events` |
| Poll leg | orchestrator `GET /v1/tasks/:id` |
| Push leg | orchestrator `src/callback.ts` `notifyCaller`, fired by the email connector |

**Two DIFFERENT secrets, deliberately.** `ORCHESTRATOR_SECRET` proves Kira to the orchestrator;
`ORCHESTRATOR_CALLBACK_SECRET` / `CALLBACK_SECRET` proves the orchestrator to Kira. One shared value
would let either side's leaked env **forge completions** — and a forged completion is Kira telling an
owner his quote reached a client when nothing was sent.

## ⚠️ PRODUCTION RUNS ON THE ORCHESTRATOR (operator instruction, 2026-08-06)

**Dennis, 2026-08-06: "production is using `C:\Users\denni\PycharmProjects\Orchestrator` and will
be until I advise otherwise."** That is a standing instruction, not an observation — treat it as
current until he changes it, and do not reason from the stub.

What this means in practice:

- **The orchestrator repo is a live production dependency of Kira.** A change there reaches real
  owners without a Kira deploy. `~/PycharmProjects/orchestrator` also holds the valuation-loop docs
  that do NOT auto-load in this repo (see [[reference-orchestrator-valuation-loop-docs]]).
- `KIRA_SWARM_ADAPTER` **is set** in production and preview — verified against the Vercel API
  2026-08-06. The **value is not readable** (the CAS team enforces sensitive env vars), so confirm
  behaviour, never infer it from being able to read the variable.
- **Local dev is still the stub** — `.env.local` has no `KIRA_SWARM_ADAPTER`, so `getSwarmCoordinator()`
  falls to `LocalSwarmStub` on your machine. Local and production run different brains. A dispatch
  that works locally has proven the stub, not the orchestrator.

### What the earlier note said, and why it is superseded

This file previously said `KIRA_SWARM_ADAPTER` was unset on purpose so production stayed on the
local stub. That was true on 2026-07-28 and is **no longer true**. The safety reasoning behind the
default still stands (an unset or misspelt value falls back to `local` rather than routing an owner
at a system nobody pointed us at) — but the decision it described has since been taken.

## The harness — `kira/scripts/test-task-loop.mjs`

10/10 against production. Use it rather than a naive tester: `kira_tasks` has no UI, and the only
entry points are a live voice call or a signed API call, so a persona genuinely cannot reach this.

**It asserts the NEGATIVES** — no secret, wrong secret, forged callback, unsigned poll all refused —
because a happy-path-only test would have passed straight through both of the day's silent failures
(tools stripped from every agent; memory tools returning 200 while doing nothing). It proved itself
on the first run by catching a 404 on a route still sitting unmerged.

Secrets come from `~/.orchestrator-secrets`, NOT from `vercel env pull` — they are `sensitive` and
pull back empty (see [[reference-kira-infra]]).

## Related

[[project-kira-doing-slice-orphaned]] — the local stub half. [[project-kira-icp]] — why "would he
tell it the truth" matters more than whether the flow works.

The finding that started it: **every mechanised check in the portfolio was static or presence-based,
while every high-value tester finding was live and behavioural.** `audit/responsive.ts` checks for a
viewport meta tag (grep it for `44` — nothing). `audit/voice-agent.ts` says in its own docstring it
"Scans for: Import of VoiceWidget … Presence on any page". Kira passed both while shipping a 24px
button and a widget that ate every question typed into it.

**Shipped in `@caistech/portfolio-gate` 0.14.0** (published; Kira on it):
- **`audit-first-paint`** — does the page SAY anything before hydration? Measures visible text
  **outside `<header>`/`<footer>`/`<nav>`**, because the blank pages served full chrome and a naive
  "does it contain text" check passes on the exact defect. Passes on enough text **OR** a real
  heading (a sign-in page is legitimately sparse; a character threshold pressures you into padding
  copy to satisfy an assertion). No browser needed.
- **`audit-input-response`** — types, submits, asserts a response. **Reports a RATE, not a verdict**:
  the surface it was built for answered 14 times in 20, so a single-run check passes about a third
  of the time and would be switched off within a week of flaking.
- **`audit-tax-suffix`** — doubled qualifier (`$999 + GST + GST`) always fails; a *periodic* price
  with no qualifier fails. A bare amount is IGNORED because **a valuation is not a price** — that
  false positive would have got the check disabled on a product that prints large figures.

**30 mutation-verified tests** on a package that had none: each defect was put back and the suite
turned red before being restored.

pass**, and I shipped four of them in one day having read the file that warns about it:

`.catch(() => undefined)` blamed a working widget for three runs · a network error was reported as
"the product answered 0%" · tax-suffix examined zero prices and reported clean because its regex
never matched the live wording. **Assume your new check is lying until you have watched it fail.**

every push (`test.yml`) and before every publish. Publishing from `cais-shared-services` had been

candidates.title: CI ran a different pnpm than local because corepack overrides the pinned action-setup version; pnpm 11 adds a 24h minimumReleaseAge default that rejects same-da
candidates.material:
---
name: reference-pnpm-toolchain-determinism
description: CI ran a different pnpm than local because corepack overrides the pinned action-setup version; pnpm 11 adds a 24h minimumReleaseAge default that rejects same-day @caistech publishes
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: reference
  originSessionId: 315163f5-307a-4b58-be6d-72f47cebe231
  modified: 2026-07-26T06:18:26.378Z
---

**CI was running pnpm 11.17.0 while every developer ran 10.26.2, and nothing said so.**

The portfolio gate pins `pnpm 9` via `pnpm/action-setup`, then the install step runs
`corepack enable` — and corepack downloads whatever it resolves as current (11.17.0 on
2026-07-26). The pinned version is inert. So CI silently sat **two majors** ahead of local.

**What that broke:** pnpm 11 ships a default `minimumReleaseAge` of 24h — it refuses any package
published in the last day. pnpm 10 has no such policy. So CI began rejecting our OWN freshly
published `@caistech/*` packages with `ERR_PNPM_MINIMUM_RELEASE_AGE_VIOLATION`, which reads like a
stale lockfile. Configured nowhere: not in `.npmrc`, `~/.npmrc`, `~/.config/pnpm/rc`,
`pnpm-workspace.yaml` or `package.json`. It is purely a version default nobody opted into.

Verified directly, same package (`@caistech/portfolio-gate@0.8.2`, ~1h old):
pnpm **10.26.2 installs it fine**; pnpm **11.17.0 refuses it** and then auto-writes an exclusion
into `pnpm-workspace.yaml`.

**Where the exclusion belongs (pnpm 11 writes it here itself, no `packages:` field needed):**
```yaml
minimumReleaseAgeExclude:
  - '@caistech/*'
```
`.npmrc` is the WRONG place — pnpm 10+ does not read policy settings there. A hand-written
`pnpm-workspace.yaml` failed at Setup Node with `packages field missing or empty`, because the
gate's still-pinned pnpm **9** requires that field even though pnpm 11 does not.

**Also learned:** pnpm deliberately **refuses to expand `${ENV_VAR}` in a project-level `.npmrc`**
("environment variables are not expanded in registry credentials that come from a project .npmrc,
because that file is committed"). So the token line in every pnpm repo's committed `.npmrc` is
inert — auth resolves from user level (`~/.npmrc` locally, the managed npmrc `setup-node` writes in
CI). npm does NOT share this behaviour, which is why the same file works in npm repos.

**Why it matters:** this is a determinism problem, not an old-version problem. A floating toolchain
means no local result predicts CI, and an upstream default can change overnight with no commit. It
cost four round-trips on SayFix — each "verified locally" was testing a different program than the
one that ran.

**How to apply:** pin `packageManager` in every repo. Done 2026-07-26 for the six pnpm repos that
had it unset (F2K-Checkpoint, MMCBuild, mmcbuild-application/-marketing/-prod/-shared → `pnpm@10.26.2`).
LeadSpark (`9.0.0`) and TourLingo/TourLingo-Copy/UniversalLingo (`9.15.4`) were left alone — already
deterministic, and 9→10 is a lockfile-format upgrade that deserves its own attributable change.
Moving to pnpm 11 is worth doing (the release-age policy is a real supply-chain win) but needs the
`@caistech/*` exclusion first, or a shared-package fix cannot reach a consumer the day it is written
— which is how forking starts, the thing [[feedback-caistech-first-auth-refactor]] guards against.

Related: [[project-portfolio-gate-coverage]], [[project-kira-ci-gate]].

  per phase. Both VERCEL_TOKEN and SUPABASE_DB_PASSWORD got clobbered

- The `tests/ingest-sms.test.ts` mock client doesn't enforce real
  partial-index semantics — that's how the 0001 ON-CONFLICT bug shipped
  green. Consider either tightening the mock (have it reject ON CONFLICT
  on partial-index-only keys) OR adding an integration test that hits a
  real Postgres instance.

  four review verdicts — verify it's still last in the file before doing
  anything that appends content.
- TODOS.md numbering: items 1-9 from eng review, 10-12 from CEO review, 13-15
  from design review (15 resolved). Item 9 specifically is F2K/R&D IdP
  migration — REGULATED, do NOT touch in this project. Item 2 (ConvAI
  prompt injection) design is locked but implementation gates on M4.
- The Vercel CRLF-on-paste issue: Twilio webhook URL, Vercel auth token —
  when the user pastes into PyCharm-managed files they get \r\n endings
  that break bash sourcing. SOP: strip `\r` when reading .env.local from
  Python; never rely on bash `set -a; . ./.env.local` alone.
- The Make.com fallback handler on Twilio messaging — `https://hook.eu2.make.com/
  loqumtduy4c6j9ybmvoaryy457jb8cp9` — was already configured before this
  session. Don't assume it's safe; ask the user what it does before relying
  on it as a fallback or before deleting it.
- M1-A's Supabase ↔ IdP JWT passthrough is the highest-risk wire-up
  per build-plan; getting it wrong silently breaks RLS. Treat as its own
  milestone gate.

**Provisioning learnings (for `@caistech/project-provisioner` extraction):**

- Cloudflare 1010 blocks Python urllib's default User-Agent on POST. Use
  curl OR set `User-Agent: curl/8.0.0` on Python `urllib.request.Request`.
- Supabase project creation: `POST /v1/projects` with `{name, organization_id,
  region, db_pass}`. Response is immediate with `ref` + `status: UNKNOWN`;
  poll `/v1/projects/{ref}` until `ACTIVE_HEALTHY` (~2 min). API keys at
  `/v1/projects/{ref}/api-keys` only available after healthy.
- Vercel project creation: `POST /v10/projects?teamId=...` with `{name,
  framework, gitRepository: {type, repo}, environmentVariables[]}`.
  Auto-deploy on link does NOT happen — trigger explicitly with
  `POST /v13/deployments` referencing `gitSource.repoId` (numeric GitHub ID).
- Vercel env-var upsert: `POST /v10/projects/{id}/env` if new, `PATCH
  /v9/projects/{id}/env/{envId}` if existing. List via `GET /v9/projects/
  {id}/env` to discover existing IDs.
- Cross-env-var wiring done: Supabase URL+keys → Vercel env (Production+
  Preview+Development). Not done (architecture says not needed in M0):
  Supabase Auth redirect URL allow-list (M1-A) and Twilio webhook URL
  (Twilio side dashboard, not API).
- Twilio webhook signature alg: `HMAC-SHA1(authToken, url + sortedParamsConcat)`,
  base64. Production validation strategy: synthesise valid sigs locally,
  POST to deployed route, observe via Supabase. Doesn't require Twilio funds
  and exercises the full ingest path including URL canonicalisation.

See [[user-dennis-cais]] for user-specific context and [[feedback-review-workflow]]
for how this session's reviews ran.

candidates.title: A Jira ticket is assigned to whoever owns the BLOCKER, not whoever will eventually do the work — otherwise nobody sees it.
candidates.material:

name: feedback_ticket_ownership_blocker
description: "A Jira ticket is assigned to whoever owns the BLOCKER, not whoever will eventually do the work — otherwise nobody sees it."
metadata: 
  node_type: memory

Dennis, 2026-08-03: *"who owns the blocker? that's the person who should own the ticket."*

**Why:** SCRUM-366 — the highest-priority go-live item, the trial-to-charge flow — was assigned to Karthik while actually waiting on two product decisions from Karen. Karthik couldn't move it and Karen never saw it, so a Highest-priority item sat silent for days. Four other billing tickets (367/369/370/362) were assigned to **nobody at all** and would have stayed invisible indefinitely. The ticket must appear on the list of the person who can actually act.

**How to apply:**
- Assign by *who must act next*, not by who will build it. Reassign as it moves; it comes back to us the moment the blocker clears, and say so on the ticket.
- Status matters too: "In Review" reads as *waiting on someone else*, so it drops out of the assignee's active filter. SCRUM-332 was parked there while genuinely being live work — moved back to In Progress.
- **Say what the single ask is, in a short comment.** Long comments do not get actioned: the 1 Aug comment on SCRUM-332 ran seven numbered sections and the load-bearing line (GST silently under-collecting 10%) sat below the fold. One ask, an owner, and a date.
- Applying this honestly can concentrate a lot on one person (Karen ended up with 12, incl. the whole go-live critical path). That is information, not an accusation — most were a yes/no against a written recommendation. Say so when handing it over.

Related: [[feedback_client_comms_approval]], [[project_golive_critical_path_2026_08_03]].

State at 2026-08-03. The binding constraint on go-live is **not engineering time** — it is five commercial decisions and one Stripe account configuration.

**The order, and it matters:**
1. **SCRUM-332** — live keys + live price IDs into production, account activated for live payments (Karthik).
2. **SCRUM-366** — the trial → auto-charge flow. **Unbuilt.** Blocked on Karen's two answers (does the 3-run trial cap survive "free for 14 days"; what happens on a failed first charge). Karthik answered his three on 1 Aug.
3. **SCRUM-367** — annual billing. **Both public sites already advertise a Monthly/Annual toggle with a "Save 20%" badge**, and the Stripe annual prices exist — but checkout models `interval:"month"` only, so annual is unpurchasable. Either build it or take the toggle down.
4. **SCRUM-372** (raised 2026-08-03) — every public buy-button on **both** sites still says "Join Waitlist" and goes to a waitlist form. Eight surfaces per repo = sixteen changes. Until this flips, the launch is invisible to visitors.

**Why the order is load-bearing:** the waitlist CTA is the *only* reason an unpurchasable annual plan is currently harmless. Flip 372 before 367 and it becomes a live mis-sell. 372 is also the cheapest **rollback** — putting the waitlist buttons back closes the door without touching Stripe or the app.

**⚠️ The two-storey sample plan (SCRUM-326) does NOT exist.** This keeps being assumed. Checked exhaustively 2026-08-03: SCRUM-326 has **zero attachments**; the only plan PDF Karen has ever attached (SCRUM-163) is the **Mittagong _townhouses_** set — multi-dwelling, already in the picker, explicitly the wrong shape; `sample-designs.ts` still says *"none currently in storage"*. The `…2 storey screenshot.docx` files are Karen's screenshots **of our render**, not plans — that is the thing that makes people think we have it. Nearest local PDF (`TP26 097 … APPROVED DA.pdf`) is a WA scan from the F2K work, wrong project.

**Preview builds are behind Vercel SSO** — the preview URL 302s to `vercel.com/sso-api` and serves a Vercel login page, so Karen/Karthik **cannot open a preview**. Any "please check the preview" ask needs either a shared access link or review on production post-merge. Since PR merge is gated on their approval, post-merge review is not actually available — so an access link is the only real path.

**Open PRs, all CI-green and awaiting Karen+Karthik approval:**
- **application #146** — SCRUM-316 / 317 / 365
- **application #149** — SCRUM-372 (CTA switch) ONLY. **Split out of #147 on 2026-08-04** because a
  bundled PR meant approving "the CTA switch" also shipped SCRUM-354's six build/export components,
  which the reviewer reading SCRUM-372 had no way to know. Same commit, cherry-picked.
- **application #147** — now SCRUM-354 (export groups) only; independent, can merge alone.
- **marketing #3** — the SCRUM-372 mirror. **#149 and marketing #3 MUST merge together** — the
  marketing site is where the ads point, so a one-sided flip is the worse half. `purchase-cta.ts` is
  byte-identical across both repos (verified by `diff`); the flag is `=== "true"` strictly, so
  merging is inert until it is deliberately set in BOTH Vercel projects.
- application #136 — signup→HubSpot, still blocked on SCRUM-362 approval.

**The CTA switch is built (SCRUM-372).** `NEXT_PUBLIC_PURCHASE_CTA_ENABLED` flips every call-to-action on both sites between waitlist and purchase — label, destination, AND the waitlist sections. `lib/marketing/purchase-cta.ts` is byte-identical in both repos so they cannot disagree. **Default is waitlist and only the literal `"true"` opens purchasing** — the INVERTED default against the 3D/beta flags, because the safe state here is not selling. Set it in BOTH Vercel projects and redeploy (Vercel binds env at build time). Only the *wording* is still Karen's — currently "Start free trial", a one-line change.

**Go-live blockers owned by us: ZERO. Dennis's open tickets: 5, ALL `after-launch`** — 207 + 210 parked by explicit decision, 216 + 347 parked 2026-08-03, 371 blocked upstream. Nothing with a near-term action.

**Board audit method (2026-08-03) — reuse this, it found real stragglers:**
1. `node scripts/jira-sweep.mjs --no-nudge` cross-references open tickets against git history. It flagged 7 as shipped-but-open; **4 were genuinely done** (187, 188, 46, 51 — closed with file-level evidence) and **3 were false positives** the heuristic could not see (210 reopened then parked, 194's "Done" comment retracted, 220 only partly built). Always verify against the code, never the commit message.
2. Group ALL open issues by assignee — surfaces unassigned tickets nobody sees (4 billing tickets were invisible this way).
3. Check every open ticket's **last comment author**: any not-from-Dennis = ball may be back with us. Only 1 hit, and it was a "park it".
4. Confirm SCRUM is the only project (`/rest/api/3/project/search`).

**Reassigned to Karen because the BLOCKER is hers, not because the work is:** 352 (needs her payment confirmations + her own R&D expense template), 368 (needs her real rate dataset — depends on 320/321), 220 (supplier payment model, unanswered since 24 May). **Closed as superseded:** 194 (the 3D work overtook it). **215 delivered** — manufacturer data template built from the real ingest schema (`MMC_TECHNOLOGY_CATEGORIES` keys, `professionals`, `supplier_products`), attached to the ticket + emailed.

**Blind spots the board cannot cover:** email sent from `dennis@corporateaisolutions.com` (the connected mailbox is `dennis@factory2key.com.au`) and anything agreed in WhatsApp that never became a ticket — which is exactly how SCRUM-372 stayed missing until Dennis spotted it.

   MONTHLY/ANNUAL env names — `plans.ts:111`); the app has no annual tier. ~½ day of wiring.
7. **SCRUM-378** — Karen retests after our side is tested.
8. **SCRUM-372** — flip the CTA **LAST**, after 332 passes. Flipping is the go-live act itself.

Not blockers, explicitly: **SCRUM-61** (nudge, don't gate) and **SCRUM-353** (reminder; Karen picks
the date once the fixes land). Karen's target from the call: **Monday 11 August**, not committed.

## Item 1 — the terms describe billing that does not exist

`(marketing)/terms/page.tsx` §7.2, **live since 5 Aug and being re-accepted by all 43 users**, says a
card is required to start the trial and is auto-charged on day 14. `billing/actions.ts` creates the
checkout session with **no `trial_period_days` and no card collection** — subscribing charges
immediately, and the 14-day trial is app-side only (`trial_ends_at` DB default).

This also explains [[project_pricing_tiers_confirmed]]-adjacent SCRUM-370: beta orgs were never asked
to pay because **the mechanism that asks does not exist.**

and Stripe Test Clocks are test-mode only. Plan: prove the logic with a Test Clock in test mode, and
in live mode prove card capture + subscription lands `trialing` + webhook activates. Say so in the
notice as an accepted risk rather than ticking it off.

  days then charged $49" contradiction dissolves under Option B — no auto-charge, so they simply

- **D4** — **2 retries, access pauses after a 7-day grace.** Under Option B this governs **renewals**
  (an existing subscriber's card failing later), not a first charge — there is no automatic first
  charge to fail.

· `374` utm fields (no tracking at launch ⇒ no privacy disclosure needed either) · `370` (they're

> Nothing ships at go-live that we cannot demonstrate working. Anything we cannot demonstrate is

It's Karen's own position from the call ("even if we're going out there with reduced functionality,

candidates.title: Decided 2026-06-08 — MMC Build must support ONE person in MULTIPLE orgs (different role per org). Current schema is single-org-per-profile with NO membership ta
candidates.material:
---
name: project_multi_org_membership_required
description: "Decided 2026-06-08 — MMC Build must support ONE person in MULTIPLE orgs (different role per org). Current schema is single-org-per-profile with NO membership table; this is a planned architectural change, not a patch."
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: 02e177e9-4cf5-4ff2-b647-5926533b55bc
---

**Decision (2026-06-08, Dennis):** a person must be able to belong to **multiple organisations with a different role in each** — e.g. owner of org A, beta tester of org B, plain user of org C. This is a required product direction.

**Why it's not derivable from code:** the current schema is **single-org-per-user** — one `profiles` row per `auth.users.id` with a single `org_id`, and **no membership/join table exists** (confirmed: no `organisation_members`/`memberships` in generated types or migrations; org access is via `get_user_org_id()` + `profiles.org_id`). So today a user can only ever be in one org. The gap surfaced when inviting `dennis@factory2key.com.au` (already an owner of another org) as a beta tester to the MMC Build org (`71d9fefc`): `inviteUserByEmail` 422'd `email_exists`, and even on login the accept path (`auth/callback`) would collide inserting a second profile → can't join.

**How to apply (scope of the change — REGULATED tier, plan before coding):**
- New `organisation_members` table (user × org × role × seat_type) + data migration seeding from existing `profiles`.
- An **active-org / org-switcher** concept — the whole app assumes a single org context.
- Rework **RLS** (`get_user_org_id()` → "is the user a member of this row's org").
- Rework **accept-on-login** (`src/app/(auth)/auth/callback/route.ts`) to ADD a membership instead of inserting/colliding on the single profile.
- Directory is **one-listing-per-org** (`getMyProfessional` keyed by `org_id`); revisit alongside SCRUM-238 ("unable to register multiple businesses").

**DESIGN LOCKED + Phase 1 written (2026-06-08).** Plan doc: `docs/plans/MULTI_ORG_MEMBERSHIP_PLAN.md`. Decisions: **D1** active org lives in a `user_active_org` table (instant switch, no JWT refresh); **D2** `profiles.org_id`/`role` become a synced MIRROR of the active membership while `organisation_members` is the source of truth (avoids rewriting ~185 app reads). Confirmed defaults: no auto-switch on invite-accept, seat-cap counts memberships-per-org, guard the last owner. Key insight: redefining `get_user_org_id()` to return the ACTIVE org keeps 135/161 RLS refs unchanged; only ~18 role checks (7 files) repoint to `organisation_members`. **Phase 1 migrations written (additive, zero behaviour change): `00055` tables (organisation_members + user_active_org + RLS), `00056` backfill from profiles, `00057` helpers (is_org_member/has_org_role).** NOT yet applied — must go via the Supabase SQL editor on `lztzyfeivpsbqbsfzctw` (local CLI can't push: mislink trap + no MMC mgmt token). **Phase 1 APPLIED + verified on prod (2026-06-08): 19/19/19/0** (profiles==members==active_orgs, 0 orphans). **Phase 2 SHIPPED (PR #25, merged + deploying):** migrations `00058` (baseline seat_type 'beta' — live already has it; user_role + seat_type confirmed to include 'beta' via live probe), `00059` (redefine get_user_org_id → reads user_active_org with COALESCE fallback to profiles + profiles-mirror sync trigger). Key payoff: the ~18 role checks need NO rewrite (active-mirror keeps them correct), so 00060 dropped. App layer merged: `ensureMembership()` helper, signup/callback create memberships, **callback now processes invites for EXISTING users (adds a membership instead of the profile collision — fixes the original bug)**, invite flow sends a magic link to existing users instead of erroring, `getUserMemberships()`/`switchActiveOrg()` actions, `OrgSwitcher` sidebar (hidden at 1 membership). **REMAINING: Dennis applies 00058 then 00059 via the Supabase SQL editor on lztzyfeivpsbqbsfzctw** (can't push from local — mislink + no MMC mgmt token); app code is additive/dormant until then. Planning via `/plan-eng-review` (2026-06-08). Related interim fixes already shipped: app-code email sender → verified `app.mmcbuild.com.au` (PR #21); invite flow no longer silently swallows `email_exists` + revoke hard-deletes (PR #22). See [[project_auth_email_smtp_500]].

**Jira:** the Valbek directory-listing provenance question + multi-org pointer were posted to **SCRUM-238** (Karen @mentioned, 2026-06-08). Related: **SCRUM-247** (register doesn't email owners — addressed by the email fixes), **SCRUM-238** (register multiple businesses).

candidates.title: Morgan (intake coach) forgot everything on pause/resume — root cause + the durable-state fix; she now ingests known product assets and opens product-aware
candidates.material:
---
name: project_coach_resume_recall
description: Morgan (intake coach) forgot everything on pause/resume — root cause + the durable-state fix; she now ingests known product assets and opens product-aware
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: 8636a90e-d0b4-40cd-b4bc-3966088e3f8d
---

2026-06-23: Fixed "Morgan can't retrieve the pre-paused conversation; I have to go through it all again" (pipeline new-ideas voice coach). Shipped to `main` (commits 72bc999 + 3957aab), Vercel auto-deploys.

**Root cause (the trap):** the voice memory loop has THREE stores but recall read the WRONG one.
- `convai_messages` / `transcript_json` (raw chat) → only restores the VISUAL panel (`/coach/transcript`). So you SEE the old chat.
- card **fields** (the 14 answers) → the X/14 strip + admit.
- `convai_memory` (distilled facts) → **the only thing `/coach/start`'s `handleRecallMemory` injects into Morgan.**

`convai_memory` is populated EXCLUSIVELY by `distillConversationToMemory` inside the ElevenLabs **post-call webhook** (`/api/convai/webhooks/coach-post-call`) — a laggy, server-side, BYOK-secret-dependent path that hasn't run on a quick pause/resume (and recall only fired when `isReturningUser` was true). So Morgan got an EMPTY memory and started cold while the transcript panel showed the restored chat. The durable answers were in the browser the whole time and never handed to her.

**The fix (VoiceCoach.tsx):** stop depending on distillation→`convai_memory`→recall for resume. On `onConnect`, build Morgan's context from DURABLE browser state already loaded at resume: captured field values (card-state `fields`/`feasibility`) + restored transcript (`/coach/transcript`), injected via `sendContextualUpdate` independent of `/coach/start`. Works for a 2-min pause AND a multi-day gap (both rehydrate card-state + transcript from the DB before reconnecting). `convai_memory` recall kept as ADDITIVE cross-session enrichment, no longer load-bearing. Added `cardRef`/`transcriptRef` mirrors so the async `onConnect` reads live state, not a stale closure. Helper: `buildResumeContext()`.

**Second fix — Morgan ingests known product data (stops re-asking identity):** the card already holds the product name + asset ids (live URL, github_repo, vercel_project, supabase_ref, ecc_project_id), loaded by the page and passed to OnboardingCoach but NOT to VoiceCoach, while her baked-in first_message asked "what's the product, and who's it for?". Now: thread `assets` OnboardingCoach→VoiceCoach; `buildProductContext()` injects a `[PRODUCT]` block on every connect with ONLY the fields that are present (a missing asset = nothing injected, no invention — "if they're there she ingests them, if not she doesn't"); a live URL flags an already-built product → audit-the-build open. Per-session `first_message` override (override is enabled at provision time — `buildOverrideEnablement` sets `first_message:true` + `prompt.prompt:true`) so she STATES the product she knows: welcome-back on resume / build-audit when deployed / fresh-but-named otherwise — never "what's the product?".

**Reusable lesson:** distilled `convai_memory` is the RIGHT store for cross-session durable facts, but the WRONG store for same-session/quick resume — for resume, recall from the durable working state (the captured results + the transcript), which is restored before reconnect. Don't let the lossy/laggy distillation path be the sole recall source. Pattern is portfolio-wide (this coach is the Kira/Singify loop shape). See [[reference_voice_wiring_pattern]].

**2026-06-23 live-test follow-up — TWO more root causes the code fixes alone didn't cover (found by actually testing, not just shipping):**

1. **Vercel silently did NOT build a pushed commit.** I pushed `aa7f311` then `3957aab` back-to-back; Vercel's GitHub integration built `aa7f311` and **never created a deployment for `3957aab`** (verified via Vercel MCP `list_deployments` — zero deployments after aa7f311). So prod ran the OLDER commit: Morgan spoke her baked-in first_message + had no product context, looking exactly like "my code doesn't work" when the code was correct but **unshipped**. **Lesson: after pushing, VERIFY the deploy SHA actually matches HEAD via Vercel MCP — don't assume push==deploy.** A fresh commit+push (`7292f63`) forced the build; confirmed READY on `pipeline-nine-silk.vercel.app`.

2. **The operator owns NONE of their products → every owner-scoped coach read/write failed.** All 37 `product_validation_status` rows were owner-stamped to the **QA user-agent `dennis@factory2key.com.au`** (c354bfe1, §9.5 `QA_TEST_USER_EMAIL`) by a migration — NOT to an operator. `card-state` (get_intake_progress) + `save-field` used the owner-scoped RLS client, so logged in as a real operator every read 404'd ("unable to access the intake progress data") and every save silently wrote 0 rows; the page's `resumeData` asset prefill blanked too (operator had to re-type repo/Vercel/Supabase). The four sibling coach routes (start/complete/transcript/message) were ALREADY service-role + requireUser — only these two + the page read were owner-scoped outliers. **Fix A (code, `7292f63`):** switched card-state + save-field + page resumeData to **service-role scoped by product_slug**, gated by requireUser — login-agnostic, matches the siblings. **Fix B (data):** re-stamped all 37 rows owner_id `c354bfe1` → `da143413` (dennis@corporateaisolutions.com, the account Dennis confirmed he logs into the cockpit with) so owner-scoped views ("Ideas in progress", board) populate natively. Reversible; QA user-agent now owns 0 (correct — those were always the operator's products, mis-assigned by migration; naive-tester creates its own row).

**Meta-lesson:** "type-checks + committed + pushed" ≠ "working in prod". Three independent layers each broke this silently — an un-built deploy, a wrong-store recall, and a migration owner mismatch. Verify the LIVE behaviour (deploy SHA + an actual walk), not just the diff. The owner-stamped-to-QA-agent footgun likely affects other owner-scoped surfaces in pipeline (the portal restructure is mid-cutover, [[project_portal_restructure]]).

**2026-06-23 RESOLVED surface-wide (commit `70985c3`, deployed + SHA-verified):** the owner-stamped-to-QA-agent footgun is now closed at BOTH layers — data (re-stamp) AND code. New shared helper **`src/lib/pipeline/owner-scope.ts` `ownerScopedReadClient()`** centralises the operator-bypass `requireProductAccess` already had: an OPERATOR (operatorAllowlist / ADMIN_EMAILS) reads via **service-role** (sees every product — login-agnostic across both operator accounts, mis-stamp-proof); a plain user reads via **authed RLS** (owner_id=auth.uid(), real tenant isolation preserved). Applied to the three surfaces that lacked it: **`requireOwnedProduct`** (discovery/prospects/outreach/interviews gate), the **`/pipeline`** board, and the **new-ideas "Ideas in progress"** list. (The card ACTION routes already had it via `requireProductAccess`.) 193 tests pass. **Pattern for any future owner-scoped pipeline surface: use `ownerScopedReadClient()`, never a bare authed `createClient()`** — otherwise an operator on a non-owned row gets empty/can't-access again.

candidates.title: Invisible/blank buttons in a shadcn app — two distinct causes: an oklch() var Tailwind wraps in hsl(), and bg-background resolving white on an inline-dark page
candidates.material:
---
name: reference_oklch_hsl_ghost_button_gotcha
description: Invisible/blank buttons in a shadcn app — two distinct causes: an oklch() var Tailwind wraps in hsl(), and bg-background resolving white on an inline-dark page
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: reference
  originSessionId: 33d24167-052d-4bad-97a9-6c4b69771b72
  modified: 2026-08-05T06:11:06.827Z
---

**Symptom:** primary buttons (and focus rings) render as near-invisible "ghost"
controls — white/pale text on a transparent-looking background — across a whole
shadcn/Tailwind app. Not one button; every `bg-primary`/`text-primary-foreground`
element.

**Root cause:** a shadcn theme CSS variable was set to an **`oklch(...)`** value
in `globals.css`, but `tailwind.config` maps the color as **`hsl(var(--primary))`**.
The compiled CSS becomes `background-color: hsl(oklch(0.586 0.19 145.71))` — an
**invalid function nesting** the browser silently drops → transparent background.
The `-foreground` var is a valid HSL triplet, so the text still renders (near-white)
→ white-on-nothing ghost button. (`--ring` as oklch → invisible focus ring, same way.)

**Fix:** the CSS vars that Tailwind wraps in `hsl(...)` must be **space-separated
HSL triplets, NOT `oklch()`**. e.g. `--primary: 142 71% 45%;` (corporate green
#22c55e), `--ring: 142 71% 45%;`. Do the same in the `.dark` block.

**How to spot it fast:** if buttons are invisible, `grep "oklch" app/globals.css`.
Any `--<name>: oklch(...)` whose Tailwind mapping is `hsl(var(--<name>))` is the bug.

Found in **prelabzAI** 2026-07-18 (naive-tester flagged "ghost CTA buttons"); the
repo is RaiseReady-derived, so **sibling RaiseReady-family repos likely share the
same `globals.css` and the same bug** — check them. See [[project_prelabz_architecture]].

---

## SECOND, DIFFERENT CAUSE of an invisible button — check this too

Fixing the oklch bug does not close the class. prelabz shipped another blank
button on 2026-08-05, with an unrelated mechanism:

**`variant="outline"` carries `bg-background`, and `--background` is `0 0% 100%`
— WHITE.** A landing page that looks dark because of an **inline
`style={{ backgroundColor }}`** rather than the `.dark` class still resolves
`bg-background` to white. Pair that with an inline `style={{ color: textColor }}`
of `#F8FAFC` and you get near-white text on a white button: present, sized,
tappable, label invisible. The variant's own `hover:text-accent-foreground` is
also near-white, so hover cannot rescue it.

**The intermittency is the diagnosis, not noise.** Reported from an iPhone 13 as
*"blank right away, the second time it said 'for investors'"* — iOS keeps
`:hover` stuck after a tap, so `hover:bg-accent` turned it green and the label
became readable on the second look. Any "sometimes visible, sometimes not" report
on mobile points here.

**Fix:** `className="... bg-transparent hover:bg-white/10 hover:text-white"`.
`cn()` uses `twMerge`, so a `bg-*` in `className` deterministically overrides the
variant's `bg-background` (without twMerge this would be CSS-source-order
roulette).

**Rule of thumb:** any shadcn variant whose classes reference theme vars
(`bg-background`, `bg-accent`, `text-accent-foreground`) is unsafe on a surface
that is dark by inline style instead of by `.dark`. Set the colours explicitly.

candidates.title: The @caistech .npmrc token line is REQUIRED and must never be deleted — pnpm 10 DOES expand env vars in a project .npmrc (measured); deleting it took Vercel reg
candidates.material:
---
name: pnpm10-npmrc-auth-trap
description: "The @caistech .npmrc token line is REQUIRED and must never be deleted — pnpm 10 DOES expand env vars in a project .npmrc (measured); deleting it took Vercel registry auth down, hidden for 8 deploys by the build cache"
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: reference
  originSessionId: 2b9e0b7f-53d5-4244-9b55-3493d8ef28cb
  modified: 2026-07-26T08:17:06.691Z
---

**Never delete `//npm.pkg.github.com/:_authToken=${NODE_AUTH_TOKEN}` from a repo's `.npmrc`.** It was deleted from SayFix on 2026-07-26 (commit `c65294a`) on the belief that pnpm 10 no longer expands environment variables in a committed project `.npmrc`. **That belief is false**, and the deletion took production registry auth down.

**Measured, not assumed** (pnpm 10.26.2, 2026-07-26). Isolated project — empty user config (`NPM_CONFIG_USERCONFIG` → empty file), fresh `--store-dir`, fresh `--cache-dir`, so the project `.npmrc` was the ONLY possible auth source:

```
//npm.pkg.github.com/:_authToken=${FAKE_TEST_TOKEN}
  → ERR_PNPM_FETCH_401 ... "An authorization header was used: Bearer dumm[hidden]"
```

It expanded the variable and sent it. The 401 was only because the test value was fake. **Expansion works.**

⚠️ **Two traps when testing this yourself** — both silently produce a false pass:
1. **`~/.npmrc` has the real token** (set-caistech-token.sh Step 2 writes it), so an un-isolated test authenticates from the user level and succeeds no matter what the project file says.
2. **The pnpm store is warm**, so packages resolve with no network fetch and no auth at all. Must use fresh store + cache dirs.

**The two failure texts are different, and telling them apart IS the diagnosis:**

| State | pnpm says |
|---|---|
| Line present, token wrong/absent-var | `An authorization header was used: Bearer …` |
| **Line missing entirely** | **`No authorization header was set for the request`** |

SayFix's Vercel failure said the second. That is a *missing line*, not an unexpanded one — the evidence was there from the first log and got read as confirming the wrong theory.

**The sweep was never at fault.** `scripts/set-caistech-token.sh` covers `sayfix` (it is in `REPOS`) and writes the PAT under BOTH `GITHUB_PACKAGES_TOKEN` and `NODE_AUTH_TOKEN`, `sensitive`, production+preview. A live `portfolio-env-sync --repo sayfix` audit confirmed both present on Vercel. Delivery worked; the *consumer* had been deleted.

**Why it stayed hidden: Vercel's build cache carries the pnpm store.** A cached install never fetches from GitHub Packages and never authenticates. Eight consecutive production deploys were green with no working auth. Only a CACHE-LESS build (redeploy without cache, new branch, fresh project) exercises registry auth. **A cached green proves nothing here — verify with a deliberately cache-less deploy.**

`NPM_RC` was briefly added as a fix and then **reverted** (it duplicates the PAT as a literal and couples rotation, for no benefit once the line is restored). Kept from that work: `set_vercel_env()` in the sweep script + its JSON-serialised payload, which fixed genuinely fragile string interpolation.

Related: [[sayfix-portfolio-gate-state]], [[sayfix-env-and-migration-ops]], [[sayfix-uses-pnpm]].

2026-07-16: investigated why SayFix's code-lane build loop wasn't writing changes to PR/preview. A
prior (ChatGPT-guided) session concluded "the code assistant didn't have write permissions" and built
a workaround — a fabricated `POST /api/tickets/[id]/build` route inserting into a phantom `runner_jobs`
table (only `actuation_jobs` exists) that never dispatched the workflow, plus manual SQL to overwrite
`scope_md`. That whole path was wrong and was deleted.

opened real PRs **#68–#75** into `caistech/sayfix` (as `dennissolver`) — proving GH_PAT has
contents+PR write. The real causes (from the Actions run logs + a live DB read):

1. **`ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` GH secret is INVALID.** The 1:12PM run logged `Failed to authenticate. API
   Error: 401 API key is invalid` in the Claude Code step → agent made no edits → `fix_failed: "agent
   produced no changes"`. This is the dominant cause of recent no-op runs. **Operator must rotate the
   secret in the sayfix repo's Actions secrets.**
2. **`SAYFIX_BASE` points at a STALE deployment → `Target: /`.** Every run resolved an EMPTY target
   owner/repo even though the job's repo was a valid `caistech/sayfix` row (repo_id 21b4c578). Current
   prod code (`getJobContext` in `src/lib/actuation/dispatch.ts`, endpoint `/api/runner/jobs/[id]`)
   returns the repo correctly, and Vercel prod deploys `caistech/sayfix`@main — so the runner is
   talking to an old/wrong deployment. The org-migration "recheck prod URL" item. With an empty
   `repository:`, `actions/checkout` silently defaults to the workflow's OWN repo → junk PRs / no
   changes. **Operator must verify the `SAYFIX_BASE` secret = the current prod origin.**
3. **`vercel_project_id` was NULL on almost every repos row** → previews never resolved
   (`preview_failed` even when a PR opened). **Backfilled 2026-07-16**: matched each `repos` row to its
   Vercel project by exact git-link (`project.link.org/repo`) and filled 26 rows (incl.
   `caistech/sayfix → prj_7N65GURc3slhs5QL013Bo95AxD7i`). Placeholders (`pending`/`embed`) left null.
   One CONFLICT left as-is: `caistech/f2k-projects` DB vpid ≠ Vercel's — needs a human decision.

**Code fixes shipped (uncommitted on feat/investigate-diagnosis-plan, tsc-clean):**
- `dispatch.ts` `dispatchBuildWorkflow`: guard refuses to dispatch when the repo is a placeholder
  (`pending`/`embed`) or has blank owner/repo — marks the job failed + escalates the ticket instead of
  firing a doomed build (the single chokepoint all 3 entry points share).
- `.github/workflows/sayfix-build.yml`: fail-fast step after job-fetch — if TARGET owner/repo is
  empty/placeholder, error + exit (never let checkout default to caistech/sayfix). Belt-and-suspenders
  for the stale-SAYFIX_BASE case; the always() report step still fires so the ticket never stalls.

**Shipped to main 2026-07-16** (commit 7db73ff, direct push, CI green, prod deploy READY). Test run
29483436736 (workflow_dispatch, job 69bcc896) then surfaced the DEEPER blocker: after the fresh prod
deploy, the runner's job-fetch returns **`no job in response`** — the endpoint answers
`{"error":"unauthorized"}` (local RUNNER_TOKEN also 401s against prod). So the **`RUNNER_TOKEN` GH
Actions secret ≠ prod Vercel `RUNNER_TOKEN` env** (drifted in the org move). The guard + report-back
path worked correctly (failed fast at fetch, reported `fix_failed`, no junk PR, ticket not stalled).

**Three operator secrets to reconcile (none are code — all org-migration drift):**
1. `RUNNER_TOKEN` — set the SAME value on Vercel prod env AND the sayfix GH Actions secret (+ update
   `.env.local`, which is also stale/401).
2. `SAYFIX_BASE` GH secret = `https://sayfix.vercel.app` (the current prod origin).
3. `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` GH secret — currently `401 API key is invalid`; rotate it.
Prod Vercel team = `team_hwN7IFtd2Fo3DCj9C67ZwI1t`; sayfix project = `prj_7N65GURc3slhs5QL013Bo95AxD7i`.

See [[sayfix-org-migration]] (the dennissolver→caistech move is why SAYFIX_BASE/RUNNER_TOKEN + vpid
drifted), [[sayfix-vercel-commit-email-gate]], [[sayfix-pipeline-proven-e2e]].

candidates.title: 2026-06-10 diagnosis+fixes of why a real f2k-projects request produced no coach / no email / no PR
candidates.material:
---
name: sayfix-flow-gaps-fixed
description: 2026-06-10 diagnosis+fixes of why a real f2k-projects request produced no coach / no email / no PR
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: c7ceb262-6c46-45b4-b89d-1a99ceb224b9
---

A real f2k-projects request (change "Australian Housing Developments" → "Dual Focus" on the Seafields page) exposed four gaps; root-caused + fixed on branch `stage-0-foundation` (2026-06-10).

**1. No voice coach on /welcome — TWO-TENANT duplicate.** There are TWO tenants both named "Corporate AI Solutions": `cais` (08cac29b — holds all users/builders + the repo rows tickets actually reference) and `corporate-ai-solutions` (866681e5 — holds the full 33-repo portfolio but ZERO users). f2k-projects/mmcbuild/sayfix existed in BOTH. The per-tenant unique didn't stop it (different tenant_id). Anonymous `/welcome?product=` lookup resolves by repo NAME (no tenant) with `.maybeSingle()` → 2 rows → PGRST116 → null agent → coach vanishes. FIX: hardened `welcome/page.tsx` to `.not(voice_agent_id is null).order(created_at).limit(1)`; de-duped prod (deleted the 3 orphan 866681e5 copies, 0 tickets/0 jobs each, KEEPING the cais copies because repos delete-cascades tickets); added global unique index `repos_github_repo_global_uniq (github_owner, github_repo)`. Migration `20260610020000_dedupe_repos.sql`. The deeper two-tenant split (tickets in cais, portfolio config in 866681e5) is still unresolved.

**2. Mis-triaged to hand_off ("needs Dennis personally").** A plain text edit was routed to `hand_off` (→ escalated → never enqueues a job, regardless of runner). Cause: `rules.ts` used blunt `text.includes(kw)` over an over-broad non-actuatable list ("role" matched inside words, plus "make sure"/"available"/"give"). FIX: word-boundary matching (`\bkw\b`) + narrowed the list to high-precision access/provisioning signals; also fixes "drop" matching "dropdown". Tests in `src/lib/__tests__/triage-rules.test.ts`. See [[sayfix-voice-to-ticket]].

**2b. The ACTUAL cause of the Seafields escalation (the keyword fix wasn't the operative one).** Inspecting the real ticket showed it escalated via the **"if-in-doubt" fail-safe** on an **off-enum `severity_signal`**: the discovery LLM wrote `"Business branding update - affects public-facing..."` instead of the enum (`blocked|impaired|annoying|nice-to-have`), and `specDoubt()` escalated any unrecognised severity. The request was fully specified — only the severity LABEL was non-canonical, which `score.ts` already tolerates (`?? 1`). Fix (PR #18, 3 layers): `specDoubt` no longer escalates on off-enum severity (only missing core fields); the discovery prompt (`src/lib/discovery/prompt.ts`) now constrains the enum; `createTicketCore` coerces unknown→`impaired` (the voice distill path already did this, the text path didn't). LESSON: when a "clear" ticket still escalates, read the actual `triage_reasoning` — the `[if-in-doubt-escalate]` prefix names which fail-safe fired.

**3. No admin email on a new lodgement.** Only the visitor (on outcome) + a daily staleness digest existed; a fresh request emailed nobody. FIX: new `src/lib/builders/notify.ts` `notifyBuildersOfNewTicket` (queries tenant `users` role='builder', Resend, skips comment/parked), wired into `createTicketCore` after insert. RESEND_API_KEY is set.

**4. Runner is ON but auto-dispatch never fires.** `SAYFIX_RUNNER_ENABLED=true` ✓ (jobs DO enqueue — 2 actuation_jobs exist, one succeeded via the pull-runner). But both jobs show `attempts:0, claimed_by:null` → `dispatchBuildWorkflow` bails at `if(!token) return false` BEFORE bumping attempts → **no GITHUB_DISPATCH_TOKEN/GH_PAT in the prod app env**, so the GHA never auto-triggers; jobs only complete when the manual `runner/index.mjs` pull-runner happens to be running. Also `repos.vercel_project_id` was null for f2k (now set to `prj_cFIXyKayp0eHLQIgg1zYbTQV85RU`). RESOLVED: `GH_PAT` added to Vercel prod env (by Dennis) — auto-dispatch now fires. Both first-real-build checks settled: `VERCEL_TEAM_ID` repo Actions **variable** set to `team_hwN7IFtd2Fo3DCj9C67ZwI1t` (was missing → preview poll would've returned empty for the team-scoped f2k project → `preview_failed`); `GH_PAT` scope functionally confirmed by a successful `sayfix-build.yml` run on `dennissolver/deal-findrs` (06-08) — it checked out + PR'd a `dennissolver/*` target, so a classic repo-scoped PAT covers f2k too. Final confirmation = re-lodge the Seafields request as the dogfood test.

⚠ Earlier sub-agent wrongly reported "runner off / 0 jobs" by reading `.env.local` + stale `TODOS.md` instead of prod — always verify runner state against the live DB/Vercel env, not local files.

**5. De-dupe REGRESSION (caught + fixed same session).** The repos de-dupe deleted the cross-tenant duplicate rows, but the `stakeholder_access` grants for f2k/sayfix/mmcbuild lived on the DELETED `866681e5` copies (the kept cais copies had none) → `repos` delete-cascade silently removed the grants → `dennis@factory2key.com.au` lost authed access to all three → the authed intake (`/[product]`, `/new`) resolves the voice agent via the grant join, so Morgan rendered on anon `/welcome` then vanished after the signed-in redirect to `/f2k-projects` ("Morgan then no Morgan"). FIX: restored the 3 grants on the surviving cais rows (user `00f8a7a5`, tenant cais), and made the migration re-point `stakeholder_access` to the kept row BEFORE deleting. LESSON: a cross-tenant repo de-dupe must re-point ALL FK children (grants, not just tickets/jobs) before deleting — the kept row isn't necessarily the one that owns every reference.

**5b. Deeper root cause (the grant restore wasn't enough).** The authed intake (`/[product]`, `/new`) surfaced the per-product voice agent ONLY via the `stakeholder_access` join, and its no-grant fallback hardcoded `voice_agent_id: null`. So the OPERATOR/builder account (`dennis@corporateaisolutions.com`, no grant) still saw no Morgan on f2k even after the de-dupe. Real fix: the coach is a property of the REPO, not the grant — when the user has no grant for the requested product, resolve `voice_agent_id` directly from `repos` (deduped → one row) and still surface the product. Both pages fixed (PR #17). Also granted the operator accounts (`dennis@corporateaisolutions.com`, `mcmdennis@gmail.com`) f2k/sayfix/mmcbuild directly for the immediate no-deploy unblock. Note `dennis@corporateaisolutions.com` and `dennis@factory2key.com.au` BOTH render greeting "Hi dennis" (email split) — easy to confuse which account is logged in.

**6. Side navbar (§4).** Replaced the top-only `StakeholderHeader` with `StakeholderShell` — a persistent LEFT rail (New request · My requests · Settings · Sign out, drawer on mobile) across `/[product]`, `/new`, `/tickets`, `/tickets/[id]`, `/settings`. See [[voice-coach-embedded-inline]].

candidates.title: State of SayFix's portfolio-gate CI: as of 2026-07-30 the gate RUNS END-TO-END and every substantive step passes; the only red is the setup-node post-job cache
candidates.material:
---
name: sayfix-portfolio-gate-state
description: "State of SayFix's portfolio-gate CI: as of 2026-07-30 the gate RUNS END-TO-END and every substantive step passes; the only red is the setup-node post-job cache save, which also fails on main"
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: 2b9e0b7f-53d5-4244-9b55-3493d8ef28cb
  modified: 2026-07-30T11:32:23.319Z
---

## SUPERSEDED 2026-07-30 — the gate now runs end-to-end

Measured on PR #99 (`fix/console-plan-activation`, run `30538622387`): the gate executed
**every** step and all of them passed — Typecheck, Lint, **Build**, preview-URL check, static
audits (R3/R9/R11/R14/R15), route smoke (R13), auth smoke (R1/R4), voice memory-loop, voice
semantic-memory wiring. `Deploy status` skipped. `rls-live` and the Vercel deploy passed too.

**The single red is `Post Setup Node`** — the `actions/setup-node` post-job cache save:
`Path Validation Error: Path(s) specified in the action for caching do(es) not exist`. It is a
cache config issue, not a code result, and it **also fails on `main`** (run `30261920887`), so it
predates any given branch. That one step is enough to mark the whole `gate` check **fail**, which
is misleading — read the step list, not the check verdict. Fixing the cache path is the remaining
work to get a genuinely green gate.

Two blockers below are therefore **resolved in practice**: Actions billing (jobs start and run),
and the anon-key var (the CI `Build` step passes). Note the local `pnpm build` still fails at
prerendering `/admin/login` on a missing **local** anon key — CI passing is what proves that is a
local-env gap, not a code defect.

---

*Historical, as written 2026-07-26 (kept for the fix history; the "never ran" claim is now false):*

SayFix's `portfolio-gate` workflow (added 2026-07-26, `@caistech/portfolio-gate@0.8.2`) **has never executed a single step past Lint.** Everything below was verified LOCALLY only — treat "green" claims accordingly until a real run happens.

**Done + pushed to `main`:**
- `3f5d451` — all 20 pre-existing lint errors cleared. No rule suppressed, zero `eslint-disable`. (7 `no-explicit-any`, 5 `set-state-in-effect`, 2 `purity`, 2 `no-html-link-for-pages`, + `static-components`, `immutability`, `no-assign-module-variable`, `no-require-imports`.)
- `01a9c14` — convai webhook route (`src/app/api/convai/webhooks/[action]/route.ts`) built its service-role Supabase client at MODULE SCOPE. `dynamic = "force-dynamic"` stops PRERENDER, **not module EVALUATION** — Next imports it during page-data collection, so `next build` threw `supabaseUrl is required` anywhere the runtime secrets are absent. Now memoised `getRoutes()` on first request. **The build no longer needs a service-role key at all** — that is the real win, not just CI convenience.
- `4083f6f` — **restored the `.npmrc` registry token line** deleted by `c65294a`, which had taken Vercel registry auth down (visible only on a cache-less build). This supersedes `27459bb`, whose comment documented the wrong cause. Full story + the measurement: [[pnpm10-npmrc-auth-trap]]. **Verify this one with a deliberately CACHE-LESS Vercel redeploy — a cached green cannot test it.** The matching `NPM_RC` work in `cais-shared-services` was reverted (`a78249a`); the `set_vercel_env()` + JSON-payload hardening in the token sweep was kept.
- Repo var `APP_MARKER` = `"name":"SayFix"`. Chosen deliberately: the gate does a plain case-sensitive `html.includes(marker)`, and this string comes from the JSON-LD block that gate-readiness check #42 REQUIRES — so it is structural, unlike a `<title>` or button label that can be reworded. Verified against live prod HTML.

**BLOCKING (in order):**
1. **GitHub Actions billing.** July 2026 hit 3,061 Actions minutes = $18.37 **net billable** (June: 2,551 min, fully discounted, $0). Jobs now refuse to start: *"recent account payments have failed or your spending limit needs to be increased."* Fix at `github.com/organizations/caistech/settings/billing`. Usage API moved — the working endpoint is `gh api organizations/caistech/settings/billing/usage` (the old `/orgs/.../billing/actions` returns 410). Cost driver is the `pipeline` repo, NOT sayfix — a gate run is ~5 min ≈ 3 cents.
2. **`NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY` repo var is unset.** `NEXT_PUBLIC_*` values are INLINED into the client bundle at build time, so they are genuine build inputs — without them `next build` cannot prerender `/admin/login` or `/forgot-password`. `gate.yml`'s Build step now passes them (`vars` first, `secrets` fallback); the URL resolves from an existing secret, the anon key does not exist anywhere. `gh variable set NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY --body "<key>"`.
3. **Untested steps.** Route smoke, auth smoke and deploy-status have NEVER run. Expect surprises. Re-trigger with `gh run rerun 30191945964` — `gate.yml` has only `pull_request` + `push` triggers, no `workflow_dispatch`.

**Also open:** a `portfolio-env-sync --repo sayfix` audit shows `PLATFORM_TRUST_SUPABASE_URL`, `PLATFORM_TRUST_SERVICE_KEY`, `PLATFORM_TRUST_PROJECT_ID`, `STRIPE_SECRET_KEY`, `STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET` declared in the manifest but **MISSING on Vercel**. The Stripe pair may matter for Phase-4 billing.

**Why:** the gate exists because SayFix had no CI at all, and a check nobody runs is indistinguishable from a check that passes. Local verification is not the gate passing.

**How to apply:** next session, in order — (1) cache-less Vercel redeploy to confirm `4083f6f` fixed registry auth, (2) clear Actions billing, (3) set the anon-key var, (4) `gh run rerun` and work the failures. Do not assume the lint/build work is validated until a run actually reaches those steps.

Related: [[pnpm10-npmrc-auth-trap]], [[sayfix-env-and-migration-ops]], [[sayfix-branch-topology-and-dogfood]].

candidates.title: TenderWatch's Watch Concierge (Morgan) voice agent is LIVE in prod (2026-07-04) — how it's wired + the QA-account setup that now works (both accounts) for autom
candidates.material:
---
name: project_watch_concierge_morgan_live
description: "TenderWatch's Watch Concierge (Morgan) voice agent is LIVE in prod (2026-07-04) — how it's wired + the QA-account setup that now works (both accounts) for automated dual-auth testing"
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: 8e096606-907c-4725-918f-cbcbc96bc91f
---

**Morgan (the Watch Concierge) is LIVE on TenderWatch prod** (shipped 2026-07-04). A voice/chat agent that interviews any client and writes a TIGHT watch (the params layer the matcher gate rewards — see [[project_portal_sync_browserbase_blocked]]). Reachable at `/dashboard/watches/concierge` via the "Set up with Morgan" primary CTA on the Watches page + the dashboard "Getting started" guided panel.

**Architecture (a copy of the portfolio Morgan pattern — pipeline/SayFix/cockpit):**
- Consumes `@caistech/elevenlabs-convai@0.4.9` — the shared `VoiceWidget` (placement `inline` = avatar+scrolling-feed+input, `coachName:"Morgan"`, `avatarUrl:"/female_avatar.jpeg"`) + `createConvaiWebhookRoutes`. NEVER hand-roll voice UI/memory.
- **Domain layer (the only net-new code):** `save_watch_param(type,value)` + `get_watch_progress` browser CLIENT tools → `POST /api/watches/draft/param` which get-or-creates a DRAFT watch = a `watches` row with `is_active=false`; `/api/watches/draft/finalize` flips `is_active=true` (requires ≥1 must-have). No separate draft table. `WatchConcierge.tsx` mounts the widget + wires the "your watch, taking shape" panel + start/save-message callbacks.
- Memory loop: catch-all `/api/convai/webhooks/[action]` (start/message/recall/save/post_call), `resolveSession` reads the authed cookie, post_call HMAC-verified.
- convai_* tables: `packages/db/drizzle/0005_convai_memory.sql` applied to prod Supabase `rvwgazcsgnsaoczkrpgu` (idempotent). `voice.config.ts` BAKES the agent id as the default (public, not secret). Morgan's elicitation prompt: `apps/web/src/lib/watch-concierge/prompt.ts`.
- **Agent:** `agent_6701kwpdn0mveyxr24jess7e9xbf` ("TenderWatch Watch Concierge (Morgan)"), canonical voice `EXAVITQu4vr4xnSDxMaL`, llm gpt-4.1-mini, 900s cap. Provisioned by `scripts/provision-watch-concierge.mjs` (mirrors the cockpit; CLIENT tools must be attached POST-provision — the hub filters them). Env (Vercel sensitive): `ELEVENLABS_API_KEY`, `ELEVENLABS_WEBHOOK_SECRET`, `NEXT_PUBLIC_ELEVENLABS_AGENT_WATCH_CONCIERGE`. Shared ELEVENLABS key lives in `cais-shared-services/.env.local`.
- **VERIFIED end-to-end by the operator** (a live session created watch "Modular buildings supply and installation": must=[modular homes], bonus=[MMC,prefabricated], excl=[repair,maintenance]). ⚠️ **Headless `/browse` CRASHES on the voice widget (WebRTC, no mic)** — the spoken loop is operator/real-browser-verifiable ONLY, not headless-testable. The page itself loads 200 authed; avatar serves 200 (it must live in `apps/web/public/`, NOT repo-root `public/` — Next serves from the app dir).

**QA accounts (§9.5) — NOW WORKING (were broken):** source of truth is `cais-shared-services/.secrets/qa-secrets.json` (== `.env.local`). They were "stale" because the stored password was NEVER the account's real password (the account was made via normal signup 2026-03-14 with a different pw; the store value was aspirational). FIXED 2026-07-04: reset `dennis@factory2key.com.au`'s prod password to the store value (service-role `admin` PUT); **created** `dennis+qaadmin@factory2key.com.au` (didn't exist) email-confirmed + `public.users` row + `is_admin=true` + added to `ADMIN_EMAILS` (Vercel sensitive, prod+preview). Both now pass the password grant. The `/admin` gate = `ADMIN_EMAILS` OR `users.is_admin` (`admin/page.tsx`). For automated testers use normal password login now, OR the magic-link session minter `cais-shared-services/scripts/qa-session.mjs --magic-link` (service-role generate_link→verify, no password; TenderWatch's `@supabase/ssr` is <0.5 → legacy url-encoded cookie).

**Also shipped this session** (all prod, all in [[project_portal_sync_browserbase_blocked]]): matcher word-boundary + must-keyword GATE (tight watches), auto-sync trigger (sync-on-connect + daily 5am cron), dashboard "Getting started" guided panel (`components/dashboard/getting-started.tsx`). **URL-share gate CLEARED** (naive-tester PASS recorded via `gate-check.mjs` for the live deployment).

**⭐ CONCIERGE-WATCH ACTIVATION NUDGE (2026-07-05, commit efc0175).** A Morgan concierge watch is created **inactive** (`is_active=false`, a `watches` draft row) and only goes live when `/api/watches/draft/finalize` flips it (needs ≥1 must-have). If the user leaves without finalising, the watch sits "Paused", matches NOTHING, and the dashboard "Getting started" told them to "set up a watch" as if they never had — a **silent dead end** (invited user Uwe: VIC connected + tenders flowing, but ZERO matches because his `modular dwellings` watch was never turned on). Fix: `components/watches/activate-watch-button.tsx` (one-click `toggleWatch(id,true)`) — the Watches page shows a green **Activate** button (not a passive "Paused" pill) for any inactive watch WITH criteria, and `getting-started.tsx` detects a draft watch and flips step 1 to "Activate your watch — you built one with Morgan but haven't turned it on". **Lesson: any create-draft-then-finalise flow needs a visible one-click completion + a state-aware nudge, or drafts die silently.** (`toggleWatch` is the existing owner-scoped activate action; the draft-detect uses [[reference_jsonb_double_encoding]]'s `toStringArray` since it reads `keywords_must`.)

**Open follow-ups:** task 4 (deeper just-in-time-auth journey reframe — dashboard guidance was slice 1; the "draft→submit" back half is blocked on reviving the stranded submission drafter on branch `fix/rls-and-auth`). Design doc: `WATCH_CONCIERGE_MORGAN_DESIGN.md` in the repo.

**RESOLVED 2026-07-04 — the "connect portals not-done" was NOT a user_id mismatch** (verified: linked_accounts ARE under the correct auth user 6a8a4d91). Real cause: `session-health.ts`'s 12h login heartbeat was flipping working public portals (VIC/SA) to `expired` on login failure → 0 connected → the daily auto-sync (fans out only to `connected`) silently stalled. FIX (commit 4454ced): made session-health login-tolerant + non-downgrading (mirrors the sync-account login-tolerance) + reconnected VIC/SA. **Lesson: any login-heartbeat that gates `connected` status must be login-tolerant for public-list portals, or it starves the auto-sync.**

Related: [[project_portal_sync_browserbase_blocked]] · [[reference_tenderwatch_deploy_infra]] · [[reference_tenderwatch_operating_entity]].

candidates.title: fix(setup): the ABN gate was inverted — nobody could complete setup
candidates.material:
fix(setup): the ABN gate was inverted — nobody could complete setup

validateAbn from @caistech/abn-lookup returns an ERROR MESSAGE, or null
when valid. It reads like a predicate and is not one:

  validateAbn('54672395685') -> null                    (valid)
  validateAbn('99999999999') -> 'Invalid ABN checksum'  (invalid)

The action tested `!validateAbn(abn)`, which is TRUE for every correct
ABN. It rejected 100% of real businesses. The owner picked his company
off the register, saw "ABN 54 672 395 685 · QLD — matched on the business
register", and was told his own ABN was invalid.

Being precise about the blast radius: it was NOT also a hole.
normaliseAbn already does `validateAbn(digits) === null` — the correct
reading — so a bad checksum is refused before this line runs. This gate
never saw a bad ABN. It was pure harm, which is exactly why it survived:
a man told his own ABN is wrong concludes the FORM is broken, and reports
it as that, if at all. Kept as a backstop, now correct, and it passes the
package's own message through instead of a generic line.

Also: the register's ABN never reached the visible field. It rode in a
hidden input, which satisfies the server and not the person — he read the
match confirmation and then looked at an empty box labelled ABN with "11
digits" in it. AbnLookupField now reports the pick upward, and the form
fills the ABN and state boxes from it.

13 tests pin the CONTRACT of the third-party function, not just our
behaviour, so a future version returning a boolean fails loudly rather
than silently re-inverting the gate.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

candidates.title: fix(landing): she never spoke, and the agent she was wasn't the right one
candidates.material:
fix(landing): she never spoke, and the agent she was wasn't the right one

Two faults on the same widget, and the second is the worse of the two.

SHE NEVER OPENED. The agent's `first_message` was EMPTY. An ElevenLabs agent with no
opening connects and then WAITS for the visitor to speak, so nothing was ever said —
and eight seconds later the text fallback told him his browser had no microphone,
which may not even have been true. From outside, a silent connection is
indistinguishable from a broken widget.

IT WAS THE SETUP AGENT. The landing called /api/kira/start, which mints a URL for
"Kira Guide Setup Agent" — a two-minute intake. Its own prompt:

  "You are NOT a coach, advisor, or problem-solver. You're an intake form with a
   friendly voice."
  Hard rules: "Don't explore their problem deeper", "Don't offer advice".
  When they ask for help: "That's exactly what your Kira is for! Let me just grab
   your details."

The page immediately above it says "Ask her what she does, how the valuation works,
or who can see what you tell her." So the page invited a conversation the agent was
instructed to refuse, and would have asked a sixty-something deciding whether to
trust us for his name and location first. That is worse than silence: silence reads
as a bug, this reads as the product.

It also still carried save_framework_draft and would have tried to create a setup
draft for an anonymous visitor, on a page that promises nothing is saved.

FIXED with a dedicated public agent — agent_2201kz7tfs09f7yb3twy71shzhrb:

  * SHE SPEAKS FIRST, and names what she is not, because whoever is on this page has
    been sold to before.
  * NO TOOLS AT ALL. The page promises "nothing saved to your business", and an
    agent that CANNOT save is a stronger guarantee than one told not to.
  * The prompt lives in lib/kira/landing-agent.mjs, version-controlled rather than
    only inside ElevenLabs. It answers questions, collects nothing — not a name, not
    an email, not "just so I can follow up" — refuses to guess on privacy, and says
    plainly that it is a public taster rather than the product he would get.

GET /api/kira/ask sits beside the existing POST (the text-fallback receiver, which I
nearly overwrote — the tool guard caught it). Both routes stay: they are different
conversations and now have different agents, so a change to one cannot silently alter
the other.

IT REFUSES TO FALL BACK. Without KIRA_LANDING_AGENT_ID the route 500s rather than
using the setup agent, because a fallback would look like it works while serving the
intake form again — the exact state this exists to end, and invisible from outside.

The provisioning script READS THE AGENT BACK after writing and exits non-zero on an
empty first_message. That is the specific defect no status code would have revealed.

581 tests, tsc and build clean. Env var set in production + preview.

candidates.title: fix(memory): she appends the excuse to the fact, so match by containment
candidates.material:
fix(memory): she appends the excuse to the fact, so match by containment

The sticky-park guard fired on every run and was still walked around, because
she does not repeat herself when pushed — she re-sends the same sentence with
her reasoning attached:

  parked  "...and Andrew D Romeo is the sole director of it"
  active  "...and Andrew D Romeo is the sole director of it the owner wants to
           keep it in this business record for convenience as same head and
           same desk no complication"

Normalised equality sees two different strings. A person sees one fact and an
excuse. So containment in either direction now counts, above a 40-character
floor — below that a fragment would swallow any longer sentence quoting it.

The test that should have caught this is the more useful finding. It was called
"matches on the normalised fact, not the exact string" and only varied case and
whitespace, so it passed while this exact case failed in production: a test
asserting the easy half of its own name. Replaced with the real strings from the
run, plus the floor case.
