candidates.title: fix(tasks): she told an owner his email was sent, and it never left
candidates.material:
fix(tasks): she told an owner his email was sent, and it never left

Found in production. The 08:03 conversation is summarised as "sending a test
email, which the agent successfully drafted and dispatched." The task is sitting
in the orchestrator right now, status `queued`, undrafted and unsent, and the
recipient it captured was mcdennis@gmail.com — a voice transcription that dropped
a letter from the owner's own address, so even a successful send would have gone
to a stranger.

ROOT CAUSE. askModel swallows every failure and returns null, so a 429, a timeout
and a malformed completion are indistinguishable from "nothing to draft".
draftForIntent then returns null, and /v1/dispatch treated that identically to a
background job awaiting its turn: the row went in as `queued` and the caller was
answered "Accepted." Kira read that back as success. Being told a thing happened
when it did not is worse than being told it cannot happen at all — the owner acts
on it, and finds out from his client.

A spoken request the classifier RECOGNISED but the drafter could not produce is
now `failed`, carries result.error='draft_failed', and answers with something Kira
can say out loud: nothing has been sent.

Kira now reports the outcome rather than inferring it. approve_task returns
explicit `sent` and `failed` alongside `done`, and the agents are told to read the
result instead of assuming it — "accepted", "queued" and "noted" are not "sent".

THE BUILD QUEUE WAS READING THE WRONG DATABASE. /admin/asked-for and the alert,
shipped an hour earlier, both read kira_tasks — but with KIRA_SWARM_ADAPTER live,
dispatch goes to the orchestrator's own Supabase project. The page would have sat
showing this morning's stale rows while real requests arrived somewhere it never
looks, which reads as "nobody is asking for anything" — the worst possible failure
for a queue whose only job is to tell you what to build. Undone dispatches are now
mirrored into kira_tasks whichever brain handled them, and the alert fires on
`failed` as well as `unsupported`, since `failed` is exactly what this bug produces.

AND THE PATCH SCRIPT WAS APPENDING, NOT REPLACING. Its dedupe logic was correct
and unused: the PATCH body still sent `current + boundary` while `next` sat
computed two lines above, so every run stacked another copy of the section onto
the same prompt — four deep on one agent before anyone counted. The read-back
checked only that the marker was PRESENT, which cannot see this failure because it
is present four times. It now asserts exactly one, and collapsed the fleet back to
one copy on the next run.

Cause of that one is worth naming: a multi-substitution edit where only the first
match landed, guarded by a single assertion that the file changed at all.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

candidates.title: fix(voice+doing): platform-fill the conversation id, and give reminders a clock (#42)
candidates.material:
fix(voice+doing): platform-fill the conversation id, and give reminders a clock (#42)

* fix(voice+doing): platform-fill the conversation id, and give reminders a clock

Two silent failures, both of the same species: something reported success while
doing nothing.

1. save_message and update_conversation_topic were almost certainly never
   working in a live call. Their conversation_id was declared LLM-filled, and an
   agent is never told its own conversation id, so it either omitted the field
   (400) or invented one. @caistech/elevenlabs-convai 0.11.0 added
   platformIdentity for exactly this — it binds the identity params to
   ElevenLabs' system__conversation_id / system__agent_id so the PLATFORM fills
   them — and Kira, on 0.11.2, was not passing it.

   Nothing surfaced this because the post-call webhook persists the whole
   transcript to conversation_messages afterwards, so the rows appeared anyway
   and the table looked healthy. Capture-as-you-go was being reconstructed after
   the call rather than happening during it. get_conversation_context had the
   same defect on both its id params.

   uid identity is unchanged and is not an alternative to this: uid answers
   "whose memory", the platform-filled conversation id answers "which
   conversation", and save_message needs the second one.

2. reminder was the one kind the product could not keep its promise on. The
   owner said "remind me tomorrow", the classifier captured a free-text due_hint
   that nothing ever parsed, approval marked the row done, and Kira said "Done."
   Nothing fired, then or ever, because nothing swept the table.

   The classifier now resolves the spoken time to an absolute timestamp against
   a stated current time; approval moves the row to 'scheduled' with a due_at
   rather than claiming completion; and an hourly sweep delivers it. A reminder
   with no resolvable time now fails honestly at approval instead of being
   accepted and silently never firing.

   Idempotent by status — the sweep reads only 'scheduled' rows and flips each to
   'done' on success, so a re-run cannot double-send, and a delivery failure
   stays scheduled to retry rather than burning the reminder.

Migration applied to prod via the Management API (this repo has known migration
history drift, so never a blind db push).

KNOWN LIMIT, stated rather than hidden: there is no per-owner timezone — users
carries no timezone column — so relative times resolve against a portfolio
default (KIRA_DEFAULT_TIMEZONE, Australia/Perth). An owner in Sydney saying
"9am" currently gets 9am Perth. The timezone used is recorded on the task
artifact so a wrong reminder is diagnosable rather than mysterious.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(reminders): give the owner a timezone, and stop the script reverting the tool fix

Closes the limitation the previous commit declared rather than leaving it as a
note. users.timezone is nullable on purpose: a default would be a guess wearing
the costume of a fact, silently giving every existing owner 'Australia/Perth'
with no way to tell a confirmed zone from an assumed one. NULL means "not
captured", the caller falls back to KIRA_DEFAULT_TIMEZONE explicitly, and a
later capture is an improvement rather than an overwrite. IANA names only —
an offset cannot survive daylight saving, which is exactly when a reminder
would silently drift by an hour.

The zone is recorded on the task artifact and the spoken readback reads it back
from there rather than from the current default, so a readback always describes
the clock the reminder was actually set against, even if the owner's timezone
is captured or corrected afterwards.

Also: scripts/reprovision-kira-agents.mjs called createConversationTools
DIRECTLY, so it never saw the platformIdentity flag added to kiraMemoryTools —
re-provisioning would have quietly reverted every agent to LLM-filled
conversation ids, undoing the fix in the same commit that shipped it. This is
the second instance today of the same hazard: the script cannot import the TS
module, so the construction is duplicated, and a duplicate that drifts is a
regression waiting for someone to run it. Flagged in both places.

Migration applied to prod via the Management API.

candidates.title: fix(portfolio-gate): first-paint reported PASS having verified nothing
candidates.material:
fix(portfolio-gate): first-paint reported PASS having verified nothing

Two defects found by running the check against real deployments rather than by
reasoning about it. The first is the serious one.

1. NOT MEASURED read as PASSED.

Non-200 routes were skipped on the grounds that reachability is public-routes'
verdict — which is true, and which silently produced a green tick over a Vercel
preview whose deployment protection redirected all ELEVEN marked routes to an SSO
wall: 0 findings, exit 0, nothing whatsoever verified.

That is precisely the failure this package documents in three other files and
exists to end, reintroduced here on the first run of the newest check. It is worth
stating plainly because of how it happened: the trap was read, understood, quoted
while writing the file, and then walked into anyway, because "defer to the other
audit" and "check nothing" look identical in code and only diverge in the result.

An unmeasurable route is now a warning, and the audit FAILS outright when none
could be measured, naming the protection wall as the usual cause. A green tick
must never be available to a run that established nothing.

2. Hex character references inflated every measurement.

The entity decoder handled `'` but not `'`, and Next.js emits the hex
form — so "what's" counted as eleven visible characters instead of six, on
any page containing an apostrophe, which is most of them. Both forms now decode.

Verified against Kira production across the fix that motivated the check:
/plan 16 -> 300 characters of content, /login 16 -> 49, and /login passes on the
heading signal rather than the character count, which is the case the
text-OR-heading disjunction was written for.

Client-side the victim sees a SUCCESS screen — the worst variant, because the lead believes they have been received and never follows up. Server-side variant returns a 400 to a real user whose browser filled the field."
ATTEMPTS: [{"tried":"Checked email deliverability and spam folders","result":"Not the cause — the request never reached the server at all."},{"tried":"Compared Vercel logs against the reporter's account of events","result":"DIAGNOSTIC: 1 of 3 reported submissions present. The absence of the request is the finding."},{"tried":"z.string().max(0) on the honeypot server-side","result":"Wrong fix — 400s a real user whose browser autofilled it."}]
SOLUTION: {"approach":"Name the honeypot autofill-neutral (hp_field — never website_url/company_url/email/name/phone/address/url/company), plus off-screen + aria-hidden + tabIndex=-1 + autocomplete=\"off\". Make the PRIMARY bot signal a time-trap (submitted in under ~2.5s), which has zero autofill false positives; the honeypot is secondary. Server accepts any value (z.string().optional()) and silently no-ops when filled. Never show a fake success screen that skips the API call.","code_path":"f2k developer/funder/employer/buyer forms; PRODUCT_STANDARDS.md §9 codicil"}
GENERALISES: Any anti-abuse control on a public form must fail toward accepting a human. Losing a real lead silently costs more than accepting a bot.

candidates.title: MMC Build's trial model (CARD AT SIGNUP, Option A — Karen's call) and how annual billing is wired, with the traps in both.
candidates.material:
---
name: project_annual_billing_and_trial_model
description: "MMC Build's trial model (CARD AT SIGNUP, Option A — Karen's call) and how annual billing is wired, with the traps in both."
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: 9a4f6f31-7ef5-4024-bfa0-576c9cb87cd9
  modified: 2026-08-08T04:43:30.192Z
---

Two billing changes shipped 2026-08-07. Both carry traps that do not throw at build or deploy time.

## The trial model — Option A: CARD AT SIGNUP (Karen's call, 7 Aug)

⚠️ **Anything you read saying "Option B / no card" is STALE.** We proposed no-card, flagged it on
SCRUM-366 inviting Karen to overrule, and **she overruled — Option A.** Built and shipped 7 Aug
(`35053b2`).

**14 days free, card taken at signup, auto-charge at day 14.** In `createCheckoutSession`:
`trial_period_days: TRIAL_DAYS` + **`payment_method_collection: "always"`** — that second flag is
load-bearing. With a trial and Stripe's `if_required` default, Stripe creates the subscription with
**no card** and the first charge silently fails thirty days later.

Live values (`src/lib/stripe/plans.ts`): `TRIAL_DAYS = 14`, `TRIAL_RUN_LIMIT = 10`,
`TRIAL_UPLOAD_LIMIT = 5`.

⚠️ **The 10-run / 5-upload figures are KAREN'S ANSWER, given on SCRUM-366 on 4 Aug — which I did not
read.** I read the ticket description (listing D1–D5 as open) and not the comments, recorded "3-run
cap stays", and shipped that into published terms. She replied *"Not sure why this was assigned back
to me as I commented on this Jira 3 days ago."* **Read the comments before treating a decision as
open.** Apologised on-ticket and corrected.

Because the charge is real and automatic, **day 7 / 11 / 13 reminder emails** ship with it
(`src/lib/billing/trial-reminders.ts`) — each names the exact gross amount and date, and the builder
**throws** rather than send a warning it cannot put a number on.

⚠️ **The terms promise and the software must be checked as a pair.** From 5 Aug the terms promised
card-and-auto-charge while the software did neither; now the software matches. When either moves,
grep the CLASS (`card is required`, `automatically charged`) across `(marketing)/terms/page.tsx`
**and `components/legal/terms-gate.tsx`** — the acceptance modal is the text people actually read
before ticking the box, and it is the one that gets missed.

`TERMS_VERSION` (`src/lib/legal/terms.ts`) is now `"2026-08-trial-card"`. Bumping re-prompts EVERY
user; that is accepted, because silently editing an already-accepted document is worse.

## Annual billing — built, but NOT sellable until Karthik confirms env

Live Stripe annual prices: **Essential $470, Professional $1,910** (AUD, GST-exclusive). Both match
what the marketing page computes via its flat `× 0.8` — verified, they tie exactly.

- Env names follow Karthik's convention: `STRIPE_ESSENTIAL_ANNUAL_PRICE_ID` /
  `STRIPE_PROFESSIONAL_ANNUAL_PRICE_ID`. **Unverified in prod — SCRUM-385.**
- ⚠️ **`getPlanByPriceId` MUST match annual ids.** It previously matched only launch + standard
  prices. Miss this when adding any new price and a customer pays for a year, the webhook resolves
  the subscription to NO tier, and they are charged and granted nothing. Nothing errors.
- The toggle is **all-or-nothing and server-resolved**: `annualBillingAvailable()` requires EVERY
  `SELLABLE_PLAN_IDS` tier to have an id. Annual ids are secrets (not `NEXT_PUBLIC_`), so the browser
  cannot know — `billing/page.tsx` (server) resolves it and passes `annualAvailable` down to the
  client `BillingContent`. Half-configured reads as unavailable.
- `tests/unit/billing/annual-pricing.test.ts` guards the three silent failures (unresolvable price,
  annual ≥ 12× monthly, annual offered unconfigured). **Mutation-verified.**

## Verification gotcha worth keeping

A `grep -c` for the OLD copy reported a false positive because the NEW sentence contained it as a
substring — *"**No** payment card is required to start the trial"* contains *"payment card is
required to start the trial"*. Pick a discriminating token (`valid payment card` → 0) before
reporting a stale page. Nearly shipped as a wrong claim in a status update.

See [[project_golive_frozen_list_2026_08_06]], [[project_gst_exclusive_pricing]],
[[project_pricing_tiers_confirmed]].

candidates.title: Only 28 of 59 repos have a gate at all — 8 voice repos had none, which is why executorai's missing memory loop went unseen; plus the full recipe a working gate
candidates.material:
---
name: project-portfolio-gate-coverage
description: "Only 28 of 59 repos have a gate at all — 8 voice repos had none, which is why executorai's missing memory loop went unseen; plus the full recipe a working gate needs"
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: 315163f5-307a-4b58-be6d-72f47cebe231
  modified: 2026-07-26T06:19:06.423Z
---

**The recurring failure is coverage, not the checks.** Three instances in one day (2026-07-26):
`probeMemoryLoop` shipped in convai 0.7.0 and ran in **zero** repos; a gate step swept in the day
before **404'd instead of skipping** in 26 of 27 repos; and the voice-memory audit works perfectly
but did not run in the 8 voice repos most likely to fail it. Each time the guard was fine and the
wiring was not.

**State as at 2026-07-26:** 59 repos have `package.json` + git. **28 have `gate.yml`; 31 have
none** — including 8 that consume `@caistech/elevenlabs-convai`: MMCBuild, Mova, PartReady, SayFix,
community-question-responder, executorai, pipeline, singify-platform. That is the structural reason
executorai's absent memory loop was invisible to every check run from here.

**Two of those 8 are not voice repos at all** — MMCBuild and community-question-responder declare
convai with **zero source imports** (it appears only in a planned feature manifest / an
auto-generated README dep list). The dependency should be removed. So real convai consumers = 18,
not 20.

## What a working gate actually needs (adding gate.yml alone yields a red repo)

- `.github/workflows/gate.yml` from `@caistech/portfolio-gate/templates`
- `@caistech/portfolio-gate` as a devDependency
- `routes.config.json` — only routes returning a **direct 200**; a 307 asserted as a page makes the
  check meaningless (`curl -L` hides this — probe without following redirects)
- `auth.config.json`, `memory-loop.config.json`
- repo **vars**: `PORTFOLIO_GATE_PREVIEW_URL`, `PUBLIC_ALIAS`, `VERCEL_PROJECT_ID`, `VERCEL_TEAM_ID`
- repo **secrets**: `CAISTECH_PACKAGES_TOKEN`, `VERCEL_TOKEN`

`VERCEL_PROJECT_ID`/`VERCEL_TEAM_ID` must be vars because `deploy-status` documents reading them
from `.vercel/project.json`, which **Vercel's own scaffold gitignores** — so that fallback can never
work in CI. That step could not pass in any repo until this was fixed (portfolio-gate 0.8.x).

## Three gate defects that punished honesty (all fixed, explicit-declaration only)

- memory-loop probe **failed** a repo that correctly declared `semanticMemory:false` → new
  `memoryLoop: false`
- auth smoke **hard-errored (exit 2)** on a product with no auth → new `auth: false`
- gate **could not start** without a committed lockfile (10 repos gitignore all three) → empty cache
  key + a warning about reproducibility

All three skip **only** on an explicit declaration; absence still fails loudly. "We decided against
this" and "nobody configured it yet" must never produce the same result.

**Proven end-to-end:** PartReady went from no gate to **16/16 green** using this recipe. SayFix is
provisioned correctly but blocked on **20 pre-existing lint errors in its own source**.

Related: [[reference-pnpm-toolchain-determinism]] (why "verified locally" kept failing in CI),
[[feedback-grade-capability-not-function-name]], [[project-kira-ci-gate]].

candidates.material:
PATTERN: kira_tasks.status contains a JSON object ({"taskGroupId":...,"status":"queued","draft":{...}}) instead of one of the six TaskState strings
SYMPTOMS: "Tasks are in the database and on NO page. /admin/asked-for looks calm, the approval flow finds nothing, the owner is told his email was drafted and it never sends. Rows have handled_by='orchestrator' and a non-terminal status. Nothing errors; no log line; the row looks healthy in the table. Only rows older than the 15-minute grace window are affected, which makes it look like a dispatch bug when the dispatch was fine."
ATTEMPTS: [{"tried":"Inspected the dispatch-time writer (lib/kira/swarm/tool-handlers.ts mirrorTask, status: result.status) and the wire adapter (orchestrator-adapter.ts) and the orchestrator's own /v1/dispatch route","result":"FAILED to explain it - all three are correct on disk. Led to a false 'the deployed build must differ from main' theory. It did not; deployed == origin/main."},{"tried":"Compared deployed Vercel production against origin/main HEAD","result":"Ruled out deploy drift - no unpushed commits, latest prod deploy is the current HEAD"},{"tried":"Grepped for EVERY writer of the table rather than the obvious two","result":"SUCCESS - found a third writer nobody had checked: the reconcile cron"}]
SOLUTION: {"approach":"app/api/cron/reconcile-tasks/route.ts called coordinator.getTaskState(), which returns a TaskStatus OBJECT, then wrote `status: live` (the object) instead of `live.status`. The guard hid it: `live === task.status` compares an object to a string, so it is NEVER equal, every row looked changed, and every 20-minute run rewrote the same damage. Fix: read live.status, validate it with a new runtime validator asTaskState() (a bare `x as TaskState` cast validates nothing and is what let an object through), skip the row when unreadable, and add a CHECK constraint on kira_tasks.status so the write errors instead of persisting. GENERAL LESSON: when a column holds a serialised object, enumerate EVERY writer of that table - the culprit is the one nobody thought was a writer - and never trust an equality guard that compares across types.","code_path":"app/api/cron/reconcile-tasks/route.ts; lib/kira/swarm/coordinator.ts (asTaskState); supabase/migrations/20260730090000_kira_tasks_status_integrity.sql"}

| 14 | Factory Floor essay #1 draft | 203bb03 (cais-shared-services repo) |

## What's NOT shipped (intentional defers)

- **Wizard live E2E** — real ElevenLabs agent creation against a fresh install. Has cost + creates real vendor-side state. Run at operator opt-in on a fresh install.
- **Factory Floor essay publication on Substack** — draft is in `cais-shared-services/foundation/factory-floor/essay-01-cqr-launch.md`. Publishing decision separate.
- **PORTFOLIO_LINKS.factoryFloorEssay** — still null in CQR repo. Flip to canonical URL once essay #1 is publicly published.

## Architectural snapshot at ship

- Next.js 14 App Router on Vercel
- Supabase (PostgreSQL + pgvector + Auth) — 5 migrations applied to remote `vhslputasuxnxbffwcxu`
- Single-row `system_config` table holds operator identity + deployment_mode + agent_id + install_id + telemetry preference
- BYOK across every external service (verified zero (c)-class env vars in `lib/config.ts`)
- Slack bot tokens only (xoxb-); user tokens (xoxp-) rejected at validator
- Discord already bot-token
- Voice FAB mounted in dashboard layout — silently skips render until `system_config.agent_id` populated
- First-run wizard at `/setup` outside `(dashboard)`; redirect from `(dashboard)` layout until setup_complete=true
- 3 setup API routes: `/api/setup/identity`, `/api/setup/create-agent`, `/api/setup/complete` (last fires install telemetry)
- Drafter substitutes `{{operator_signature}}` from system_config at draft time
- Posting in customer-self-serve mode skips `provider.postMessage`; audit log records `approved_locally_no_post`

## Phase status

Phase 1c of `~/MONETISATION_EXECUTION_PLAN.md` — **CLOSED**. CQR was the canonical "first BYOK-free product" milestone. Next portfolio tool to follow the same gate template inherits the @caistech/* substrate, the system_config foundation, the bot-token migration pattern, the voice FAB integration, the first-run wizard shape, the install telemetry helper, and the README/LICENSE/landing-page scaffolding.

candidates.title: ElevenLabs migrated ConvAI tools to WORKSPACE entities (~April 2026): the inline conversation_config.agent.tools shape is SILENTLY STRIPPED — agents end up with
candidates.material:
---
name: project_elevenlabs_convai_tools_fix
description: "ElevenLabs migrated ConvAI tools to WORKSPACE entities (~April 2026): the inline conversation_config.agent.tools shape is SILENTLY STRIPPED — agents end up with ZERO tools, so the memory pull-loop (recall/save) never fires. 0.4.0 fixed WEBHOOK tools; but CLIENT tools (for in-context clarifiers) are STILL dropped by ensureWorkspaceTools (webhook-only filter) AND missed by the self-verify (counts webhook-only) — so a client-tool agent ships toolless and falsely passes verify. Attach client tools directly until the hub adds support. Re-provision every voice agent against 0.4.0; presence != working."
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: b578152f-1ad0-4e80-907b-4d71a5a0759d
---

**The bug (found live on Singify, 2026-05-25).** An agent showed `prompt.tools: []` /
`prompt.tool_ids: []` despite provisioning "succeeding". ElevenLabs moved ConvAI tools to
**workspace tool entities** (~April 2026): the deprecated inline
`conversation_config.agent.tools` shape is **silently stripped** (200 OK, no error), so the
agent ends up with **zero tools** and the persistent-memory pull-loop is non-functional.
Same migration class as the workspace-webhook move already documented in CLAUDE.md's voice
failure-modes.

**The fix — `@caistech/elevenlabs-convai@0.4.0`** (published 2026-05-25; commit `c1dc56e`):
- Tools are created as **workspace entities** (`POST /v1/convai/tools`, `tool_config` envelope)
  and referenced by **`conversation_config.agent.prompt.tool_ids`** — never inline.
  `ensureWorkspaceTools()` is **idempotent on name + url** (NOT name alone): workspace tools are
  workspace-scoped, so reuse-by-name would bind product B's agent to product A's tool (the
  cross-product leak class). `toWorkspaceToolConfig()` maps a `ConvAITool` to the wire shape
  (params → `api_schema.request_body_schema`).
- **`bindWorkspaceWebhook` now returns `{ webhookId, webhookSecret? }`** (was a bare string that
  discarded the secret). The `webhook_secret` is shown ONLY at creation → capture it into
  `ELEVENLABS_WEBHOOK_SECRET` (sensitive env, per [[project_vercel_sensitive_env_vars]]); undefined
  when an existing webhook is reused.
- **`provisionVoiceAgent` self-verifies** (`verifyAgentProvisioned()`): after provisioning it
  re-GETs the live agent and asserts `tool_ids` count + webhook bound + overrides — and **throws**
  if not. *(BREAKING: bindWorkspaceWebhook return shape changed → 0.4.0.)*

**The lesson — presence ≠ working.** Several repos had reported "full cycle voice success" while
the loop was silently broken, because those checks verified *presence* (agent exists, webhook
bound, widget connects, transcript stored) not *behaviour* (the agent actually has tools and recall
fires). This is exactly what `VOICE_MEMORY_STANDARD`'s behavioural gate + the hub's self-verify now
catch. See [[project_voice_placement_auditor]] (the `/voice-auditor` behavioural pass).

**How to apply.** (1) Any voice product: depend on `@caistech/elevenlabs-convai@^0.4.0` and
**re-provision** — agents provisioned before 0.4.0 likely have zero tools (silent strip). (2) Capture
the returned `webhookSecret` → `ELEVENLABS_WEBHOOK_SECRET`. (3) Never hand-roll the tools/webhook
provisioning per product — consume the hub (rule 19). (4) Trust only behavioural verification (does
"welcome-back" recall fire), not a 200 from provisioning. Portfolio re-audit (post-0.4.0) sweeps
Kira / Connexions / RaiseReady / MOVA / LingoPure for silently-toolless agents.

---

**Follow-on (2026-05-25, CAS methodology cockpit clarifier): 0.4.0 fixed WEBHOOK tools but NOT
CLIENT tools.** The in-context clarifier (VOICE AI rule point 8) uses **client tools**
(`useConversation` runs the implementations in the browser; the agent only needs the declaration).
Two gaps in 0.4.0 make `provisionVoiceAgent` ship a client-tool agent with **zero tools** AND report
success:
- `ensureWorkspaceTools()` (`agent-client.ts`) does `tools.filter(t => t.type === 'webhook')` and
  `if (webhookTools.length === 0) return []` — **client tools are dropped entirely**, so `tool_ids`
  stays `[]`.
- `verifyAgentProvisioned`'s expected count is `(tools||[]).filter(t => t.type==='webhook').length`
  (`provision.ts` ~line 379) — **client tools aren't counted**, so the self-verify expects 0, finds 0,
  and passes. The "presence ≠ working" guard is itself blind to client tools.

Symptom: the clarifier connects + talks but **deflects every card-specific question** (no
`get_card_state` to call). Diagnose by GET `/v1/convai/agents/{id}` → `conversation_config.agent.prompt.tool_ids`
is `[]`.

**Workaround until the hub supports client tools** (CAS `scripts/attach-clarifier-client-tools.ts`):
create each as a workspace tool with `tool_config = { type:'client', name, description,
expects_response:true, response_timeout_secs:20, parameters:{type:'object',properties:{},required:[]} }`
via `POST /v1/convai/tools`, then PATCH `conversation_config.agent.prompt.tool_ids` (merge into the
existing prompt — don't clobber it). `expects_response:true` is essential or the agent fires-and-forgets
and never gets the result. The client-tool NAME must exactly match the key in the widget's
`clientTools` map. Run the attach AFTER `provisionVoiceAgent` (its update path wipes `tool_ids` to `[]`).

**Hub fix needed (cais-shared-services):** `ensureWorkspaceTools` should create `type:'client'` tools
too (no `api_schema`; `expects_response`+`response_timeout_secs` instead), and `verifyAgentProvisioned`
should count client tools. Until then, any product wiring an in-context clarifier must attach client
tools directly.

---

**Follow-on (2026-05-25, Kira + Connexions sweep). Two more durable gotchas:**

1. **Server-tool requests are NOT HMAC-signed — they auth via a header secret you configure on the
   tool.** Confirmed against ElevenLabs docs: only **post-call webhooks** carry the
   `elevenlabs-signature` HMAC (verified by `verifyWebhookSignature`). **Server tools** (recall_memory /
   save_memory etc.) authenticate via a header you set on the tool definition ("add a header, type
   Secret") — there is **no** HMAC on tool calls. So putting `verifyWebhookSignature` on a *tool*
   endpoint is the wrong scheme: it 401s every legit tool call (and fires a false-alarm warn if left in
   warn-mode). Correct: provision each tool to send `x-<product>-tool-secret`, verify it in the handler
   with a constant-time compare, gate on an env so it's inert until the tools are re-provisioned. (This
   was Kira's `TODO(strict)` — resolved: the elevenlabs-router now uses the header-secret shape, inert
   until `KIRA_TOOL_SECRET` is set.)

2. **Reusable reprovision/check pattern: `scripts/provision-existing-agents.mjs`** (built for Kira +
   Connexions). Read-only **check** by default (lists the product's agent rows, GETs each, reports
   `workspace_overrides.webhooks.post_call_webhook_id` bound? + `platform_settings.auth.allowlist` count);
   `--apply` binds the workspace webhook + sets `standardAllowlist(host)` per agent (idempotent —
   reuses the one workspace webhook by URL, no dup). **Run `--apply` with `NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL`=the
   PROD host** (dotenv won't clobber a shell-set var) or it binds to localhost. White-label tenant
   agents are per-tenant-host → out of scope for the public-`agents`-table sweep. Sweep result: Kira 9/9
   + Connexions 3/3 agents backfilled, 0 gaps. The deprecated per-agent `platform_settings.webhook` +
   empty allowlist were live on BOTH repos' create paths before this — now consume `bindWorkspaceWebhook`
   + `setAllowlist` from the hub at every create site (rule 19). Kira-specific state: [[project_kira_voice_state]].

name: portfolio-naive-tester-resweep-2026-05-20
description: "2026-05-20 cheap-probe re-sweep of the 27 portfolio products that went through naive-tester on 2026-05-19. **Date:** 2026-05-20  
**Trigger:** Dennis wanted to confirm the portfolio was "clean before we start overwriting with the BYOK model."  
**Outcome:** Cheap-probe re-sweep run + per-repo addenda appended + portfolio brief published.

## What was learned

1. **CORRECTED 2026-05-20 late session:** The earlier claim that "almost no fixes shipped" was wrong — based on reading stale `Status:` lines in the remediation docs instead of `git log`. **Substantial work shipped and pushed on 2026-05-19** across at least 12 products. The doc status headers were not updated when code landed (only universal-interviews + NDISSDAAutomate updated theirs). Lesson: `git log --since=DATE` is the source of truth for "what shipped"; doc headers are not.

   **Per-product reality (all commits pushed to origin):**
   - **StoryVerse:** `de31877` — Privacy Act + COPPA + GDPR-K exposure CLOSED (RC7) via `/privacy` `/terms` `/parents` `/safety` `/cookies` stubs
   - **Connexions:** `bb9c301` — RC7 PII leak CLOSED (auth-gated `/api/panels` + `/api/agents`, drop `USING(true)` RLS)
   - **universal-interviews:** `92c4c28` + `3f990d5` — RC7 PII leak + Track 1.2 forgot-password 404 BOTH CLOSED
   - **NDISSDAAutomate:** `db75395` — RC7 phishing-by-URL CLOSED (verified live 2026-05-20)
   - **platform-trust:** `f19bc35` — C1 `/api/scan` + `/api/audit` auth-gated CLOSED
   - **mmcbuild-webapp:** `184a3c2` — every Hamish finding addressed (but artifact is orphan migration scaffold — wasted)
   - **F2K-Checkpoint:** `0655e1a5` + `92d1d0dd` + `fdf08b5c` + 9 Watchdog commits — Stuart's CRITICAL backcheck-submit fix + explanatory headers + full Watchdog buildout
   - **DealFindrs:** 8 commits — signup-silent-fail fixed, auth+reset wired, hero data flipped, demo button removed
   - **RaiseReadyTemplate:** `28baa12` — RC9 vendor-identity scrub via `NEXT_PUBLIC_VENDOR_*` env vars CLOSED
   - **LongtailAIVentureStudio:** `5ab276e` — RLS RC7 CLOSED (LP-viewer gap remains open)
   - **F2K-Projects:** `095b649` — admin allowlist denial surface (minor — main persona findings open)
   - **Corporate-AI-Solutions:** wave2 + wave3 BYOK pivot (`/marketplace/cqr`, `/engagement`, `/clients`, retire `/launchstack`) + `/studio/partner` 301 redirect CLOSES Helen's finding

   **Products with ZERO naive-tester remediation 2026-05-19** (13): AIFTIS-Demo, easy-claude-code, F2K-Fund-Tokenisation, F2K-OffshoreModular, HairStylistAI, Kira, LaunchReady, LessonsLearned, LingoPureAI, PrelabzAI, property-services, storefront-mcp, TourLingo. Plus R-and-D-Tax (RC1 routing-bleed fixed today 2026-05-20 at the URL layer only — content fixes still plan-only).

2. **Cheap probe pass-rate:** 🟢 2 / 🟡 24 / 🔴 1.
   - GREEN: ndissda-automate, universal-interviews (basic URL plumbing OK only — not a clean bill of health)
   - RED: r-and-d-tax (regressed from "Vercel 401 wall" last week to bare 404)
   - AMBER: everything else has at least one broken key route from the 2026-05-19 finding still 404ing

3. **`platform-trust` `/api/audit` → 401 is correct behaviour** (C1 hardening from 2026-05-19). The probe records it as broken because it's classifying non-2xx as failed, but this is the intended response. Don't treat platform-trust's amber as a regression.

4. **`r-and-d-tax` regression** is worth checking — went from Vercel-protected to bare 404. Could be accidental deletion or domain reassignment.

## BYOK gating decision (locked)

**CQR (Community Question Responder) remains the first BYOK target.** Per [[project_cqr_byok_distribution]] (decided 2026-05-20 with 14-item release gate). CQR was not in the 27-product naive-tester sweep — it's newer and needs its own walkthrough before public-publish.

**Of the 27 legacy products, none are ready as a *first* BYOK template.** The 2 GREENs are wrong brand surfaces for BYOK:
- `ndissda-automate` is a paying-client/regulated product (PF Platform) — not portable
- `universal-interviews` had a Privacy Act incident last week — not a clean lead surface

**Realistic 2nd/3rd BYOK candidates** (after CQR ships) — REVISED 2026-05-20 late session per git-log truth:
1. **`raiseready-template`** — CLOSEST of the legacy 27. Purpose-built clean-room template; RC9 vendor-identity scrub shipped via env vars. Residual: content edits only (pricing/licensing/data-ownership statements per actions D–H).
2. **`investor-pilot`** — 50 commits of pipeline + AI Interview wizard buildout. Persona-positive baseline ("best auth page in portfolio"). Single buying blocker = `/pricing` "Coming soon" — one focused fix to close.
3. **`dealfindrs`** — heavy shipped remediation (signup, auth, demo, hero data). Most persona findings closed.
4. **`storyverse`** — Privacy Act + COPPA + GDPR-K exposure closed. Children's-data regulatory bar always high though.
5. **`universal-interviews`** — RC7/RC9/forgot-password closed. Privacy Act incident overhead may disqualify as a *lead* BYOK brand surface.

## Top-3 remediation queue (signal-to-effort) — updated 2026-05-20

1. ~~**mmcbuild-webapp**~~ — DROPPED. Orphaned migration scaffold per [[project_mmc_vercel_team_migration]], not a live paying-client surface. Real MMC Build lives on Supabase `skyeqimwnyuuozvhubdc` + separate Vercel team. Persona findings were correct for the artifact; the artifact has zero real users.
2. ~~**ndissda-automate**~~ — ALREADY DONE. Commit `db75395` (the whitelist-`?error=` security fix) was pushed to main + origin (the doc status header was stale). Verified live in prod: phishing payload `?error=Your+account+has+been+suspended.+Call+1800-555-0123` returns 0 matches in rendered HTML. Open follow-up: confirm or override placeholder `admin@propertyfriends.com.au` mailto (set `NEXT_PUBLIC_PF_ADMIN_EMAIL` in Vercel if a different mailbox is canonical).
3. ~~**r-and-d-tax**~~ — DONE. Not a regression — same RC1 routing-bleed as the 2026-05-20 4-repo batch (connexions/ndissda-automate/partner-pilot/gbta-openclaw). Fix: ssoProtection patched `all_except_custom_domains` → `preview` via Vercel API + CAS marketing site URL un-truncated in constants.ts:383. Canonical URL now serves real product (title: *R&D Tax Tracker — Automated R&D Tax Incentive Recording*). Persona's deeper findings (no branded landing, no "request beta" CTA) remain plan-only.

**New artifact:** `cais-shared-services/scripts/patch-ssoprotection.py` — re-usable for any future RC1 routing-bleed product. Requires a fresh SAML-scoped Vercel token (script's error message explains the refresh path).

## Where things live

- Portfolio brief: `cais-shared-services/PORTFOLIO_NAIVE_RESWEEP_2026-05-20.md`
- Auto-generated table: `cais-shared-services/probe-summary-2026-05-20.md`

## What this re-sweep can NOT say

The cheap probe is HTTP-only. It cannot detect:
- Broken CTAs that return 200 but go nowhere
- Data leaks behind 200 auth pages (RLS holes)
- Copy quality, trust signals, persona-level concerns

For all of that, the 2026-05-19 persona reports at `C:/Users/denni/naive-tester-reports/2026-05-19-1711/` remain authoritative. The 2026-05-20 addendum in each repo is a plumbing snapshot, NOT a closure signal for the persona findings.

candidates.title: Dependabot (not a hand-run script) is now the delivery path for @caistech substrate updates across 21 repos — plus the Dependabot-secret gotcha that breaks it s
candidates.material:
---
name: project_caistech_delivery_path
description: Dependabot (not a hand-run script) is now the delivery path for @caistech substrate updates across 21 repos — plus the Dependabot-secret gotcha that breaks it silently.
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: 97c8b151-98c4-4dc8-8e3d-726419c17f5e
  modified: 2026-07-26T06:01:24.975Z
---

As of 2026-07-26, `@caistech/*` updates reach consumers via **per-repo `.github/dependabot.yml`**
in 21 repos — scoped to `@caistech/*` only, grouped into one weekly PR (Monday).

**The gotcha that will cost an hour if forgotten:** `dependabot.yml` resolves `${{secrets.X}}` from
**Dependabot secrets**, NOT Actions secrets. Repos already had `CAISTECH_PACKAGES_TOKEN` as an
*Actions* secret; Dependabot cannot read it, and the failure looks like an unauthenticated 401 on
the private registry — reads like a token-scope problem and isn't. Now set as a Dependabot secret:
**org-wide on `caistech`** (19 repos) and **per-repo on the 3 `dennissolver` repos**
(AIFTIS-Demo, deal-findrs, mova). A new repo in another org needs its own.

**Deleted, do not recreate:** `scripts/bump-consumers.sh` and `scripts/finalize-consumers.sh` in
cais-shared-services. Both kept hardcoded consumer lists that went stale faster than they were used
(archived `mmcbuild` twice, `gbta-openclaw`, `SmartBoard`; omitted over half the real consumers).
`finalize-consumers.sh` additionally had a *hardcoded commit message* frozen to one 2026 migration.
Their onboarding handlers in `scripts/_onboard-update-bash-lists.py` were removed too — deleting the
scripts without that would break `onboard-new-project.sh` on a missing path.

**Why this exists:** shipping a shared fix and *reaching the fleet* were separate jobs and only the
first had a mechanism. A fail-closed fix for a live auth hole sat documented for weeks as a result
(see [[project_convai_post_call_failopen]]).

**How to apply:** never hand-sweep a `@caistech` bump across repos again — publish, then let
Dependabot open the PRs. If a consumer isn't getting PRs, check (1) `dependabot.yml` is on the
repo's **default branch** (Dependabot ignores other branches), (2) the Dependabot secret exists for
that org/repo. Related: [[reference_caistech_packages_token_migration]].

name: project_f2k_checkpoint_tenant_and_panel
description: "F2K-Checkpoint Supabase ref, canonical Factory2Key tenant id, the 2026-06-23 GBTA→F2K consolidation, and the new Geraldton vendor panel + panel_rate table."

F2K-Checkpoint prod Supabase = ref **`curqlivhisgakpajnmdt`** (its own instance; runs as postgres via the Management API query endpoint `POST /v1/projects/<ref>/database/query` with `~/.supabase-token`). RLS convention for tenant-scoped tables is the **`current_tenant_id()`** helper (NOT `profiles`/`auth.uid()`).

**Canonical operating tenant = Factory2Key = `d40bc5e0-1fb7-4b1f-8940-155686f14731`** (admin `dennis@factory2key.com.au`). On **2026-06-23** all projects + data were consolidated here from two legacy Global Buildtech tenants — `00ad897c-…` (Global Buildtech Australia) and `43648220-…` (GLOBAL BUILDTECH AUSTRALIA PTY LTD) — by flipping `tenant_id` across ~25 data tables inside one atomic `DO` block run with `session_replication_role=replica` (needed to bypass the `prevent_snapshot_mutation` immutability trigger on `schedule_snapshots` + audit triggers). The two GBTA tenants were **retained but emptied** (their admin `profiles` kept: `mcmdennis@gmail.com`, `user@test.checkpoint.com`). Duplicate **Lot 442 Half Moon Drive** kept BOTH copies — the incoming GBTA one renamed `Lot 442 Half Moon Drive Waggrakine (GBTA)` to clear the `projects` UNIQUE(tenant_id, project_name) constraint. `trade_map` (UNIQUE per category) merged uniques + dropped 14 colliding dups. **`organization_id` is a separate free uuid column (no FK, no `organizations` table) that the first tenant_id pass MISSED — a follow-up flipped `organization_id` GBTA→F2K across all 25 org-scoped tables too, so both scoping columns are now F2K.** **Lot 109 Wavecrest** project created under F2K (id `24c55511-…`; lot_no 109, 2500 m², Koala70, buyers Jacob & Annabelle Peers, estate-anchor coords cloned from Lot 91) — but its **197-task lifecycle is NOT generated** (app-side via `POST /api/projects/generate-tasks`, needs a session; a raw projects INSERT does not trigger it).

**Geraldton vendor panel** seeded under F2K (13 suppliers) + a **NEW `panel_rate` table** (region × trade × provider × price × validity × provenance — the standing-price home, since `suppliers` has no price column and `quotes`/`rfq_quotes` are RFQ-bound). Priced rows from real Gmail/Drive-mined quotes: Quantum Surveys, Flow Consulting (geotech $1,750/lot), Porter ($26,500 ex, expired), Structerre ($19,800, expired), Elite Electrical ($29,926.60), Peak Consultants (Western Power $1,595/site). `panel_rate` is now a **tracked migration** (`supabase/migrations/20260623120000_panel_rate.sql`, idempotent) as well as live; seed lives in `docs/geraldton-panel-rate.DRAFT.sql`.

This all serves auto-generating **pre-contract proposals** (two-type model) — **fully BUILT, shipped to main + deployed (2026-06-23)**. Engine: `proposalGenerator.ts` (pure deterministic, unit-aware so a whole-development quote is NOT applied firm to a single lot), `proposalCatalog.ts` (service menu + fixed $2,000 coord fee), `proposalData.ts` (region-matched panel rates, Waggrakine→Geraldton alias), `proposalPdf.ts` (**branded** — Factory2Key logo header + blue/orange + legal-entity footer: *The Trustee for Factory2Key Unit Trust · ABN 51 700 805 298*). Route `GET /api/projects/[id]/proposal?services=&mode=auto|generic|site_specific&scale=lot&format=json|md|pdf`. **UI**: `[id]/proposal` page + panel (service picker, mode toggle, preview, Download PDF, **Email to client**). **Email-from-platform**: `emailProposal` action renders the branded PDF server-side + sends as Factory2Key via Resend (`emailService.sendEmail` gained `attachments`) with a cover note — needs `RESEND_API_KEY` in Vercel. Tests: proposalGenerator (17) + proposalPdf render/logo-decode (3). Assessment: `docs/PRECONTRACT_PROPOSAL_GENERATION_FINDINGS.md`.

**Gotchas burned this session (see [[reference_serverless_pdf_jspdf_gotchas]]):** (1) `jspdf-autotable` v5 — use the functional `autoTable(doc, opts)`, the `doc.autoTable` prototype patch doesn't register under vitest. (2) the logo "missing from header" was because `public/factory2key_logo_transparent.png` was **never git-tracked** → not deployed → fetch 404'd → silent fallback; fixed by **embedding** a downscaled base64 logo (`proposalLogo.ts`) instead of fetching public/ (serverless doesn't bundle public/).

**Team-invite + INP fixes (2026-06-23, PRs #29/#30, on main + deployed):** (1) **Invites never sent.**
The "Add Team Member" form (`admin/users/create`) called `supabase.auth.admin.createUser` /
`inviteUserByEmail` **from the BROWSER client** — admin auth methods need the service-role key, so
they silently failed (anon key); and `createUser({email_confirm:true})` sends NO email anyway, and
nothing set the new user's tenant. Fix: `inviteTeamMember` **server action** (`lib/actions/team.ts`)
using `createAdminClient()` → `inviteUserByEmail` (sends via the Resend SMTP, which IS configured on
this ref: smtp.resend.com, `rate_limit_email_sent=30`, sender `noreply@updates.corporateaisolutions.com`)
→ then assigns the new profile to the inviter's tenant + role, because **the `handle_user_created`
trigger creates `public.profiles` (keyed by `id`) but does NOT set `tenant_id`** (so a raw invite
leaves the user tenant-less = invisible + no data access). Inviting an already-registered email
(e.g. the operator's own `mcmdennis@gmail.com`) is a no-op — returns a clear "already has an account"
message, never an email. **Lesson: Supabase admin-auth methods are server-only (service role); and
the new-user trigger here doesn't tenant-scope — assign tenant explicitly after invite.** (2) **INP
250ms** on the project task timeline: `WorkflowTimeline` re-filtered all 201 tasks + re-rendered every
`TaskRow` on each expand/collapse (no memo, unstable props). Fixed with `useMemo` (categories + stage
grouping), module-scoped pure helpers, and `React.memo(TaskRow)` + boolean `isUpdating` + stable
`useCallback` handlers. The popup itself was only ever visible to the operator (Vercel Toolbar /
DevTools / Web-Vitals extension) — NEVER to end users — but the jank was real.

**Also done 2026-06-23 (all on main + deployed):** Lot 109 lifecycle generated; **crane pinned to 14 Jan 2027** (lead items back to Aug 2026) via the new pinned scheduler. **Scheduling overhaul** (`projectScheduler.ts`): the schedule is a rigid offset body, so it now supports **forward-from-start**, **back-from-delivery**, and **pin-any-task** (fix one task's date, reschedule around it) — editable `ScheduleAnchor` card on the Schedule tab + an inline "reschedule around this date" checkbox in `TaskEditDialog`. ESRD is now editable post-creation (`setProjectSchedule` action; was wizard-only). **Lot 442 reconciled**: live = `c85988dc` (buyer Uwe Jacobs) renamed back to the clean `Lot 442 Half Moon Drive Waggrakine`; empty dup `52050846` renamed + status `Archived` (reversible). **Discover-step fixed**: `competitive-rfq.ts` local-supplier query is now region-scoped (alias) + limit 50 + soft trade-match (no hard trade filter — provider_category vs trade_category vocab mismatch). ⚠️ **This repo has ACTIVE concurrent sessions** — `git pull --rebase` before pushing (rebased several times). Pre-existing `landing-page.test.ts` flake (LLM-evaluator) is not ours.

fslkzhmqcrjsswyrgwnc). Prompted by an Inngest "Agent Evals" article — concluded NOT to adopt
Inngest: the pipeline already implements outcome-based scoring natively (durable wait = the
`pipeline.interview_responses` stub claimed-at-connect; resume = the convai webhook; scorer =
`demand-score.ts`). Don't add a workflow engine to bridge a gap a Supabase row already bridges.

**Key finding:** `scoreDemand`/`proposeDecision` (the §5 Gate-2 GO/REDESIGN/NO-GO judge) was
FULLY wired — but to `public.methodology_responses`, which only the RETIRED `/sync` path writes.
The live in-process return leg (`lib/interview/ingest.ts`) writes `pipeline.interview_responses`.
So every live interview updated per-hypothesis validation but was INVISIBLE to the demand band.

**Shipped (all tests green — 220 pass; both migrations applied to fslkz + recorded):**
1. **Evidence bridge** in `ingest.ts` — on a NEW completion (dedup-gated) also inserts the mapped
   evidence row into `methodology_responses` so the scorer sees in-process interviews. No LLM in the
   webhook (proposeDecision's judge would blow maxDuration=60); scoring stays on-demand (`/propose`).
2. **No-outcome sweep** (`lib/interview/sweep.ts`, folded into `cron/run-discovery-jobs`) — flips
   `pending` interview stubs past a 24h TTL → new terminal status `no_outcome` (migration
   20260618000000). Stabilises the response-rate denominator.
3. **Confidence floor** (agreed reading: a no-show is a CONFIDENCE signal, not demand) — `StreamEvidence`
   gains `attempted`; `assessEvidenceSufficiency` (both streams ≥3 completed AND ≥30% response rate)
   → `scoreDemand` caps a would-be GO to REDESIGN only, never below (`evidenceCap`). Floors are
   exported tunable constants; recalibrate after first real run.
4. **Active mark-stale** (migration 20260618010000 adds `methodology_proposals.stale`) —
   `lib/methodology/proposal-staleness.ts`; ingest (new evidence) + sweep (swept slugs) flag the
   card's latest proposal stale. Per THIN_MVP_RUBRIC §6 knob #7 (mark stale, recompute on demand).

**Open / not done:** the cockpit UI doesn't yet READ `stale` to show a "re-score" badge (data layer
only). Nothing committed to git yet (working tree). Longer-term: repoint `/propose` to read
`pipeline.interview_responses` directly and retire `methodology_responses` + `/sync` (one store).

candidates.title: Canonical Supabase auth-email pattern — token_hash links (NOT ConfirmationURL/PKCE); the F2K reset-bug root cause + fix.
candidates.material:
---
name: reference_auth_email_token_hash_canon
description: Canonical Supabase auth-email pattern — token_hash links (NOT ConfirmationURL/PKCE); the F2K reset-bug root cause + fix.
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: reference
  originSessionId: 938ad867-9124-4102-a6e8-84ea4edb6404
---

The canonical auth-email link for every caistech product is the **self-contained token_hash form**, NOT `{{ .ConfirmationURL }}`:

```
{{ .SiteURL }}/auth/callback?token_hash={{ .TokenHash }}&type=<recovery|magiclink|signup|invite|email_change>&next=<path>
```

**Why (the F2K-Projects bug Uwe hit, 2026-06-14):** under the PKCE flow (`@supabase/ssr` default), `{{ .ConfirmationURL }}` always yields a `?code=` link whose `exchangeCodeForSession` needs the `code_verifier` cookie set in the **same browser+domain** that requested the email. Open it on another device, another browser, or after a short-alias→site_url domain hop → fails with **`invalid request: both auth code and code verifier should be non-empty`**. `token_hash`→`verifyOtp` needs NO verifier → cross-device / cross-domain / SSR-safe. Magic-link only "worked" by luck (same-browser clicks).

**Three things must all be true:**
1. **Email templates** use the token_hash form (set by `cais-shared-services/scripts/configure-email-templates.sh` — fixed 2026-06-14; was emitting ConfirmationURL).
2. **The product's `/auth/callback` route handles `?token_hash=&type=`** (verifyOtp), not just `?code=`. The canonical `cais-build-template-v2/app/auth/callback/route.ts` does. A **PKCE-only callback breaks these links** — retrofit the callback FIRST.
3. **site_url = the SHORT public domain users actually type** (e.g. `f2k-projects.vercel.app`), with that short domain + `/**` in `uri_allow_list`. Trailing slash trimmed so `{{ .SiteURL }}/auth/callback` can't become `//auth/callback`.

**NEVER** hand-roll `{{ .RedirectTo }}&token_hash={{ .TokenHash }}` — if the client redirectTo isn't allowlisted, RedirectTo falls back to bare site_url → malformed `<domain>&token_hash=` (the original executorai bug).

**Git Bash gotcha:** MSYS mangles leading-slash values (`/reset-password` → `C:/Program Files/Git/reset-password`) when passed as argv to python.exe — it silently corrupted all 7 swept templates on 2026-06-14 before being un-mangled (`C:/Program Files/Git/` → `/`). The canonical script now `export MSYS_NO_PATHCONV=1`. When scripting Supabase template PATCHes from Git Bash, set that or build paths as Python literals, never bash argv.

**Retrofit ORDER (hard rule, learned 2026-06-14):** deploy the callback code to PRODUCTION first, THEN flip the template. Flipping first strands users (emails point at a token_hash flow the deployed callback can't handle). For repos on a feature branch, land just the callback file on main via a `git worktree origin/main` (don't merge unrelated WIP). Also: the script defaults `CALLBACK_PATH=/auth/callback`; legacy repos use `/api/auth/callback` — pass `CALLBACK_PATH` or the email links 404.

**SSO-walled-alias gotcha (pipeline + sayfix, 2026-06-14):** the FIRST config-only batch **hardcoded** each repo's then-current `site_url` origin into the email links (it predated the script's `{{ .SiteURL }}` fix). For repos whose canonical domain was the **team-slug alias** `<slug>-corporate-ai-solutions.vercel.app`, that alias is **SSO-protected (401 wall)** — so the links worked structurally but dumped users on a login wall. The real public domain is the short/random-suffix alias (pipeline → `pipeline-nine-silk.vercel.app`, sayfix → `sayfix.vercel.app`; find it via the Vercel deployment's `alias[]`). Fix: set `site_url` to the public alias + allowlist it, then **re-run the canonical script** so links use `{{ .SiteURL }}` (dynamic, never hardcoded). Rule going forward: always run the *fixed* script (uses `{{ .SiteURL }}`); never hardcode a domain. Audited the other early repos — F2K-Projects/deal-findrs/executorai/F2K-Checkpoint/LingoPureAI/singify all hardcoded their *public* domain (work fine) but are still on hardcoded links; re-run the script if any site_url ever changes.

**DONE — on canonical token_hash flow (14 caistech products):**
- Config-only (callback already token_hash-capable): F2K-Projects, deal-findrs, executorai, F2K-Checkpoint, LingoPureAI, pipeline, SayFix, singify-platform.
- 🔴 callback-retrofit + deploy + flip: LaunchReady (pilot), OutreachReady, F2K-OffshoreModular (OMQ), preflight, community-question-responder, universal-interviews.

**REMAINING 🔴 (need a careful/supervised pass — multi-callback consolidation or regulated):** Connexions (2 callbacks + owner-allowlist), Corporate-AI-Solutions cockpit (2 callbacks, magic-link, shared ref tfgtfhwvrswjvkyeyvsp), PrelabzAI (4 callbacks), R-and-D-Tax (REGULATED + server-action exception), NDISSDAAutomate (REGULATED, monorepo 2 apps). **⚪ maybe-no-password-auth:** Kira, platform-trust, property-services, RehearsalsAI, PartReady, storefront-mcp, easy-claude-code. **❓ refs:** TourLingo+UniversalLingo SHARE ref tqvyqhwrpehcgocxpbph (errored — likely env copy-paste bug, investigate); cais-starter/ConferenceLingo/investor-pilot/raiseready-core keep refs only in Vercel env. **Excluded (still dennissolver org):** AIFTIS-Demo. See [[project_canonical_auth_foundation]].

candidates.title: Drizzle db:push creates tables but never enables RLS — and Supabase grants anon ALL by default — so push-managed tables ship world-readable/writable until RLS i
candidates.material:
---
name: reference_drizzle_push_skips_rls
description: Drizzle db:push creates tables but never enables RLS — and Supabase grants anon ALL by default — so push-managed tables ship world-readable/writable until RLS is added by hand. Audit any repo with no SQL migrations.
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: reference
  originSessionId: 03b02d38-4039-4f7c-8a9e-fd0ca27fd32c
---

**Drizzle `db:push` (and dashboard-created tables) leave Supabase RLS OFF, and Supabase's default `GRANT ALL ON public.* TO anon, authenticated` means RLS is the *only* gate — so a push-managed table is fully exposed to the public anon key (which ships in the client bundle) until RLS is enabled manually.**

**Discovered (2026-06-23, TenderWatch):** `public.users` (PII: email, ABN, director name, home address, phone) and `public.linked_accounts` (`encrypted_credentials` + live portal `session_data`) had `rowsecurity=false` while `anon` held INSERT/SELECT/UPDATE/DELETE/**TRUNCATE**. Anyone with the anon key could read all PII/creds or `truncate users`. Root cause: TenderWatch uses Drizzle push (`packages/db`, one hand SQL migration that only ALTERs columns) — tables were created by push, RLS never written. The whole 7-table schema was off; only `users` had been flipped on by an earlier partial attempt.

**Why it stays invisible:** the app reads/writes via Drizzle over `DATABASE_URL` (postgres role, BYPASSRLS), so the app works perfectly with RLS off — nothing breaks, nothing warns. The hole only shows if you query via the anon/PostgREST path (or get breached). The "every repo meant to be migrated" intent had no enforcement sweep, so gaps persist silently.

**The fix (applied to TenderWatch, `packages/db/drizzle/0002_enable_rls.sql` + `0003`):**
1. A **defensive** RLS migration: `to_regclass()`-guarded `do $$` blocks (live schema drifts from code under push, so guard each table), `enable row level security` + own-row policies `to authenticated using (auth.uid()::text = <id/user_id>)`. **IDs are CUID2 text and `public.users.id` stores the auth UID as text → the `::text` cast is mandatory** (uncast `auth.uid() = id` throws `42883 uuid = text`). No `FORCE`, so the Drizzle/service-role path keeps working; only anon is gated.
2. A **`on_auth_user_created` SECURITY DEFINER trigger** to create the profile row — because enabling RLS breaks any client-side profile insert that runs as `anon` (signup with email-confirm-on). Definer bypasses RLS.
3. Prove it: `curl '<ref>.supabase.co/rest/v1/<table>?select=*' -H "apikey: <ANON_KEY>"` returns `[]` after.

**How to apply portfolio-wide:** any repo using Drizzle-push or with a `supabase/` dir but **no SQL migrations** is suspect — run the live check in each instance:
```sql
select tablename, rowsecurity as rls_on from pg_tables where schemaname='public' order by tablename;
```
PII/credential tables with `rls_on=false` are exposures. **Regulated tier verified code-safe 2026-06-24** — NDIS SDA (`cfgbitbsmwpvrblmyuug`, 23/23), R&D-Tax (`jwtpokyxmnbrkcpdyjaz`, 53/53), F2K-Checkpoint (`curqlivhisgakpajnmdt`, 46/48; the 2 without RLS are public `wind_*` reference tables, fine) — all use hand-written Supabase SQL migrations with explicit RLS, NOT Drizzle-push. Live `pg_tables` confirm still recommended (code≠live; `channels` proved drift). Remaining unchecked = lower-stakes push/no-migration repos (executorai, investorpilot, RaiseReady, SayFix, storefront-mcp), none holding regulated PII. Note Supabase's `DATABASE_URL` migration in code only catches repos that *use* SQL migrations — push-managed repos must be checked live, not from code. The canonical-auth migration (consume `@caistech/corporate-components` AuthForm) is the durable fix that retires the hand-rolled auth this surfaced in — see [[project_canonical_auth_foundation]].

candidates.title: property-services /derive cache behaviour (deploys don't bust it) + the LGA fuzzy-matcher must be state-scoped — two engine gotchas from the 2026-07-05 8-state
candidates.material:
---
name: reference_property_services_engine_gotchas
description: "property-services /derive cache behaviour (deploys don't bust it) + the LGA fuzzy-matcher must be state-scoped — two engine gotchas from the 2026-07-05 8-state verification"
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: reference
  originSessionId: a3f6b62f-4083-4d91-8b7d-80d8f7b688ce
---

Two operational facts about the **property-services** engine (edge functions at ref
`qppddipgixhinprliyxh`), learned live 2026-07-05. Related: [[project_canonical_property_feed_enforcement]].

**1. A code deploy does NOT refresh the `/derive` cache — evict to roll a fix out.**
`/derive` (`supabase/functions/derive/index.ts`) caches every result in the **`property_lookups`**
table, keyed by **`address_normalised`** = `normaliseAddress(address)` (lowercased, punctuation
stripped — e.g. `1 london circuit canberra act 2600`). On a request it does
`.eq("address_normalised", normalised)` and, if a row with a `profile` exists, **returns that stored
profile verbatim** (sets `metadata.cached=true`, fires `increment_lookup_hit`) and runs NO derivation.
Only a cache MISS runs the real logic + upserts (`onConflict: "address_normalised"`).
→ `supabase functions deploy derive` changes the CODE; the cache is DATA. A bug fix is **invisible for
any already-derived address** until its row is evicted or overwritten. Proven this session: after
deploying the LGA fix, `1 London Circuit` STILL returned the old wrong value until I
`DELETE FROM property_lookups WHERE address_normalised ILIKE '%london circuit%'` and re-derived.
**Rules:** to VERIFY an engine fix, test a never-cached address OR delete the test row first; to ROLL A
DATA-CORRECTING FIX to existing users, **sweep the cache** (evict every now-wrong row) or they keep the
old value. Treat the cache as serve-until-evicted (observed stale served with no TTL refresh, despite a
`metadata.expiresAt`). "Green deploy ≠ users see the fix" — the metered cache sits in front of the engine.
Evict/sweep via the Management API (node `fetch`, `~/.supabase-token` sbp_, not curl-execFileSync on Windows).

**2. The LGA fuzzy name-matcher MUST be state-scoped (the ACT→Gold Coast bug).**
`resolveLGACode(name, state)` (`_shared/lga-resolve.ts`) maps a council NAME (Mapbox reverse-geocode
`text`, or a state portal) to an `lga_plans` row by fuzzy matching across all ~547 LGAs nationally, in
tiers: exact → partial substring (either direction) → keyword. BUG: tiers 1-2 ignored the `state` arg
(callers `derive-council.ts:29` + `qld-globe.ts:295` DO pass it; only tier 3 honoured it), so a Canberra
address's Mapbox name substring-matched **"Gold Coast City Council"** (QLD) → `1 London Circuit,
Canberra ACT 2600` returned `lgaName="Gold Coast City Council"`. `.find()` returns the FIRST national
match, so the wrong state wins. FIX (deployed + on main `99d0c7e`): `inState = (l) => !state ||
l.state===state`, gate every fuzzy tier on it → an ACT lookup can only match an ACT LGA; worst case →
null → the boundary-GeoJSON point-in-polygon fallback (authoritative) or raw name — both safer than a
confident wrong-state LGA. **Principle:** any fuzzy/substring resolution against a national dataset, when
the jurisdiction is already known, MUST filter to that jurisdiction first — fuzzy match is a last resort
on an already-narrowed set, never the whole country. Corollary: prefer geographic (point-in-polygon)
resolution over name fuzzy-matching wherever a boundary dataset exists.

**Also confirmed 2026-07-05 (8-state live derive):** the engine returns real zoning + cadastre + overlays
across all 8 states for **normal residential addresses**; CBD/commercial parcels can return null zoning/lot
(hard parcels, not engine gaps). Universal layer (slope via Mapbox-DEM ~30m fallback / QLD LiDAR, wind,
climate, BAL) is genuinely 8/8. So "full suite" = full-coverage/mixed-fidelity for typical addresses, with
deliberate planner-by-design gaps (title/contamination/servicing/native-title), NOT "authoritative
everything everywhere."

session's name.

**Why it bites:** uncommitted changes live in the working tree, **not the branch**. They follow
whoever runs `git checkout`, and they get swept into whatever the *other* session commits next.

**Two real collisions in one day:**
1. This session began Kira work while checked out on `fix/canonical-memory-guard` — the branch
   behind an **open, CI-green PR #28** — and an `npm install` dirtied its `package.json` before
   anyone noticed. Caught and moved; PR #28 was untouched, but only by luck.
2. The reverse: the Kira session's commit `1e78ce6` ("one Mnemo client…") **swallowed this
   session's uncommitted `SHARED_SERVICES.md` and briefing edits**. Nothing was lost, but that
   commit contains work its message doesn't mention, and `git log -S` is the only way to find it.

**How to apply:**
- **Check `git branch --show-current` and `git status` BEFORE editing any repo**, especially one you
  were just directed to. Never start work on a branch behind an open PR.
- **Commit before you stop or switch.** Leaving a dirty tree hands the hazard to the next session.
  This overrides the usual "don't commit unless asked" instinct *when another session shares the
  tree* — say so when you do it.
- **Hand work over in a file, not in the tree.** The pattern that worked: commit to a branch, push
  it, and write a handover doc (`docs/HANDOFF_FROM_BUCKETLYST_SESSION.md`,
  `packages/elevenlabs-convai/BRIEFING_FOR_KIRA_SESSION.md`). Dennis then carries the notes to the
  other session himself — he explicitly asked for this rather than having one session finish the
  other's work.
- One session asked to be **sole editor of `portfolio-manifest.yaml`** because it pushes secrets to
  21 projects. Respect single-editor claims on shared config.

Related: [[project_bucketlyst_next_session]].

candidates.title: BucketLyst moved to the CAS GitHub org + Vercel team; how the @caistech registry token is wired across its three consumers, and the traps hit getting there
candidates.material:
---
name: project_bucketlyst_token_wiring
description: "BucketLyst moved to the CAS GitHub org + Vercel team; how the @caistech registry token is wired across its three consumers, and the traps hit getting there"
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: 77cc4cf0-899e-4a86-b29d-8086fe1c9afa
  modified: 2026-07-26T05:34:10.810Z
---

Settled 2026-07-26. **BucketLyst is now `caistech/bucketLyst` on GitHub and on the CAS Vercel team
(`team_hwN7IFtd2Fo3DCj9C67ZwI1t`), project `prj_IYykh42Wq5QrOKjP8VxgtKiiAAni`.** The old memory that
"no token on this machine can reach it" is DEAD — CAS tokens and the Vercel MCP reach it now.
`dennissolver/bucketLyst` still resolves via GitHub's redirect, so both paths look alive; the
canonical remote is the caistech one.

**The @caistech registry token has THREE consumers and they must all name the same variable:**

| consumer | mechanism | now reads |
|---|---|---|
| local `npm install` | repo-local `.npmrc` (overrides `~/.npmrc` for that registry) | `${NODE_AUTH_TOKEN}` |
| Vercel build | repo `.npmrc` + a project env var — **there is no setup-node on Vercel**, so this is the only mechanism there | `NODE_AUTH_TOKEN` (and `GITHUB_PACKAGES_TOKEN` also set, belt-and-braces) |
| GitHub Actions | `gate.yml`: `setup-node@v4` `registry-url` + `scope`, install env `NODE_AUTH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.CAISTECH_PACKAGES_TOKEN }}` | secret `CAISTECH_PACKAGES_TOKEN` |

Two portfolio mechanisms exist and point OPPOSITE ways — don't quote one without checking the other.
`scripts/set-caistech-token.sh` is the OLD home-rolled sweep and writes **`GITHUB_PACKAGES_TOKEN`**;
`scripts/patch-node-auth-token.mjs` (commit `757eb33`) is a deliberate migration TO the official
setup-node + **`NODE_AUTH_TOKEN`** path, because `${VAR}` expansion inside a repo-local `.npmrc` is
unreliable in CI (npm sends the literal placeholder and GitHub 401s). The patcher **no-ops on
BucketLyst** — its exact-string match misses because this repo pins `cache: npm` and stores CRLF, so
`gate.yml` was patched by hand to the same shape.

**Traps hit, in the order they bit:**
1. **BucketLyst was in no sweep list** (not the repo pass, not the Vercel pass, and no `skip` line
   either) despite being in `portfolio-manifest.yaml` line 282. Whatever list that script reads, the
   manifest is not it.
2. **The repo had ZERO Actions secrets**, so `gate.yml` had been 401ing at install every run, long
   before any rotation. Set `CAISTECH_PACKAGES_TOKEN` and it went green.
3. **A build failed with `Bearer <chat text> ... is not a legal HTTP header value`** — the Vercel env
   var's VALUE was a pasted chunk of conversation, not a token. The variable NAME was never the
   problem. Vercel `sensitive` vars are non-readable, so the API cannot tell you which one is
   corrupt: delete + recreate both is the only safe repair (a PATCH also keeps the old value — the
   documented reason `GITHUB_PACKAGES_TOKEN` sat unrotated portfolio-wide from 2026-06-11).
4. **`pnpm install` in this npm repo** writes `pnpm-lock.yaml`, and `gate.yml` tests for it BEFORE
   `package-lock.json` — committing it silently migrates CI (and likely Vercel) off npm. Now
   gitignored.
5. **`prepare` was `husky install 2>/dev/null || true`** — POSIX-only, so it hard-fails on
   PowerShell and takes the install down. Worse, **husky was never a dependency**, so the tracked
   `.husky/pre-push` hook (typecheck + build) has NEVER run. Script removed; the hook is still in
   the repo and still inert. Wiring it for real = add husky + `"prepare": "husky"`, which is a
   decision about push latency, not a fix.

**Verified 2026-07-26, not inherited:** prod READY on `8069701`; the earlier `04634ec` was proven
live by seeding one throwaway prod gift, hitting `?step=choose&error=1&missing=amount`, confirming
the new message + retained pick, then deleting it (prod back to 11 gifts).

Related: [[project_bucketlyst]], [[project_bucketlyst_next_session]].

candidates.title: Before reporting a finding, check the instrument — on 2026-07-27 five 'findings' were artefacts of how they were measured, including a false cross-tenant LEAK.
candidates.material:
---
name: feedback_verify_your_own_measurement
description: "Before reporting a finding, check the instrument — on 2026-07-27 five 'findings' were artefacts of how they were measured, including a false cross-tenant LEAK."
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: feedback
  originSessionId: 60026155-98c3-42ab-bee3-50214f40f639
  modified: 2026-07-27T13:25:47.467Z
---

**When a check reports something alarming or surprising, verify the MEASUREMENT before reporting
the finding.** In one session (2026-07-27) five separate "findings" turned out to be artefacts:

| Reported | Actually |
|---|---|
| "**LEAK** — owner B can read A's memory" | The not-found response **echoes the query** into its summary; the marker WAS the query, so a substring assertion matched its own echo. Assert on `found`, never substring. |
| "Mova already has the tool routes" | The directories exist and are **EMPTY** — inferred from names, nothing git-tracked. |
| "BucketLyst has 0 agents, needs building" | Read its **LOCAL** Supabase; prod had 2 agents and passed **7/7** untouched. |
| "BucketLyst has 0 tool routes" | It uses a **catch-all `[action]` route**; a directory-name scan cannot see it. |
| "gate.yml is not on origin/main" | **Git Bash mangled the path** — `origin/main:.github/...` became `origin\main;.github\...`. `ls-tree` proved the file was there. |
| "audit exit code 0 on failure" | `$?` **after a pipe** reads `tail`'s status, not the tool's. |
| "Kira's memory-loop gate is FAILING" | The run was a **Dependabot PR**, and GitHub **withholds Actions secrets from `dependabot`-triggered runs** — `MEMORY_LOOP_UID`/`CONVAI_TOOL_SECRET`/Supabase vars were all empty strings. The secrets *are* set; gate is green on every push to `main`. Check the triggering **event** before reading a red as a defect. |
| "the fleet bump sweep succeeded" | It printed `SWEEP-DONE`, exited **0**, and pushed **nothing**. `MSYS_NO_PATHCONV=1` (set to stop Git Bash mangling `git show ref:path`) also disables the POSIX→Windows conversion `git worktree add` needs, so `/c/w/bN` became `C:/c/w/bN`; git reported success and every later step no-oped. **A fix for one Git Bash path trap caused another.** |
| "PR #37 carries the portfolio-gate bump" | Read **LaunchReady's** grouped Dependabot PR body and generalised. #37 was `platform-trust-middleware`. Grouped bump PRs do **not** contain the same packages across repos — read each one. |

**Why:** each of these looked like a real defect and would have caused real damage if acted on —
the first would have reported a critical cross-tenant breach in an estate product; the third would
have "rebuilt" a working production loop.

**How to apply:** when a result is surprising, ask *what would produce this reading if the system
were fine?* Then test that. Concretely: prefer structured fields (`found`) over string matching;
confirm which DB/URL/branch you actually touched; check `${PIPESTATUS[0]}` not `$?` after pipes;
and on Windows use `git ls-tree`/blob hashes rather than `rev:path` syntax in Git Bash.

**The inverse also holds:** a guard that has never failed is indistinguishable from one that cannot.
Prove a new check catches the bug by REINTRODUCING it — done for the middleware audit (removing one
exclusion flipped exit 0 → 1 naming the exact route) and the deletion guard (inserting each blocking
condition in turn). See [[project_voice_memory_fleet_state]].

metadata:
