**State as at 2026-08-06: the site is ready and the copy is written. What is outstanding is
sending it.**

## What the push is

Dennis has capacity for a couple of builds and is asking his network for introductions, pointing at
`/services` — Opportunity Audit $2,500 + GST, Deployment Sprint $18,000 + GST, Run & Extend
$3,500/month + GST.

## The copy — written, in this session, ready to send

Two pieces, both drafted and unsent:

1. **A DM** (first target Lucretia, reusable for anyone).
2. **A LinkedIn post** for reshare. **Daniel Maneveld explicitly asked for one** — *"Do you have a
   post on LinkedIn I can reshare please… I'll do that tomorrow when back in Vietnam"* (2026-08-05).
   He is warm and waiting; this is the highest-value unsent item.

**Why the original message failed, and the principle behind the rewrite.** The first version said
*"I'm on the hunt for a few gigs"* and linked the services page. That asks the reader to do the work —
they do not know who to think of, so they think of nobody. **A referral message must hand them a
sentence they might actually hear someone say.** The rewrite's trigger line:

> *"we looked at automating that, but it was six months and a fortune."*

Other principles applied: "capacity for a couple of builds" rather than "hunting for gigs" (same
fact, different footing); prices **in the message** so the referrer can gauge fit without clicking;
one ask per message; and the LinkedIn post opens on the reader's problem, not on availability,
because **nobody reshares a plea**. The post's *"What I don't do"* section buys more credibility than
any claim in it.

⚠️ **Kira goes in a SEPARATE message.** Two links and two audiences halve the clarity of both — Kira
is a product for exiting business owners, not a services referral.

## The site was NOT ready, and now is

A `/naive-tester` run on 2026-08-05 returned **DO NOT SEND YET** with two blockers. Both fixed,
deployed and verified on production (`1db47e3`):

- **The contact form could never receive a lead** — see [[project_lead_capture_was_broken_twice]].
- **Morgan quoted a contradictory price list on `/services`** — "sixty-five thousand a month" and
  "fifteen thousand a month", four inches below "$18,000 + GST, fixed price", never mentioning the
  audit or the sprint, and offering "technical advisory retainers" on a page whose own disqualifier
  says retainers are not offered. Left behind when `/pricing` was retired. All four strings rewritten;
  zero occurrences remain.

Also fixed in the same pass: `/privacy` and `/terms` created (both previously 404 while the form
collected personal information and `/services` claimed *"privacy surfaces. Built in, not bolted on"*);
the shared footer now names the legal entity and ABN on every page; `/contact` server-renders instead
of shipping 27 characters; WCAG contrast on the payment terms; 44px tap targets; one call duration
everywhere (15 minutes, matching the Calendly event); and a **worked example of a sprint against a
quoting process** — the buyer persona's one unanswered question was *"what would you actually build
for a firm like mine?"*

Report + 10 screenshots: `naive-tester-reports/2026-08-05-pre-outreach/`.

## ⚠️ Outstanding

1. **Send the LinkedIn post to Daniel.** He asked for it and is waiting.
2. **An email to Brian Budd** — requested 2026-08-05, not yet written. Context file:
   `C:\Users\denni\Downloads\bbna listed members on website.txt` (BBNA member list). Apply the same
   principle: give the reader a trigger sentence, not a request to "share it around".
3. **Confirm `RESEND_API_KEY` is set in Vercel production** — without it, leads save silently and no
   notification arrives.
4. **Push `/services`, never the bare domain.** The homepage opens *"BYOK Factory · 50 live AI
   products · open source you can clone"*, written for developers. The buyer does not clone things.

## Who the copy is aimed at

Established Australian business, decision-maker who can commit without a committee, with a process
eating ~2 days a week — quoting, compliance paperwork, intake, reporting. The persona used for the
audit: a 54-year-old QLD civil contractor, 40 staff, whose estimator loses two days a week to
quoting, previously quoted $180k and six months by an agency and walked. **He is not anti-technology,
he is anti-being-sold-to**, and he reads looking for reasons to disbelieve you.

**Numbers to reconcile before anyone audits them:** 53 / 50 / 44 / 38 / 29 appear across pages as
different counts of different things. Individually true; to a sceptic they read as decorative. Pick
one, define it in the same breath, use it everywhere.

candidates.title: Why validation-run records nothing / cards go stale — producers don't prepend https:// to the URL
candidates.material:
---
name: project_validation_producer_scheme_bug
description: "Why validation-run records nothing / cards go stale — producers don't prepend https:// to the URL"
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: 0313a6c4-3cce-47eb-b83e-7046405ddc04
---

Confirmed 2026-06-10: the `validation-run` browser producers in `cais-shared-services/scripts/agents/` (naive-tester.mjs:19, voice-auditor.mjs:23, promise-judge.mjs:20, admin-tester.mjs:21) all read the URL verbatim (`const origin = arg('url').replace(/\/$/, '')`) with **no scheme prepend**. The cockpit stores `mvp_url` without `https://` (e.g. `deal-findrs.vercel.app`), so `lib.mjs goto()` → `page.goto("deal-findrs.vercel.app")` is an invalid URL → throws → `"could not load any page — recording nothing"` (exit 1). The run still shows ✅ green because producers are `continue-on-error`, so a total no-op masquerades as success — the card stays stale (deal-findrs frozen at 06-07 while the 09:22 run recorded 0 rows).

NOT a Vercel protection wall: `curl -L https://deal-findrs.vercel.app` + `/admin` both return HTTP 200, no SSO. Fix = prepend `https://` in `lib.mjs goto()` (one place fixes all producers) + optionally store mvp_url with scheme. Also: make the orchestrator fail/alarm on "recorded 0 rows" so silent no-ops can't read green.

**Why:** this is the load-bearing reliability bug behind "the pipeline ran but the card didn't update." **How to apply:** if a card looks stale after a validation-run, check this before re-diagnosing. Full punch-list (incl. deal-findrs Gate-1 blockers: QA accounts VT_D2/D3, magic-link admin-tester VT_A1–A4 na, #35 email sender) → `corporate-ai-solutions/docs/DEALFINDRS_GATE1_PUNCHLIST.md`. Pipeline extraction plan → `docs/PIPELINE_SEPARATION_PLAN.md`. Related: [[project_validation_orchestrator]].

candidates.title: ExecutorAI voice decision (2026-07-26): Morgan stays stateless now; revisit at Gate 2 with product-own Supabase, not Mnemo
candidates.material:
---
name: project_voice_memory_position
description: "ExecutorAI voice decision (2026-07-26): Morgan stays stateless now; revisit at Gate 2 with product-own Supabase, not Mnemo"
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: 51005e92-dd6b-4f27-bf04-a819235b2405
  modified: 2026-07-26T07:44:02.954Z
---

**Decision (owner, 2026-07-26): option A now, option C at Gate 2.** Morgan — the `@caistech/
elevenlabs-convai` `VoiceWidget` mounted per page — stays **stateless by design**. No
`convai_memory`/`convai_agents` tables, no webhook route, no per-user agent, one shared public
`NEXT_PUBLIC_ELEVENLABS_AGENT_ID`. Recorded in `portfolio-manifest.yaml`
(`voice_agent_status: present`, memory position in the note) and `docs/SUBSTRATE_BOUNDARY.md` §5.2
so a `/voice-auditor` run reads a **decision, not silence**.

**Why (the reasoning is the durable part).** Continuity of *task* is already deterministic —
`/api/assistant` injects `computeGaps()` into Morgan's prompt every turn, so she always knows what
the owner still has to do. Memory would add continuity of *conversation* only. Morgan is not
amnesiac about the estate; she is amnesiac about the dialogue. Against that: persisting distilled
conclusions about a person's estate, family and death **adds a processor to a data flow already
described to Iress** (`docs/iress-dd/architecture-and-data-flow.md` states exactly ONE cross-border
path — the consent-gated will document), and `REGULATORY_INCLUSIONS` I1 §4 would require naming any
new subprocessor + overseas transfer. Changing that shape while a DD submission is live with the
counterparty is the expensive part; the code is not.

**Gate 2 = option C, deliberately NOT the full loop:** distilled conclusions in **ExecutorAI's own
Supabase**, pull-only at connect — no Mnemo, no new subprocessor, no new cross-border flow. The
executor side is where it pays (a grieving once-in-a-lifetime user re-entering probate weeks later).

**How to apply.** Standing condition while stateless: **no product copy may imply Morgan remembers
a returning user.** If the loop is ever wired, **fail closed at our own route** — convai 0.9.0's
post-call webhook is STILL fail-open (`dist/routes.js:169` guards verification with
`if (postCallSecret)`, so an unset secret skips the check), and `handlePostCallWebhook` binds by ids
taken from the request body. Also then required: RLS + cascade + TTL, `ensureUserAgent`
(one-agent-per-user is mandatory — ElevenLabs never passes `conversation_id` to tool webhooks, so
the owner must be fixed at provision time), a "what Morgan remembers" surface, `probeMemoryLoop` in
CI.

**AUDIT RESULT (2026-07-26, `/voice-auditor` repo scan + live pass).** Morgan is mounted on all 7
guidance surfaces and renders/opens/degrades correctly — but was **NOT FUNCTIONAL**, and
`voice_agent_status: present` had been declared from a **code scan**, which is precisely what
`PRODUCT_STANDARDS` §6's *behavioural* gate exists to prevent. **Lesson: never declare a behavioural
status from static evidence.** Two blocking defects, both fixed: (1) `Morgan.tsx` passed
`textFallback`/`textInput` but never `onTextFallbackSubmit`, so the text box **silently discarded
every question** — the only text path on six of the seven surfaces, and the same class as the
silent-drop honeypot rule; (2) `/api/assistant` 401s on an invalid key (see
[[project_unmanaged_credential_rot]]). Also fixed: `.convai-panel` forces a floating-variant 375px
width into the inline variant, clipping the header on mobile — **local guard only, upstream fix
belongs in `@caistech/elevenlabs-convai`**.

**Still owed:** a **mic'd human pass** — headless Chromium has no mic, so every live observation used
the text fallback and **WebRTC connect remains unverified**. And an open product decision:
`/vault/recover` renders Morgan only inside the active-vault branch, so an executor with **no sealed
vault** gets one line of text at arguably the moment they are most lost. Full map:
`voice-audit/2026-07-26-0645/executorai.md`.

Related: [[project_iress_xplan_dd]] (the DD data-flow statement this protects),
[[project_unmanaged_credential_rot]], [[project_executorai_vision]].

candidates.title: How RFQ provider discovery + email ingestion works after the 2026-07-11 rebuild (DataForSEO, Hunter/Apollo, panel persistence) and its known gaps.
candidates.material:
---
name: project-procurement-discovery-stack
description: "How RFQ provider discovery + email ingestion works after the 2026-07-11 rebuild (DataForSEO, Hunter/Apollo, panel persistence) and its known gaps."
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: e28f8b9f-8055-40f2-977a-ab4d1e872e3e
---

The competitive_rfq provider-discovery pipeline was overhauled 2026-07-11 (PR #38 + follow-ups, all merged to main). The chain now is: **web search → trade-aware match → ingest with email → persist to panel → flag/alert when no email.**

- **Web search = DataForSEO** (`src/lib/services/dataforseo.ts`), which **replaced Serper** — the Serper account ran out of credits (`"Not enough credits"` 400s), which had silently killed all web discovery. DataForSEO uses `serp/google/organic/live/advanced` + `serp/google/maps/live/advanced` (Basic auth). Its `live/advanced` calls sometimes **abort under load** even at a 30s timeout — that's why niche cold trades (building certifier, energy assessor) can still come back empty.
- **Email resolution** (`src/lib/services/emailResolver.ts`) cascade, highest-quality first: `@caistech/email-finder` **Hunter→Apollo** (verified name+email by domain) → DataForSEO search-snippet → bounded homepage scrape. All fail soft. Guarded against **directory/aggregator domains** (MapQuest/Yellow Pages/Facebook) so it never resolves e.g. `cjohnson@mapquest.com`.
- **Ingest-anyway + alert:** providers with no resolvable email are kept + flagged (`needs_email`), the approval gate is forced (never auto-skipped) when any email is missing, notification reports the count, UI shows an "Email needed" badge.
- **Local-supplier fallback is trade-scoped** (`competitive-rfq.ts`): a local supplier only appears for its own trade (hard filter on `provider_category`), and suppliers tagged with cost-category labels (`materials`/`professional_fees`/`subcontractor`) or no trade are excluded. Cold trades rely on web discovery.
- **Panel now persists:** added `UNIQUE(tenant_id, name)` on `suppliers` (migration `20260711000000`), so the handler's `upsert(onConflict:"tenant_id,name")` — which had been silently no-op'ing — now works and the panel compounds across projects.

**Why:** this is the "agents search the web → ingest provider + email → alert if none" system F2K wanted for executing pre-contract services (see [[project-lot109-precontract-execution]]).

**SUBURB-PARSE BUG fixed 2026-07-13 (commit 5d25de7f) — the big one for result quality.** Discovery had parsed the suburb as `siteAddress.split(",")[0].replace(/^\d+\s+\w+\s+/,"")` → for "31 Half Moon Drive, Waggrakine WA 6530" that returns **"Moon Drive"** (the STREET), so every query became "plumber near Moon Drive WA" → Perth/overseas/aggregator junk (a Lot 442 plumber run returned an Indonesian pump company + Perth suburbs). Fix = new exported **`parseSuburb()`** (locality before STATE+postcode; handles "WA" AND "Western Australia") used in `stepDiscoverProviders` + `procurement-auto`, plus **`looksLikeAggregator()`** dropping directory/listicle titles ("21 Best…", "Top 35…", "Find a Master Plumber", "…Free Quotes", hipages/oneflare). After fix, Waggrakine plumber search returns real locals (Seabrook, BWH-Waggrakine, 6530 Plumbing&Gas, Brockman-Waggrakine, Sun City, Bubbles). Discovery is triggered from the UI via the **"Find Providers" button in RfqApprovalPanel** (rendered in WorkflowTimeline task cards + Cockpit) → `triggerProviderDiscovery(taskId)` (taskStatus.ts). Remaining: wrong-TRADE names (removals/excavator) still leak (trade-relevance, not name-based); Herricks not surfaced (coverage gap — add known locals manually).

**Fragmentation fixed 2026-07-13 (commit f7b39cb8, migrations `20260713190000`/`190100`) — "one RFQ per trade".** The lifecycle templates flagged EVERY procurement sub-step (`is_rfq=true`): "…identified", "…RFQs sent", "…quotes received", "…uploaded", "…contract signed" — so one trade span ~5 competitive_rfq pipelines each running discovery (~74 panels/project, burning DataForSEO credits ×5). Fix: keep `is_rfq` on ONE `task_templates` row per **`provider_category`** (18 trades; prefer the "…identified" title, else "…RFQs sent", else min sort_order), demote the other 66 to milestones; a second migration mirrors that onto existing `task_instances`. ⚠️ Group by **`provider_category`, NOT `gate_group`** — gate_group is coarse ("Site Provisioning" bundles portaloo+skip-bin+fencing; "Civil Site Works" bundles 4 trades). Lot 442/109 now show 16 RFQ tasks. **Re-run discovery UI:** the "Find Providers" button only shows at zero providers; a **"Re-run search"** button (commit 5bfba6d9, `rediscoverProviders`) refreshes a task that already ran. **Cockpit "Approve & Prepare RFQs"** now drives the pipeline forward immediately (commit 58d126a6) so approved providers land as scope/portal drafts in the Outbox (was: deferred to cron + old inline template). **Two open bugs:** (1) email resolver assigns an ASSOCIATION/aggregator email (e.g. `margareta@mpawa.asn.au` = Master Plumbers WA, `marketing@midwestkey.com.au`) to multiple different businesses — mpawa.asn.au/midwestkey not in the resolver's aggregator-domain guard. (2) DUPLICATE projects exist (Lot 442: active `c85988dc` + archived `52050846`) — scripts must filter `status='Active'` / exclude "(DUPLICATE" in name.

**Supplier panel management + curated-panel-first (2026-07-13, commits f0ea10ad/0b296a57).** DataForSEO went to **$0 balance** (negative) → every search 402s → discovery returns nothing (check `GET api.dataforseo.com/v3/appendix/user_data` for balance). The durable fix is the **curated `suppliers` panel**, which the local-supplier fallback in `stepDiscoverProviders` uses **without any API** — so panel entries surface even at $0. candidates.title: Why @caistech installs 401 and how CI/pnpm/Vercel auth actually works in this repo — the gotchas that cost a whole session.
candidates.material:
---
name: reference-caistech-registry-auth-and-ci
description: Why @caistech installs 401 and how CI/pnpm/Vercel auth actually works in this repo — the gotchas that cost a whole session.
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: reference
  originSessionId: 880c3896-bc20-4931-ba73-433e0db2b36b
---

The `@caistech/*` GitHub Packages auth is fragile across local / CI / Vercel. Hard-won facts (2026-06-18):

**The token lives in FIVE places — rotate all of them:**
1. `C:\Users\denni\.npmrc` — user-level, literal token (local installs).
2. `NODE_AUTH_TOKEN` — Windows user env var via `setx` (local installs). NOT in any `.env.local`.
3. `GITHUB_PACKAGES_TOKEN` — Windows user env var; **redundant** (npm reads NODE_AUTH_TOKEN). Can delete.
4. `CAISTECH_PACKAGES_TOKEN` — **repo-level** GitHub Actions secret (CI), per-repo, set via `gh secret set`.
5. Vercel project `NODE_AUTH_TOKEN` — env var on `f2k-checkpoint-new` (build-time).

**The shadowing trap (cost hours):** committed project `.npmrc` has `_authToken=${NODE_AUTH_TOKEN}`. When `NODE_AUTH_TOKEN` is unset in the env, it expands to an EMPTY string that **overrides the valid user-level `~/.npmrc` token** (project .npmrc wins) → 401 inside the repo even when `npm view` works from the home dir. Fix: `setx NODE_AUTH_TOKEN <token>` + reopen terminal. Verify with `npm view @caistech/email-compliance version` (want a version, not 401).

**pnpm 10 specifics (CI uses pnpm, not npm):**
- pnpm REFUSES to expand `${NODE_AUTH_TOKEN}` from a committed project `.npmrc` (could leak). Workflows must use `actions/setup-node` with `registry-url: https://npm.pkg.github.com` + `scope: '@caistech'` so it writes auth to the trusted user-level `~/.npmrc` that pnpm WILL expand — the env var alone isn't enough.
- pnpm 10 no longer reads the `pnpm` field in `package.json`; build-script approval (`onlyBuiltDependencies`) must live in `pnpm-workspace.yaml` (which also needs a `packages: ['.']` field once it exists).
- `corepack enable` overrides `pnpm/action-setup`'s pinned version with a newer/stricter pnpm — drop it; pin `action-setup@v4 version: 10`.

**Dual lockfiles:** repo has BOTH `package-lock.json` AND `pnpm-lock.yaml`. CI uses pnpm. A local `npm install` diverges from CI — e.g. the "js-tiktoken missing" build error only reproduces under local npm; CI's pnpm-lock has it. Always check the ACTUAL CI logs, not a local build, before diagnosing.

**portfolio-gate (`gate.yml`) quirks:** its Build step needs the same placeholder env as `ci.yml` (`OPENAI_API_KEY` etc.) or it fails "Missing credentials" collecting page data. Its route/auth smoke tests run against a FIXED preview URL (`PORTFOLIO_GATE_PREVIEW_URL`), NOT the PR's deploy — and the migrator seeds generic `routes.config.json`/`auth.config.json` (`/about`,`/privacy`,`/api/auth/login`…) that this app doesn't implement; trim to real routes (auth smoke is lenient: missing action paths 404 < 500 = pass).

**Vercel token EXPIRES → all deploys silently error (2026-07-13):** the Vercel `NODE_AUTH_TOKEN` on `f2k-checkpoint-new` (team `team_hwN7IFtd2Fo3DCj9C67ZwI1t` = corporate-ai-solutions) held an expired classic PAT (`ghp_…`) → every `pnpm install` 401'd on `@caistech/property-services-sdk` → 3 pushes in a row showed `● Error` in `vercel ls` while the code was fine. Rotated it to the local **`gho_` OAuth token** (`echo $NODE_AUTH_TOKEN`, verified with `curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOK" <pkg-download-url>` → want 302 not 401). ⚠️ `gho_` is a personal OAuth token — **breaks if `gh auth login` re-runs**; replace with a durable fine-grained PAT (`read:packages`) when convenient. CLI ops (the `~/.vercel-token` works but needs `--scope=team_hwN7IFtd2Fo3DCj9C67ZwI1t`): `vercel env rm NODE_AUTH_TOKEN production --yes`, `printf '%s' "$TOK" | vercel env add NODE_AUTH_TOKEN production --sensitive`, then `vercel redeploy <last-url>` to rebuild the same commit with the new env (a git push does NOT auto-rebuild on env change). Diagnose deploy health with `vercel ls f2k-checkpoint-new --scope=…` — don't assume a green `git push` deployed.

See [[project-open-followups-2026-06-18]] for the dual-lockfile cleanup + SDK-republish follow-ups.

Admins can take any estate page on/off from **/admin → "Estate Pages"** (sidebar link near the top,
under Dashboard; distinct from the lower "Estates" content/blog switcher) → `/admin/estates`.

**Deactivating also STOPS ALL COMMS + NOTIFIES STAKEHOLDERS — LIVE in prod since 2026-07-26
(commits `78eb212` + `d734276`, migration 0073, first real run announced 3 estates):**
- `archived` is now a hard gate on every outbound estate path via `src/lib/estates/comms.ts`
  (`isEstateCommsPaused` / `estateArchivedPublicGuard` 410 / `estateArchivedSendGuard` 409): the
  roi-nudge cron, both daily digests, live blog-post sends, and all 7 register/qualification
  endpoints. Reactivating restores every one of them, no deploy.
- On toggle, agents (`agents.estate_access` ∋ slug, active) + admins + `<estate>_notify_recipients`
  are emailed. **Registrants are NEVER emailed by the system** — each agent instead gets THEIR OWN
  registrant list and is asked to contact them outside the system; unassigned registrants (no
  introducing agent) are reported to admins to own. Agent emails carry a signed one-click
  "I've told my clients" link (GET renders a confirm page, POST writes — link scanners prefetch).
- **Sends are paced 150ms apart** — Resend caps at 10 req/sec and the serial loop tripped it on the
  very first 11-recipient run, silently losing one announcement. Any bulk serial send in this repo
  needs the same pacing; see [[f2k-build-ops-learnings]].
- Receipts in `estate_status_notifications`; `estate_status.status_notified_at/_count` show on the
  admin row (amber "hasn't been announced" when null). **"Announce status" / "Re-send notice"**
  button (`POST /api/admin/estates/status/notify`) announces the CURRENT status without toggling —
  built for estates archived before this existed. Impact preview (`.../status/impact`) shows agent +
  buyer counts BEFORE the click.

- **Deactivate = archive** (never delete). An archived estate disappears from every public surface —
  nav mega-menu, the Australia landing map (pin + state count), landing cards, and the per-state
  `/estates/<state>` page — exactly like the code-level `parked` flag; and its own URL renders a
  branded "page archived" notice (NOT a 404). Reactivate restores it everywhere. No deploy needed.
- **Backed by** the `estate_status` table (migration 0072, slug/archived/archived_at/by/reason),
  read via `src/lib/estates/status.ts` (`getArchivedSlugs`/`isEstateArchived`, tag-cached with
  `revalidateTag("estate-status")` on toggle, fully fail-soft). API: `/api/admin/estates/status`
  (GET list + POST toggle), gated by the `manage_estate_status` permission (super_admin / fund_manager).
- **Deactivation requires a reason (≥10 chars)** — same amber gate as [[admin-settings-page-reference-impl]]'s
  material-change pattern (AdminLotEditModal); enforced client + server (400). Activation needs none.
- Code-`parked` estates (Wavecrest) show a grey **"Parked (unlisted)"** pill, not "Live" — `parked`
  (code, needs a deploy) and `archived` (DB toggle) are independent; public-hidden = parked OR archived.

**⚠️ Operational caveat — the `estate_status` table is the SAME Supabase across prod/preview/demo**
(Sydney `zzajvnhsesqrrepflrrx`; demo `cjlcywifsrwcecajammi` got 0072 too). So toggling an estate from
ANY environment changes what the LIVE public site shows. Deactivating a live revenue estate
(Seafields/Branscombe) hides a real page — treat it as an outward-facing action. See [[demo-repo-mirror-rule]].

candidates.title: f2k infra how-tos — Supabase service-key fetch, migration-apply path, eslint no-explicit-any, audit_log uuid silent-fail, Resend 10/sec cap, and the real prod d
candidates.material:
---
name: f2k-build-ops-learnings
description: "f2k infra how-tos — Supabase service-key fetch, migration-apply path, eslint no-explicit-any, audit_log uuid silent-fail, Resend 10/sec cap, and the real prod domain"
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: 04a24498-50aa-43d0-89ef-9f9a2430dc8d
  modified: 2026-07-31T05:00:15.721Z
---

Reusable build-ops facts confirmed 2026-07-01/02 while building the pipeline + funder dataroom.

**Apply migrations / run SQL against live + demo:** `jq` is NOT on this box, and local `.env.local` `POSTGRES_URL` still points at the decommissioned **Seoul** DB — so DON'T use the supabase-query/push scripts blindly. Use the **Management API** with the on-disk token: `node` + `fetch` POST to `https://api.supabase.com/v1/projects/<ref>/database/query` with `Authorization: Bearer $(cat ~/.supabase-token)`, body `{query}`. Refs: live Sydney `zzajvnhsesqrrepflrrx`, demo Tokyo `cjlcywifsrwcecajammi`.

Two things that make this cheaper than it reads (confirmed 2026-07-31 applying 0074):
- **`scripts/apply-migration-live.mjs <file>` now wraps the live half** — pins the ref in code (no CLI-link drift), applies the SQL, and records the version in `supabase_migrations.schema_migrations`. Use it instead of hand-rolling the fetch each time.
- **The DEMO half is already automatic.** `.github/workflows/demo-db-sync.yml` applies migrations ADDED in a push to main against the demo project. Verify with `gh run list --workflow=demo-db-sync.yml` rather than hand-applying — the older "apply to BOTH by hand" instruction is superseded for anything that lands on main.

Also note **`.env.local` is permission-blocked to this agent** (Read and grep both denied), so any recipe that starts "read the key out of .env.local" is a dead end — go to the Management API.

**Mint a REAL admin session to test authenticated routes against prod** (this is how the design-editor loop was verified end-to-end rather than assumed). The canonical minter is `cais-shared-services/scripts/qa-session.mjs`, but it reads Supabase config from `<root>/.env.local` — blocked here — so **inject it instead**: pull `anon` from `GET /v1/projects/<ref>/api-keys?reveal=true`, set `NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL` + `NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY` + `QA_TEST_EMAIL`/`QA_TEST_PASSWORD` (from `cais-shared-services/.secrets/qa-secrets.json`, keys `QA_TEST_ADMIN_*`) in the child env, then `spawnSync` it with `--root <repo> --origin https://f2k-projects.vercel.app`. Parse the `sb-<ref>-auth-token…` cookie lines out of stdout and send them as a `cookie` header. `dennis+qaadmin@factory2key.com.au` is `super_admin` in `admin_users`, so it reaches every admin route.

**Vercel `x-vercel-cache` is the fastest way to tell "did the page re-render?" from "is the data stale?"** — `HIT` = served from cache, `REVALIDATED` = it genuinely re-rendered. If you see REVALIDATED and the content still hasn't changed, the caching is NOT your bug; look at the render path (in the 2026-07-31 case, an archived estate returning early — see [[estate-home-designs-editor]]).

**Get the Supabase service_role key for seeding/scripts (no need to ask Dennis):** `GET https://api.supabase.com/v1/projects/<ref>/api-keys?reveal=true` (Bearer `~/.supabase-token`) returns anon + service_role. With the service key you can hit the project's auth admin (`POST {ref}.supabase.co/auth/v1/admin/users` to create/confirm users), Storage (`/storage/v1/object/<bucket>/<path>`), and PostgREST (`/rest/v1/...`). pgvector inserts via PostgREST: pass the embedding as a **stringified literal** `"[0.1,0.2,...]"` (Postgres casts text→vector). Node processes hang after fetch — end scripts with `process.exit(0)`.

**ESLint build gotcha:** this repo's ESLint config does NOT register `@typescript-eslint/no-explicit-any`. A `// eslint-disable-next-line @typescript-eslint/no-explicit-any` comment therefore **FAILS `next build`** with "Definition for rule ... was not found". Plain `any` is allowed (no rule flags it) — so just use `any` / `Record<string, any>` and never add a disable comment for that rule. `react-hooks/exhaustive-deps` IS registered (warns, doesn't fail).

**`audit_log.entity_id` is a UUID column — passing a text key (e.g. an estate slug) fails the insert
SILENTLY.** `auditLog()` in `src/lib/admin-auth.ts` only `console.error`s on failure, so the caller
sees success and no row is written. This is why NO `estate_archived`/`estate_activated` row has ever
existed despite the confirm dialog promising "the audit log records it" (found 2026-07-26, since
0072). Pass `entity_id: null` and put the text key in `details`. Check any new `auditLog` call whose
entity is keyed by slug/name rather than a UUID.

**Resend rate-limits at 10 requests/second — pace any serial send loop.** A fan-out with no network
wait between calls (admin notifications, bulk agent email, digests to N recipients) trips it around
the 10th recipient and the send is LOST, not retried. 150ms between sends (~6.7/sec) is the pattern
used in `src/lib/estates/archive-notify.ts`. Cost one dropped announcement on its first live run.

**Domain reality:** `factory2key.com.au` (apex AND www) is the **WordPress** corporate site, NOT this
app — even `/seafields-estate` 404s there. The Vercel project has **no custom domain**; production
is only `f2k-projects.vercel.app` (+ the two `*-corporate-ai-solutions.vercel.app` aliases). The
`https://www.factory2key.com.au` string in the deployed HTML is a hardcoded marketing link in
`ProjectsHeader.tsx`/`ProjectsFooter.tsx`, not `NEXT_PUBLIC_CANONICAL_URL` (which is `sensitive` in
Vercel and cannot be read back — infer it, don't try to fetch it).

**Verify prod/demo deploys:** `~/.vercel-token` + `GET https://api.vercel.com/v6/deployments?app=f2k-projects&limit=N`. `next build` after adding deps can take 7+ min (not a hang) — log to a file and tail. See also [[supabase-cli-link-drift-footgun]] + [[f2k-resend-email-infra-resolved]].

**Lead-loss bug, fixed 2026-06-29 (PR #44).** Every public f2k registration form STILL had the
FORBIDDEN client-side fake-success bot-trap:
`const elapsedMs = Date.now()-formLoadedAt.current; if (honeypot || elapsedMs < 2500) { setSuccess(true); return; }`
— it showed "Registration Received" WITHOUT calling the API, so any submit < 2.5s (fast/autofilled
buyers) or with an autofilled honeypot was **silently dropped: no DB row, no email.** The 2026-06-15
"sweep" only renamed the field to `hp_field` + added the time-trap; it KEPT the client-side
fake-success (see [[email-spam-act-compliance]] / PRODUCT_STANDARDS anti-bot codicil).

**Diagnosed** when Dennis live-tested Seafields: form showed success but no row hit the live Sydney DB,
while a direct API POST landed fine → proved the form-level trap was eating submissions.

**Fix (5 forms: seafields, branscombe, wavecrest, dutton, developers):** removed the client
fake-success; client now sends `hp_field` + `elapsed_ms` (JSON body; **FormData** for the developers
onboarding form); each API route accepts them (honeypot = any value, never a 400) and applies the trap
**server-side** — returns the route's normal success shape WITHOUT writing when hp filled or
elapsed<2500. A real submission now always reaches the server; a bot gets no signal. The ROI forms
(`/api/roi/waitlist`, `/api/roi/qualification` + WaitlistForm/QualificationForm) were already correct
(built server-side from the start).

**Verified live:** human submit (elapsed 9999) saves; bot submit (elapsed 900) returns 200 but does
NOT save. ⚠️ Past fast/honeypot-tripped real leads were never recorded (unrecoverable) — fix prevents
future loss only. **To test a form: fill it over ~3s with a REAL email** (`dennis@factory2key.com.au`
is the QA account → email rerouted to `dennis@corporateaisolutions.com`; `mcmdennis@gmail.com` for a
true delivery test).

**SECOND fix same day — honeypot was ALSO a false-positive (PR #45, 2026-06-29).** Even after the
server-side move, Dennis's real 54-second Seafields submit was still dropped. Vercel runtime logs
(`get_runtime_logs` MCP, projectId `prj_cFIXyKayp0eHLQIgg1zYbTQV85RU`, team `team_hwN7IFtd2Fo3DCj9C67ZwI1t`)
showed the smoking gun: `seafields register bot trap: { hp: true, elapsed: 54482 }` — his browser's
**password manager autofilled the hidden `hp_field`** (and the legacy autofill-prone `website_url` on
the developers form). Fix: the honeypot is now **NON-BLOCKING + logged** across all 5 routes; the
**time-trap (elapsed < 2500ms) is the ONLY hard block** (it's the false-positive-free primary signal).
Verified live: honeypot-filled + 54s slow → SAVES; empty + 900ms → blocked. **Lesson: never let a
honeypot HARD-block — password managers fill hidden fields; time-trap is the reliable gate. Runtime
logs are the definitive diagnostic for "form shows success but no row" (tells trap-blocked vs
never-reached-server).** Also: the cutover was a RED HERRING — post-Sydney-cutover writes land fine
(proven repeatedly); the "last reg 27 Jun" gap was the bot-traps + low traffic, not the migration.

**Unrelated note surfaced same session:** Seafields live page header now says "Developer: Dual Focus"
(Dual Focus = the LANDOWNER, intentionally changed from Factory2Key) while the details table still
reads "Developer: Factory2Key Pty Ltd" — a content inconsistency (landowner-vs-developer wording), NOT
related to the bug; Dennis to decide the wording.

candidates.title: F2K admin login has TWO gates: Supabase auth (password) + public.admin_users allowlist. A password-fine user with no admin_users row bounces silently — looks li
candidates.material:
---
name: seafields-admin-allowlist-gate
description: "F2K admin login has TWO gates: Supabase auth (password) + public.admin_users allowlist. A password-fine user with no admin_users row bounces silently — looks like a login failure but isn't."
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: a07ad1df-6d89-4637-af4f-69532881fbc2
---

The F2K Projects admin login has two independent gates. Diagnose them in order.

1. **Supabase auth** (`auth.users`) — password / OTP / magic link. Returns "Invalid login credentials" on mismatch. Visible to user.
2. **App-level allowlist** (`public.admin_users`) — checked server-side in `src/app/admin/layout.tsx` via `getAdminUser()` in `src/lib/admin-auth.ts`. Before today's fix this rejected silently by redirecting to `/admin/login` with no error param — looked indistinguishable from a failed sign-in.

After 2026-05-19 the layout passes `?error=This account isn't on the admin allowlist. Contact Dennis to be added.` when there's a valid session but no `admin_users` row, so the failure mode now surfaces clearly. Don't remove that branch.

**Why:** Uwe spent ~hours on 2026-05-19 reporting "invalid login" / "invalid email address" after Dennis personally invited him. The password reset worked, the temp password worked, Supabase let him in — and then the admin layout silently bounced him because his `admin_users` row was missing. Diagnosis was slow because `auth.users` looked clean. The lesson: when an F2K admin reports a login failure, check `public.admin_users` for their row before touching anything in `auth.*`.

**How to apply:** When debugging an admin login report:
- First query: `select * from public.admin_users where email = '<reported-email>'`. No row → that's the cause; insert one (see [[seafields-admin-onboarding-flow]]).
- Only if a row exists, then look at `auth.users` (password reset, email confirmation, etc).
- If both look right, check `auth_user_id` matches `auth.users.id` — the `link_admin_user_trigger` only fires AFTER INSERT on `auth.users`, so a manually-created admin needs the FK set manually too.

Related: [[seafields-admin-onboarding-flow]].

candidates.title: Self-authenticating API routes in this project (webhooks, cron, public invite GET) must be explicitly allowlisted in src/lib/supabase/middleware.ts or they retu
candidates.material:
---
name: middleware-allowlist-pattern
description: "Self-authenticating API routes in this project (webhooks, cron, public invite GET) must be explicitly allowlisted in src/lib/supabase/middleware.ts or they return 401 before the route handler ever runs. Same class of bug has bitten twice — once for webhooks (b443916), once for cron (this fix)."
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: feedback
  originSessionId: f1e31636-1d6d-4eab-9f38-f1af7a983154
---

When adding a new API route under `/api/*` in InvestorPilot that authenticates itself (CRON_SECRET, svix webhook signature, shared-secret header, signed query token, etc.), you MUST also add an allowlist entry in `src/lib/supabase/middleware.ts:81-90`. The middleware gate runs BEFORE the route handler and returns `{ error: 'Unauthorized' }` 401 for any `/api/*` request without a valid Supabase auth cookie.

**Why:** Same class of bug has now bitten twice in this repo:
1. 2026-05-17 — `/api/webhooks/resend` + `/api/webhooks/unipile/account` silently 401'd for unknown duration; surfaced by Resend bounce events not landing. Fixed in b443916 by adding `!path.startsWith('/api/webhooks')`.
2. 2026-05-18 — `/api/cron/sequencer` silently 401'd for days; Vercel cron has been firing but every invocation returned 401 before the route's CRON_SECRET check ran. Surfaced while trying to trigger a render to verify Vietnamese localisation. Fixed in 4b90971 by adding `!path.startsWith('/api/cron')`. Burned ~20 minutes of debugging because the user-facing failure was "401 Unauthorized" with no hint that middleware was the gate (looked like a CRON_SECRET problem, which was *also* broken — empty value on Vercel — but turned out to be a red herring).

**How to apply:**
- When you add a route under `/api/cron/*`, `/api/webhooks/*`, or any other self-authenticating path: open `src/lib/supabase/middleware.ts`, find the allowlist condition (around line 81), add `!path.startsWith('/api/<your-prefix>')` to the negated conjunction. Document WHY in the comment block so the next person doesn't re-introduce the gate trying to "tighten security".
- When debugging a 401 from a self-authenticating API route: first check middleware, not the route's own auth logic. The 401 body shape `{ error: 'Unauthorized' }` (exact string) is the middleware's, while route handlers tend to be more specific.
- Don't add specific auth-cookie-skipping logic inside the route — keep the allowlist centralised in middleware. Two layers of "skip auth here" is a recipe for the next gap.

**Related:** [[reference-vercel-deploy-workflow]] mentions the curl auth-cookie pattern for testing — those tests automatically pass middleware. Curl tests of self-authenticating routes will reveal middleware gaps because they don't carry the cookie.

candidates.title: Org-merge / org-delete migrations must guarantee canonical membership exists before re-anchoring, OR refuse + surface broken profiles for manual review. Silent
candidates.material:
---
name: org-merge-membership-guarantee
description: "Org-merge / org-delete migrations must guarantee canonical membership exists before re-anchoring, OR refuse + surface broken profiles for manual review. Silent NULL strands users."
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: feedback
  originSessionId: 7a593fb5-3c82-4a67-abab-d344f95ee288
---

When writing any migration that deletes / merges / consolidates organisations,
the re-anchor step MUST either:
  (a) GUARANTEE the canonical membership row exists for every affected user
      BEFORE setting their `profile.active_organisation_id`, or
  (b) REFUSE to re-anchor those users + surface them via RAISE NOTICE for
      manual review.

Never silently set `active_organisation_id = NULL` for users who happen to
not have a canonical membership at apply time. Same applies to bulk
membership cleanup, org-archive flows, and the eventual "Lane C drops
the legacy organisation_id column" cutover.

**Why:** On 2026-05-21, migration 038 deleted a duplicate "Corporate AI
Solutions" org. The migration's UPDATE on profiles used `CASE WHEN
EXISTS(canonical membership) THEN canonical ELSE NULL`. The problem: the
doomed-org cascade had already deleted the user's old membership row
before the CASE check ran in the same statement, AND the canonical
membership turned out not to exist for dennis@corporateaisolutions.com
(despite him actively browsing the canonical org earlier the same day —
something cleared that membership between then and apply time). Result:
his profile got `active_organisation_id = NULL` with `memberships =
[]` → authenticated session but stranded outside any org → silent
`/dashboard` 404 on every sign-in attempt. Took two middleware patches
(neither of which could help, since there was no membership to fall
back to) plus a diagnostic migration 039 to pin down. The CASE-NULL
branch is the load-bearing failure mode — it looks defensive but it's
actually destructive.

**How to apply:**
- In any migration that DELETEs or merges orgs, write the membership
  upsert FIRST (`INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING` for every affected
  user → canonical), THEN re-anchor profiles, THEN drop the doomed org.
- If you can't guarantee canonical membership (e.g. you don't know the
  right role to grant), don't NULL the column — instead leave the
  active_organisation_id pointing at the doomed UUID and RAISE NOTICE
  the affected user list so a human can adjudicate. A dangling UUID is
  recoverable (the middleware fallback can find another membership);
  a NULL with zero memberships is not.
- For the eventual Lane C drop of `profile.organisation_id` legacy
  column (per [[multi-org-legacy-column-audit]]), audit must include
  the same guarantee: every active user has at least one membership
  row before the column is dropped.
- Same DNA as [[clarify-over-fail]] — silent degradation strands the
  user; surface for human decision instead. Same DNA as
  [[atomic-migration-sequencing]] — order matters, and "looks
  defensive" is not the same as "is defensive."

candidates.title: All information from all sources — uploaded docs, URLs, search results, enrichment fetches — must be part of the KB ingestion and assessment process. No source
candidates.material:
---
name: unified-kb-ingestion
description: "All information from all sources — uploaded docs, URLs, search results, enrichment fetches — must be part of the KB ingestion and assessment process. No source of truth left orphaned outside the KB."
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: feedback
  originSessionId: 2455b2ce-932f-4f1e-b4f2-ef9585d365ab
---

Every piece of information the system surfaces during a project workflow — uploaded PDFs / pasted text, URLs added to the KB, Brave search snippets pulled during discovery, LinkedIn profile/post content pulled during enrichment, generated assets like rubrics / sequences / outreach copy — must feed back into the project's Knowledge Base and be available for subsequent auto-fill / rubric / sequence regeneration. The current state has source-of-truth fragments scattered: uploaded docs in `product_sources`, search results on `partners` rows, LinkedIn enrichment on `partners` profile fields, generated rubrics on the project row — but the auto-fill / rubric / sequence generators only read `product_sources`. Anything learned downstream is invisible to upstream regeneration.

**Why:** Operators experience this as "I told the system X already, why doesn't it know?". The system is functionally amnesic across regenerations. When the operator clicks Auto-fill from KB a second time after Brave discovery has surfaced 20 named SEA seed VCs and LinkedIn enrichment has pulled their recent posts, that signal should improve the next auto-fill — but today it's discarded because the regenerator only reads `product_sources`. This was raised on 2026-05-17 after a LingoPure run where auto-fill regressed to old funding numbers because the new $12M one-pager hadn't made it into `product_sources` and the system silently used the older Claude-feedback PDF instead.

**How to apply:** Anywhere new information enters the system:

1. **Brave search results during discovery** — write the firm-level snippets to `product_sources` (source_type='search_result', auto-tagged with the query that produced them) so the next rubric regeneration can ground in observed market evidence.
2. **LinkedIn profile + post content from enrichment** — write to `product_sources` as source_type='linkedin_profile' so the next sequence regeneration can reference what real investors in this niche are posting about.
3. **Generated assets** — when the rubric / sequence / draft is generated, also persist a "what we generated" record back to KB so the operator's next regeneration prompt can include "previously we generated X; here's what's new".
4. **Webhook ingestion** — any inbound reply, calendar booking, engagement signal should feed back into the project's KB so future cold drafts can reference real conversation context, not just original positioning docs.
5. **External documents** (Google Drive, Dropbox, Notion) — when the operator points the system at a folder, the system pulls every doc inside as if they were uploaded individually (see related [[clarify-over-fail]] for the diff/confirm pattern when sources contradict).

The pattern across all five: nothing the system learns is allowed to die outside the KB. Every downstream action becomes upstream context for the next regeneration. Related: [[clarify-over-fail]] — when newly-ingested sources contradict the existing KB, surface the conflict rather than silently overwriting.

candidates.title: After migration 029 added profiles.active_organisation_id as a SECOND FK to organisations, Supabase relational queries like `organisations(*)` return PostgREST
candidates.material:
---
name: dual-fk-relational-trap
description: "After migration 029 added profiles.active_organisation_id as a SECOND FK to organisations, Supabase relational queries like `organisations(*)` return PostgREST 300 PGRST201 (\"more than one relationship found\"). Must qualify with FK alias like `organisations!profiles_active_organisation_id_fkey(*)`."
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: reference
  originSessionId: f1e31636-1d6d-4eab-9f38-f1af7a983154
---

When a table has two foreign keys to the same target table, PostgREST relational shorthand becomes ambiguous and the request returns HTTP 300 with code PGRST201. Symptom: the join field silently becomes null in client code, fields downstream render "not set" / blank.

InvestorPilot example (introduced 2026-05-18 in migration 029, surfaced same day):
- `profiles.organisation_id` → `organisations.id` (legacy, kept for backwards compat)
- `profiles.active_organisation_id` → `organisations.id` (new — multi-org)

The query that broke:
```ts
await supabase.from('profiles').select('*, organisations(*)').single();
```

PostgREST 300 response (`PGRST201`) includes the disambiguation hint:
> Try changing 'organisations' to one of: 'organisations!profiles_active_organisation_id_fkey', 'organisations!profiles_organisation_id_fkey'

Resolved by:
```ts
await supabase.from('profiles').select('*, organisations!profiles_active_organisation_id_fkey(*)').single();
```

**How to apply:**
- Any time you add a second FK from table A to table B in a migration, immediately grep the codebase for `B(\*)` or `B(<columns>)` in `.select(` calls and disambiguate. The 300 returns no rows but the surrounding code reads it as `data.B = null` — there's no exception, so the bug is invisible until QA.
- When pairing a "legacy" FK with a "live" FK during a multi-org / multi-tenant transition, the LIVE FK is almost always the one you want in app code. Use the FK-alias form so reviewers immediately see which lineage is being followed.
- Related: [[session-handoff-2026-05-18-evening]] — captured the regression chain across the same session. [[multi-org-legacy-column-audit]] — broader sweep still pending for org-scoped reads/writes.

**Decided by Dennis 2026-07-28, in his words: "owed but unbilled til 30th is the correct wording."**
**BUILT the same day. NOT yet exercised against Stripe — see the gap at the bottom.**

The model: card captured day 1, the month **owed from the start and simply not invoiced until the
period closes**. Cancel before that bill falls due and the in-progress month is **waived as a gift**,
no proration. Because the waiver is permanent rather than a month-one offer, the sales line beats any
trial: **"You're never billed for the month you're in."**

## What exists now

- **`@caistech/subscription-billing` v0.2.0** (published to GitHub Packages; Kira depends on `^0.2.0`):
  `ensureBillingMeter` / `ensureMeteredPrice` / `reportPeriodOwed` / `cancelWithWaiver`, plus an
  `arrears: true` line item. `trialDays` + arrears now **throws**.
- **Kira:** `lib/billing/arrears.ts`, reporting hooked on the adapter's `apply`,
  `POST /api/billing/cancel`, `CancelPlanButton` in Settings, migration
  `20260728180000_billing_periods_reported.sql` **applied to prod and verified** (RLS on).
- 13 Kira tests + 12 package tests. Full Kira suite green; `next build` green.

## Three corrections to what this memory used to say — don't re-plan off the old version

1. **It could NOT be a `usage_type` flag on `DynamicPriceLineItem`.** Checkout's inline
   `price_data.recurring` takes only `interval`/`interval_count` — no `usage_type`, no `meter` — so
   an arrears Price must exist BEFORE the session. That's `ensureMeteredPrice`, idempotent on a
   deterministic `lookup_key`.
2. **LaunchReady is NOT a consumer.** Kira is the only repo depending on the package; LaunchReady
   still runs its own `app/api/stripe/*` fork (pre-existing un-migrated debt). The "no orphaned
   consumers" reconciliation was not required.
3. **Legacy usage records are gone in Stripe ≥18** — this is Billing Meters. Aggregation is `sum`,
   not `last`, to stay compilable on the package's stripe ≥17 peer floor.

## Two already-broken things it uncovered

- **`introductions.status` was never advanced** — nothing wrote `trialing`/`paying`, so the
  introducer board's headline tiles read zero however many owners were billed. Now synced from the
  subscription, fail-soft.
- **The pre-charge notice would have gone silent** — `trial_reminder_sent_at` was a once-ever stamp;
  arrears has a charge every month. Re-keyed to `users.charge_notice_period_end`.

## ⚠️ Still open

- ~~**Never run against real Stripe** / a LIVE key sits in the test slot so the integration test
  skips.~~ **STALE as of 2026-08-01** — `STRIPE_SECRET_KEY` now holds an `sk_test` key and the
  integration suite **executes** against Stripe test mode (observed: 4 tests, real network timings).
  The guard is intact and is the thing to trust: `describe.skipIf` on
  `stripeKey.startsWith('sk_test')`, so it can only ever run in test mode.
- **The Settings price positive path has NEVER rendered.** `getSubscriptionPrice()` reads the real
  monthly from Stripe (added 2026-08-01, `c13d5a1`) but no subscribed account exists, so only the
  null path has been observed. Pinned by 8 unit tests, not by a screenshot — worth 30 seconds of eyes
  once a real subscription exists. See [[project-kira-landing-honesty]].
- **Before going live:** run `node scripts/configure-billing-portal.mjs` against LIVE. Stripe's
  portal cancel cannot waive (it invoices either way), and two doors, one of which breaks the
  promise, is not a promise. Test and live portals are separate configurations.
- Live-mode Stripe webhook endpoint still doesn't exist (only test-mode).

Copy moved WITH the mechanism — every live-mode "30 days free" string is now the arrears promise,
including `lib/billing/plan-state.ts`, which had derived every sentence from a free month. Leaving
them would have armed a lie to fire the instant `STRIPE_LIVE_MODE` flips.

Related: [[project-kira-icp]] (an invoice after a cancel is what ends the referral relationship),
[[project-kira-advisor-demo-channel]], [[project-kira-naive-tester-state]].

candidates.title: Kira's doing-slice tools were attached then silently STRIPPED by the reprovision script; re-attached to 10/10 business agents 2026-07-27, root cause fixed — one
candidates.material:
---
name: project-kira-doing-slice-orphaned
description: "Kira's doing-slice tools were attached then silently STRIPPED by the reprovision script; re-attached to 10/10 business agents 2026-07-27, root cause fixed — one round trip still unproven"
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: ca1e9e44-7aae-45a3-8c38-47d024f91422
  modified: 2026-07-27T14:38:37.963Z
---

**Resolved 2026-07-27: all 10 business agents now carry `dispatch_task` + `approve_task`, uid-baked,
route verified live.** What is still unproven is one end-to-end round trip (draft → approve → `done`).

⚠️ **Kira RENAMES the convai tables** via `KIRA_CONVAI_TABLES` (`lib/kira/convai.ts`). There is no
`convai_agents` / `convai_memory` — querying those returns "table not found" and reads as nothing
being provisioned. The real tables are **`kira_agents`, `kira_memory`, `kira_conversations`**.

## The root cause — the part worth remembering

The earlier reading ("the tools were never added") was **wrong**. They *were* added:
`reprovisionBusinessAgentsForExec({apply:true})` had run, and the ElevenLabs workspace held 5 owners ×
a correct, uid-baked `dispatch_task`/`approve_task` pair. Every one was **orphaned — referenced by no
agent.**

They were stripped by **`scripts/reprovision-kira-agents.mjs`**, whose `buildToolsForUser` built only
memory + knowledge. **`setAgentTools` REPLACES an agent's tool list**, so a tool omitted there is not
skipped, it is removed. The tool-secret migration (commit `81f37e7`, "migration complete") is a run of
that very script — closing one gap silently opened another. Two reprovision paths existed with
different tool sets, and the incomplete one ran last.

**The lesson generalises:** where an API call *replaces* a set rather than merging into it, any second
code path that builds that set is a regression waiting for its turn to run. `doing-tools-def.mjs` even
names the script as one of its two consumers — the comment was aspirational, the import was absent.

## Fixed — merged as `d76c8a0` (PR #41), deployed + verified in prod 2026-07-27

- `scripts/reprovision-kira-agents.mjs` now imports the doing tools from the single source and
  scopes them to `journey_type === 'business'` — a dry run caught that the naive version would have
  put `dispatch_task` on the **personal-journey coaches** (`Kira_Personal_Dennis`, `Kira_Tom`), which
  `exec-reprovision.ts` deliberately excludes.
- Added `--tools-only` (skips the prompt append **and `bindWorkspaceWebhook`** — rebinding races and
  can leave two webhooks with different secrets, breaking post-call HMAC) and `--dry-run`.

## Operational notes for next time

- **`vercel env pull` returns `""` for the newer Production-only vars** (`ADMIN_EMAILS`,
  `ELEVENLABS_WEBHOOK_SECRET`, `KIRA_TOOL_WEBHOOK_SECRET`) while older ones pull real values. Do NOT
  read that as "the variable is empty in production" — it nearly produced a false report of an empty
  admin allowlist. Cross-check against behaviour (the memory loop passing proves the webhook secret
  is set).
- **The tool secret is recoverable from the workspace tool definitions** — `GET /v1/convai/tools`
  returns `x-convai-tool-secret` in `api_schema.request_headers`. Verify it matches a
  currently-attached, working tool (compare hashes) before reusing it.
- Audit script that answers "do the live agents carry the tools": zero-dep, reads `kira_agents` via
  Supabase REST + the ElevenLabs workspace catalogue, maps `tool_ids` → names. Worth re-creating —
  agent tool state is not visible from the repo.

## Proven end to end (2026-07-27)

`dispatch_task` → `awaiting_approval` (nothing sent, `needs_recipient_email: true`) → `approve_task`
with the recipient supplied at approval → `done`, mail accepted by Resend and **received**. That
closes the old `no recipient email captured` failure. Post-deploy re-check against prod drafts a
correct `Thanks,\nDennis` sign-off. Discarding via `approve=false` works and sends nothing.

## Still open

1. **The doing-slice is 3 task kinds** (`quote`/`email`/`reminder`); everything else lands
   `unsupported`. `reminder` has no notification transport — the row IS the reminder.
2. The orchestrator (`~/PycharmProjects/orchestrator/`) is **specification only** — ten markdown docs,
   no code, not a repo. `getSwarmCoordinator()` has only the `local` case; the adapter slot is a
   commented-out line. See [[reference-orchestrator-valuation-loop-docs]].

candidates.title: An agent can be created with ZERO tools while tools_attach logs success — a Kira with no memory that looks completely normal
candidates.material:
---
name: project-kira-silent-toolless-agent
description: An agent can be created with ZERO tools while tools_attach logs success — a Kira with no memory that looks completely normal
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: 15fc9835-6ae0-479b-8020-dad635c756a7
  modified: 2026-08-07T03:54:48.639Z
---

**⚠️ Read this before trusting any `kira_logs` "success", and before concluding an owner's memory problem is a prompt problem.**

## What happened

On 2026-08-07 the re-provision **dry run** reported `Kira_Ray_HaveRun_a6c8 (agent_4901kzczf133ehsamnpwt97pdfxa): 0 tool(s) attached`.

`kira_logs` had recorded `tools_attach: success` for that agent at 02:05:11 the same morning. The success was written because `setAgentTools` did not throw — **a fact about the call, not about the agent.**

## Why it matters more than it sounds

An agent with no tools cannot call `get_conversation_context`, `recall_memory` or `save_memory`. That is not a degraded Kira — it is a Kira with **no memory whatsoever**, which is the entire product. And it presents as completely normal: she talks, she answers, she silently knows nothing about him and stores nothing he says. The owner has no way to tell, and the failure carries its own log entry saying it went fine.

This is the failure family in [[feedback-verify-the-effect-not-the-edit]], in the one place where the effect *is* the product.

## What is NOT established

**Whether the write silently did not take, or something removed the tools afterwards.** Both fit the evidence. Do not repeat a guess as a cause — the second Ray agent (`dfb8`, created 03:21 the same morning through the same route) got 18 tools and kept them.

## The fix (shipped, `240e6da`)

`app/api/kira/create/route.ts` now **reads the agent back** via `getAgent` after `setAgentTools`, compares the observed `conversation_config.agent.prompt.tool_ids` count against the desired list, retries once, and only then logs. It stays non-fatal — nobody should lose an account because ElevenLabs was slow — but non-fatal must not mean unnoticed. **`tools_attach: success` now means the tools are on the agent.**

The read-back catches both candidate causes, which is why it was the right fix for a cause still unknown.

## How to check this yourself

```
npx vite-node -c vitest.config.ts scripts/reprovision-kira-agents.mjs -- --dry-run
```
Prints `N tool(s) attached` per live agent. Anything below 18 on a business agent is a memory-less Kira. The dry run mutates nothing; dropping `--dry-run` **applies to every live agent** (see [[reference-kira-agent-scripts-default-apply]]).

Related: [[project-kira-doing-slice-orphaned]] (the other time a tool list went missing — `setAgentTools` REPLACES, it does not merge), [[project-kira-new-owner-path]], [[project-kira-firstrun-pass-and-seed-test]].

candidates.title: @caistech/sayfix-embed's placement engine avoids controls but is blind to content — Dennis confirmed it is MEANT to avoid both and took the fix scope himself 20
candidates.material: --- name: project-sayfix-placement-content-blindness description: "@caistech/sayfix-embed's placement engine avoids controls but is blind to content — Dennis confirmed it is MEANT to avoid both and took the fix scope himself 2026-08-01" metadata: node_type: memory type: project originSessionId: 2bc087c3-cfd2-4111-92f9-d10db0cb6710 modified: 2026-08-01T05:36:37.153Z --- **Dennis, 2026-08-01: "it's meant to avoid both."** The catalogue had recorded content-blindness as a known *limit*; he ruled it a **defect**. **He took the scope — do not start this in a Kira session without checking with him first.** ## The gap (confirmed in source, `packages/sayfix-embed/src/placement.ts` v0.6.0) `collectObstacles` has exactly two passes: (1) visible `position: fixed | sticky` elements, (2) `INTERACTIVE_SELECTOR` = `button, a[href], input, select, textarea, [role="button"], [role="link"]`. A heading, paragraph, price, voucher code, ``, `` or chart is **invisible to it**. The engine then reports `conflicts: 0` and is **correct by its own model** — a confident wrong answer, which is worse than a crash. ## Why the obvious fix is wrong Adding text elements as obstacles fails: on a content page *everything* is text, every candidate takes an overlap hit, `OVERLAP_PENALTY` (220) swamps every preference bonus, all corners score equally terrible, and the choice degenerates to candidate order. **"Never cover any content" is unsatisfiable for a floating overlay.** There is also a hard constraint: the file-level security note is explicit that it reads **geometry and structural metadata only, never text content**, because it runs on third-party customer sites. So it cannot rank importance by reading what the text says. ## The recommended shape (given to Dennis, not built) Stop asking *"where is the content?"* and ask *"what am I covering, and is there somewhere covering less?"* — via `document.elementsFromPoint()`: - sample ~5–9 points per candidate rect (corners + centre) - take the topmost element at each that is not SayFix's own subtree - a leaf carrying content (non-empty text node, `img`, `svg`, `canvas`, `video`) = a real conflict; `body` or an empty container = free Checking *whether* a text node is non-empty is existence, not value — nothing captured or transmitted, so the security posture holds. It also catches images/canvas/video (currently missed entirely) and is **cheaper** than today's two 400-element scans (~20 hit-tests). **Implementation shape that preserves the tests:** add it as a **third pass inside `collectObstacles`** emitting `kind: 'content'` at a lower weight than `interactive`. `computePlacement` stays pure and untouched, so `test/placement.test.ts` keeps passing. Pair with a `data-sayfix-avoid` host opt-out as the escape hatch. ## Second defect in the same file, same trip **The documented "mobile collapses to a right-edge tab" never happens at default props.** `position` defaults to `'bottom-right'` and is passed as `preferred` (`PREFERRED_BONUS` +8), which beats `right-edge-tab`'s candidate rank (+6) on first render; `REMEMBERED_BONUS` (+14) then writes that to localStorage and locks it in. The edge tab only wins when a real obstacle overlaps bottom-right. ## Scope warning Shared package → the **no-orphaned-consumers** propagation rule applies (bump, publish, reconcile every consumer). Evidence base is BucketLyst (launcher covered the voucher redemption code and its ACL-mandated expiry date). **Kira is NOT a confirmed instance** — its launcher sits over empty panel space; an earlier claim otherwise in the Kira session was overstated.

candidates.title: The gstack browse daemon crashes mid-walk and is what kills long naive-tester runs — short chained calls with fresh page loads survive, long persona walkthrough
candidates.material:
---
name: reference-browse-daemon-crashes-testers
description: "The gstack browse daemon crashes mid-walk and is what kills long naive-tester runs — short chained calls with fresh page loads survive, long persona walkthroughs do not"
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: reference
  originSessionId: cda27037-5bc8-46a2-a8cf-81d0f292d00f
  modified: 2026-07-28T04:09:21.093Z
---

Three naive-tester runs on 2026-07-28 (anneke, connor, ray) produced 20 screenshots and **no
reports** — they died mid-walk. Reproduced directly the same day: the `browse` daemon failed four
times in one verification pass with `Page crashed`, `Target crashed`, `Server failed to start
within 15s`, and one silent reset to `about:blank` that lost all page state and every `@ref`.

This is the harness, not the product, and it is not new — it just kept being written off as
tooling noise in individual reports:
- Mobile Marcus, 2026-07-27: *"the browser tab crashed twice during long automated runs."*
- Anneke, 2026-07-27 rerun: could not complete sign-in, so the whole authenticated half of the
  walkthrough came back **unverified** — she marked authenticated-chrome ❌ for that reason alone.
- Ray, 2026-07-28: *"the browser dropped its session on me a few times mid-walk."*

**Cost when it bites:** a report that never gets written, or worse, a **false negative** — a
crash-corrupted probe reads as "the feature is broken." On 2026-07-28 a re-probe of the industry
matcher returned "no dropdown" for eight words that had matched correctly minutes earlier in a
clean pass. Discard crash-adjacent results; do not report them. A false failure gets a real fix
reverted (see [[feedback-grade-capability-not-function-name]]).

## What works

- **One `$B chain` call per unit of work**, each starting with its own `goto`, so a crash costs one
  probe rather than the run.
- **Re-`snapshot` after every navigation** — refs do not survive, and a stale `@e3` reports
  "Ref not found" which is indistinguishable from a missing element.
- **`$B stop` then re-issue** when the daemon wedges; it restarts clean.
- Read the *dropdown/confirmation* state via `snapshot -i` (options render as buttons) or `text`,
  not via bespoke `js` DOM-walking, which returns empty far more often than it returns a wrong
  answer.

## What to do instead of a long walkthrough

Targeted verification of named findings — type the words, read the one page, check the one string
— finishes in minutes and survives. Full 45-minute persona walkthroughs through this daemon are
currently a coin-flip, and the coin has landed badly 3 of the last 6 runs. If a full persona pass
is genuinely needed, expect to resume it, and have the tester write findings incrementally rather
than composing the whole report at the end.

Strategic decision recorded 2026-05-16. **LessonsLearned is no longer a
standalone product.** It is being built as a monitoring + foresight layer
*inside* F2K Checkpoint, reading Checkpoint's own database. The
LessonsLearned standalone repo at
`C:\Users\denni\PycharmProjects\LessonsLearned\` is effectively paused —
the auth surface, org chrome, dashboard, and backfill wizard scaffold I
built earlier remain on disk but are not the path forward. Don't extend
that codebase without re-confirming intent with the user.

**Why:** Checkpoint already owns `programmes → packages → dwellings →
projects → task_instances → task_steps`, the 197 task templates, the
procurement pipeline, and the spend ledger. LessonsLearned's
baseline-vs-actual analysis needs that exact data graph. Building a
parallel app to "watch" Checkpoint via integration was rejected;
one platform with two faces (Checkpoint = plan/procure/execute forward,
LessonsLearned = variance/watch-outs/lessons backward + real-time) is
the locked architecture.

**The directive doc is the source of truth.** Path:
`C:\Users\denni\PycharmProjects\F2K-Checkpoint\docs\checkpoint-lessonslearned-directive.md`.
Always read it before resuming LL work — it captures sequenced phases,
hard constraints, and the standing data-handling rules that apply at
N=1 users.

**What's being built in the current Checkpoint engagement (parallel to
this repo):**

- **Phase 1 — verify (read-only):** confirm whether `log_audit_event()`
  trigger is attached to `task_instances` in the production DB
  (`ggwveltavnvvscgqekhy` — wait no that's platform-trust;
  Checkpoint's ref is separate, check Checkpoint .env), confirm

The schema audit run on 2026-05-16 (this session) found Checkpoint has
NO actual-side data for planned-vs-actual: planned dates are recomputed
live from `lead_time_days` against ESRD; there's no frozen baseline
anywhere. Phase 2 is fixing this so LL has something to read.

**Two future backfill paths — both are roadmap items, neither is in
the current Checkpoint engagement:**

1. **Checkpoint-native analysis** (the retention engine). Any project

The standalone LL app I built earlier was heading toward path 2; that
work is on ice until Checkpoint's foundation is in.

candidates.title: spatial_layout extraction failed silently due to missing DOMMatrix polyfill; fixed by pinning @napi-rs/canvas as direct dep
candidates.material:
---
name: 3d-viewer-was-silently-broken-in-production-until-2026-05-14
description: spatial_layout extraction failed silently due to missing DOMMatrix polyfill; fixed by pinning @napi-rs/canvas as direct dep
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: 3cf41998-f37d-4647-a3f0-36702080f926
---

The MMC Build 3D plan viewer ([[project_3d_plan_viewer]]) had been silently broken in production for an unknown period before 2026-05-14, not just incomplete (overlays missing).

**Root cause:** `pdfjs-dist@5` (used by `pdf-to-img` in `src/lib/build/spatial/pdf-to-image.ts`) requires `@napi-rs/canvas` at runtime to polyfill `globalThis.DOMMatrix`, `ImageData`, and `Path2D` — Node.js doesn't have these. `@napi-rs/canvas` was only present as a transitive optional dep of `pdfjs-dist`, so Vercel's serverless bundler wasn't reliably including it. Every PDF render threw `DOMMatrix is not defined`. The Inngest pipeline at `src/lib/inngest/functions/run-design-optimisation.ts:132-135` caught it as "non-fatal" and stored `spatial_layout = null` on `design_checks`. The report page conditional `{check.spatial_layout && <Plan3DReveal ... />}` then never rendered the 3D button — users saw optimisation suggestions but no 3D view and assumed that was the design.

**Fix (commit `e39e277`, 2026-05-14):** Pinned `@napi-rs/canvas@^0.1.97` as a direct project dependency (matches pdfjs-dist's `^0.1.88` optional range) and added `pdf-to-img`, `pdfjs-dist`, `@napi-rs/canvas` to `serverExternalPackages` in `next.config.ts` so Next.js leaves the native binaries as runtime requires rather than trying to webpack-bundle them.

**Implication for ICP-facing work:** the 3D viewer feature, which has been a key product-differentiator talking point, has not been demonstrable on real production data until this fix landed. Any prior demo screenshots that showed extracted geometry were either (a) from before pdfjs-dist v5 upgrade, (b) from a different machine/env that happened to have canvas, or (c) constructed manually. Re-running optimisation on existing projects after 2026-05-14 should now populate `spatial_layout` for the first time, and the 3D button will start appearing on report pages.

**How to apply:**
- When debugging "feature works locally but not in prod" patterns, check for native-dep bundling issues. Vercel's serverless bundler skips transitive optional deps with native binaries unless they're pinned at project level.
- For any future image / PDF / native-rendering package, check `serverExternalPackages` in `next.config.ts`.
- Update [[project_3d_plan_viewer]] to reflect: the gap was bigger than "extractor doesn't populate wall_ids" — the entire pipeline was failing before that. The wall_id gap is what's exposed *after* this fix, not before.

candidates.title: Always branch from main, never from whatever branch is checked out — a docs PR silently carried an unapproved feature and would have bypassed a client sign-off
candidates.material:
---
name: feedback_branch_from_main_not_current
description: "Always branch from main, never from whatever branch is checked out — a docs PR silently carried an unapproved feature and would have bypassed a client sign-off gate."
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: feedback
  originSessionId: 530edc3b-5673-4252-b018-ce864bb7fed7
  modified: 2026-07-31T04:32:27.991Z
---

**Always `git checkout main` BEFORE `git checkout -b <new-branch>`.** Branching from whatever happens
to be checked out makes the new PR contain the *other* branch's commits too.

**Why:** on 2026-07-31 a docs branch was cut while sitting on `feat/signup-hubspot-capture`, so
**PR #137 ("docs only — a spec") actually contained PR #136's unapproved signup→HubSpot feature.**
Merging what read as a harmless spec would have shipped code that was explicitly being held for
Karen + Karthik sign-off, on a REGULATED client product — silently bypassing the exact gate #136's
own description existed to enforce. It was caught only because Dennis asked an unrelated question
about why the repo was sitting on a branch, which prompted a `git diff --stat main...HEAD`.

This repo makes it likelier than usual: the working tree is **shared across sessions**, so the
checked-out branch is often not the one you left, and `git branch --show-current` is already a
standing check here (see [[project_call_backlog_2026_06_25]]).

**How to apply:**
- Before `checkout -b`, confirm the base: `git branch --show-current` → `git checkout main`.
- After opening any PR, verify it contains only what you intend:
  `git log --oneline main..HEAD` and `gh pr view <n> --json changedFiles,commits`.
  A PR described as "docs only" that reports 6 changed files is the tell.
- Fix a wrong base with `git rebase --onto main <wrong-base> <branch>` then
  `git push --force-with-lease` — safe when the branch is new and unreviewed, and `--force-with-lease`
  refuses if anything changed underneath. Confirm with Dennis first: force-push is on the
  safety list.
- **Never describe a PR's scope from the commit you wrote — describe it from what the PR reports.**
  Saying "docs-only, safe to merge" about an unverified diff is how the gate gets bypassed.
