candidates.title: Large DWG (36.9MB) uploads crash process-plan with a 500/OOM, not an upload failure; PR #37 size-guards the DXF parse so it degrades to manual_review.
candidates.material:
---
name: project_dwg_large_oom_2026_06_11
description: "Large DWG (36.9MB) uploads crash process-plan with a 500/OOM, not an upload failure; PR #37 size-guards the DXF parse so it degrades to manual_review."
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: 64fba2b5-3008-44bf-ac91-a8aa51b47178
---

Karen reported a 36.9MB DWG "failing to upload" (2026-06-11, "TH01 Terraces 01 by Carter Williamson-technical-01.dwg"). **The upload actually succeeded** — `plan/uploaded` fired with a valid storage `fileUrl`. The failure was the **`Process Plan Upload` Inngest function** (`src/lib/inngest/functions/process-plan.ts`): `invalid status code: 500` with a raw Next.js 500 HTML page, after **~252s** (under the 300s `maxDuration` → **OOM, not timeout**).

**Root cause:** `extractLayersFromDxf` / `extractSpatialLayoutFromDxf` (`src/lib/plans/dxf-extractor.ts`) do `dxfBuffer.toString("utf-8")` + dxf-parser `parseSync` synchronously. A dense multi-sheet *technical* DWG → huge DXF → parseSync object graph exceeds the function's ~1.7GB default memory → invocation killed. An OOM kill is **not a catchable throw**, so the existing `try/catch → manual_review` fallback never ran; the plan was stranded in `status: "error"`. Same chokepoint feeds the 3D render path (`test-3d-runner.ts`, `run-test-3d-extraction.ts`).

**Diagnostic lesson:** "upload failing" was the user-visible symptom; the Inngest event (HTML-500 body + sub-maxDuration runtime) was the real signal pointing at OOM. A raw HTML-500 from an Inngest step = the Vercel function was killed (OOM/timeout), which try/catch can't save.

**Fix — PR #37 `fix/dwg-large-dxf-oom-guard` (MERGED to main 2026-06-11, `42d4cb1`):** `MAX_DXF_PARSE_BYTES` (60MB, tunable) + `dxfTooLargeToParse()`; both parse fns bail to null above the cap (logging actual DXF size for calibration). Regression test `tests/unit/lib/plans/dxf-parse-guard.test.ts`.

**Fix — PR #38 `fix/consolidate-3d-dwg-handling` (MERGED to main 2026-06-11):** the SQL revealed THREE failures: (1) plans `error` = process-plan OOM [#37]; (2) `test_3d_jobs ff22b841` = the 3D render died on **CloudConvert dwg→PDF 502 Bad Gateway with NO retry**; (3) `test_3d_jobs ab294d42` = orphaned `processing` job. #38: (a) **deleted the duplicate `test-3d-runner.ts`** (a 2nd synchronous copy of the 3D pipeline w/ zero callers — only its `Test3DResult` type was used; moved to `test-3d-types.ts`). The LIVE 3D render is ONE process: prod `/build`, projects flow, AND test-3d harness all emit `test3d/extract.requested` → single `run-test-3d-extraction` Inngest fn; (b) **process-plan DWG path now falls back DWG→PDF→ingest** instead of dead-ending at manual_review (mirrors the 3D path); (c) **`fetchWithRetry` retries transient CloudConvert 5xx** (the actual render fix — was single-shot) + test `cloudconvert-retry.test.ts`. DXF parse-guard + 3D fall-through means a too-large DWG now auto-routes to the PDF render path.

**✅ KAREN'S ISSUE RESOLVED END-TO-END (2026-06-11):** she refreshed TH01 → upload worked → plan activated → opened in Build → 3D render ran. Confirms #37+#38 in prod. (`main`→prod auto-deploy IS working — the old "disconnected SCRUM-278" note is stale; see [[reference_mmcbuild_vercel_github_topology]].)

**SEQUEL BUG — Design Optimisation on a DWG (PR #39, MERGED 2026-06-11):** after the 3D worked, running optimisation failed with a useless "Something went wrong". `design_checks` row: `status=error, summary="No plan content found..."`. Two bugs: (1) optimisation is RAG-based and HARD-FAILED when the plan had no text chunks — a DWG renders in 3D (geometry) but a DWG→PDF export has no text layer → `retrievePlanChunks` null → dead-end, even though the spatial layout was available. Fix: only error when BOTH text AND layout are missing; else analyse on the layout + selected systems via a fallback prompt (`run-design-optimisation.ts`). (2) DIAGNOSTIC INTEGRITY — the UI (`optimisation-progress.tsx`) threw away `design_checks.summary` (the real reason, already returned by `getDesignReport`) and hardcoded the generic string; now surfaces the real reason via `initialSummary` prop + poll capture. **Same generic-message bug still in Comply `check-progress.tsx` + Quote `estimation-progress.tsx` — flagged same-pattern follow-up (each needs its reason field confirmed).**

**SCRUM-290 (OpenAI vision fallback) — IMPLEMENTED, PR #40 (`feat/scrum-290-vision-fallback`), 2026-06-11.** Eng-reviewed via /plan-eng-review; decisions: **D1 = FULL migration** (all 7 extractor call sites route through `callModel`); **D2 = capped-N rasterise** on the OpenAI PDF leg (hinted page else first 12, log truncation); **D3 = inject the rasteriser** (AI layer keeps ZERO dep on plans/CloudConvert; build supplies `rasterizePdf` via options). Built: `ModelCallOptions` += `pdf`/`thinkingBudget`/`rasterizePdf`; Anthropic provider doc-block + thinking (byte-identical primary path); OpenAI provider rasterises PDF→images (throws if no rasteriser); new `plan_page_classify:[haiku→gpt-4o-mini]` chain; `dwg-converter.runCloudConvertJob` now returns ALL files + new `rasterizePdfPages`; extractor migrated via `src/lib/build/spatial/vision-call.ts` `callVisionModel` (extractor.ts ×3, page-classifier ×2, sheet-decomposer ×2 — removed per-file Anthropic clients + hardcoded model ids). Tests `tests/unit/lib/ai/vision-providers.test.ts`; full suite 127 green. **⚠️ Needs a funded `OPENAI_API_KEY` in prod for the fallback to fire** (registry lists gpt-4o/mini). PR #40 open, CI running at last note.

**DWG-OOM follow-ups still open:** split `download-and-ingest` per-stage; raise Inngest fn memory; entity-count/stream parse; **reaper for orphaned `processing` jobs**; Comply+Quote honest-error message.

**⚠️ SEPARATE, CONFIRMED-STILL-OPEN — SCRUM-290 (OpenAI fallback for the 3D extractor).** The router `callModel` HAS the chain `plan_vision: ["claude-sonnet-4"→"gpt-4o"]` (and registry `claude-sonnet-4`→`claude-sonnet-4-6` per #36), BUT the **entire 3D extractor chain bypasses the router** — `extractor.ts`, `sheet-decomposer.ts`, `page-classifier.ts` all call `new Anthropic()` / `messages.create` directly (7+ sites); NO `import OpenAI`; `callModel` used nowhere in `src/lib/build/`. So **if Claude is unavailable (outage/404 retired-model/429/credit — the 2026-06-10/11 incident class) the 3D extraction has NO fallback and fails.** Blocker: `callModel` doesn't support multi-part vision/document content. Fix options: (a) extend `callModel` for vision then route the extractor through it (clean, bigger), or (b) add a GPT-4o vision fallback in the extractor (note: OpenAI needs the PDF rasterised/files-API, not Anthropic-native PDF). NOT a quick drop-in. See [[project_anthropic_credit_outage_2026_06_10]].

candidates.title: A migration marked \"applied to prod\" in Jira can be an isolated un-applied skip — verify against the live DB via REST probe before trusting it
candidates.material:
---
name: project_migration_drift_00081_verify
description: "A migration marked \"applied to prod\" in Jira can be an isolated un-applied skip — verify against the live DB via REST probe before trusting it"
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: 9ab6e6a3-bceb-464c-9442-a995cbc90b6f
---

2026-07-17: SCRUM-56's migration **00081 (`professionals.contact_name`)** was marked
"applied to production" in a Jira comment but had **never landed** on the live DB
(`lztzyfeivpsbqbsfzctw`). It was an **isolated skip** — 00080 (before) and 00082 (after)
both applied fine; only 00081 was missed in the manual per-file apply. The code from PR #110
wrote `contact_name` on every Direct listing save, so **every register/edit save failed** in
prod with "Could not find the 'contact_name' column of 'professionals' in the schema cache"
— this is what actually blocked Karen on SCRUM-238 (not the duplicate-listing guard).

**Verification method (use this to confirm a prod column/table exists — authoritative, beats
trusting a "marked applied" note):** probe the REST API with the service-role key
(`~/.mmc-serv-rol`):
`curl -H "apikey: $SRK" -H "Authorization: Bearer $SRK" "https://lztzyfeivpsbqbsfzctw.supabase.co/rest/v1/<table>?select=<col>&limit=1"`
— **HTTP 400 + code `42703` "column ... does not exist"** = genuinely absent in Postgres (a
stale PostgREST cache would still return data on a *read*, so 42703 is real absence, not cache).
A neighbouring column added by a different migration returning 200 on the same table proves it's
not a wrong-project/wrong-table probe. The Management API token (`~/.supabase-token`) **lacks
privilege** for `information_schema`/migration-history queries (403), so REST-probe per-object.

**Why:** REGULATED tier — a "marked applied" Jira comment is NOT proof a migration ran; the
manual per-file pooler apply (see [[reference_mmcbuild_migration_apply]]) can silently skip one.
**How to apply:** after any migration, REST-probe the new column/table against prod before
closing the ticket; if 42703, re-run the `ALTER … ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS …` + `NOTIFY pgrst,
'reload schema'` in the SQL editor for `lztzyfeivpsbqbsfzctw`. Fix verified live 2026-07-17.

candidates.title: The 3-layer tenant-isolation model (app checks + CI gate + RLS backstop); any server action reading via db()/admin by a caller-supplied id MUST assert org owner
candidates.material:
---
name: project_server_action_org_ownership_guard
description: The 3-layer tenant-isolation model (app checks + CI gate + RLS backstop); any server action reading via db()/admin by a caller-supplied id MUST assert org ownership or the CI gate fails the build.
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: 3b4a7d04-e6bb-4955-9232-11cae54b4e86
---

**Standing rule + how it's now ENFORCED.** Any server action / API route that takes a
caller-supplied id (`projectId`/`checkId`/`estimateId`/`enquiryId`/`lessonId`/`kbId`/…) and
reads/writes via the RLS-bypassing `db()` (= `createAdminClient()`) MUST assert the record
belongs to the caller's `profile.org_id` **before** using it. `db()` bypasses RLS by design, so
that check is the only tenant boundary on the path. Canonical inline pattern: read the row's
`org_id`, reject with `"…not found"` when it ≠ `profile.org_id` (same message for foreign +
missing → no existence leak). Findings-style child tables gate via the parent (`authorizeFindingResolution`).

**Three independent layers now protect tenant isolation** (all shipped 2026-07-10):
1. **App-layer checks** — unit-tested, PRIMARY enforcement. Inline org assert per action.
2. **CI gate (the enforcement)** — `scripts/check-cross-tenant-guards.mjs`, npm `check:cross-tenant`,
   a **hard step in `.github/workflows/ci.yml`**. It FAILS the build when an exported action/route
   uses `db()`/`createAdminClient()` filtered by an id with no ownership signal. Genuine cross-org /
   public / user-owned reads opt out with a `// @cross-tenant-ok: <reason>` marker (grep-checked).
   Recognized ownership signals: `org_id`, `authorizeFindingResolution(`, `assertProjectOwnership(`,
   `…InScope(`, `…InCallerOrg(`, `…BelongsToOrg(`, or the marker. **A new leak can't merge silently.**
3. **RLS policies** — DB-layer backstop, now complete on all tenant tables (migrations 00076 closed
   the KB `FOR ALL USING(true)` hole; 00077 filled write-policy gaps + tightened `compliance_findings`
   open INSERT). `get_user_org_id()` returns the SINGLE active org (migration 00059).

**Shared helper:** `src/lib/auth/ownership.ts` → `projectBelongsToOrg(projectId, orgId)`.

**History (all Done):** SCRUM-340 (first 7 leaks) → SCRUM-342 Phase A (27-leak sweep, PR #97) →
SCRUM-343 Phase B (the gate + 11 more leaks the gate found, PR #98) → SCRUM-344 spike (RLS backstop
completed; **read-path code migration DELIBERATELY NOT pursued** — the 3 layers already suffice, and
swapping ~20 REGULATED files to the RLS client would delete tested protection for marginal gain; memo
at `docs/SCRUM-344-rls-migration-spike.md`).

**Found by adversarial review + the gate, NOT normal tests** — unit/integration tests run as the
resource OWNER, never cross-tenant (same blind spot as [[project_beta_role_upload_rls_fix]]). When
adding a server action, add a foreign-org test case AND make sure the gate stays green.
Related: [[project_operator_vs_org_admin_gating]], [[project_ai_router_and_honest_error_standards]].

candidates.title: Two non-interchangeable id conventions in MMC Build's schema: beta_feedback.user_id = auth user id, but run tables' created_by = profiles.id (profile PK). Plus
candidates.material:
---
name: reference_mmcbuild_id_conventions
description: "Two non-interchangeable id conventions in MMC Build's schema: beta_feedback.user_id = auth user id, but run tables' created_by = profiles.id (profile PK). Plus the multi-org activity-stamping gotcha."
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: reference
  originSessionId: d447830a-a9a0-4dc7-be51-003e6e7d0edb
---

**Two id conventions in the MMC Build schema — NOT interchangeable** (verified against live DB `lztzyfeivpsbqbsfzctw` 2026-06-17):

- **`beta_feedback.user_id`** = the **auth user id** (`profiles.user_id` / `auth.users.id`).
- **Run tables' `created_by`** (`compliance_checks`, `design_checks`, `cost_estimates`, also `plans`, `projects`) = the **profile PK** (`profiles.id`), **NOT** the auth user id.

So to join a run row to a person you must go `created_by → profiles.id → profiles.user_id`. Treating `created_by` as an auth id silently matches nothing — counts hit phantom keys and every real user shows 0 runs (no error, just wrong numbers). Build a `userIdByProfileId` map from a full `profiles` fetch (`select id,user_id,...`) and translate before attributing.

**Multi-org activity-stamping gotcha:** activity rows (`beta_feedback.org_id`, run `org_id`) are stamped with the **active** org at the time, which is not always the actor's **home** org (`profiles.org_id`). E.g. Karen's main account `karen.engel@mmcbuild.com.au` has home org `449db4d1` but her 5-module beta feedback + ~20 runs are stamped to the **MMC Build** org `71d9fefc`. So any per-org activity view must build its subject list as the **UNION** of (profiles with org_id = target) + (distinct actors in beta_feedback/run tables for that org) — listing by `profiles.org_id` alone orphans real activity. See [[project_multi_org_membership_required]].

First consumer: the `/admin/beta-activity` page (PR #47, **MERGED to main + live in prod** 2026-06-17, commit `84bcb01`) — admin-only per-tester view (last sign-in + per-module beta status/rating/feedback + real run counts), org-scoped, linked from Admin Dashboard → Operations → Beta Activity.

candidates.title: Where MMC Build client-call recordings and transcripts actually live (~/Downloads, not the repo) — and the naming quirks that make them hard to grep for.
candidates.material:
---
name: reference_mmcbuild_meeting_transcripts
description: "Where MMC Build client-call recordings and transcripts actually live (~/Downloads, not the repo) — and the naming quirks that make them hard to grep for."
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: reference
  originSessionId: 530edc3b-5673-4252-b018-ce864bb7fed7
  modified: 2026-08-06T13:05:16.836Z
---

MMC Build client-call recordings + transcripts land in **`~/Downloads`**, NOT in the repo. Only one
older call was ever copied into the repo (`docs/MMCBUILD ZOOM/`, 2026-06-25) — so "check the repo"
finds the wrong meeting and looks like the transcript doesn't exist.

Known: **`~/Downloads/mmc build 29 uly transcript.txt`** (2026-07-29 call — the trial/billing +
3D-off + HubSpot decisions) with `audio1232725669.m4a` / `video1232725669.mp4` alongside.

**Naming quirks that defeat a glob:** the filename is typo'd (`29 uly`, not `29 july`), lowercase,
space-separated, and the audio/video siblings are named only by a numeric id — so `*july*` and
`*Zoom*` both miss. Find them by **date-sorting Downloads** (`ls -lt ~/Downloads | head -20`) around
the call date rather than by name.

The transcript is ASR output: it garbles terms (`CDA` = CTA, `Superbase` = Supabase) and carries a
generated summary in the **first ~20 lines** that is a reliable fast index into the decisions. Grep
it for topic keywords, then read ±100 lines for context — decisions get **reversed mid-discussion**
(see [[project_session_2026_07_30_golive]] for the trial cut-off→auto-charge reversal), so the
first statement on a topic is often not the settled one.

Also known: **`~/Downloads/mmc build zoom 5 august/`** (2026-08-05 call, 87 min — the go-live call:
case-studies/testimonials hiding, HubSpot-vs-Supabase data ownership, the BPMN request). Transcribed
to `out/mmc-5-august.txt` + `out/mmc-5-august-timestamped.txt`.

## Transcribing these locally — the working path, and two silent failures

**Use `C:\Users\denni\transcribe_mmc_fast.py`** (faster-whisper, offline). 87 min of audio → ~25 min
wall clock on the 20-core i7-13700H. Point `AUDIO` at the new file and run it.

Two failure modes here are **silent** — no error, no traceback, the process just stops:

1. **The `whisper` CLI segfaults** on this machine and exits with no output at all.
2. **`openai-whisper`'s `load_model("small")` dies** because `~/.cache/whisper/small.pt` is a
   **partial 51 MB download** (should be ~461 MB), left by an interrupted fetch. The log stops at
   `loading model` and never reaches `model loaded` — which reads exactly like "still running".

`faster-whisper`'s small model IS fully cached (`models--Systran--faster-whisper-small`), so running
it with `local_files_only=True` sidesteps both — no network, so a flaky connection can't stall it.
`medium.pt` is also fully downloaded if accuracy matters more than speed, but that's the slow path.

Launch it **detached** (`Start-Process -WindowStyle Hidden`), not as a child of the shell — a run
started in-session dies when the session closes, which is how ~10 min was lost on 2026-08-06.

Quality note: `small` garbles proper nouns (`Kathik` = Karthik, `SuperBase` = Supabase) on top of the
ASR quirks above. Good enough to recover decisions; not good enough to quote verbatim.

Decisions that matter get lifted into the repo as a PRD + a Jira ticket — the transcript is the
source, never the record. See [[feedback_client_comms_approval]].

The in-process discovery (`src/lib/discovery/runner.ts` → `brave.ts` / `email-finder.ts` / `unipile.ts` / `scorer.ts`) is fully wired to the `@caistech` substrate and all provider keys are present in the pipeline Vercel env. It is a **2-channel contact base**: Brave→Hunter/Apollo gives EMAIL contacts (discarded if uncontactable — `scorer.ts:138` "Brave discard contract": out-of-scope OR no email OR no name → discard); Unipile LinkedIn People search gives LINKEDIN contacts (source==='linkedin' is EXEMPT from the email-discard, kept with profile). Outreach is channel-typed: `linkedin_connect` / `linkedin_dm` / `email` (format tied to channel).

**Why sayfix discovery returned 0 prospects despite "completed" (diagnosed 2026-06-16):**
- **Brave: working** — 153 candidates, real AU agency domains (23digital.com.au, acidgreen.com.au, iconagency.com.au…). Domain quality is fine.
- **Hunter (primary email-finder): account RESTRICTED** — key is valid (`/account` 200, Starter 0/2000) but `domain-search` returns `429 restricted_account: "Your account was restricted. Please log in to Hunter."` → no email for any domain. **Operator must clear the restriction at hunter.io** (account-side; can't be fixed via API).
- **Apollo (fallback): working** — found a real contact for intercom.com via the cascade, but coverage skews US/large-company, so small AU agencies fall through. So all 30 Brave candidates were uncontactable → discarded.
- **Unipile (LinkedIn): was MISCONFIGURED, now FIXED.** `UNIPILE_ACCOUNT_ID` had been set to the DSN/base-url `api44.unipile.com:17412` instead of a real account id, so LinkedIn search ran against a non-existent account → 0 people (silently). The 3 real connected accounts (all "Dennis McMahon", status OK) are `1U9qmI8zRdeMN_nuFx7ZNg` / `Htd8N98cQx-fM2Tb9yfqGA` / `Oxdl-iGETSahibgYntZJRQ`. **Fixed** to `1U9qmI8z…` in both pipeline Vercel projects (prod+preview, sensitive) + local .env.local; redeploy be95e52. Verified: `searchLinkedInPeople` then returns 10 real on-ICP agency owners.

**UPDATE 2026-06-16 — both channels now flow.**
- **Hunter: CLEARED** (operator paid → restriction lifted). `domain-search` returns 200 + emails (verified ruchir@23digital.com.au etc.). Email channel works.
- **LinkedIn: the account-id fix was necessary but NOT sufficient.** Two more bugs in `runner.ts` (fixed PR #15, commit 4ca7909): (1) **timeout** — Unipile's live LinkedIn search takes **25-40s/query**; the runner capped ALL searches at `SEARCH_TIMEOUT_MS=15s` → every LinkedIn search timed out → `[]` → 0 candidates, invisibly (timeout ≠ counted failure). Added `LINKEDIN_SEARCH_TIMEOUT_MS=45_000` (fn maxDuration=300s). (2) **cap truncation** — Brave runs first (~150 rows), LinkedIn appended after; dedup Map insertion-order + `slice(0,30)` filled all 30 cap slots with Brave → LinkedIn truncated before scoring. Now round-robin interleave (LinkedIn-first) before cap. (3) `top_prospects` hardcoded `source:'brave_search'` → fixed to real source.
- **Verified (sayfix):** scored 3→18, discarded 27→12, **10 email + 15 LinkedIn** real agency owners (scores to 7.3).

**KEY DISTINCTION:** discovery (find+score prospects) runs WITHOUT Gate 1 — build the contact graph anytime. But **outreach INVITE generation** (`/api/methodology/cards/[slug]/outreach/generate` → `outbound_messages`) is **Gate-1-gated** (requires `card.mvp_url` + `mvp_ready`, since the invite embeds the MVP link) AND is a **separate manual step nothing auto-triggers after discovery**. sayfix has `mvp_url=null, mvp_ready=false` → Outreach tab correctly empty. candidates.title: Prelabz investor portal — how access is granted, why roles are capabilities not identities, and why every cross-founder read must be a service-role route
candidates.material:
---
name: project_prelabz_investor_portal
description: "Prelabz investor portal — how access is granted, why roles are capabilities not identities, and why every cross-founder read must be a service-role route"
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: 6701dc1e-3323-4588-bd0d-f2f49d7a8d6b
  modified: 2026-08-05T06:10:35.398Z
---

**There is no investor signup.** `app/(auth)/signup/page.tsx` says so in a
comment: *"Founder-only signup — investor signup is disabled; admins are created
manually."* `/portal/*` requires `user_roles.role = 'portal_admin'`, and
`user_roles` is RLS-locked to own-row SELECT with no client INSERT — so the row
can only be written with the service role, by hand. If someone "can't get into
the investor portal", this is almost always why: there was never a path.

**Three separate surfaces, often conflated when someone asks for "user and
admin" access:**
- founder app `/founder/*` — any authenticated user
- investor portal `/portal/*` — `portal_admin` row in `user_roles`
- operator console `/admin/*` — the `ADMIN_EMAILS` env allowlist (middleware)

**Roles are CAPABILITIES, not one exclusive identity** (fixed 2026-08-05,
`hooks/use-auth.ts`). `getUserRole` used to resolve `portal_admin` first and
return a single winning role, so granting someone the portal silently threw them
off every `/founder/*` page — they gained the portal and lost the founder app,
with no way to hold both. Now `getUserRoles` returns a Set: everyone
authenticated holds `'founder'`, `portal_admin` is additive. `userRole` still
reports the primary role so `watchlist-button` / `project-card` branch as
before. **Before granting `portal_admin` to someone who is also a founder,
confirm this fix is deployed** or you will lock them out of the founder side.

**Every cross-founder read MUST be a service-role route.** `founders`,
`pitch_decks` (and anything joined off them) are RLS-scoped to the owning
founder, so a browser query from an investor returns nothing — which reads as a
missing feature, not a permission model working correctly. This has now bitten
three surfaces:
- `/admin/users`, `/admin/cohort` → `/api/admin/founders` (gated `isAdminEmail`)
- `/portal/dashboard` pipeline → `/api/portal/submissions` (gated `portal_admin`)
- `/portal/watchlist` → `/api/portal/watchlist` (gated `portal_admin`) — here the
  watchlist ROW read fine and only the embedded `founders(...)`/`pitch_decks(...)`
  joins came back empty, which is easy to misread as "no data"

Pattern for new portal reads: service-role client, role checked with the USER's
client (own-row SELECT only, so it can't be steered), **explicit narrow column
list — never `select('*')`** (the founders table carries phone numbers and full
narrative answers an investor has no need for, and a wildcard leaks every future
column), and `is_latest` on decks so a re-uploading founder appears once.

**Who has access (2026-08-05):** Stephen Munich `munich.stephen@gmail.com`,
Daniel Maneveld `danjmaneveld@gmail.com` (created by Supabase invite), Alex Vo
`alexphanvo@yahoo.com`, plus `dennis@corporateaisolutions.com`. All three new
ones are also in `ADMIN_EMAILS` (added as a SEPARATE `ADMIN_EMAILS` var —
`lib/auth/admin-emails.ts` merges `ADMIN_EMAILS` + legacy `ADMIN_EMAIL`, so the
existing sensitive/non-readable `ADMIN_EMAIL` was left untouched rather than
rewritten from a possibly-stale local copy).

**⚠️ Alex Vo has TWO accounts:** founder `hello.prelabz@gmail.com`, investor
`alexphanvo@yahoo.com`. Dennis refers to the investor one as
`alexphanvo@gmail.com` — that address does not exist; yahoo is the live one.

See [[project_prelabz_architecture]].

The **Pipeline Gate** (APPROVED design: `~/.gstack/projects/SayFix/dennis-stage-0-foundation-design-20260526-190028.md`) turns the factory's gates from advisory docs into execution-path enforcement. Built + live as of 2026-05-26.

**If a turn gets "blocked" when you try to hand over a `*.vercel.app` product URL, that is the gate working, not a bug.** A Stop hook (`cais-shared-services/hooks/url-share-gate.mjs`, wired as the 3rd Stop hook in `~/.claude/settings.json` — NOT tracked in any repo) refuses to let the turn end unless a `/naive-tester` PASS is recorded for what production is *currently serving*. To clear it: run `/naive-tester` against the production URL, fix any ❌, then `node cais-shared-services/scripts/gate-check.mjs record <slug> naive-tester pass --deployment <live-id> --commit <sha> --artifact <report>`. The hook fails **closed** (any error → blocked) and fails **open** for non-product/unknown URLs.

**Pieces (all committed):** the ledger is `pipeline_gates` in the cockpit Supabase (`tfgtfhwvrswjvkyeyvsp`, Corporate-AI-Solutions). `gate-check.mjs` is the shared dependency-free accessor (`hasGatePassed`/`recordGate`/`getLiveProductionDeployment` + CLI: `url-share-allowed`, `scale-infra-allowed`). **Delta 2:** a naive-tester PASS binds to the LIVE production *deployment id*, not git HEAD — a stale build or env-only regression (broken sender) invalidates it. **Delta 1:** `scale-infra-allowed` blocks multi-tenant/billing/white-label/domain without a Gate-2 GO; the thin-MVP creator runs free (the thin MVP = full experience, single-tenant, zero scale-infra — see [[thin-mvp-bright-line]]).

Design doc Approach A, steps 1–7 (steps 0/0b = the convai adoption + gpt-4.1-mini, already done). Commits `11319cd` (P1+2) + `24c6ec8` (P3+4). typecheck clean; migration applied to live SayFix DB.

Flow: benefit-first question ("Want me to let you know when this is fixed?") → name/email up-front-but-skippable → cookie-keyed `visitors` row (extend, don't add a table) → session-bound greeting from SayFix's OWN durable `visitors`/`tickets` (not the hub's purgeable anon memory) → `sayfix-nudges` email on state change → consent + a real `/privacy` page (also closes a naive-tester trust gap). Plan to list SayFix on the **Semrush App Center** (marketplace of installed marketing/SEO SaaS
apps at semrush.com/apps — a meta-distributor pointed straight at SayFix's ICP: agencies + SMB
site-owners). Explored 2026-07-14; not yet built.

## The integration contract (confirmed from Semrush's own JS SDK docs)
- **iframe + JWT app.** SayFix renders *inside* Semrush's UI in an iframe. No OAuth, no Stripe, no
  SayFix login for these users.
- **Auth:** load Semrush JS SDK → `SM.init()` → `SM.client('getAccessToken')` returns a 5-min JWT
  you **verify server-side with `SEMRUSH_APP_SECRET`**. JWT fields: `aud` (app id), `viewer_id`
  (the customer id — **shared across a corporate account's sub-users → this is the SayFix tenant
  key**), `is_main_product_active` (purchased/trial → gate features on this), `active_products`
  (in-app purchases, each with a `value` count), `is_main_product_trial_available`, etc.
- **Billing is Semrush's, not yours.** Paywall + payment page = `SM.client('requestMainProductPurchase')`;
  add-ons/per-site = `requestInAppPurchase`. You just gate on the JWT booleans. **This forces a
  flat SKU** (no value-slider possible) — which resolves the "flat vs value-pricing" tension: the
  own-site value model stays on sayfix's own site; Semrush is a forced-flat channel.
- **Emails** can ride Semrush's rail (`requestEmailReports` / `requestEmailSubscriptionChange`) — no
  Resend/Spam-Act footer to manage for these users.
- **Design:** use Semrush's **Intergalactic** React design system (MIT) so the embed looks native
  (directly fixes the "screams AI-made" concern — see [[sayfix-design-brief-shah]]).
- **Registration is email-gated, NOT self-serve:** dev account → `partnerteam@semrush.com`; register
  app → `app-center@semrush.com` (they create the app record, hand you `SEMRUSH_APP_ID` /
  `SEMRUSH_APP_SECRET`, and set your test-app iframe URL, e.g. to localhost). Sample app:
  github.com/semrush/app-center-sample-app.

## Structure: ONE Semrush listing (no-code only); coded → GitHub Marketplace
**REVISED 2026-07-14** after reading Semrush's Security Requirements + a codebase map. Original plan
was two capability-split listings on Semrush (no-code $99 + developer $149). **The Developer listing
was cut from Semrush** for two independent reasons:
1. Semrush's **"users mustn't be forced to integrate third-party accounts"** rule → GitHub-App
   connect needs Semrush **Legal pre-approval**.
2. The existing GitHub callback (`src/app/api/github/app/callback/route.ts:22`) **binds install→tenant
   via the Supabase COOKIE session** — which the **cookie-free** Semrush iframe (see security rules)
   doesn't have → it's a rebuild, not a reuse.
GitHub connect is native on **GitHub Marketplace** anyway, so the coded auto-fix product ships there
as separate scope.
- **Semrush = "SayFix for No-Code Sites"** (Wix/WordPress/Squarespace/Shopify/Framer) — *diagnosis +
  steps*, ~**$99/mo**. Collects only a website URL (not PII) → clean under the no-PII rule.
- Marketplace rule that drove all this = **the listing sets the promise; never resolve it after the
  click** (no bait-and-switch — Dennis 2026-07-14).
- **Hybrid (Framer + coded app) = the Semrush no-code app + the GitHub-Marketplace coded app**, two
  purchases, per the "register each surface as its own site" model ([[sayfix-mixed-stack-install-gap]]).
- Detection guardrail **deferred** — platform auto-detection doesn't exist in the code
  (`website_type` is user-declared), and it matters little for a single-purpose listing.

## Semrush SECURITY requirements (hard gates, from the Jan-2025 App Requirements doc)
- **JWT-only auth, NO cookies/localStorage.** AJAX must work cookie-free; pass `getAccessToken` JWT
  as an HTTP header, verified **server-side every request**. SayFix's normal app is Supabase-cookie →
  the `/embed/semrush/*` surface is a **fully separate cookie-free auth path** (the spine of the build).
- **App restricted to Semrush** — must 401 outside the iframe / when JWT expires (5-min `exp`).
- **NO PII forms** — no email/phone/CC collection; no forced 3rd-party account integration (this is
  what killed the coded listing on Semrush).
- **CSP `frame-ancestors https://*.semrush.com`** (header, not meta), Referrer-Policy
  (strict-origin-when-cross-origin / no-referrer), `Cache-Control: no-store` on data pages, HTTPS/TLS.
- **"Scripts" review track** applies because the widget installs on the customer site → the
  `@caistech/sayfix-embed` script must be documented, **un-obfuscated**, declared network sources,
  minimized collection → **longer review, submit early**.
- Ops: 2FA on the Semrush dev account; vuln-fix SLA (Critical 2 business days … Low 3 months); 14-char
  internal passwords.

## Codebase map (verified 2026-07-14) — reuse vs build
Baseline: Next **16.2.6** App Router, Supabase SSR, Stripe. **Almost everything reusable.**
- **REUSE:** ticket pipeline convergence `createTicketCore` (`src/lib/tickets/create.ts:56`); tenant
  provisioning reference `/api/beta/signup` (`src/app/api/beta/signup/route.ts`); monitoring = set
  `repos.health_url` → `/api/cron/sensors` + `raiseSensorTicket` pick it up; billing gate
  `tenantBillingLapsed` (`src/lib/billing.ts:54`); `github_owner='embed'` = no-code tell;
  `tenants.site_key` publishable key.
- **BUILD NEW:** (1) no JWT lib in tree → add `jose` + `src/lib/semrush/verify.ts` (HS256 verify with
  `SEMRUSH_APP_SECRET`, check `aud`=`SEMRUSH_APP_ID` + `exp`); (2) no `/embed/*` page group → new
  `src/app/embed/semrush/` pages; (3) middleware allowlist `/embed/semrush` + `/api/embed/semrush`
  from the Supabase cookie gate (`middleware.ts:39-68`) + JWT check before line 39;
  (4) `provisionSemrushTenant()` idempotent on `viewer_id`; (5) Semrush `plan`/`billing_status` values
  so `tenantBillingLapsed` stays green (Semrush bills, not Stripe).
Spec doc: `docs/SAYFIX_SEMRUSH_NOCODE_ADAPTER_SPEC.md`.

## Auto-detection = GUARDRAIL, not router
Corrected mid-discussion: don't silently route by detected stack (that IS a surprise). The listing
is the door; the domain-probe just **confirms** they chose right, and on mismatch says so plainly
(*"this looks like WordPress — you probably want SayFix for No-Code Sites →"*) and links the other
listing. Reuse existing stack-detection (health-probe + `github_owner='embed'` tell); good forcing
function to replace the manual `website_type` question with detection portfolio-wide.

## Pricing rationale (Dennis: "don't undersell")
Semrush store bands: **floor $35–59 = commodity AI generators** (content/video/social); **serious-tool
band $69–129 = revenue-protecting monitoring/intelligence** (AI Website Testing $69 [direct analog],
Brand Monitoring $79, SERP Gap $99, CallRail $125); **premium $169–349** (Crazy Egg $249, AdClarity
$349). SayFix = revenue-protection, **NOT** a generator → belongs in the serious-tool band, above the
$69 AI Website Testing analog (SayFix does more: continuous monitoring + intake + diagnosis). The
own-site **$19 must NEVER appear on Semrush** — reads as unserious next to a buyer already paying
Semrush $140–500/mo. Every app leads with a **free trial + premium sticker** (matches SayFix's 14-day
beta). Launch $79–99, raise with reviews. Coded auto-fix has **no comparable on the shelf** (nothing
else *fixes* your code) → price it freely at $149+. Semrush takes an (unpublished) **revenue-share
cut** — get the % from the partner agreement; price with headroom.

Next: `/spec` the two-front-door embed adapter (JWT session vs Supabase split · viewer_id→tenant
provisioning · detection guardrail · dual setup paths). Only Tier-C-style no-code + the coded
link-out fit; see [[sayfix-onboarding-tiers-and-mnemo]], [[sayfix-beta-funnel]].

TenderWatch submission pipeline (the a–f vision: link portal creds → set watch criteria → pull tenders + download docs → score relevance → draft the submission → submit). Built 2026-06-23/24; full plan + per-task status (T0–T10) in repo `SUBMISSION_PIPELINE_PLAN.md`.

**⭐ ONBOARDING-FRICTION REDUCERS SHIPPED 2026-07-09 (Tier 1 + Tier 2, both LIVE on prod main).** The must-write sections (capability/experience/personnel/insurance/referees — held EMPTY as `needs_you` per legal #7) were a blank-amber-box drop-off. Two fixes, both #7-safe (sections stay `needs_you`, attestation gate unchanged):
- **Tier 1 — guided scaffold** (commit 0376445): `mustWriteScaffold(title)` in `packages/processor/src/draft.ts` (pure, unit-tested) seeds each must-write section with a category-tailored BRACKETED template ("• Project 1 — client, value, year …") instead of "". A prompt, never a claim. Wired in `draft-submission.ts` create-sections.
- **Tier 2 — self-populate from the bidder's website** (commit 531b194): **consumes `@caistech/extractors`** (`extractProfile`, the shared business-profile extractor — `@caistech`-first, installed via the .npmrc GitHub-Packages token; do NOT re-fork a scraper). `packages/processor/src/profile-draft.ts` = `extractBusinessProfile(url)` + `draftSectionFromProfile()` (grounds each section STRICTLY on extracted facts, `[bracketed placeholders]` for gaps, verify banner, invents nothing). New **`enrich-submission` Inngest fn** (`packages/jobs/src/enrich-submission.ts`) fills only still-`needs_you` must-write sections; `enrichFromWebsite` server action (ownership-checked, URL-validated); editor "Start your about-your-business sections from your website" panel. ⚠️ **enrich-submission is a NEW Inngest fn → required the PUT re-sync** (`curl -X PUT .../api/webhooks/inngest` → `modified:true`, done 2026-07-09). **LIVE-VERIFIED against real sites** (factory2key.com.au + 6 more AU business sites): the extraction+drafting works and #7 holds (grounds strictly on site facts, `[bracketed placeholders]` for gaps incl. a clean insurance template when the site has none). **The go-live forced a real fix** (commit 228aeab): the extractor's DEFAULT bot UA ("StoreFrontMCP-Audit") + 10s timeout FAIL on real sites — `extractBusinessProfile` must pass a **browser-like UA + 20s timeout + 3× retry** (the fetch is intermittently slow; two of the multi-site successes only got through on retry). **Real-world extraction rate ~60–70% first-try** (7-site sweep: 4 ✅ / 3 ❌ — nulls on JS-heavy/large sites that fetch 200 but yield little text, + one genuinely-slow site). **Fails SAFE by design:** a null extraction leaves the Tier-1 scaffold in place + surfaces an error — the user is never worse off. Do NOT patch `@caistech/extractors` here to chase JS-rendered sites (portfolio-wide change, not a fork). Sample outputs + the reliability table live in `docs/tier2-extraction-samples.md`. web tsc + 29 processor tests green.

**⭐ REACHABILITY + MOBILE-NAV SHIPPED 2026-07-05 (naive-tester PASS, URL gate cleared).** Drafted submissions were unreachable once you left the editor — no nav entry, no list route. Added: `/dashboard/submissions/page.tsx` (list, owner-scoped `getSubmissions()` joins tender + rolls up section progress) + a "Submissions" sidebar item (commit 32a87ef). The `/naive-tester` run against that deploy then found the app had **NO mobile navigation** (sidebar is `hidden md:block`, no hamburger) — a HARD §1 fail — plus a chain of 375px horizontal-overflow bugs. Fixed across 3 commits (e67f610, 44f1321, 2807a2f): new `components/dashboard/mobile-nav.tsx` (hamburger→left drawer, same links via shared `components/dashboard/nav-items.ts` that the desktop `sidebar.tsx` now also consumes) + killed 4 same-class overflows by adding `min-w-0` to flex/grid items that couldn't shrink (`<main>`, submissions cards, dashboard grid, watches card left column — the "regions" string `ACT, NSW, …` was the widest). **Final naive-tester PASS 2026-07-05** on deploy `dpl_9xG116uD…`: all 7 authed pages 375==375, mobile nav present → gate-check recorded (id c3ac5e4d) → URL-share gate CLEARED. **Lesson: grid/flex items default to `min-width:auto` and won't shrink below content — long unbreakable strings blow out the viewport; `min-w-0` on the item is the fix.** ⚠️ The editor's live VISUAL render is still only headless-verifiable when the renderer doesn't crash (it did earlier, didn't in the final runs). Portal/source coverage has **NO Tasmania** (7 sources: austender/nsw/qld/vic/sa/wa/tenderlink; TAS/NT/ACT are region filters only, no adapter).

**⭐ SMOKE-VERIFIED 2026-07-05 (axes A+B, the "finishing" pass).** Confirmed the drafter output persists correctly in prod + the RLS read path is live, WITHOUT a working browser. Champion (`dennis@factory2key.com.au`, user_id `6a8a4d91-19bd-44eb-b6a2-c9498abb5c33`) has **1 submission `934e8e88-c33c-435e-95a2-57ca8903812a`** (water-treatment tender "Disinfection Upgrades at Seymour-Cobram-Murchison WTP", status `draft`): **20 sections — 15 LLM-drafted (1748–2469 chars each), 5 must-write held EMPTY** (`needs_you`, 0 chars: Capability Statement / Relevant Experience / Key Personnel / Insurance Details / Referee Details) = the #7 legal guardrail holding. **RLS live on prod:** `submissions` RLS ENABLED + 4 owner-scoped policies (`auth.uid()::text = user_id`); `submission_sections` RLS ENABLED + 3 policies gated via EXISTS on the parent submission. Read-only helpers left in `scripts/`: `check-submissions.mjs`, `check-submission-rls.mjs` (reuse smoke-draft.mjs's postgres-js + `NODE_TLS_REJECT_UNAUTHORIZED=0` env-key pattern). **⚠️ STILL OPERATOR-ONLY: the editor's VISUAL render (two-pane, amber must-write, attestation gate) is unverified** — headless `/browse` Chromium CRASHES (`Target crashed`) on TenderWatch's authenticated pages (login→dashboard settle AND the expanded match panel), same class as the documented voice-widget WebRTC crash but broader. Login worked + 11 matched VIC tenders rendered + the match card DID expand before the renderer died; the click-through-to-editor + editor paint need a real browser (operator or `$B handoff`).

**⭐ UPDATE 2026-07-05 — the DRAFTER CORE (gap e) is REVIVED onto main + LIVE + PROVEN in prod.** The branch `fix/rls-and-auth` was 28 commits stale, so I LIFTED the drafter onto current main (branch `feat/submission-drafter` → merged, commit a9f1259) rather than merge the stale branch. **Deferred the doc-download/PDF/LLM-scoring pipeline (T2–T6)** — the draft job reads the tender's OWN `full_text`/`description`, so it works without downloaded docs; doc-enrichment is a clean follow-on. Migrations 0001+0002 applied to prod. **End-to-end smoke-proven:** "Draft submission" on a tender → `startDraft` → `submission/draft` Inngest job → `extractRequirements` produced 20 real sections for a water-treatment construction tender → 15 LLM-drafted (~28KB) + **5 must-write sections (capability/experience/personnel/insurance/referees) correctly held EMPTY as `needs_you`** (legal #7 guardrail). Two-pane editor + attestation gate wired. **TWO GOTCHAS fixed in the go-live (remember these):** (1) the hardcoded model `claude-sonnet-4-20250514` is RETIRED (Anthropic 404s it — this was the FIRST code to actually call Claude in prod; `generateSummary` was built-but-never-called) → bumped all 4 call sites (draft×2, score, summarizer) to `claude-sonnet-5`; (2) **adding an Inngest function requires a MANUAL re-sync after deploy** — `curl -X PUT https://tenderwatch-alpha.vercel.app/api/webhooks/inngest` (the serve route is `/api/webhooks/inngest`, NOT `/api/inngest`); a code-only change needs no re-sync, but a new function in `functions[]` does or the event fires into the void (0 handler). Still OPEN (drafter follow-ons): doc-download pipeline (T2–T6), the RLS client policies for the `/dashboard/submissions` UI (jobs write via service role today), and a browser smoke of the editor UI itself.

- **Gaps a–e were BUILT + unit-tested (51 tests green) on branch `fix/rls-and-auth`** (a preview deploy, SSO-walled). Gap e (drafter) now on prod per the update above; a–d doc pipeline still branch-only. (f) auto-submit deliberately deferred (TODOS #7: post-20-paying-customers; manual lodgement is v1).
- Prod Supabase DB is fully provisioned for it: T5a dup-index `tenders(source,source_id)` + T7 `submissions`/`submission_sections` tables + enums + RLS policies + the private `tender-docs` Storage bucket — all applied (migrations in `packages/db/manual-migrations/0001*,0002*`).
- **Why kept off prod:** the pipeline rewrites `process-tender.ts` + `sync-account.ts` behaviour and needs a live end-to-end verification round (link a portal → sync → docs download+extract → score → click Draft → editor) before going live for the champion.
- **How to take it live:** merge `fix/rls-and-auth` → main AFTER verifying on the preview. Needs Vercel **Preview** env to match prod (DATABASE_URL with the working pooler pw + `CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY`). T1 crypto was already wired (validate-account encrypts); it only needed `CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY` in env.
- **Open follow-ups (tracked, not blocking):** (1) voice agent §6 — NOT built, needs ElevenLabs provisioning, recorded as an accepted exception in the naive-tester gate; (2) **T0 adapter enrichment** — `AusTenderAdapter.fetchTenderDetail` hardcodes empty `regions`/`categories` + no `fullText`, so region-filtered watches under-match and scoring runs near-blind until adapters are enriched (T3 backfills `fullText` from downloaded docs, partial mitigation); (3) LLM evals for the score + draft prompts; (4) sync-path session-reuse (download job reuses cookies, sync job still re-logs-in); (5) `ABR_GUID` is now set in Vercel (ABN lookup works).
- The naive-tester URL-share gate was **cleared 2026-06-24** by shipping 9 production marketing/auth polish fixes to main (mobile hamburger nav, auth 44px/16px + toggle aria-label, magic-link, `/how-it-works`+`/about` content, favicon, post-signup `/check-email` screen, Agency white-label pricing tier, ABN→ABR lookup) — separate from the pipeline. candidates.title: 1. Before you spend a tester run
candidates.material:
## 1. Before you spend a tester run

A run that reports defects a five-minute script would have caught has been half wasted, and the
findings that matter get buried under them.

- [ ] **Gate zero — is production serving the code you think it is?**
      `npx portfolio-gate-deploy-status --public-url <prod> --app-marker "<Product>"`.
      A stale production is *healthy*: it returns 200 all day. Only comparing the deployed commit
      SHA to your ref exposes it. Testing a build that is not the one you changed produces findings
      nobody can act on and "repeats" that were never fixed because they were never deployed.
- [ ] **Walk the whole user path yourself, once, end to end.** Landing → the primary action → the
      result → the paywall/gate → the first authenticated screen. At **375px and 1440px**. Submit
      one real input at every step, including any text box.
- [ ] **Open every page behind a primary CTA and count the seconds to first content.** Blank-then-
      appear is indistinguishable from broken, and a tester will (correctly) report it as broken.
- [ ] **Grep for the class of anything you changed.** Changed a price? Grep every price string.
      Changed a tax label? Grep every tax label. Changed a policy? Grep every statement of it.
- [ ] **Re-read the diff's surrounding screen, not just the diff.** The defects cluster at the joins
      between what you changed and what you did not.

candidates.title: 2.2 Proving PRESENCE and reporting FUNCTION
candidates.material:
### 2.2 Proving PRESENCE and reporting FUNCTION

A voice widget was added and reported as *"launcher × 2, panel × 1 — the voice agent is live."* Both
numbers were true. The widget's text fallback then **swallowed every question typed into it** —
input cleared, zero network requests, no answer, no error — because the package hands the text to an
optional `onTextFallbackSubmit` callback and clears the box regardless, and no handler had been
supplied.

`PRODUCT_STANDARDS` §6 already says the voice gate is *"behavioural, not presence-only."* The rule
was known, quoted that same day, and applied as presence-only anyway.

> **Rule.** Rendering is not working. If a control accepts input, submit input and assert the
> **response**. If it makes a network call, assert the call happened.

candidates.title: | @caistech/mnemo | The ONE Mnemo client — transport only. Mnemo had been written FO
candidates.material: | `@caistech/mnemo` | **The ONE Mnemo client — transport only.** Mnemo had been written FOUR times before this existed (`planning-memory`, `scripts/bug-memory.mjs`, Kira's `lib/kira/mnemo.ts`, SayFix's `src/lib/mnemo.ts`) — all making the same two calls to `/v1/memories` and `/v1/search`, differing only in scope. So: **this package owns the TRANSPORT, each consumer owns its SCOPE POLICY** — deliberately, because the policies must NOT be unified (planning = shared + jurisdiction-keyed so depth compounds; bug-knowledge = one portfolio scope; voice = PER-USER isolation per DATA_STANDARD S2; SayFix = per-website). A single "correct" scope would break three of the four. `createMnemoClient({apiKey?, apiUrl?, label?, fetchImpl?})` → `enabled()` / `add(scope, contents)` / `search(scope, query, limit)`, plus `orgScope(id)` and `normaliseFact(text)` (duplicate detection — without it an append-every-conversation loop fills Mnemo with the same fact and recall degrades in a way that reads as the model getting worse). **FAIL-SOFT IS THE CONTRACT**: no key → `add` no-ops, `search` returns []; every network/parse error swallowed; never throws. Memory is an enhancement — an outage must degrade recall, never break the call path (DATA_STANDARD R4). Key resolved PER CALL, not at construction (a module built during `next build` has no env). Zero deps, native fetch. 14 tests. **v0.2.0 adds the verb a user-facing product needs: `find` + `forget`.** A product whose users can delete a fact could delete it everywhere EXCEPT here — Kira's owner removes a line from his Business Genome, it leaves the page, his recall and his export, and the dual-written copy in the semantic lane survived, so she could still bring it up in a later conversation. He would have taken it back from everything he could see and been wrong; for an owner whose most sensitive line is that he is selling and has told nobody, that is the product failing the one promise it makes about his privacy. `search` was throwing away the `memoryId` the API already returns, so nothing had a handle to act on — **`find(scope, query, limit)` keeps it** (`{id, content}[]`, dropping any result missing either half, since an id with no content cannot be confirmed and content with no id cannot be acted on) and **`forget(id)`** calls `DELETE /v1/memories/{id}`, which is Mnemo's SOFT delete inside a recoverable window — the same park-don't-drop posture the consumers already take, so a mistake is recoverable on both sides rather than one. A 404 counts as forgotten (the caller wanted it gone and it is gone; reporting failure turns an already-correct state into a retry loop). `search` is deliberately UNCHANGED — four consumers depend on its `string[]` return and a shared package earns its keep by not making them all edit. Fail-soft cuts both ways here: `forget` returns false rather than throwing, so a partial redaction is never reported to a user as done. 20 tests. |

candidates.title: | @caistech/subscription-billing | Stripe subscription lifecycle — the mechanics eve
candidates.material: | `@caistech/subscription-billing` | **Stripe subscription lifecycle** — the mechanics every product repeats, extracted so the PRICE and the TABLE stay product-local. `createSubscriptionCheckoutSession` (fixed `priceId` **or** dynamic `price_data` for server-computed pricing; `trialDays`; **`cardAtSignup` defaults TRUE** — with a trial + `if_required` Stripe creates the subscription with NO card and the first charge silently fails 30 days later) + `createBillingPortalSession`. `handleSubscriptionWebhook` = verify → **claim on `event.id`** → **out-of-order guard on `event.created`** vs the row's `last_stripe_event_at` → normalize → apply, returning a named `outcome` (`applied`/`duplicate`/`stale`/`subscriber_missing`/`ignored_type`/…) so "why didn't the subscription update?" is a one-line log answer. Handles checkout-completed (**retrieves the subscription so a trial records as `trialing`, not a flat `active`**), subscription created/updated/deleted, and invoice payment failed/succeeded; tolerates both pre- and post-2025-03 API shapes (`current_period_end` on the item, invoice→subscription under `parent.subscription_details`) so consumers needn't align SDK majors. **One deliberate departure from `api-key-auth`'s model: a failed apply RELEASES the claim** before returning 500 — otherwise Stripe's retry is answered "duplicate" and one transient DB error permanently drops the event. Products converge by CONFIG, not a second handler: `createSupabaseSubscriptionAdapter` is a column map + `extraColumns` projection (Kira `users.subscription_status` and LaunchReady `profiles.plan`/`stripe_subscription_status` are the same call with different maps); implement `SubscriptionAdapter` directly for anything the map can't express. Normalizes Stripe's `canceled` → the portfolio's **`cancelled`**. Ships `migration.sql` (`stripe_webhook_events`, RLS-on service-role-only) + 28 tests. **Built because the two pre-existing forks (Kira, LaunchReady) were BOTH non-idempotent and ordering-unsafe** — one redelivery from double-applying, one out-of-order event from resurrecting cancelled state. ⚠️ **Only Kira actually consumes it — LaunchReady still runs its own `app/api/stripe/*` fork** and is un-migrated debt, so "the other consumer" in older notes is aspirational, not a dependency. **v0.2.0 adds ARREARS — "you are never billed for the month you are in".** The period is owed from day one, invoiced when it CLOSES, and a cancellation before the bill falls due **waives** it. This is not `trialDays`, which is what a product reaches for first: the two are identical for thirty days and then invert — the day-30 charge buys days 30–60 under a trial and pays for days 0–30 under arrears, so a product that means arrears and ships a trial **under-bills by one month per customer, forever**. Passing both now throws. It could NOT be a flag on `DynamicPriceLineItem` as originally scoped: Checkout's inline `price_data.recurring` accepts only `interval`/`interval_count` — no `usage_type`, no `meter` — so the Price must exist *before* the session, which is `ensureMeteredPrice` (idempotent on a deterministic `lookup_key`, so a per-customer price doesn't mint a new Price object every checkout) over `ensureBillingMeter` (idempotent on `event_name` — two meters on one name silently SPLIT the usage). Legacy usage records are gone in Stripe ≥18, so this is Billing Meters; aggregation is `sum` (not `last`) to stay compilable on the stripe ≥17 peer floor, with double-reporting prevented by the event `identifier` + the caller's webhook idempotency instead. `reportPeriodOwed` **throws** on failure by design — an unreported period invoices **$0** against a subscription that looks entirely healthy, the silent-guard failure this portfolio has already been bitten by twice. `cancelWithWaiver` (`prorate:false` + `invoice_now:false` — `invoice_now` alone still collects prorations) exists as a NAMED function rather than two options set correctly at a call site, because an invoice landing after a customer cancelled and was told the month was on us is the failure the whole shape exists to make structurally impossible. +12 tests (40 total). **v0.3.0 adds the `/mode` subpath — the canonical TEST↔LIVE switch.** Both key sets live in env at once and going live is a **flag flip, not a key swap** (`STRIPE_LIVE_MODE=true`; anything else — typo, empty, missing — is TEST, because *the safe state should be the one you fall into by accident*), so it reverses in seconds under pressure. **Fail-closed in BOTH directions**, the part most implementations get half-right: live-mode-with-no-live-key **throws** instead of falling back to test (a fallback takes fake payments that look real and you learn from the bank statement), and test-mode-with-a-live-key-in-the-test-slot **also throws** (that direction charges real cards during a rehearsal). The webhook secret is mode-aware because test and live signing secrets **both start `whsec_`** — nothing in the string reveals a mismatch, so flipping the key without it means every webhook fails signature verification *silently* while checkout looks perfect. Lifted from Kira's `lib/billing/stripe-mode.ts` (the mature implementation; MMCBuild's one-key/no-mode `stripe/client.ts` is a migration target, not a source) plus **two halves Kira never needed and therefore never had**: (1) **`stripePriceId(name)`** — a Stripe `price_…` belongs to ONE mode, so a product holding fixed ids in single-slot vars keeps sending TEST prices after the flip and the live API answers `No such price` **at checkout, in front of a customer**. Resolves `STRIPE_PRICE_<NAME>_LIVE|_TEST` with a legacy `STRIPE_<NAME>_PRICE_ID` test fallback (adopt without renaming), **throws** on missing — never `?? ''`, which fails deep inside a Stripe call instead of at config time — and rejects a `prod_…` pasted where a `price_…` belongs. Kira dodged this entirely by pricing dynamically via `price_data`, which is why the pattern reached maturity **without the switch ever be

candidates.title: | @caistech/attribution | First-touch referral attribution for referrals that PAY some
candidates.material: | `@caistech/attribution` | **First-touch referral attribution for referrals that PAY someone.** Extracted from F2K-Projects' ROI portal — the portfolio's only implementation that could survive a commission dispute (every other variant was a capture-only `?ref=` tag: fine for analytics, unusable for deciding who gets paid). Three properties stop being optional once money rides on it: **tamper-evident** (HMAC-signed payload — nobody rewrites themselves into someone else's introduction from page JS), **first-touch wins** (`retainFirstTouch`/`shouldWrite` — the person who made the introduction is paid, not the last click), and **immutable once written** (`migration.sql` ships `enforce_attribution_immutability()`: `NULL→value` allowed, `value→different` raises; override needs `x-allow-attribution-override: true` or the session var AND always writes an audit row — an app-layer-only rule is one forgotten admin screen away from a silent reassignment). `createAttribution({secret, cookiePrefix, maxAgeSeconds})` → `cookieName(scope)`/`sign`/`parse`/`cookieOptions`/`retainFirstTouch`/`shouldWrite`; scoped cookies let one person be introduced to different things by different referrers. Cookie is HttpOnly + **SameSite=Lax, not Strict** (the link is followed cross-site, and Strict drops the cookie on the very navigation that establishes attribution). An **expired** touch parses as `null` = *no* attribution, not *stale* — so a later valid referrer can still be recorded. Keep a self-reported "who told you about us?" field OUTSIDE the protected set: it's a hint, not an attribution. **Wire format (`e`/`a`/`g`/`t`/`ts`) is pinned by a test to stay compatible with cookies F2K already issued** — don't tidy it. Zero deps. 17 tests. **v0.1.0.** |

candidates.title: 9. CODICILS (other non-negotiables that bite)
candidates.material:
## 9. CODICILS (other non-negotiables that bite)

- [ ] **Consequence clarity** — any irreversible (delete/kill), cost-incurring (real API discovery), or outreach-firing action names its consequence *before* the click and requires confirm + (for terminal) a reason. *(Cross-cut of UX-flow-first + the human-in-the-loop principle; reinforced by the 2026-05-25 cockpit naive-test.)*
- [ ] **Email sender** is `noreply@updates.corporateaisolutions.com` (the only Resend-verified subdomain). The bare apex is NOT verified. *(CLAUDE.md "EMAIL INFRASTRUCTURE".)*
- [ ] **CANONICAL SENDER IDENTITY — the legal entity on every portfolio email (Spam Act pillar 2).** The *sending domain* and the *legal sender* are different things: mail goes out from the verified subdomain above, but the identification footer must name the entity behind it. **Locked 2026-07-26:**

  | Var | Value |
  |---|---|
  | `EMAIL_SENDER_NAME` | `Global Buildtech Australia Pty Ltd` |
  | `EMAIL_SENDER_EMAIL` | `dennis@corporateaisolutions.com` |
  | `EMAIL_SENDER_ABN` | `54 672 395 685` (ACN 672 395 685) |
  | `EMAIL_SENDER_POSTAL` | `76-84 Brunswick Street, Fortitude Valley QLD 4006` |
  | `EMAIL_SENDER_PHONE` | `+61402612471` |

  **Single source of truth: `portfolio-manifest.yaml` → `shared:`** — push to any project with `@caistech/portfolio-env-sync`; never retype them into a repo. They are **not secrets** (they are printed at the bottom of emails on purpose), but stay production+preview only per the Vercel env rule. `@caistech/email-compliance`'s `senderFromEnv()` reads them; **without `EMAIL_SENDER_NAME` + `EMAIL_SENDER_EMAIL` it throws**, and consumers that degrade instead will ship mail with **no identification footer** — a Spam Act gap that is invisible until someone complains.

  ⚠️ **White-label gate:** a distributor product sends under the **DISTRIBUTOR's** name and ABN, never these. Override per send with `compliance.sender` (`@caistech/email-send`). Putting our ABN on a distributor's marketing is the failure this rule exists to prevent. *(Codified 2026-07-26 after Kira shipped live email paths with the footer silently absent.)*
- [ ] **Australian Spam Act 2003 compliance on EVERY commercial email — non-negotiable, all repos.** Any commercial electronic message (cold outreach, campaigns, newsletters, registration acknowledgements, nurture sends) MUST satisfy the three pillars: **(1) consent** — express (opted in) or inferred (a conspicuously-published business address, messaged about its function), with the basis stated to the reader; **(2) identification** — the sender's name **+ ABN** + a reply-capable postal address + contact email, valid ≥30 days; **(3) a functional, prominent unsubscribe**, honoured within 5 business days. **Wire `@caistech/email-compliance`** — `complianceFooterHtml`/`complianceFooterText`/`withComplianceFooter` for the footer and **`assertCompliant()` in the send path** so a non-compliant commercial send throws (missing ABN or unsubscribe = hard error). Brand-configurable: **a white-label / distributor product carries the DISTRIBUTOR's identity + ABN, never a CAS one** (the "whose brand travels" gate). Transactional, recipient-initiated mail (password reset, receipt) is not "commercial" and may omit the unsubscribe — but still carries the identification footer. **Registration/opt-in acknowledgements** must record the consent (timestamp + that they agreed to receive further info about the offer) and state that basis in the email. Removal/opt-out requests are honoured by flipping the prospect to an `unsubscribed`/suppressed state the send query excludes (durable against list re-import), never just a one-off delete. *(Codified 2026-06-16 from the f2k employer-campaign + the WA Mining Club removal; package `@caistech/email-compliance`.)*
- [ ] **Jurisdiction guard — we are cleared for AUSTRALIA ONLY; email outreach to non-AU contacts is BLOCKED portfolio-wide until that country's compliance is set up.** Every other country has its own email-marketing law (US CAN-SPAM, Canada CASL, EU/UK GDPR+PECR, …); sending commercial email there before configuring it is a legal exposure. The send path calls `assertJurisdictionAllowed(recipientCountry)` (or passes `recipientCountry` to `assertCompliant`) — a non-AU contact **hard-throws** until the country is added to `SUPPORTED_OUTREACH_JURISDICTIONS` *and* its consent/identification/unsubscribe rules are implemented. Contacts must be country-tagged before a send (unknown country also blocks). **Scope is EMAIL only — LinkedIn outreach (via `@caistech/unipile-channels`) is already within platform compliance and is NOT gated.** *(Codified 2026-06-16; `@caistech/email-compliance` ≥0.2.0.)*
- [ ] **Custom SMTP (Resend) is the STANDARD on every auth-bearing product — the Supabase built-in mailer is NEVER acceptable past the first smoke test.** Three things must all be true, set self-serve via the Management API (`~/.supabase-token`), never by asking the operator or "click the dashboard":
  1. **Custom SMTP configured + enabled** — `smtp_host=smtp.resend.com`, port 465, user `resend`, password = the Resend API key, `smtp_admin_email` = the verified subdomain sender above. (Built-in caps ~2–4/hr and sends from a Supabase address — fails real use.)
  2. **`rate_limit_email_sent` raised off the default `2`/hr** (e.g. 30). This is a SEPARATE Supabase Auth knob from the SMTP config — switching to custom SMTP does **not** raise it, so "SMTP is set up but I'm hitting rate limits" = this value is still 2. (corporate-ai-solutions cockpit `tfgtfhwvrswjvkyeyvsp` bit by exactly this, 2026-06-07: SMTP correct, limit still 2 → raised to 30.) `smtp_max_frequency` (per-address min interval, default 60s) is the secondary throttle.
  3. **Branded, user-friendly email templates** (confirm-signup, magic-link, reset, invite, email-change) — set via `configure-email-templates.sh`, NOT the bland Supabase defaults. Product name + sender voice, not "Confirm your signup".
  **Setup trigger:** t

candidates.title: Storage — the S-rules
candidates.material:
### Storage — the S-rules
- **S1 — Own the substrate for authoritative data + document RAG.** Structured facts and the RAG
  corpus/embeddings live in **our** Supabase (the moat). Managed externals (Mnemo) hold **only
  distilled experiential memory**, never the canonical facts or the citable corpus.
- **S2 — Isolation is mandatory.** RLS on every table; RAG scoped by jurisdiction/state; Mnemo
  scoped by a **stable id** (a row UUID, never a mutable `owner/repo` string that collides across
  tenants). One scope's data can never surface for another.
- **S3 — Freshness + provenance.** Carry `version_date`; set TTL where data goes stale; mark
  snapshots stale rather than silently recompute. No orphan chunks/memories.
- **S4 — REGULATED / PII discipline.** Exact facts stay in auditable tables. Anything that leaves
  our infra (Mnemo) is **distilled + consent-covered**; raw PII never leaves. REGULATED-tier
  products (F2K-Checkpoint, NDIS-SDA, R&D-Tax, disaster-support) get the strictest read of S1/S4.

candidates.title: fix(paid): the path a payment leads to, and the last way to make a personal Kira
candidates.material:
fix(paid): the path a payment leads to, and the last way to make a personal Kira

Walked the paid path end to end for the first time (Stripe test mode, real card
form, local dev against production Supabase). It completes: session reaches
`complete`, the account is created, the dashboard renders with the right name and
gap. Of the 20 checkout sessions in Stripe's visible test history, not one had
ever reached `complete` before this — the register's claim that this was unwalked
was not merely unproven, it was measurably true.

Two things it found, both fixed here.

PERSONAL JOURNEY, STILL REACHABLE (worse than it was filed as)

/setup/draft/[draftId] initialised journeyType to 'personal' and only corrected
itself once the draft fetch returned. So a paying owner did not need to mis-tap
to get the deprecated shape — a slow or failed fetch was enough. A personal Kira
carries the six memory tools and none of the eighteen business ones: no email, no
Drive, no contacts. On 2026-08-05 that agent told a paying owner she had no
connection to his Gmail, Drive or Xero and then distilled the denial into his
memory as a fact about his business.

State now defaults to 'business'; the draft's journey_type is no longer read back,
because a pre-deprecation draft still says 'personal'; the toggle is removed
rather than disabled, since a greyed-out option still tells an owner there is a
version he is not getting. journeyType still travels in the create payload, so the
API contract is unchanged.

PAYING DID NOT LEAD ANYWHERE

/api/onboarding/complete makes the account and stops. Agents are only ever created
from an approved draft, so kira_agents was 0 rows after a real payment, and the
dashboard's "Talk to Kira" button silently fell back to /start.

Every previous attempt at this fixed the routing — which door the button opens —
and the door was never the problem. The paid path now leads INTO the flow that
makes her: /start?journey=business&from=paid, framed as the step it is ("Last step
— let's set up your Kira. About three minutes."). The dashboard fallback stays as
the recovery route and is named as such.

/start also stops looking like a different product. autoConnect is gone, so the
widget renders its pre-connect launcher — "Talk to the assistant", the same button
every other surface shows — instead of dropping a 66-year-old into an already-open
microphone. "Back to selection" offered a way back to a chooser that has had one
option since the personal journey was deprecated; it now goes to the dashboard.

ensureUserAgent IS STILL CALLED NOWHERE, AND THAT IS NOW A DECISION

It is the canonical one-agent-per-user orchestration and wiring it at payment was
the obvious move. Two reasons not to, both recorded at the call site: an agent
provisioned there has no brief, which loses the seeded first message that made the
2026-08-07 fresh-signup test pass — she named his trade, his 35 years and his two
builders; and create/route.ts:11 makes a NEW agent per draft, so provisioning
early hands him a second one the moment he finishes the brief, which is the
duplicate-agent state D2 recorded. Closing it properly means collapsing
create-per-draft into update-the-existing-agent first.

VERIFIED

- /start?journey=business&from=paid renders the new copy, the launcher and the new
  back-link (live, headed browser)
- the review page has no Journey Type label and neither "Personal" nor "Business"
  anywhere (live, fresh draft 6632bb4e)
- /start -> agent creation walked through to a real agent: 18 tools, 38,285-char
  prompt, journey_type=business, status=active — closing the "NOT VERIFIED END TO
  END" warning that has been on 64092a6 since 4 August
- tsc clean, ESLint 0 errors

NOT VERIFIED

- the post-payment redirect itself. It needs a second completed checkout and this
  walk used the one session; everything downstream of the hop is confirmed, the
  hop is not.

candidates.title: fix(create): a returned call is not an attached tool — read the agent back
candidates.material:
fix(create): a returned call is not an attached tool — read the agent back

Found by the re-provision dry run, not by a test.

`tools_attach` logged SUCCESS for Ray's first account at 02:05:11. Seventy-five
minutes later the dry run inspected that same agent and reported `0 tool(s)
attached`. The success was recorded because setAgentTools did not throw, which
is a fact about the call and not about the agent.

An agent with no tools cannot call get_conversation_context, recall_memory or
save_memory. That is not a degraded Kira, it is a Kira with no memory at all —
the entire product — and it looks completely normal from the outside. She talks,
she answers, she silently knows nothing and stores nothing. The owner cannot
tell, and the failure keeps its own log entry saying it went fine.

Whether the write silently did not take or something removed the tools
afterwards is NOT established, and I am not guessing. The read-back catches
both, which is why it is the right fix for a cause still unknown.

Still non-fatal — nobody should lose an account because ElevenLabs was slow —
but non-fatal must not mean unnoticed. One retry, then a log naming the observed
count. `tools_attach: success` now means the tools are on the agent.

candidates.title: fix(valuation): the parts add up to the whole, and a claim stops looking like a failure (#68)
candidates.material:
fix(valuation): the parts add up to the whole, and a claim stops looking like a failure (#68)

The fresh-signup run proved the memory seed works — first message on a brand-new
account, she named the trade, the tenure, the eleven tradesmen, the two builders,
and that he had not told staff or family. Nothing uploaded, nothing retyped, and
it held across a cold page load.

Four things she got right made the four things around her more visible.

1. THE PARTS DID NOT ADD UP. The four contributors under "Where that value is
   hiding" were each rounded independently and summed to $179,500 under a
   headline of $180,000. The model already reconciles the raw uplifts; the page
   then broke that by rounding per line. `displayedUplifts` reconciles them in
   DISPLAYED terms, putting the remainder on the largest line exactly as
   computeValuation does with the raw one. Mutation-verified: reverting the
   reconciliation reproduces 179,500.

2. THE CLAIM CARD PRINTED THE RAW GAP — $179,503, ninety seconds after the
   result page said $180,000, on the first screen after email confirmation. It
   was the one place not yet moved onto displayedFigures, because it lives in a
   component and the sweep that fixed the pages walked past it.

3. CLAIMING LOOKED LIKE IT FAILED. router.refresh() is fire-and-forget, and the
   card was hidden in the same tick — uncovering the untouched "Kira doesn't
   have a starting point" block underneath for a whole round trip. The claim had
   worked. Wrapped in a transition so the card holds its place with an explicit
   saved-and-updating state until the server tree actually arrives.

4. SHE LED WITH THE CAVEAT. "I don't have any additional stored details about
   your business beyond what you initially shared when we started: ..." — true,
   rescued by the colon, and read by the owner as very nearly the sentence the
   seed was built to delete. Ordering, not content. Prompt rule pinned by a
   marker so a rebuild cannot silently drop it; budget raised 37,000 -> 37,300
   with the number and the reason, per that guard's own doctrine.

Also: the auth placeholder now says "Loading the secure form" in words. The
aria-label already said it, to the one visitor who was never confused.

735 tests pass. Prompt change needs a re-provision to reach live agents.

candidates.title: fix(setup): Save looked like it did nothing, and the state box emptied itself
candidates.material:
fix(setup): Save looked like it did nothing, and the state box emptied itself

Three POSTs to /setup/business, three 200s, no row written. Nothing in
the logs, because the server was behaving correctly the whole time.

TWO CAUSES, and each hid the other.

1. THE STATE FIELD SILENTLY EMPTIED. @caistech/mapbox returns
   short_code.replace('AU-','') — "WA" — when Mapbox supplies a short
   code, and falls back to the region's plain text — "Western Australia"
   — when it does not. Same lookup, same day. A <select> can only hold
   the first; the second matched no option, so the box reverted to
   "Choose…" AFTER an address had been picked, with suburb and postcode
   visibly correct either side of it. No reason to look at it again.

   It is now a filled text input like the other two — which is what it
   should have been anyway, a select being the fiddliest control on a
   phone — and normaliseState accepts the code, the full name, or
   anything typed, storing the code either way.

2. THE ERROR WAS SHOWN WHERE HE COULD NOT SEE IT. Every field renders
   its own error and that was not enough: the form is eleven fields
   tall, so the Save button and the field that failed are rarely on
   screen together. Press Save on a phone and the page does not move,
   nothing near the thumb changes, and the only feedback is red text
   several hundred pixels above the fold. From outside, a button that
   does nothing.

   Now a summary at the top, focused on failure so a screen reader gets
   it too.

This is the first screen after paying, for an owner in his sixties. A
silent button there is not a papercut.
